This is selected link configuration and diagnostics, rather than the complete saved model. The separate admin jellyseerr/settings/{type} endpoint can return upstream API keys.

Host compatibility returns {builtFor,hostTarget,hostVersion,pluginVersion,mismatch,expectedAsset,manifestUrl,message}. It diagnoses an installed artifact targeting a different Jellyfin version; no feature toggle is required.

docs.title: Static-resource limits and caching
docs.text:
Use these rules when loading or retaining JE scripts, translations, fonts, and mirrored assets.

Setting Default What it does Dev Mode false DevMode; switches script/bundle delivery to no-store; bundles rebuild per request.

Production scripts, CSS, component bundles/maps, and fonts use one-year immutable caching. Use a version/build cache key in resource URLs when retaining them. Embedded missing resources return 404; unavailable bundle instance 503, bundle-build failure 500.

Locale JSON tries the requested code, then a base-language fallback such as de-DE → de, then returns 404.

Font names are materialsymbolsrounded-subset.woff2, materialsymbolsoutlined-subset.woff2, materialsymbolsrounded.woff2, materialsymbolsoutlined.woff2. Unsupported/missing names return 404.

CDN source is one of selfhst, jellyfish, dashboard-icons, zesty, jelly-helper, moonbase, flagcdn, flag-icons, ibb, locales, je-docs-img, je-css, icon-metadata, elsewhere-res, award-logos, mdblist-logos, mdblist-static, ddd-static. It is a fixed-source mirror, rather than a generic URL proxy.

Paths/content types are validated, and some sources allow only fixed assets. Unknown/refused/unavailable assets return 404; success uses the asset MIME, one-day public caching, ETag and 304. No client feature toggle gates fonts/CDN.

docs.title: *arr (Sonarr/Radarr/Bazarr)
docs.text: JE queries configured Sonarr/Radarr instances for links, downloads, and calendar data; the calendar can also use configured Shoko. These routes do not provide a general Bazarr API proxy. See *arr settings for multi-instance configuration and browser URL mappings.

docs.title: Validation and instance lookup
docs.text:
All routes in this table require Administrator access. Lookup routes query enabled instances and do not check a client link toggle.

Method Path Inputs → response GET arr/validate/sonarr Query url, header X-Arr-ApiKey → {ok:true}. GET arr/validate/radarr Query url, header X-Arr-ApiKey → {ok:true}. GET arr/identify-url Query url → {reachable,service}. GET arr/series-slug Positive query tvdbId; first enabled Sonarr → {titleSlug}. GET arr/series-slugs Positive query tvdbId; all enabled Sonarr → {matches,errors}. GET arr/movie-instances Positive query tmdbId; all enabled Radarr → {matches,errors}. GET arr/links Query tmdbIds/tvdbIds lists → {movies:{id:{matches,errors}},series:{id:{matches,errors}}}. 
ARR_URL='http://sonarr:8989'
ARR_KEY='YOUR_SONARR_API_KEY'
curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H "X-Arr-ApiKey: $ARR_KEY" --data-urlencode "url=$ARR_URL" \
  "$JE_URL/arr/validate/sonarr"

curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'tmdbIds=603,604' --data-urlencode 'tvdbIds=121361' \
  "$JE_URL/arr/links"

Validation tests supplied URL/key values, including unsaved values. Missing/rejected inputs return 400; invalid upstream auth returns 401; timeout 504; connection failure 502; other upstream statuses can pass through. Failures use {ok:false,message}. URLs use the same HTTP(S)/address guard described under Seerr.

URL identification probes the supplied URL without looking up an item. Service values include Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr, Jellyfin, Seerr, arr, unknown. Invalid input returns 400 {reachable:false,service:"unknown"}; an unrecognized responding site can return reachable:true,service:"unknown".

Single series lookup returns 400 for nonpositive IDs, 404 for no configured/found series/slug, 500 for missing/corrupt configuration, 502 for instance-fetch failure.

Multi-instance lookups require a positive ID (400), return 500 for absent plugin configuration, and retain partial matches and separate per-instance errors. No configured instances yields empty maps/arrays; all-disabled/corrupt settings add errors.

A series match contains instanceName, instanceUrl, urlMappings, titleSlug, episodeFileCount, episodeCount, percentOfEpisodes, sizeOnDisk, rootFolderPath.

A movie match contains instanceName, instanceUrl, urlMappings, hasFile, sizeOnDisk, rootFolderPath; size is bytes. Errors contain instanceName, reason.

Batch inputs are comma-separated positive integer movie TMDB IDs and series TVDB IDs. Invalid values/duplicates are ignored. No valid IDs or more than 100 combined IDs returns 400; disconnect can return 499. Plural series lookup accepts one series ID across instances, rather than multiple IDs.

docs.title: Queue, history, and Requests data
docs.text:
These reads require authentication. Queue/history are administrator-visible without Seerr linkage; non-admin filtering depends on server settings and a linked caller's requests.

Setting Default What it does Filter Downloads by User Requests true DownloadsFilterByUserRequests; filters non-admin queue/history by caller's linked Seerr requests. Show Download History Section true DownloadsShowHistory; controls history availability. Restrict Download History to Admins false DownloadsHistoryAdminOnly; hides history from viewers. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 DownloadsPollIntervalSeconds; also cache TTL, clamped 5..300 seconds. Method Path Parameters → response GET arr/queue No parameters → {items,errors}. GET arr/history take=20 clamped 1..50, skip=0 minimum 0 → {items,totalPages,visible}. GET arr/requests take=20 clamped 1..200, skip=0 minimum 0, optional filter, userOnly=false → {requests,totalPages,totalResults,canApproveRequests}. POST arr/requests/{requestId}/approve Seerr request ID, no body → {success:true}. POST arr/requests/{requestId}/decline Seerr request ID, no body → {success:true}. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/arr/history?take=20&skip=0"
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/arr/requests?filter=processing&userOnly=true"
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/arr/requests/42/approve"

Queue items contain id, source, instanceName, title, subtitle, nullable seasonNumber, episodeNumber, status, progress, totalSize, sizeRemaining, timeRemaining, posterUrl, tmdbId. Progress is percentage (rounded to one decimal); sizes are bytes. Errors contain instanceName, source, reason. Per-instance failures preserve other instances' items.

History items contain source, instanceName, title, subtitle, eventType, date, posterUrl, tmdbId; grouped Sonarr packs additionally contain episodeCount, importedCount, failedCount. Event types include imported, failed, and grouped partial. The merged history is bounded to 200 entries before caller filtering/paging; totalPages covers this visible window, rather than all upstream history.

Instance failures can yield partial/empty history without an errors array.

History disabled or admin-restricted returns successful empty results with visible:false. Unavailable non-admin linkage/request data can return successful empty queue/history with history visible:true.

Thus an empty successful result can mean privacy filtering, rather than an empty server queue. Missing plugin configuration returns 500.

Requests uses Seerr credentials and caller linkage (400 for missing caller claim, 404 for unlinked). Missing saved URL/key can return an empty successful response without canApproveRequests; other unavailable upstream results return error statuses rather than a successful empty list.

This enriched endpoint differs from the raw jellyseerr/request proxy. It does not merge queue items into its requests array; queue is fetched separately.

Request records contain id, type, title, year, posterUrl, tmdbId, tvdbId, mediaStatus, requestStatus, requestedBy, requestedByAvatar, createdAt, jellyfinMediaId, digitalReleaseDate, theatricalReleaseDate, initialAirDate, nextAirDate, isComingSoon, isOrphaned. Optional fields can be missing/null.

Raw request statuses are 1 Pending, 2 Approved, 3 Declined, 4 Failed, 5 Completed, separate from media availability.

filter recognizes pending, approved, available, processing, comingsoon; other values use the upstream unfiltered list. Callers without REQUEST_VIEW, MANAGE_REQUESTS, or admin authority see only their own requests; userOnly=true also enforces this.

Processing/Coming Soon split a 500-record upstream processing window: future release/air-date items go to Coming Soon, others Processing, excluding orphaned rows from both.

Orphan detection considers old Approved/Processing requests and missing content in configured *arr instances. Counts/pagination on the split are bounded to that source window. Parental filtering applies.

Approve/decline requires a linked caller with Jellyfin administrator authority, Seerr ADMIN, or MANAGE_REQUESTS. Missing setup returns 503; missing caller identity 400; unlinked 404; insufficient permission 403. It uses the first configured URL and passes upstream failure statuses through. An administrator API key lacking a linked caller cannot bypass linkage.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
Read upcoming events from configured sources, then use user-data to retrieve favorite and watched flags for event references.

Setting Default What it does Filter by Library Access true CalendarFilterByLibraryAccess; excludes events with known inaccessible items/root folders. Method Path Access Request → response GET arr/calendar Authenticated Optional query start, end → {events,errors}. POST arr/calendar/user-data Existing caller {Events:[<event reference>]} → {results:[{id,isFavorite,isWatched}]}.

GET defaults to today's UTC date through 90 days ahead. Parseable dates override each endpoint; invalid dates retain defaults, reversed ranges swap, ranges over 365 days cap at 365. Missing configuration returns 500. Enabled Sonarr/Radarr and configured Shoko contribute events; per-source errors contain instanceName, source, reason.

Calendar events contain id, source, type, title, subtitle, releaseDate, releaseType, hasFile, monitored, posterUrl, backdropUrl, imdbId, Jellyfin itemId, itemEpisodeId, overview, tvdbId, seasonNumber, episodeNumber, episodeTvdbId, episodeImdbId, upstream seriesId, tmdbId, shokoSeriesId, shokoEpisodeId, instanceName, alsoInInstances. Nullable fields can be absent.

Duplicate entries across instances are combined, preferring accessible/file-backed entries and recording other instance names.

Internal root-folder access information is not serialized in calendar events. If item/root-folder access cannot be determined, an event can pass the access filter. Requested-only display preferences operate in the client.

curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/arr/calendar?start=2026-10-01&end=2026-10-31"
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/arr/calendar/user-data" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"events":[{"id":"fixture","type":"Movie","itemId":"9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd"}]}'

User-data references accept optional Id, Type, Title, nullable GUID ItemId, ItemEpisodeId, nullable integer TvdbId, TmdbId, SeasonNumber, EpisodeNumber, and nullable string ImdbId.

Only IDs/type are needed for flag reads. Use exact Type:"Movie"/"Series" for watched-state handling. isFavorite actually reads Likes == true; isWatched includes Played or positive resume ticks on a movie, or on the supplied episode for Series.

This POST does not save preferences. Missing caller/account returns 401; empty events return an empty array; lookup failures can leave partial results.

docs.title: Activity Feed & What's New
docs.text:
Activity merges recent watched/favorited entries with user reviews into library cards. What's New is the administrator's server-wide settings acknowledgment.

Setting Default What it does Enable Activity Feed false ActivityFeedEnabled; disabled API returns 404. Show recently watched true ActivityFeedShowWatched; includes watched entries. Show recently favorited true ActivityFeedShowFavorited; includes favorite entries. Show recently reviewed true ActivityFeedShowReviewed; includes reviews. Method Path Access Contract GET activity Existing caller limit=50, clamped 1..200 → {items:[<activity>]}, no-store. GET whats-new Administrator {pluginVersion,newSettings}. POST whats-new/dismiss Administrator No body → empty 200; acknowledges server-wide state. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/activity?limit=50"

Activity requires a nonempty existing caller (403 otherwise).

Rows have ActivityType (Watched, Favorited, Reviewed), UserId, UserName, UserHasPrimaryImage, Unix-millisecond Timestamp, Item, nullable Rating/Content, boolean Completed, numeric Progress (fraction 0..1).

Item summaries contain Id, Name, Type, ProductionYear, SeriesName, SeriesId, SeasonNumber, EpisodeNumber, HasPrimaryImage, HasThumbImage, SeriesHasPrimaryImage, SeriesHasThumbImage.

Results are newest first and respect viewer library access and configured author visibility, including admin/self exceptions. Missing items and filtered authors are skipped; review keys resolve to the parent title for cards.

Watched records can represent partial playback; Completed distinguishes completion and Progress retains the highest observed fraction.

What's New newSettings maps setting-control IDs to the plugin version in which each was first detected; absent state returns null pluginVersion and {}.

docs.title: Catch Up API
docs.text:
Log Catch Up swipes and retrieve an administrator feed/summary. Ingestion records events; it does not mark an item watched, dismiss it, or mutate watchlists.

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up false CatchUpEnabled; required for recording. Record Catch Up activity true CatchUpLogEnabled; required for recording. Method Path Access Contract POST catchup/event Authenticated; existing caller when recording Event body → empty 204. GET catchup/events Administrator Filters below → {events,users,total}. GET catchup/summary Administrator {users,topWatched,topDismissed,topWatchlisted}. 
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/catchup/event" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"type":"swipe","action":"watched","itemId":"9285e8b54149414941494edb9e464dcd","ok":true,"seasons":["1"]}'
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/catchup/events?action=watched,undo&limit=200"

Body fields: required valid type and action, optional undoOf, nullable GUID itemId, nullable boolean ok, optional string array seasons.

Type/action are lowercased; type must be swipe, actions watched, dismiss, watchlist, open, undo. Supplied undoOf must be a known action. Invalid action/type returns 400; missing existing caller returns 401 when recording.

Identity, time, title, and item kind are server-derived. Seasons retain at most 100 entries, each clipped to eight characters; "all" represents all seasons.

With either recording toggle off, requests reaching the action return 204 without its identity/event validation. Authentication and MVC binding still apply. 204 is acceptance rather than a JSON receipt or guaranteed durable write: logging I/O failures are caught internally.

Feed query Default/rules user Unset; username equality, case-insensitive. action Unset; comma-separated known values, compared case-sensitively to stored lowercase actions. q Unset; title substring, case-insensitive. since Unset; inclusive lexical comparison with stored UTC yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ strings. limit 200; clamped 1..1000.

Events return in reverse retained-log order. Each has ts, userId, user, type, action, undoOf, itemId, itemName, kind, ok, seasons; optional values can be null. users and total cover the entire retained log, rather than only the filtered page.

Summary users entries have user, lastSeen, watched, dismiss, watchlist. Top lists have at most 15 {itemId,name,kind,count,users} records each. Counts are distinct surviving username/item/action marks, ignore ok:false, and account for undo.

Storage is catchup-log.jsonl plus catchup-log.1.jsonl at the shared plugin configuration root. The live file rotates before the next append once it exceeds 5 MiB, replacing older rotated history. Retention is bounded. Admin reads work with recording disabled.

docs.title: Usage Analytics API
docs.text:
Track the plugin's supported usage counters or preview a report. See community analytics for reporting behavior.

Setting Default What it does Share Anonymous Usage Statistics false AnalyticsEnabled; master opt-in. Feature toggle states (on/off only) true AnalyticsShareFeatureFlags; report flag category. Feature usage counts true AnalyticsShareUsageCounts; enables tracking alongside master. Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) true AnalyticsShareDataSizes; report size category. Method Path Access Contract POST usage/track Authenticated {"key":"seerr.request_submitted"} → empty 200. POST usage/preview Administrator JSON object with optional booleans shareFeatureFlags, shareUsageCounts, shareDataSizes → preview. 
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/usage/preview" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"shareFeatureFlags":true,"shareUsageCounts":true,"shareDataSizes":false}'

Allowed counter keys are seerr.request_submitted, continue_watching.auto_removed. Tracking returns empty 200 without recording unless master and usage counts are both enabled.

When active, an expected object with missing/non-string, invalid-format, or unknown key returns 400. Use an object; action-level 400 behavior is not guaranteed for arbitrary non-object JSON.

Preview falls back to saved category values for omitted/non-boolean properties. It returns Payload, LastReportedAt (Unix milliseconds), and LastPayloadJson (string).

Payload contains strings InstallId, PluginVersion, JellyfinVersion, JellyfinTarget, Period, nullable boolean map Config, nullable string map Settings, nullable byte-size map DataFileSizes, and nullable Events array of {key,count}.

It neither registers an installation nor transmits a report. An unregistered installation shows a placeholder ID. Missing configuration returns 503.

The admin Preview button sends unsaved category values; its controls appear when the master checkbox is checked.

docs.title: Active Streams & Proxy
docs.text: Use these routes to read playback sessions, broadcast messages, retrieve avatars, or find Jellyfin item IDs from provider IDs.

docs.title: Sessions and broadcasts
docs.text:
Read now-playing sessions or send an administrator message to sessions with usable usernames.

Setting Default What it does Active Streams Header Widget false ActiveStreamsEnabled; disabled sessions/broadcast return 503. Show widget to non-admins false ActiveStreamsAllUsers; allows viewer session reads, otherwise 403. Method Path Access Contract GET active-streams/sessions Administrator, or authenticated with viewer setting enabled Bare now-playing session array. POST active-streams/broadcast Administrator {Header,Text,TimeoutMs} → {sent,skipped,errors}. GET proxy/avatar Authenticated Query path → cached raster image bytes. GET items/by-providers Authenticated Query provider dictionary and optional types → one matching GUID. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/active-streams/sessions"
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/active-streams/broadcast" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"Header":"Notice","Text":"Please finish playback soon.","TimeoutMs":30000}'

Non-admin RemoteEndPoint is null/omitted. Session lookup failure returns 500.

Session response fields

Session fields are UserId, UserName, UserHasPrimaryImage, Client, DeviceName, RemoteEndPoint, LastActivityDate, NowPlayingItem, PlayState, TranscodingInfo.

  • NowPlayingItem has Id, Type, Name, SeriesName, RunTimeTicks, ProductionYear, ParentIndexNumber, IndexNumber, ImageTags, SeriesId, SeriesPrimaryImageTag, MediaStreams (Type, Codec, BitRate).
  • PlayState has IsPaused, PositionTicks, PlayMethod.
  • TranscodingInfo has IsVideoDirect, VideoCodec, AudioCodec, Bitrate, TranscodeReasons, CompletionPercentage, Width, Height, Framerate.

Broadcast requires nonblank Text (400 otherwise), optional nullable Header/TimeoutMs.

It attempts all sessions with a usable username other than Unknown, including idle sessions. Send failures increment skipped and add error strings; a successful HTTP response can contain failures.

docs.title: Avatar and item-ID lookup
docs.text:
Retrieve an avatar from the first configured Seerr URL, or look up a Jellyfin item by provider IDs.

Avatar uses the first configured Seerr URL and strips query/fragment from path. It accepts /avatar/, /avatarproxy/, /api/v1/avatar/; traversal/scheme/unsafe paths return 400.

Missing setup/image, upstream failure, or unsupported MIME returns 404. Supported raster MIME types are PNG, JPEG/JPG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP.

It caches for one hour with ETag and 304; no caller linkage is required.

curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'path=/avatar/example.png' "$JE_URL/proxy/avatar"
curl -G -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'providers[Tmdb]=603' --data-urlencode 'types=Movie' \
  "$JE_URL/items/by-providers"

Provider lookup accepts multiple dictionary entries such as providers[Tmdb], providers[Imdb]. types is a comma-separated item-kind list parsed case-insensitively; invalid kinds are ignored. No IDs/match returns 400 with No provider ids supplied or no items found; success is a GUID value.

Repository lookup is not filtered to caller library access and does not establish permission to view the returned item.

docs.title: Branding
docs.text:
Upload, retrieve, and remove custom branding assets. No enable toggle is required for storage operations.

Valid slots are icon-transparent.png, banner-light.png, banner-dark.png, favicon.ico, apple-touch-icon.png; names normalize to lowercase.

Method Path Access Request → response POST UploadBrandingImage Administrator Multipart first file plus form fileName → success string File uploaded successfully. GET BrandingStatus Authenticated Filename-to-existence boolean map for all five slots. GET BrandingImage Authenticated Query fileName → stored bytes with extension-derived MIME. POST DeleteBrandingImage Administrator Form fileName → success string File deleted successfully. 
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/UploadBrandingImage" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -F 'file=@logo.png;type=image/png' -F 'fileName=icon-transparent.png'
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/DeleteBrandingImage" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'fileName=icon-transparent.png'

Upload checks an image/ MIME prefix and a 10 MiB maximum; it does not decode-validate image contents.

Missing files/fields in a valid form, a missing retrieval fileName, unsupported slot/MIME, or oversized upload returns 400.

Upload/delete requests without a supported form content type return 500 when the actions try to read form data. Missing retrieval/deletion file returns 404; filesystem permission failures on upload/delete return 403; internal/filesystem errors 500.

Delete reads a form, rather than JSON, and uses POST. Upload overwrites the selected slot.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text:
Use these routes to check, enable, or end a maintenance window and send maintenance messages.

These routes require Administrator access. See Other settings for maintenance configuration.

Method Path Request → response GET MaintenanceMode/Status Current state object. POST MaintenanceMode/Enable JSON request below → {"success":true}. POST MaintenanceMode/Disable Optional query includeScheduled=true → {"success":true}. GET MaintenanceMode/Users Bare array of all eligible non-admin {Id,Username,HasImage} accounts. POST MaintenanceMode/Broadcast {Header,Text,TimeoutMs} → {sent,skipped,errors}. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/MaintenanceMode/Status"
curl -X POST "$JE_URL/MaintenanceMode/Enable" \
  -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"Message":"Maintenance notice","DurationMinutes":15,"Action":"none"}'
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" \
  "$JE_URL/MaintenanceMode/Disable?includeScheduled=true"
Enable property Default Meaning Message Empty effective message Banner text. NotificationMessage Null Optional popup text; falls back to message. DurationMinutes 0 Positive minutes set a deadline; nonpositive means open-ended. Action "disable_accounts" Recognized, case-sensitive strings: none, disable_accounts, disable_remote, both. AffectedUserIds Null Null/empty targets all non-admin users. Otherwise string-array target IDs.

Maintenance access changes

disable_accounts and both can disable selected accounts; disable_remote and both can disable remote access. Use Action:"none" for a notice-only window. Unknown action strings are not rejected, but disable neither account nor remote access.

For an active manual window, resending the same duration, action, and affected-user set preserves the existing deadline. Target-set comparison ignores order/duplicates but compares supplied strings, so differently formatted IDs can compare differently. Changing these values can establish a new deadline.

Status fields are IsActive, Message, NotificationMessage, Action, Source (manual/schedule when active), StartedAt, EndsAt, AccountDisabledCount, RemoteDisabledCount, ServerLocalTime (HH:mm), ServerUtcOffset (such as +08:00). End time can be null for open-ended maintenance.

The Users list is the full non-admin selector list, rather than just currently affected users.

Disable defaults to ending any active manual/scheduled window. includeScheduled=false leaves a scheduled window running. Ending a scheduled window suppresses it until the next day's window.

Broadcast can run without active maintenance. It requires nonblank Text (400 otherwise) and accepts optional Header and TimeoutMs=30000. It resolves {countdown}/{ends_at} against the maintenance state. Nonpositive timeouts fall back to 30000 ms.

It attempts all sessions with a usable username, including idle sessions. Send failures are returned in errors and included in skipped.

docs.title: Misc
docs.text:
Use these routes to reset user preferences from server defaults or retrieve a registered JE page's HTML.

Method Path Access Contract POST reset-all-users-settings Administrator No body → {success,userCount,totalUsers,skippedSettingsUserIds,skippedHcUserIds}. GET {viewName} Authenticated Exact registered plugin view name → HTML. 
curl -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"$TOKEN\"" "$JE_URL/bookmarksPage"

Reset enumerates existing canonical user configuration directories and replaces Enhanced settings using copied server defaults, with model-default exceptions. WatchProgressMode resets to "percentage" and WatchProgressTimeFormat to "hours", even when the saved server defaults differ.

Reset also resets Hidden Content settings while retaining items, and preferences in existing Spoiler Guard files while retaining protection lists. It does not reset bookmarks, reviews, shortcuts, or Elsewhere.

success:true can accompany skipped settings/Hidden Content users. Spoiler preference-reset failures are logged without a separate skipped-ID list. Missing configuration returns 500.

The authenticated HTML catch-all recognizes exact names calendarPage, downloadsPage, bookmarksPage, hiddenContentPage, recommendationsPage, activityPage, catchUpPage.

These are resource URLs, separate from Jellyfin web hash navigation or placement in Plugin Pages/Custom Tabs. Unknown names/missing resources return 404; absent plugin instance 400. See JE Pages & Tabs for placement options.

docs.title: Full Endpoint Index
docs.text:
The endpoint tables above enumerate all 173 controller method/path entries, including the three catch-all templates. Each group documents effective access, inputs, response shape, and limits; shared proxy rows intentionally retain the configured upstream service's JSON contract.

For implementation details, JellyfinEnhancedController.cs implements all indexed routes except catchup/*, which is in CatchUpController.cs. These upstream source links may advance beyond this versioned reference.

docs.title: Community Analytics
docs.text:
JE can share installation statistics to help you see how the community uses the plugin. Reporting is opt-in and off by default; an administrator must enable Share Anonymous Usage Statistics and save.

About the dashboard

The dashboard reads aggregate results from public views. Visiting this page makes browser requests to the analytics service, Google Fonts and external tab-icon assets, even if your Jellyfin server has never enabled reporting. These requests are separate from installation reports.

The figures show trends among installations that choose to report. They do not count all JE installations.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
Choose the categories you want to share, and use Preview to check the statistics before saving.

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Admin → Usage Statistics.
  2. Turn on Share Anonymous Usage Statistics to show the category, interval, and Preview controls. Uncheck any categories you do not want to share.
  3. Optionally click Preview to inspect your selections.
  4. Save. JE queues the first reporting attempt automatically; you do not need to use Preview first.

The page shows the last successful report time, or tells you that no report has been sent yet.

Administrator settings:

Setting Default What it does Share Anonymous Usage Statistics Off Enables server reporting to the community analytics service. Feature toggle states (on/off only) On Shares on/off settings and selected text settings, despite the checkbox wording. Feature usage counts On Shares action counts and current totals of stored entries. Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) On Shares the total size of the custom branding directory. Reporting interval (days) 15 Sets how often reports are sent, within 7–30 days. Details

On first enablement, the interface checks all three categories. After you save your choices, later enables preserve them. The category defaults do not enable reporting while the master setting is off.

If you uncheck all three categories, reports still include version information, installation credentials, the counting-period start date and build proof. See Always included below. The reporting interval is clamped to 7–30 days.

docs.title: What Preview shows
docs.text:
Preview lets you inspect the selected statistics without registering your installation or sending a report. It uses the category selections currently on screen, including unsaved changes.

Previewing a report does not enable sharing.

Other configuration values come from your saved server configuration. Counts and file sizes show the current state and may change before JE sends the report.

How it works

The preview route is administrator-only: POST /JellyfinEnhanced/usage/preview. Before registration, the install ID reads (not registered yet; assigned on first real send).

Preview shows readable property names. The actual report uses p_* field names and also sends the installation secret and a build-proof field, neither of which appears in Preview. The proof comes from the plugin assembly, installation ID and plugin version. It can be null if JE cannot read the assembly.

docs.title: What's collected
docs.text: Every enabled report includes installation and version information. The three optional categories add settings, counts or branding-directory size.

docs.title: Always included
docs.text:
Every enabled report includes these fields, even if you uncheck all three categories:

  • A persistent installation ID assigned by the reporting service.
  • The plugin version, Jellyfin server version and build target.
  • The start date of the counting period.
  • The installation secret used to authenticate the report, and the build-proof field.
How it works

The build target is jf10 or jf12. During registration, the service returns the installation ID and secret. JE stores them in its plugin configuration.

docs.title: Feature toggle states
docs.text:
This category shows which features participating servers use. It shares on/off settings, whether TMDB and MDBList keys are configured, and a selected set of text settings.

Select Feature toggle states (on/off only) before saving to include this category.

How it works

Boolean settings are included except properties beginning with Analytics and properties marked [AnalyticsExclude]. TmdbEnabled and MdblistEnabled indicate whether keys are configured; the keys themselves are not sent.

The selected text settings are:

Choice Reported property and filtering Icon style IconStyle Maintenance actions and affected users MaintenanceModeAction, MaintenanceScheduleAction and MaintenanceModeAffectedUsers. The user scope is reduced to all or selected, without selected user IDs. Tag positions QualityTagsPosition, GenreTagsPosition, LanguageTagsPosition, RatingTagsPosition, AgeRatingTagsPosition Tag styling TagStyleTarget, TagStylePreset, TagStyleApplyScope Language priority LanguageTagsPriority, filtered to tokens shaped like language codes and converted to lowercase Additional Native Poster Tags client exclusions NativePosterTagsWebClientNames, filtered to short app-name-shaped entries, deduplicated and limited to 20. Built-in web clients are omitted.

Nonempty strings marked [AnalyticsInclude] are included as stored. Other strings are excluded unless the reporting code explicitly derives and filters them. Checking the shape of language/client strings does not guarantee what the entered text means.

The report does not include configured service URLs, media-service API keys, branding text or image contents.

docs.title: Feature usage counts
docs.text:
This category shares counts of Seerr requests and qualifying home-row removal events, plus totals of stored entries. It sends counts rather than titles, review contents or user records.

Select Feature usage counts before saving to include this category.

Current totals cover:

  • Bookmarks across user files.
  • Hidden-content entries, including home-row suppression entries.
  • Direct Spoiler Guard series, movie and collection entries; pending protection intents are excluded.
  • Reviews in the shared review store.

These totals count entries. The same title can contribute entries for several users, so the totals do not count unique titles or users.

How it works

Action counters record:

Counter Meaning seerr.request_submitted Submitted Seerr requests recorded by the client. continue_watching.auto_removed Playback-start events that clear or demote qualifying home-row removals while the Remove Continue Watching feature is enabled. Counts events, not individual entries removed.

Actions count only while reporting and the usage-count category are enabled. JE does not reconstruct earlier activity. Each off-to-on reporting transition clears counters at the point you enable reporting.

Every successful report advances the counting period and subtracts the captured counter snapshot. This also happens when Feature usage counts is unchecked and those earlier counts were omitted from the report. Increments during transmission carry forward. Failed attempts do not subtract the captured counts.

docs.title: Data file sizes
docs.text:
This category shares the total size of your custom branding directory, without file names or contents. It does not include other plugin data-file sizes.

Select Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) before saving to include this category.

How it works

The report uses the key custom_branding. It sends the total bytes in the branding directory, or zero if the directory is absent, empty or unreadable.

docs.title: Reporting, storage and opt-out
docs.text:
JE checks whether a report is due at startup and through the Send Anonymous Usage Report scheduled task. Turning reporting on and saving queues an immediate attempt.

To stop reporting:

  1. Open Admin → Usage Statistics in the plugin configuration.
  2. Turn off Share Anonymous Usage Statistics and save.

Opting out and remote history

For a registered installation, JE asks the service to exclude it from public views while keeping its history. Re-enabling reporting asks the service to include it again. Both effects depend on successful requests and the external service. Turning reporting off does not request remote deletion.

How it works

The server sends HTTPS requests to https://cgsdfzfdoxunzoofzhgd.supabase.co. Registration uses /rest/v1/rpc/register_install; reports use /rest/v1/rpc/report_stats.

The scheduled task's default trigger is every 24 hours. It sends only when the configured interval has elapsed or the plugin version, Jellyfin version or build target has changed. Running the task manually uses the same check. Saving an off-to-on transition bypasses the check for its immediate attempt.

Failed registration or reporting logs a warning, retains unsent counts and leaves the last-success timestamp unchanged. Repeated credential rejection can cause JE to clear its credentials and register again on the next attempt.

Credentials, the last report projection and report state are saved in plugin configuration. Action counters are stored locally in usage-counters.json.

Opting out queues a best-effort /rest/v1/rpc/set_opted_out request using the installation ID and secret. Re-enabling queues a report intended to clear that flag.

Details

Reports have no dedicated username, media-title or IP-address fields. They do use persistent installation credentials and selected text settings. This repository does not establish the remote service's retention policy or access-log practices. The dashboard shows aggregate results.

docs.title: Local Catch Up activity log
docs.text:
Catch Up has a separate local activity log for administrators. Its records are not included in installation analytics reports.

With Enable Catch Up and Record Catch Up activity enabled, the server records the user's username and ID, title and ID, action, time, reported success, and selected seasons where applicable. Only administrators can retrieve the log and summary through JE.

To stop future recording, turn off Record Catch Up activity and save.

Administrator settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up Off Enables the Catch Up page. Record Catch Up activity On Records local activity when Catch Up is enabled. How it works

The server keeps catchup-log.jsonl and one rotated catchup-log.1.jsonl beside JE's shared data files. Rotation occurs at approximately 5 MiB per file.

See Catch Up and Activity and settings.

docs.title: Live Dashboard
docs.text:
Browse aggregate results from participating installations. Usage covers the last 45 days; totals show current stored entries.

  1. Use the facet buttons to select a settings tab.
  2. Type to filter a table.
  3. Click a column heading to sort; click it again to reverse the order.

Data reloads when you arrive on the page or refresh your browser. A version warning means the build target does not match the Jellyfin major version.

Details

Feature Toggle Adoption lists settings present in reporting data. New or unreported settings may be absent; it is not a complete configuration catalog.

Labels and defaults come from the generated settings map. Unknown labels use readable versions of property names, and unknown groups use Other.

Queries have these limits:

Data Limit Versions Up to 500 rows fetched; the largest 50 fetched groups appear in the version table Usage 20 rows Current totals 24 rows Feature flags 500 rows Setting values 500 rows

Settings percentages use the fetched value rows for each setting. These limits can further reduce the sample.

Loading live data…

docs.title: CSS Custom Styling
docs.text:
Use Custom CSS to change the appearance of Jellyfin Enhanced's web overlays, tags, settings panel, and notifications.

These recipes target elements created by JE's injected web client. The feature must be enabled and its metadata available before CSS can style it.

For feature setup and client requirements, see Compatibility, Tags & Badges, and Enhanced Settings.

docs.title: Applying Custom CSS
docs.text:
As a Jellyfin administrator:

  1. Open Dashboard → Branding.
  2. Paste the recipes you want into Custom CSS Code, alongside your existing CSS.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Reload the web client. Use Ctrl+F5 for a hard refresh in browsers that support it.

This applies CSS server-wide to web clients that load Jellyfin's Custom CSS. Test the result on desktop and phone layouts.

To undo a recipe, remove its rules, save, and reload.

docs.title: When a rule has no effect
docs.text:
Inspect the element in your browser's developer tools and check its actual classes, attributes, and computed styles. A disabled feature, absent metadata, or a native poster image can leave nothing for the selector to match.

The examples use !important where needed to beat built-in colors, inline styles, or responsive rules. Scope changes to a JE container and keep hover, selected, disabled, and focus states usable.

How CSS rules compete

JE uses ordinary stylesheets, ordinary inline styles, and !important declarations:

  • An ordinary inline style beats ordinary stylesheet rules.
  • An important stylesheet rule can override an ordinary inline style.
  • Among competing important rules in these stylesheets, higher specificity wins. Equal specificity falls back to document order.

JE appends shared styles, pause-screen styles, and Tag Styles overrides to the document head. On Jellyfin 12 web, Custom CSS is rendered in the body, after those head styles. Equal-specificity rules can therefore win even if JE injected its style later in time.

The panel also embeds its own style element in the body. Inspect the winning declaration instead of assuming all styles have the same order, especially on Jellyfin 10.11.

docs.title: Pause Screen
docs.text:
The pause screen shows artwork, item details, plot, and a progress snapshot while playback is paused. Enable it in your personal Playback Settings, pause a video, and leave the player idle to preview your CSS.

The administrator sets the default; viewers can override it in the Enhanced panel.

Setting Default What it does Enable Custom Pause Screen (admin) / Custom Pause Screen (viewer) On PauseScreenEnabled: enables the pause overlay. Delay before showing (seconds): (viewer) 5 PauseScreenDelaySeconds: delay during paused inactivity; the panel accepts 1–60 seconds.

Clicks, touches, key presses, scrolling, and mouse movement beyond the movement threshold reset the inactivity timer.

Missing logo or disc artwork stays hidden. Artwork lookup considers the item and applicable parent/series artwork.

docs.title: Elements and visibility
docs.text:
Use these selectors to style or hide individual parts of the pause screen.

Element CSS selector What it contains Dialog #pause-screen-overlay Outer overlay; visible when aria-hidden="false". Content #pause-screen-content Backdrop, logo, details, plot, progress, and close button. Logo #pause-screen-logo Item logo image. Details #pause-screen-details Item metadata. Plot #pause-screen-plot Scrollable synopsis. Progress wrapper #pause-screen-progress-wrap Bar and labels. Progress track #pause-screen-progress-bar Track behind the fill. Progress fill #pause-screen-progress-bar > span Playback snapshot; width is written inline. Progress labels #pause-screen-progress-meta .progress-time, .progress-percentage, .progress-ends-at. Spinning disc #pause-screen-disc Disc image; a direct child of the overlay. Backdrop #pause-screen-backdrop Background artwork layer. Close button #pause-screen-close-btn Dismisses the overlay for this pause without resuming.

Hide any optional region using its ID. For example:

#pause-screen-logo,
#pause-screen-details,
#pause-screen-plot,
#pause-screen-progress-wrap,
#pause-screen-disc,
#pause-screen-backdrop {
    display: none !important;
}

Keep only the selectors for regions you want to hide. You can style the remaining regions independently:

#pause-screen-progress-bar > span {
    background: gold !important;
}

#pause-screen-progress-meta .progress-ends-at {
    display: none !important;
}

#pause-screen-overlay #pause-screen-progress-meta .progress-percentage {
    color: gold !important;
    font-weight: bold !important;
}

#pause-screen-plot {
    height: 30vh !important;
    overflow-y: auto !important;
}

#pause-screen-disc {
    animation: none !important;
}

#pause-screen-backdrop {
    opacity: 0.15 !important;
}

The progress fill is not a seek control. Press Space or Enter to resume. Clicking or touching an empty overlay/content surface schedules resume after 500 ms.

Note

Hide individual regions rather than the dialog itself. While active, JE adds .pause-screen-active to the HTML root and suppresses parts of the player's controls. Hiding the whole dialog with CSS leaves that state active.

Keep the close button and the focus helpers (#pause-screen-focus-start, #pause-screen-focus-end) usable, or turn off Custom Pause Screen to remove the feature.

docs.title: CSS variables
docs.text:
These are CSS custom properties, separate from plugin settings. Assign them to #pause-screen-overlay so its children inherit your values instead of the responsive root defaults.

Custom property Base default What it changes --pause-screen-overlay-bg rgba(0,0,0,.78) Overlay background. --pause-screen-blur 50px Content backdrop blur. --pause-screen-logo-max-w 45vw Logo maximum width. --pause-screen-logo-max-h 20vh Logo maximum height. --pause-screen-logo-top 20vh Logo top position. --pause-screen-logo-left 8vw Logo left position. --pause-screen-details-top 45vh Details top position. --pause-screen-details-left 8vw Details and progress wrapper left position. --pause-screen-details-gap 2rem Space between detail items. --pause-screen-text-size 1.2rem Details font size. --pause-screen-plot-top 55vh Plot top position. --pause-screen-plot-left 8vw Plot left position. --pause-screen-plot-max-w 50vw Plot maximum width. --pause-screen-plot-font 1.25rem Plot font size. --pause-screen-progress-top 85vh Progress wrapper top position. --pause-screen-progress-width 48vw Progress wrapper width. --pause-screen-progress-height 6px Progress track height. --pause-screen-progress-radius 999px Progress track corner radius. --pause-screen-disc-w 26vw Disc width; also determines its vertical centering. --pause-screen-disc-right 5vw Disc distance from the right edge. --pause-screen-disc-rot-sec 60s Duration of one disc rotation. 
#pause-screen-overlay {
    --pause-screen-blur: 20px;
    --pause-screen-logo-max-w: 35vw;
    --pause-screen-plot-max-w: 60vw;
    --pause-screen-progress-height: 10px;
}
Responsive layouts and disc animation

Built-in layouts adjust root defaults at widths of 1400px and 768px, and in landscape at heights of 500px or less.

Some phone positions, font sizes, and plot dimensions are set directly on elements, so variables do not control every dimension. Narrow layouts hide the disc; the later landscape rule can show it again. Reduced-motion preferences stop its rotation.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Poster tags use separate containers for quality, genre, language, rating, and age-rating badges. People tags decorate cast portraits on detail pages. Enable the relevant personal setting in UI Settings before trying a recipe.

docs.title: Prerequisites and placement
docs.text:
The administrator's Display → Media Tags settings provide defaults. All six tag features start off at factory defaults.

Setting Default What it does Enable Quality Tags (admin) / Show Quality Tags (viewer) Off QualityTagsEnabled: resolution, source, format, and sound badges. Enable Genre Tags (admin) / Show Genre Tags (viewer) Off GenreTagsEnabled: genre icons and hover labels. Enable Language Tags (admin) / Show Language Tags (viewer) Off LanguageTagsEnabled: audio-language flags. Enable Rating Tags (admin) / Show Rating Tags (viewer) Off RatingTagsEnabled: community and critic scores. Enable Age Rating Tags (admin) / Show Age Rating Tags (viewer) Off AgeRatingTagsEnabled: official age/content certification. Enable People Tags (admin) / Show People Tags (viewer) Off PeopleTagsEnabled: cast ages, birthplace, and deceased status. Hide Tags on Hover (admin and viewer) Off TagsHideOnHover: adds body.je-tags-hide-on-hover; an important hover rule hides the poster tag host.

New user settings for the six tag features are seeded from the plugin configuration. Existing non-null user values take precedence over admin defaults. Changing a default does not replace a saved personal choice. See Settings Overview for default management.

Server and saved user properties use PascalCase. Resolved client settings use camelCase, such as qualityTagsEnabled.

Users can change Hide Tags on Hover later in their personal UI Settings.

If tag data is stale or missing, also check the server's cache configuration under Display → Media Tags:

Setting (admin) Default What it does Exclude libraries from the tag cache Off TagCacheExcludeLibraries: enables library exclusions. Libraries to exclude Empty TagCacheExcludedLibraryIds: selected libraries to skip; an empty selection excludes nothing.

Exclusion changes affect the next cache rebuild. Click Save Settings, then open Admin → Tag Cache and click Rebuild Server Tag Cache. Confirm the full rebuild. See Tags & Badges for cache operation; CSS only styles the resulting elements.

Use the position grids in UI Settings to move tag containers between corners.

The normal poster structure places .je-tag-host inside .cardScalable, before .cardOverlayContainer. Fallback targets are used when that structure is unavailable.

Tag container Position property Factory corner .quality-overlay-container QualityTagsPosition top-left .genre-overlay-container GenreTagsPosition top-right .language-overlay-container LanguageTagsPosition bottom-left .rating-overlay-container RatingTagsPosition bottom-right .age-rating-overlay-container AgeRatingTagsPosition bottom-right

Containers carry data-je-corner with one of those four corner values. JE stacks containers sharing a corner with inline transforms and a 4px gap, and offsets top-right tags around card indicators. Custom transforms can disrupt that stacking.

Poster tags generally ignore pointer input. Container-query sizing adapts badges to card width, with separate mobile rules. Fixed sizes can crowd small posters.

Processing markers such as data-je-quality-tagged, data-je-genre-tagged, data-je-language-tagged, data-je-rating-tagged, and data-je-age-rating-tagged record processing. They do not guarantee a visible badge.

docs.title: Tag Styles and native posters
docs.text:
Use the built-in Tag Styles editor for supported colors; that guide covers presets, tabs, scope, opacity, and bulk controls. See Native Poster Tags for native-client setup and refresh requirements. CSS remains useful for web shape, sizing, visibility, and other surfaces.

Web overrides use important selectors. Their specificity is (0,4,0) for quality, (0,3,0) for age and rating chips, and (0,2,0) for genre. These beat simple color recipes; more specific important Custom CSS can override them.

Critic styles also match user-review chips because those share .rating-tag-critic.

Checking Tag Styles through the API

For troubleshooting, authenticated GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-styles returns effective web overrides only when enabled and targeting web or both. Otherwise it returns empty styles. Unavailable configuration returns HTTP 503.

GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-styles/catalog additionally requires an administrator. See the API reference.

CSS selectors cannot individually restyle pixels drawn into a poster image. Use Tag Styles targeting poster images for supported color changes; native output requires Native Poster Tags.

docs.title: Quality Tags
docs.text:
Quality badges use .quality-overlay-label and a normalized data-quality value. Inspect the attribute rather than matching the displayed text: a badge reading ATMOS 7.1 has data-quality="ATMOS".

Category Recognized data-quality values Additional class Resolution 8K, 4K, 1440p, 1080p, 720p, 576p, 480p, LOW-RES, SD .resolution Source BluRay, HD DVD, DVD, VHS, HDTV, Physical .other-quality Dynamic range Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HDR .video-codec Special format IMAX, 3D .video-codec Video codec AV1, HEVC, H265, VP9, H264, VP8, XVID, DIVX, WMV, MPEG2, MPEG4, MJPEG, THEORA .video-format Sound ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS, Dolby Digital+, 7.1, 5.1 .audio-codec

The codec class names are historical: .video-format means video codec, while .video-codec means HDR or special format. Unknown labels use .other-quality.

Which quality values can appear
  • SD is recognized for sorting/styling, but the current resolution detector emits the other eight resolution values. Unknown or stale cached values can also pass through.
  • Only the best resolution is retained.
  • Source detection requires a .disc media stub and selects one source badge.
  • Standalone channel fallback produces 7.1 or 5.1. 2.0 can be appended to a codec label but is not a standalone fallback.

Use the Quality Tags category controls before CSS hiding; that guide covers administrator defaults, personal overrides, and category order.

Resize all quality badges:

.quality-overlay-label {
    font-size: 0.8rem !important;
    padding: 3px 10px !important;
}

Change a color while allowing admin Tag Styles to take precedence:

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="4K"] {
    background: purple !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

This selector beats the built-in (0,3,0) color rule, but loses to the editor's (0,4,0) override. To deliberately override the editor too, use:

.quality-overlay-container.quality-overlay-container
.quality-overlay-label.quality-overlay-label[data-quality="4K"] {
    background: purple !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

Hide unwanted values:

.quality-overlay-label[data-quality="H264"],
.quality-overlay-label[data-quality="Physical"] {
    display: none !important;
}

Customize media-stub source colors:

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="BluRay"] {
    background: rgba(0, 150, 255, 0.95) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="HD DVD"] {
    background: rgba(200, 0, 50, 0.95) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="DVD"] {
    background: rgba(200, 100, 0, 0.95) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="VHS"] {
    background: rgba(160, 82, 45, 0.95) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

div.quality-overlay-container .quality-overlay-label[data-quality="HDTV"] {
    background: rgba(100, 100, 100, 0.95) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

docs.title: Sound-tag language selection
docs.text:
Audio preferences can change which sound badge appears for the same item across viewers.

Setting Default What it does Preferred Audio Language for Sound Tags (admin) No preference (best track overall) ("") QualityTagsPreferredAudioLanguage: server language preference. Use Each User's Jellyfin Audio Language (admin) Off QualityTagsAudioLanguageFromUser: uses each viewer's Jellyfin audio preference as server policy. Preferred audio language for the sound tag (viewer) Server default ("") Overrides server policy with My Jellyfin audio language (auto), No preference (best track overall) (none), or a language code.

Matching tries regional language matches, then base-language matches, then all tracks. Inspect the resolved badge before targeting an audio data-quality value.

docs.title: Genre Tags CSS
docs.text:
Use these hooks to style genre icons and their hover labels. Up to three genres appear.

  • Icons use .genre-tag > .je-msym-outlined.
  • Text uses .genre-text inside .genre-overlay-container.
  • Target a particular genre through its original title, such as .genre-tag[title="Drama"]. JE does not emit data-genre.

By default, text appears on hover and floats inward from the selected corner. To keep labels visible inside wider chips:

  1. Turn off Hide Tags on Hover.
  2. Reload so existing chips include text spans.
  3. Apply the following CSS:
.genre-tag {
    width: auto !important;
    border-radius: 14px !important;
    gap: 4px;
    padding: 0 6px;
}

.genre-tag .genre-text {
    position: static !important;
    transform: none !important;
    opacity: 1 !important;
}

Changing display alone does not reveal text hidden by opacity. CSS cannot restore a span omitted when hover hiding was enabled. Long labels can cover more of the poster.

docs.title: Language Tags CSS
docs.text:
Use .language-overlay-container and .language-flag to style language flags.

  • data-lang is a lowercase flag-country code: jp targets the Japanese flag, while Japanese's language code is ja.
  • data-lang-name contains represented language names.
  • Partial flags also have .language-flag-partial and data-partial="true".
Setting (admin) Default What it does Priority Languages Empty LanguageTagsPriority: prioritizes language flags. Only Show Priority Languages Off LanguageTagsPriorityStrict: restricts output to the priority list. Merge Regional Variants Off LanguageTagsMergeRegions: regional and script variants share the base language's flag.

Flags are deduplicated by country and limited to three. Full flags normally precede partial flags, but priority ordering takes precedence.

When different languages share a flag, it is partial only if all represented languages are partial. Hiding a flag with CSS does not cause a fourth flag to render.

Resize flags or hide a specific flag:

.language-flag {
    width: 30px !important;
    height: auto !important;
}

.language-flag[data-lang="jp"] {
    display: none !important;
}

Restyle flags for audio that does not cover every episode of a series/season:

.language-flag-partial {
    opacity: 1 !important;
    filter: none !important;
    outline: 2px solid gold !important;
    /* To hide partial flags instead: display: none !important; */
}

Partial flags normally use opacity 0.55, saturation 0.5, a dashed outline, and a dark shadow ring.

This recipe keeps the existing ring and outline offset. Add box-shadow: none !important or outline-offset: 0 !important if desired.

docs.title: Rating Tags CSS
docs.text:
Use .rating-overlay-container, .rating-tag, and .rating-text to style poster scores. Community and critic chips have separate hooks:

  • .rating-tag-tmdb displays Jellyfin's CommunityRating; the class name does not guarantee TMDB supplied the metadata. Its star is .rating-star-icon.
  • Critic chips use .rating-tag-critic and .rating-tomato-icon.fresh or .rating-tomato-icon.rotten. Scores below 60 are rotten, and scores of 60 or more are fresh.

Use the Rating Tags scope controls to choose item types and home rows; that guide covers administrator defaults and personal overrides.

Change the community-score background:

.rating-tag-tmdb {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) !important;
}

This beats ordinary defaults; enabled admin community Tag Styles take precedence.

Hide critic chips while keeping user-review chips:

.rating-tag-critic:not(.je-userreview-tag) {
    display: none !important;
}

Using .rating-tag-critic without the exclusion also hides user-review chips.

docs.title: User-review poster chips
docs.text:
These chips show the aggregate 1–5 review average converted to a /10 score.

They require a resolvable TMDB item key, personal Show Rating Tags, and the following admin settings under Elsewhere & Reviews → User Reviews:

Setting Default What it does Enable User Written Reviews Off ShowUserReviews: enables user reviews. Show average user rating on poster cards Off ShowUserRatingOnPosters: adds the review-average chip. Show "—" on posters for unrated items On ShowUserRatingDash: a null average shows a dash; off removes the chip when no average is available.

The chip has .rating-tag.rating-tag-critic.je-userreview-tag, with .je-userreview-icon and .rating-text children. The associated container carries data-je-review-key for updates.

Built-in chip and icon text colors are important pink declarations. Override both when recoloring:

.rating-overlay-container .rating-tag.rating-tag-critic.je-userreview-tag,
.rating-overlay-container .je-userreview-tag .je-userreview-icon {
    color: gold !important;
}

See User Reviews for writing and managing reviews.

docs.title: Age Rating Tags CSS
docs.text:
Use .age-rating-overlay-container and .age-rating-tag[rating="…"] to style poster certifications.

The attribute holds a normalized rating, not necessarily the raw metadata spelling. For example, DE-12 and FSK 12 become FSK-12, and supported unrated names become NR. Inspect it before writing a selector.

Resize and recolor the poster badge:

.age-rating-tag {
    border-radius: 999px !important;
    font-size: 12px !important;
}

.age-rating-tag[rating="TV-MA"] {
    background-color: #000 !important;
}

Poster badges independently reuse rating-specific colors from the Colored Ratings stylesheet, stripping its important flags. The TV-MA rule beats those shipped colors but loses to a more specific important admin age Tag Style. The fallback is blue-grey.

Detail/player certifications use .mediaInfoOfficialRating, a separate surface. The administrator controls their colors under Extras → UI Tweaks.

Setting Default What it does Colored Ratings Backgrounds Off ColoredRatingsEnabled: loads the full stylesheet for official age/content certifications, including supported international boards, US TV descriptors, and ESRB labels.

To override a shipped detail/player color:

.mediaInfoOfficialRating.mediaInfoOfficialRating[rating="TV-MA"] {
    background-color: #000 !important;
}

docs.title: People Tags CSS
docs.text:
People tags appear on cast and guest-cast portraits on item detail pages. Use the hooks below to style age chips and birthplace banners.

Birth/death and item-release metadata determine current age, age at death, and age at release. Birthplace text needs birthplace metadata; flags also need a recognized country.

Hook What it styles .je-people-age-container Age-chip stack. .je-people-age-chip Shared chip shape. .je-people-age-current Current age; green by default. .je-people-age-deceased Age at death; red by default. .je-people-age-release Age at item release; blue by default. .je-people-age-icon, .je-people-age-text Chip icon and <number>y text. .je-people-place-banner Birthplace banner. .je-people-flag, .je-people-place-icon, .je-people-place-text Flag, location icon, and birthplace text. .je-people-round Portrait wrapper when JE detects a circular theme layout. .je-deceased-poster Portrait wrapper with deceased styling.

Chip/banner styles are normally inline. Circular portraits receive additional important rules, so use the detail-page ID to override both layouts:

#itemDetailPage .je-people-age-chip {
    padding: 6px 12px !important;
    font-size: 13px !important;
}

#itemDetailPage .je-people-place-banner {
    display: none !important;
}

Larger chips can overlap portraits.

The emitted birthplace class is .je-people-place-banner. .je-people-tag-banner appears in internal CSS but is not the rendered banner hook.

Deceased image treatment and the cross can be styled separately:

#itemDetailPage .je-deceased-poster .cardImageContainer {
    filter: grayscale(50%) opacity(0.9) !important;
}

#itemDetailPage .je-deceased-poster .cardScalable::after {
    color: gold !important;
}

docs.title: *arr Tag Links
docs.text:
Enable Show synced tags as links under the admin *arr → Tags Sync section. Matching tags already present on an item become links in .itemExternalLinks on its detail page. Importing tags is a separate operation; see *arr Features.

Setting (admin) Default What it does Show synced tags as links On ArrTagsShowAsLinks: creates links for matching item tags. Tag Prefix JE Arr Tag: ArrTagsPrefix: case-sensitive prefix used to identify tags. Show as Links Filter Empty ArrTagsLinksFilter: optional allow list of unprefixed names, one per line. Hide Specific Links Filter Empty ArrTagsLinksHideFilter: hides matching names, one per line; takes precedence over the allow list.

Filter comparisons ignore case after reconstructing each full prefixed name. Initial prefix matching is case-sensitive.

The factory prefix includes a trailing space. If the admin prefix field is empty on load or save, the admin UI substitutes Requested by:. Inspect the actual configured prefix.

The following admin settings under Tags Sync control tag imports:

Setting Default What it does Enable Tags Sync Off ArrTagsSyncEnabled: allows the sync task to import tags from configured Radarr and Sonarr instances. Clear old tags before sync On ArrTagsClearOldTags: removes existing tags with the configured prefix before adding the imported tags. Sync to Jellyfin Filter Empty ArrTagsSyncFilter: restricts which tags are imported; empty syncs all tags.

The *Sync Tags from arr to Jellyfin task has no default triggers; run it manually or configure a schedule.

docs.title: Link structure and attributes
docs.text:
This illustrative link uses the factory prefix. Replace the item/server placeholders with actual values when inspecting your page:

<a is="emby-linkbutton"
   class="button-link emby-button arr-tag-link"
   href="#!/list.html?type=tag&tag=JE%20Arr%20Tag%3A%20in-netflix&serverId=SERVER_ID"
   title="View all items with tag: JE Arr Tag: in-netflix"
   data-item-id="ITEM_ID"
   data-id="in-netflix"
   data-tag="JE Arr Tag: in-netflix"
   data-tag-name="in-netflix"
   data-tag-prefix="JE Arr Tag: ">
  <span class="arr-tag-link-icon" aria-hidden="true" style="margin-right: 5px;">
    <!-- JE icon markup; depends on Use Icons in UI and Icon Style -->
  </span>
  <span class="arr-tag-link-text"
        data-id="in-netflix"
        data-tag="JE Arr Tag: in-netflix"
        data-tag-name="in-netflix"
        data-tag-prefix="JE Arr Tag: ">JE Arr Tag: in-netflix</span>
</a>
Hook Meaning .arr-tag-link Link anchor. .arr-tag-link-icon Icon wrapper. .arr-tag-link-text Visible label wrapper. data-id Normalized slug of the trimmed name after removing the prefix; on anchor and label. data-tag Full original tag, including prefix; on anchor and label. data-tag-name Trimmed name without prefix; on anchor and label. data-tag-prefix Configured prefix; on anchor and label. data-item-id Current item ID; anchor only.

Different names can share a slug. Use exact data-tag-name or data-tag when needed.

How tag slugs are generated

Slug generation follows these steps:

  1. Decompose Unicode and remove combining accents.
  2. Lowercase and trim.
  3. Replace whitespace and unsupported characters with hyphens.
  4. Collapse repeated hyphens and remove edge hyphens.

ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores survive. For example, 1 - n00bcodr becomes 1-n00bcodr.

Links navigate to #!/list.html?type=tag&tag=<encoded full tag>&serverId=<server>. JE uses Dashboard.navigate when available and the equivalent hash otherwise.

docs.title: Common recipes
docs.text:
Use these recipes to change link labels, visibility, icons, or colors.

Rename a visible label:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-tag-name="1 - n00bcodr"] .arr-tag-link-text {
    display: none !important;
}

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-tag-name="1 - n00bcodr"]::after {
    content: " N00bCodr";
}

This changes visible text only. The tooltip, stored tag, and navigation still use the original full tag.

Hide a link:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="in-netflix"] {
    display: none !important;
}

You can alternatively match [data-tag-name="in-netflix"].

To hide it globally through settings, use Tags Sync → Tag Filters → Hide Specific Links Filter. Enter the name without its prefix, one per line.

Replace the icon, or remove it by using only the first rule:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link .arr-tag-link-icon {
    display: none !important;
}

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link::before {
    content: "🔖";
    margin-right: 0.25rem;
}

Make links into pills:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link {
    padding: 8px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5);
    border: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8);
}

Give specific names different colors using their normalized slugs:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="1-n00bcodr"] {
    background: #d81f26;
    color: #fff;
}

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="2-jellyfish"] {
    background: #00a8e1;
    color: #fff;
}

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="3-admin"] {
    background: #0c1a38;
    color: #8dd0ff;
}

docs.title: Configurable icons
docs.text:
These admin settings control configurable JE icons:

Setting Default What it does Use Icons in UI On UseIcons: shows configurable JE icons; turning it off leaves the *arr icon wrapper empty. Icon Style Emoji (emoji) IconStyle: selects Emoji, Lucide Icons (lucide), or Material UI Icons (mui).

The markup depends on the icon style:

  • Emoji markup uses .je-emoji.
  • Lucide icons can use a wrapper containing an SVG.
  • Material UI icons use Material icon spans.

Renderers can fall back to wrapped emoji.

Examples of the contents inside .arr-tag-link-icon (Lucide geometry is abbreviated):

<!-- Emoji -->
<span class="je-emoji">🏷️</span>
<!-- Lucide -->
<span style="display:inline-flex;vertical-align:middle;">
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1em" height="1em"
       viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><!-- paths --></svg>
</span>
<!-- Material UI -->
<span class="material-icons" style="font-size:1em;vertical-align:middle;">label</span>

Target the outer .arr-tag-link-icon to handle all renderers. A CSS ::before replacement stays visible even with configurable icons off.

Genre and people tags emit their own Material Symbols hooks and are not governed by this configurable icon switch.

docs.title: Enhanced Panel
docs.text:
Open Enhanced Panel from the sidebar to preview panel styling.

Other entry points use Jellyfin Enhanced or Jellyfin Enhanced - User Settings, depending on the surface. See Settings Overview for access and personal settings.

docs.title: Automatic theme detection
docs.text:
Check these variables when customizing how the panel uses your theme's colors and effects.

JE checks identifying root CSS variables for Jellyfish, ElegantFin, and Zesty, in that order. The first nonempty identifier other than none wins. Other themes receive Default styling. These variables are supplied by themes, not defined by JE.

Theme Detection variable Variables consumed by JE Jellyfish --theme-updated-on --primary-background-transparent, --secondary-background-transparent, --primary-accent-color, --text-color, --alt-accent-color, --blur, --logo ElegantFin --elegantFinFooterText --headerColor, --drawerColor, --activeColor, --textColor, --selectorBackgroundColor, --blurDefault Zesty --honey-yellow --darkest, --dark, --accent, --white, --dark-highlight, --rounding

Reopen the panel after changing theme values. Reload to redetect a different theme.

Theme fallbacks and cached detection

Missing values have fallbacks. Detection is cached, but JE reads the selected theme's values again when constructing a panel and inserts them as literal styles.

Zesty's --rounding feeds JE's blur input. Some surfaces, including the panel root and phone content background, also have fixed defaults.

docs.title: Shell and navigation hooks
docs.text:
Use these hooks to style the panel's layout and section navigation. Scope these classes to #jellyfin-enhanced-panel.

Hook What it styles #jellyfin-enhanced-panel Panel root. .panel-header, #closeSettingsPanel Header and close button. .je-panel-body Navigation/content wrapper; gains .je-pane-open when a section is open. .je-panel-nav, .je-panel-nav-items Navigation column and its button list. .je-panel-search, #jePanelSearch Section search field. .tab-button[data-tab="…"], .tab-button.active Navigation entry and selected entry. .je-panel-main Content area. .je-pane[data-pane="…"], .je-pane.active Section pane and selected pane. .je-pane-title Section heading. .je-pane-back, #jePanelBack Phone back button. .panel-footer, .close-helptext Closing-help bar. #releaseNotesBtn, [data-pane="about"] a, .footer-logo Release Notes, Contribute, and optional theme logo in About.

Pane values always include playback, auto-skip, subtitles, random-button, ui, language, and about. Other panes depend on their features:

  • shortcuts appears when shortcuts are enabled.
  • hidden-content requires its module.
  • spoiler-guard requires admin enablement and its pane builder.

The layout changes with screen size:

  • Desktop uses a 230px navigation column and restores LastOpenedTab.
  • At widths of 760px or less, the panel fills the screen and starts with the section list.

Search matches pane text and filters navigation entries; Back returns to the list. Preserve .active, inactive-pane visibility, .je-pane-open, and the phone layers' inert focus restrictions.

Entry-point hooks outside the panel are .jellyfinEnhancedSection, #jellyfinEnhancedSettingsLink, #jellyfinEnhancedUserMenuLink, #jellyfinEnhancedUserPrefsLink, and #enhancedSettingsBtn. The player entry is hidden under .layout-desktop.

docs.title: Panel surfaces and header
docs.text:
Changing the root background alone leaves backgrounds on the body, navigation, and phone content area intact. This recipe changes those surfaces together:

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel {
    background: rgba(25, 35, 45, 0.85) !important;
    border: 1px solid rgba(125, 150, 175, 0.3) !important;
    backdrop-filter: blur(20px) !important;
    color: #e6e6e6 !important;
    box-shadow: 0 10px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .je-panel-body {
    background: rgba(25, 35, 45, 0.85) !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .je-panel-nav {
    background: rgba(10, 20, 30, 0.6) !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .je-panel-main {
    background: transparent !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel > .panel-header {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25) !important;
    border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(125, 150, 175, 0.3) !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel > .panel-header > div:first-child {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #00a4dc, #aa5cc3) !important;
    -webkit-background-clip: text !important;
    -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .panel-footer {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25) !important;
    border-top: 1px solid rgba(125, 150, 175, 0.3) !important;
}

The panel's first element is an embedded style element, so select .panel-header directly. The title is the header's first child.

On phones, transparent content can reveal the navigation layer beneath. Use an opaque .je-panel-main background if that is distracting.

docs.title: Navigation and headings
docs.text:
This recipe changes navigation-button colors, the selected-entry marker, and section headings.

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .tab-button {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) !important;
    color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7) !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .tab-button:hover {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .tab-button.active {
    background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) !important;
    color: #fff !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .tab-button.active::before {
    background: #00a4dc !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .je-pane-title {
    color: #00a4dc !important;
}

Current sections use panes and navigation buttons. Settings-section details/summary recipes from older panel versions do not match this structure.

docs.title: Controls and previews
docs.text:

Conditional controls appear only when their feature is available.
