child div[data-pos="top-left"] (also the other three corners) Language and About #displayLanguageSelect, #clearTranslationCacheButton, #releaseNotesBtn, conditional .footer-logo

Category rows use data-cat-key, and quality rows also have data-order-key and data-default-order.

Expanders use aria-expanded; arrow buttons have disabled states. Preserve those states when styling.

The conditional Hidden Content pane exposes:

Group Hooks Main controls #hiddenContentEnabledToggle, #hiddenShowHideButtons, #hiddenShowConfirmation, #manageHiddenContentBtn Hide-button placement #hiddenShowButtonJellyseerr, #hiddenShowButtonLibrary, #hiddenShowButtonDetails, #hiddenShowButtonCast Filtering surfaces #hiddenContentSurfaceToggles, #hiddenFilterLibrary, #hiddenFilterDiscovery, #hiddenFilterSearch, #hiddenFilterCalendar, #hiddenFilterUpcoming, #hiddenFilterRecommendations, #hiddenFilterRequests, #hiddenFilterNextUp, #hiddenFilterContinueWatching, #hiddenExperimentalCollections

Many selection and hover colors are written inline. Preserve selected, disabled, hidden, warning, and focus states; avoid forcing every preview or control visible.

For a simple checkbox accent change:

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel input[type="checkbox"] {
    accent-color: #aa5cc3 !important;
}

docs.title: Shortcut keys and About actions
docs.text:
Use the following recipe to style shortcut keys while keeping editing feedback visible.

Shortcut hooks include .shortcuts-container, #shortcuts-content, .shortcut-key[data-action="…"], .shortcut-toggle, .modified-indicator, and .shake-error.

Readonly chips have data-readonly="1" and are excluded from editing. Editable chips listen while focused; keep their focus, listening, and error feedback visible.

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel kbd:not(.shake-error):not(:focus),
#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .shortcut-key:not(.shake-error):not(:focus) {
    background: #34495e !important;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel kbd,
#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .shortcut-key {
    color: #ecf0f1 !important;
    box-shadow: 0 2px 0 #2c3e50;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel .shortcut-key:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid gold;
    outline-offset: 2px;
}

The background rule excludes focused keys and .shake-error so the editor's inline feedback remains visible.

While listening, the editor changes the key's text, border color, and width. Conflicting or reserved bindings set a red background and trigger the shake animation.

Release Notes and Contribute are in About. The footer contains closing instructions, not an action-button wrapper.

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel #releaseNotesBtn,
#jellyfin-enhanced-panel [data-pane="about"] a {
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08) !important;
    transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
}

#jellyfin-enhanced-panel #releaseNotesBtn:hover,
#jellyfin-enhanced-panel [data-pane="about"] a:hover {
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15) !important;
}

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Use these recipes to change toast and release-note styling. Both are separate body-level elements, so panel-scoped rules do not reach them.

  • Toasts use .jellyfin-enhanced-toast with ordinary inline styles and transform animation.
  • Release Notes fetches the latest GitHub release and opens #jellyfin-release-notes-notification.
.jellyfin-enhanced-toast {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #00a4dc, #aa5cc3) !important;
    color: white !important;
    border: none !important;
    backdrop-filter: blur(10px) !important;
}

#jellyfin-release-notes-notification {
    background: rgba(25, 35, 45, 0.95) !important;
}
Setting (admin, Playback) Default What it does Toast Notification Duration (ms) 1500 ToastDuration: configured toast lifetime; individual calls can specify another duration. Shortcuts Panel Autoclose Delay (ms) 15000 HelpPanelAutocloseDelay: Enhanced panel idle-close delay.

Release notes uses a separate 20-second idle-close timer. CSS transitions do not change JavaScript removal timers.

Keep transform animation intact when changing notification styling.

docs.title: Player rating surfaces
docs.text:
Player ratings have different hooks from poster badges. Enable the relevant admin setting, start playback, and inspect the player controls or startup card.

Setting (admin) Default What it does Show Rating in Video Player On ShowRatingInPlayer: community/critic chips in the player's on-screen controls. Show Age Rating When Playback Starts Off ShowPlaybackRatingBadge: startup certification card.

The control chips are inside #je-osd-rating-container[data-item-id]. Scope .je-chip.tmdb, .je-chip.critic, .je-star, .je-text, .je-tomato.fresh, and .je-tomato.rotten to that container.

The startup card uses #je-playback-rating-badge, the visibility class .je-visible, and children .je-age-rating, .je-age-why, and .je-age-genres.

  • It displays for five seconds with a 400ms fade.
  • Advisory and genre lines are limited to three entries each.
  • Its accent reads --theme-primary-color, then --primary-accent-color, then falls back to #00a4dc.
  • The age element also has .mediaInfoOfficialRating, so Colored Ratings can affect it.
#je-osd-rating-container .je-chip {
    border-radius: 999px !important;
}

#je-playback-rating-badge {
    border-left-color: gold !important;
}

Keep .je-visible and the timed visibility behavior intact. See Enhanced Features for playback features.

#randomItemButton .je-dice-spin {

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Use this map to find the files responsible for a feature before changing it. Jellyfin Enhanced has two parts: a C# server plugin and an injected JavaScript client.

The server owns configuration, persistence, integration proxies and response filters. The client adds controls and pages to Jellyfin Web.

Unless a repository-root path is stated, source paths below are relative to Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/. Leading slashes denote HTTP routes.

For endpoint details, see the API reference. For setup and placement, see Settings Overview and JE Pages & Tabs.

docs.title: Client delivery and initialization
docs.text:
This section follows the client from loader injection through initialization and user switches.

Services/ScriptInjectionStartupFilter.cs injects the loader into web responses. GET /JellyfinEnhanced/script serves js/plugin.js; it is separate from the component bundle. JellyfinEnhanced.csproj embeds js/**, and GetScript in Controllers/JellyfinEnhancedController.cs serves individual resources at /JellyfinEnhanced/js/{path}.

The ordered module list lives in js/component-scripts.json: 161 component modules, with paths relative to js/. Entries starting with // are ordering notes.

Modules execute in manifest order. Place a module after every producer whose exports it reads at load time. A consumer loaded too early can capture undefined.

The initialization stages and user-switch behavior are:

Stage Owner and behavior Early UI Dedicated loaders inject js/others/splashscreen.js and, when enabled, js/extras/login-image.js before the component stage so they can affect the login screen. Translations js/enhanced/translations.js starts loading at the beginning of initialize(), in parallel with bootstrap. It loads/caches locale JSON and resolves JE.t before components run. Bootstrap Authenticated GET /JellyfinEnhanced/bootstrap returns version, token user ID, public configuration, administrator-only private configuration, Custom Tabs / Plugin Pages presence flags, five user documents and the component list. Non-admin PrivateConfig is null. The loader falls back to individual endpoints if bootstrap fails. Components After configuration is applied, production loads GET /JellyfinEnhanced/bundle.js; development mode and bundle failure use individual scripts. User switches js/core/session.js detects identity changes and resets registered feature state. The loader reloads the incoming user's documents and emits je:user-data-loaded. Async work uses identity epochs to discard stale results.

The bootstrap's UserSettings members are Settings, Shortcuts, Bookmark, Elsewhere and HiddenContent. A document-loading failure yields null for that document. Bootstrap always loads the token user's data, with no target-user parameter, and is served with no-store.

Bootstrap's Prefetched block can carry SpoilerBlurSeries, SeerrUserStatus, SeerrStatus and ActiveStreamSessions. These reuse standalone response bodies under the same feature, access and cache gates. Seerr answers are included only when no upstream lookup is needed; sessions follow the active-streams access gate.

Components consume a value once, shortly after bootstrap, through JE.takePrefetched(name). Otherwise, they call their endpoint normally. Bootstrap does not fetch every feature's data.

docs.title: Bundle and development mode
docs.text:
Services/ClientScriptBundle.cs builds the bundle on first use and caches it by the plugin's script cache key (version plus DLL timestamp). It wraps each manifest file in a function and publishes window.__JE_BUNDLE_MODULES.

The index source map at /JellyfinEnhanced/bundle.js.map uses sections to preserve original filenames and line numbers in DevTools and stack traces. Bundle and map routes are anonymous; production responses use public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

The loader waits for browser idle time, with a 100 ms timeout. It then executes functions in order, yielding between modules at an approximately 10 ms budget. This reduces interference with initial rendering; a synchronous module can still exceed the budget and occupy the main thread. A top-level exception is reported and skipped without re-running that module.

If the bundle request fails or the bundle does not define a valid module array, the loader injects individual files with script.async = false. Downloads can overlap; execution follows manifest order.

Administrator setting, under Admin → Developer Settings:

Setting Default What it does Dev Mode Off (DevMode=false) Loads individual component scripts and serves script responses with no-store. Direct bundle requests also rebuild rather than using the process cache.

Note

Development mode still serves embedded resources. Rebuild the plugin and load the new assembly after editing JavaScript; it does not read loose source files from your checkout.

DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware=false is a server configuration property without an admin-page control. It gates the request-time injection middleware. BrandingAssetStartupFilter.cs handles custom image assets separately from script injection.

docs.title: Build targets and logging
docs.text:
JellyfinEnhanced.csproj uses the root namespace and assembly name Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced. Directory organization does not always match C# namespaces: for example, services in Services/SpoilerGuard/ and Services/Identity/ use Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced.Services. Check declarations rather than deriving namespaces from folders.

JellyfinTarget Jellyfin references Framework Compilation symbol jf12 (default) 12.0.0 net10.0 JF12 jf10 10.11.0 net9.0 JF10

Build separate artifacts for the two targets. Package-reference changes require refreshing both plugin lock files and both locks beside tests/backend/JE.Tests.csproj. See CONTRIBUTING.md for build and locked-restore instructions.

Logger.cs forwards messages to Jellyfin's main log and writes JellyfinEnhanced_YYYY-MM-DD.log under Jellyfin's log directory. Services/HostCompatibilityService.cs compares the assembly's build target with the running host and exposes mismatch diagnostics.

docs.title: Configuration and persistence
docs.text:
This table maps server settings, per-user documents and the configuration UI to their source files. Storage locations follow it.

Source Responsibility Configuration/PluginConfiguration.cs Server settings and administrator defaults. Configuration/configPage.html, configPage.css Admin UI, control labels, save wiring and styling. Tabs: Overview, Display, Playback, Pages, Seerr, *arr, Elsewhere & Reviews, Extras, Keyboard, Admin, Docs. Configuration/UserConfiguration.cs Per-user document models, including settings, shortcuts, bookmarks, Elsewhere, Hidden Content and Spoiler Guard. Configuration/UserConfigurationManager.cs Server file storage, locking, writes, shared stores and migration of historical user-ID directory variants. Configuration/whats-new-seed.json Fallback baseline for detecting new admin controls; this is a historical baseline, not current defaults or a feature count. js/enhanced/config.js Resolves effective values from server-stored user settings, admin defaults and client fallbacks; serializes per-user saves to the server in order. It does not store user settings in localStorage.

Per-user files live under <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/<normalized-user-id>/. IDs are lowercase with hyphens removed. Bootstrap loads settings.json, shortcuts.json, bookmark.json, elsewhere.json and hidden-content.json; Spoiler Guard additionally uses spoilerblur.json, and Content Warnings stores its trigger picks in ddd-triggers.json, loaded on demand rather than at bootstrap.

Shared reviews.json and activity.json live in the parent plugin configuration directory, as do catchup-log.jsonl and its rotated catchup-log.1.jsonl. UserConfigurationManager owns the shared review/activity stores; CatchUpLogService owns the Catch Up log.

Browser storage serves other purposes: translation caching, IndexedDB tag snapshots and per-user Catch Up dismissals. Those are separate from the server-stored personal settings.

Admin changes may affect the server immediately, while web clients retain loaded configuration until refreshed. See Settings Overview for defaults, reset and backup procedures.

docs.title: Page wrappers and placement
docs.text:
GetPages() registers the administrator configuration page. GetViews() exposes all seven embedded feature wrappers:

File under PluginPages/ View name Client owner CalendarPage.html calendarPage js/arr/calendar/ DownloadsPage.html downloadsPage js/arr/requests/ (combined requests/downloads page) BookmarksPage.html bookmarksPage js/enhanced/bookmarks/ HiddenContentPage.html hiddenContentPage js/enhanced/hiddencontent/ RecommendationsPage.html recommendationsPage js/jellyseerr/recommendations/ ActivityPage.html activityPage js/extras/activity-page.js, activity-custom-tab.js CatchUpPage.html catchUpPage js/enhanced/catchup/

Embedded view availability is distinct from where a page appears. JellyfinEnhanced.cs manages external Plugin Pages sidebar registration and optional Custom Tabs entries. Client mounting modules implement Custom Tabs panels and JE native Home tabs.

Feature and delivery flags determine registration/mounting. Each external delivery mode requires the corresponding external plugin. Native tabs use js/enhanced/native-tabs.js and do not require those plugins. See JE Pages & Tabs for layout requirements and placement choices.

docs.title: How modules are organised
docs.text:
Each component is a single top-level IIFE. Larger features split implementation by concern. The Calendar, Requests, More Info and Recommendations directories use this pattern:

Suffix Responsibility -styles CSS injection -data State and data access: fetching and caching -render HTML/DOM construction, sometimes split into helpers or cards -actions User interactions: filters, pagination and buttons -init Bootstrap, navigation wiring and the public surface -custom-tab Mounting inside Custom Tabs or native tab panels

Other directories have local conventions: spoilerguard/ uses bare names such as state.js; settingspanel/ and jellyseerr/ui/ use ui-; discovery modules mix discovery-base.js and genre-discovery.js; itemdetails/ and homeremoval/ retain features-. Follow the directory you are touching.

Many modules idempotently create an empty namespace:

const P = (JE.internals.requestsPage = JE.internals.requestsPage || {});

That guard does not initialize state or remove ordering dependencies. requests-page-data.js owns Requests state; hidden-content-data.js owns Hidden Content data; hidden-content-page-state.js owns its management-page state; catchup-core.js owns JE.internals.catchUp. Their consumers must follow them.

jellyseerr/ui/ui-icons.js and jellyseerr/moreinfo/more-info-modal-data.js seed their respective shared namespaces, which later modules read directly.

Avoid hyphens in JavaScript directory segments under the current implicit embedded-resource naming (settingspanel, not settings-panel). Directory hyphens are rewritten in resource names, while the loaders look up paths by converting slashes to dots; file-name hyphens are supported. Supporting hyphenated directories requires resource names matching that lookup and verification of both bundle and individual-script delivery.

bootstrap-manifest.test.mjs checks manifest-order loading and the single-IIFE shape. Top-level directives or declarations outside that IIFE break the wrapping contract. These tests do not build a complete dependency graph; producer-before-consumer order remains your responsibility.

docs.title: Component Breakdown
docs.text: These indexes group client modules and relevant supporting server files by web feature area.

docs.title: Shared browser primitives: js/core/
docs.text: File Responsibility api-client.js Shared managed HTTP layer, JE.core.api.{fetch,jf,plugin}: authentication, retry/backoff, caching, deduplication, concurrency limits and abort support. Persistence, translations and some features also issue direct ApiClient.ajax or fetch requests. dom-observer.js One shared body MutationObserver with named subscribers, dedicated observers and waitForElement. lifecycle.js Registers feature observers, timers and listeners for coordinated cleanup. navigation.js Deduplicated SPA navigation notifications through onNavigate and onViewPage. session.js Hooks ApiClient.setAuthenticationInfo, follows navigation notifications and reconciles every five seconds. Runs JE.session.onUserChange reset handlers and emits je:user-changed; supplies identity epochs for async work. media-language.js Shared audio-language/region-to-flag resolution through JE.core.mediaLanguage.resolveFlag. tag-renderer-base.js Overlay creation, positioning, deduplication, caching and reinitialization for genre, language, quality, rating and age-rating tags. People and user-review renderers are independent. ui-kit.js HTML escaping, toasts, deduplicated CSS injection and scroll-friendly direct/delegated tap listeners.

docs.title: Enhanced UI: js/enhanced/
docs.text: File or directory Responsibility config.js Effective settings, shared state and server persistence. helpers.js, events.js Shared utilities and input/event wiring. header-actions.js Measures header space and moves overflow actions into a menu, retaining original buttons/listeners. Launcher: More from Jellyfin Enhanced; menu heading: More from JE. docs.title: Catch Up
docs.text:
js/enhanced/catchup/ contains catchup-core.js, catchup-styles.js, catchup-deck.js, catchup-activity.js, catchup-page.js and catchup-custom-tab.js.

Core loads first and owns state, helpers and API actions. The deck implements swipes, page code orchestrates the feature, and the mounting module follows the public page surface.

Swipes mark watched, dismiss, add to the watchlist (Jellyfin's Likes flag) or open a title. Dismissals are per-user browser-local data.

Controllers/CatchUpController.cs records authenticated users' actions through POST /JellyfinEnhanced/catchup/event; both feature and recording gates must be enabled. GET /JellyfinEnhanced/catchup/events and GET /JellyfinEnhanced/catchup/summary require authentication and enforce administrator status inside their methods. Services/CatchUpLogService.cs stores the bounded log, independently of Activity Feed.

Administrator settings under Pages:

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up Off Gates Catch Up (CatchUpEnabled). Record Catch Up activity On Gates server logging (CatchUpLogEnabled), when Catch Up is enabled. Add Catch Up as a native Home tab Off JE native-tab placement (CatchUpUseNativeTab). Use Plugin Pages Off Sidebar delivery (CatchUpUsePluginPages); requires Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off External tab delivery (CatchUpUseCustomTabs); requires Custom Tabs. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the external entry (CatchUpAutoCreateCustomTab).

CatchUpCustomTabJeOwned=false tracks internal ownership, not an administrator control. See Enhanced Features for usage.

docs.title: Seerr and discovery: js/jellyseerr/
docs.text:
File or directory Responsibility api.js, request-manager.js, seerr-status.js Seerr proxy communication, the stable alias onto JE.core.api.manager, and shared media/display status constants. jellyseerr.js Search-results integration and pagination. Other Seerr components initialize independently of the search-results gate. modal.js, issue-reporter.js Request dialog support and media problem reporting. item-details.js Similar/recommended detail rows and requests for missing series seasons. hss-discovery-handler.js, seerr-detail-link.js Home Screen Sections discovery-card interception and detail-page links to Seerr. seamless-scroll.js Shared buffer-fill scrolling and deduplication for search, discovery and category pages, with prefetching and failure backoff. Pauses for manual continuation after 40 consecutive empty pages. discovery/ discovery-base.js owns lifecycle, pagination, aborts, gating, filtering and rendering. discovery-filter-utils.js supplies shared filters/cards; genre-discovery.js, network-discovery.js, person-discovery.js, tag-discovery.js, collection-discovery.js provide feed specs. moreinfo/ Eight more-info-modal-* modules: styles, data, seasons, badges, render, TV actions, general actions and initialization. recommendations/ Eight recommendations-* modules: styles, catalog, data, render, page, category, initialization and tab mounting. Discovery rows, studio/network tiles and category pages live here. ui/ Ten ui-* modules: icons, styles, popover, badges, cards, buttons, quota, results, request modals and season modal.

docs.title: Calendar and requests: js/arr/
docs.text:
arr-links.js adds administrator detail links to Sonarr, Radarr and Bazarr; arr-tag-links.js turns synced *arr tags into filtered links.

arr/calendar/ has seven modules: calendar-page-styles.js, calendar-page-data.js, calendar-page-render-events.js, calendar-page-render-views.js, calendar-page-actions.js, calendar-page-init.js, calendar-custom-tab.js.

Calendar combines Radarr, Sonarr and Shoko data. Shoko retrieval lives in the main controller, with Jellyfin posters and deep-link handling in the calendar modules; there is no separate ShokoService.cs. Shoko is configured when both URL and API key are present. Check it alone and alongside *arr sources when changing calendar behavior. See *arr Settings for setup.

Administrator settings under *arr → Shoko:

Setting Default What it does Shoko URL Empty Server connection (ShokoUrl). Shoko API Key Empty Authentication (ShokoApiKey). Shoko URL Mappings Empty Browser-facing links (ShokoUrlMappings). Episodes On Includes regular episodes (ShokoShowEpisodes). Specials Off Includes specials (ShokoShowSpecials). Credits (OP/ED) Off Includes credits (ShokoShowCredits). Trailers Off Includes trailers (ShokoShowTrailers). Parodies Off Includes parodies (ShokoShowParodies). Other Off Includes other episode types (ShokoShowOther).

arr/requests/ has eight modules: requests-page-styles.js, requests-page-data.js, requests-page-render-helpers.js, requests-page-render-cards.js, requests-page-render.js, requests-page-actions.js, requests-page-init.js, requests-custom-tab.js. They implement the combined requests, downloads, issues and import-history page backed by Seerr and *arr integrations. See Seerr Features for the page's user-visible behavior.

docs.title: Web tags: js/tags/
docs.text:
File Responsibility genretags.js, languagetags.js, qualitytags.js Genre badges, language flags and quality tags such as resolution, dynamic range and audio format. ratingtags.js Jellyfin CommunityRating and CriticRating, with star/tomato presentation. Metadata providers or MDBList synchronization determine the upstream scores. ageratingtags.js Color-coded parental/age ratings, sharing the Colored Ratings color table. peopletags.js Cast age, birthplace flags and deceased indicators. userreviewtags.js Average of rated reviews visible to the current viewer, composed into the rating overlay. Uses tag-cache averages or batched /JellyfinEnhanced/reviews/ratings requests. tag-cache-store.js IndexedDB snapshot scoped by server and user; memory-only fallback when unavailable. tag-pipeline.js Restores/downloads the bulk server cache, applies ?since= deltas and scans cards in idle slices. tag-styles.js Retrieves validated color overrides and injects web CSS; paired with server Services/PosterTags/TagStyles.cs.

Setting Property Enable Tag Styles TagStylesEnabled Apply Tag Styles To TagStyleTarget Preset TagStylePreset Apply to TagStyleApplyScope Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental) NativePosterTagsEnabled Additional Excluded Clients NativePosterTagsWebClientNames

The editor stores TagStyleOverrides="" until overrides are saved. Native rendering uses the same validated styles.

docs.title: Activity Feed
docs.text:
js/extras/activity-page.js renders the feed; activity-custom-tab.js mounts it.

On the server, EventHandlers/ActivityPlaybackConsumer.cs records playback-stop activity after at least 5% progress or Jellyfin-reported completion. Services/ActivityFavoriteMonitor.cs watches favorite changes; ActivityService.cs supplies the recording API over UserConfigurationManager storage. ActivityFeedBuilder.cs merges activity and reviews, filters by viewer access/author visibility, then hydrates card data.

Administrator settings under Pages (the final two controls are under Extras):

Setting Default What it does Enable Activity Feed Off Gates recording/display (ActivityFeedEnabled). Show recently watched On Playback activity (ActivityFeedShowWatched). Show recently favorited On Favorite activity (ActivityFeedShowFavorited). Show recently reviewed On Review activity (ActivityFeedShowReviewed). Show Active Streams section On Live sessions section (ActivityFeedShowActiveStreams), subject to the session gate below. Add Activity as a native Home tab Off Native placement (ActivityFeedUseNativeTab). Use Plugin Pages Off Sidebar delivery (ActivityFeedUsePluginPages); requires Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off External tab delivery (ActivityFeedUseCustomTabs); requires Custom Tabs. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Entry management (ActivityFeedAutoCreateCustomTab). Active Streams Header Widget Off Enables the active-session data gate (ActiveStreamsEnabled). Show widget to non-admins Off Additionally required for non-admin session access (ActiveStreamsAllUsers).

ActivityFeedCustomTabJeOwned=false is internal ownership bookkeeping. The feed's session section shares the endpoint's gates even when the header widget itself is not mounted.

docs.title: MDBList display and metadata writes
docs.text:
js/others/mdblist-ratings.js displays the details-page ratings row. Services/MdblistService.cs fetches/caches upstream results, with cache/account models in Model/MdblistRatings.cs.

ScheduledTasks/MdblistRatingsFetchTask.cs uses MdblistRatingsFetchRunner.cs to populate the cache and stops when remaining quota reaches the reserve. MdblistRatingsSyncTask.cs writes cached scores into Jellyfin's CommunityRating and CriticRating; the display overlay does not write metadata.

See MDBList Ratings for controls and defaults. Administrator settings under Display map to these properties:

Setting Property Enable MDBList Ratings MdblistRatingsEnabled MDBList API Key MdblistApiKey Show Ratings Row on Item Details MdblistRatingsShowOnItemDetails Fetch Ratings from MDBList MdblistRatingsFetchEnabled Fetch Task Reserve MdblistFetchReserve Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin MdblistRatingsAutoSyncEnabled Star Rating Source (Community Rating) MdblistCommunityRatingSource Star Rating Fallback Source MdblistCommunityRatingFallbackSource Tomato Rating Source (Critic Rating) MdblistCriticRatingSource Tomato Rating Fallback Source MdblistCriticRatingFallbackSource Overwrite Existing Jellyfin Ratings MdblistRatingsOverwriteExisting Configure ratings shown MdblistRatingsSources Show % Symbol MdblistRatingsShowPercentSymbol

Repository-root images/mdblist-logos/ supplies logos. See Other Features for usage and limits.

docs.title: Server ownership
docs.text: The client interacts with server classes through endpoints, cookies and image responses, rather than referencing C# class names. PluginServiceRegistrator.cs is the source of truth for service lifetimes, event-consumer registrations and MVC filter order.

docs.text: Files Responsibility RadarrService.cs, SonarrService.cs *arr integration access. Shoko handling is in the main controller. docs.title: Spoiler Guard and identity
docs.text:
All files in this table are under Services/SpoilerGuard/:

File Responsibility ImageBlurService.cs SkiaSharp Gaussian blur, stock cards and pre-encoded fail-closed JPEG fallback, with result caching. SpoilerBlurImageFilter.cs Replaces protected image/trickplay responses with parent art, blur or fallback according to mode and availability. SpoilerFieldStripFilter.cs Strips/rewrites supported unwatched-item metadata in Jellyfin API responses, honoring user state and overrides. SpoilerIdentityService.cs, SpoilerIdentityTagFilter.cs Stable per-user markers and item DTO image-tag stamping for anonymous image requests. The tag filter also calls native poster stamping. ImageTagDecoration.cs Shared parsing/composition of [sb-{8hex}-]{jellyfinTag}[-jet{23hex}][-jeu{12hex}]. SpoilerUserResolver.cs Loads Spoiler Guard state for the resolved requester. SpoilerNextUnwatchedService.cs Cached per-user/per-series next-unwatched boundary for advanced category reveals. SpoilerTagDataStripper.cs Removes sensitive tag data, shared by web tag endpoints and native poster rendering. SpoilerAutoEnableFilter.cs Shared content-type/library scope gate for first-play, Seerr-request and library-add automation. SpoilerAutoEnableArmer.cs Bulk arming for users with library access, including disabled accounts, with one locked spoilerblur.json update per user. SpoilerLibraryAddAutoEnabler.cs Batches new-title library events into bulk arming. SpoilerExistingTitlesApplier.cs Preview/application for existing titles, run by ScheduledTasks/SpoilerApplyExistingTitlesTask.cs. SpoilerSeerrPendingPromoter.cs Converts pending pre-acquisition protection into library-item entries when content arrives.

Services/Identity/RequestIdentityService.cs resolves authenticated claims first, then image markers, the single-user shortcut, validated cookies and session-by-IP candidates. Consumers distinguish confident identity from ambiguous shared-IP candidates.

Server filters protect supported Jellyfin images/metadata; suppression of JE's Reviews panel happens in js/elsewhere/reviews.js. The review-list API uses author visibility rules and does not itself apply that web-panel suppression. See Spoiler Guard for protection boundaries.

docs.title: Native Poster Tags: Services/PosterTags/
docs.text:
Native rendering draws each user's tags into Primary image responses for clients that do not run web overlays. It is subject to the administrator master gate and enabled tag groups. Original artwork files are preserved. The administrator controls are listed under Web tags.

Per-user setting in the Enhanced panel:

Setting Default What it does Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) On when unset (UseNativePosterTags=null) Personal preference, subject to the administrator master gate. File or directory Responsibility NativeClientPolicy.cs Excludes known clients running web overlays plus admin-configured client names. NativePosterTagStamper.cs Metadata-time Primary tag stamping, called by SpoilerIdentityTagFilter. PosterTagSettings.cs, PosterTagSettingsProvider.cs Effective personal settings/admin defaults, rendering digest, per-user cache and invalidation on settings/config changes. PosterTagUserCache.cs, PosterTagReviewRatings.cs User lookups and viewer-aware review averages. PosterTagDataProvider.cs Cache/on-demand tag data, access checks and Spoiler Guard stripping. PosterTagModel.cs, PosterTagResolver.cs Semantic corner/group/tag layout and web-parity resolution rules. PosterTagComposer.cs Data → layout → pixels, shared by image filtering and previews; content-addressed cache keys and composition version. PosterTagImageFilter.cs Primary response composition. Registered before the blur filter, so its response processing runs after blur and draws on the protected result. Rendering failure passes through the underlying image response. PosterTagVariantToken.cs Signed -jet variants bound to user, item, settings, pixel version, flags and data hash. CompositeImageCache.cs Byte-bounded memory LRU and disk cache under Jellyfin's cache path, in-flight coalescing and bounded render concurrency. TagStyles.cs Validated shared color overrides for web CSS and native drawing. Resolution/ AgeRatingRules.cs, GenreIcons.cs, JsText.cs, LanguageFlagRules.cs, LanguageNames.cs, QualityTagRules.cs, RatingRules.cs, ResolutionData.g.cs. Rendering/ PosterTagAssets.cs, PosterTagCss.cs, PosterTagImageScaler.cs, PosterTagPlan.cs, PosterTagRenderer.cs, PosterTagText.cs, PosterTagTileCache.cs: embedded assets, layout, scaling, text shaping, drawing and reusable tile caching.

ResolutionData.g.cs is generated by repository-root tests/poster/parity/gen-resolution-data.mjs; do not edit it by hand. Renderer/composition version changes retire existing variant tokens, preventing old URLs from serving newly changed pixels under long-lived client caches.

PosterTagVariantToken.cs persists a 32-byte random signing secret at <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/native-poster-tags.key, separate from rendered-image caches. Preserve it for URL-signing continuity during restoration.

Missing or wrong-length keys are recreated; old URLs can serve original artwork until clients refresh metadata. Persistence failure logs a warning and uses a process-lifetime key, changing URLs after restart. Unix creation uses owner-only read/write permissions. This is internal state without an admin control.

docs.text:

docs.title: Repository documentation and tooling
docs.text:
Repository-root files support development, documentation and release metadata:

mkdocs.yml owns navigation and Markdown extensions. Site screenshots (WebP) and short screen recordings (MP4) live in the docs/images/<area>/ folders above; Spoiler Guard's sit beside its pages in docs/spoiler-guard/. docs/images/readme/ holds the README images. Keep the flat docs/images/ratings.png, theme-selector.png, colored-activity-icons.png, login-image.png and plugin-icons.png: the admin page loads them from main for its View Screenshot previews. overrides/ copies a few Material 9.6.12 templates, so refresh it if the Material version pin in .github/workflows/docs.yml changes.

These are documentation assets, separate from runtime fonts, native rendering assets and root feature assets. The admin Docs tab loads the hosted site from the browser, rather than an offline copy embedded in the assembly.

docs.title: Generated assets and maintenance scripts
docs.text:
Use this index to find validation and asset-generation scripts and their maintenance requirements.

Repository-root script Inputs/outputs and maintenance contract scripts/generate_config_flag_groups.py Regenerates docs/advanced/config-flag-groups.json from admin configuration markup; docs CI runs it before building. scripts/validate-translations.js Validates locale JSON against js/locales/en.json; see Contributing Translations. scripts/material-symbols/subset.py Builds the two Material Symbols subsets from bundled full fonts. Add every new runtime icon name to ICONS, install fonttools/Brotli, regenerate and include both subset outputs. Literal scanning cannot cover dynamically constructed names. scripts/build_poster_assets.py Downloads pinned upstream inputs, verifies checksums and generates Assets/PosterTags/. Outputs are committed and do not regenerate during dotnet build. scripts/poster-assets/package.json, package-lock.json, rasterize_flags.mjs Pinned Node/Playwright tooling for Chromium flag rasterization used by the poster asset generator.

js/fonts/ contains materialsymbolsrounded.woff2, materialsymbolsoutlined.woff2, materialsymbolsrounded-subset.woff2 and materialsymbolsoutlined-subset.woff2. Full fonts use the public Material Symbols family names for themes/custom CSS; subsets use private JE Material Symbols … families and .je-msym-* classes for JE's own icons. Keep those families separate so a subset does not shadow a theme's full font.

Generated Assets/PosterTags/ contains fonts/NotoSans-Bold.ttf.br, flags/*.webp, icons.json, vector-icons.json, age-rating-colours.json, quality-colours.json, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and manifest.json. The manifest records pins, tool versions, options and output checksums and is excluded from embedding. These generated assets use explicit resource names.

Full regeneration requires Python 3.10+ with the generator's pinned fonttools/Brotli/Pillow versions, plus Node 18+, pinned Playwright and Chromium for flags. Use the dependency versions in the script/manifest to reproduce bytes. From the repository root:

python3 scripts/build_poster_assets.py --check
python3 scripts/build_poster_assets.py --check --full

The fast check uses only the Python standard library to verify repository inputs and output checksums. The full check regenerates into a temporary directory and compares bytes, requiring the complete toolchain.

Real-host tests use disposable Jellyfin instances. See tests/README.md for prerequisites and suite selection.

python3 tests/run.py fast
python3 tests/run.py all
python3 tests/inventory/generate.py --check

The inventory at tests/docs/production-inventory.json records lexical production surfaces such as files, routes, configuration and tasks; it is not behavioral coverage. Regenerate it with python3 tests/inventory/generate.py after relevant surface changes. Coverage gaps and historical evidence live in tests/docs/.

docs.title: *arr Features
docs.text: Connect Sonarr and Radarr for item links, metadata tags, upcoming releases, and download monitoring. Bazarr adds subtitle-management links; Shoko adds anime events to Calendar.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Who can use these features

Service links are available to Jellyfin administrators. Signed-in viewers can use tag links and enabled Calendar and Requests pages. What they see depends on library access, request ownership, section settings, and Seerr permissions.

Configure connections under Jellyfin Enhanced → *arr. Configure the pages under Pages. See *arr settings for every control and its default, or troubleshooting if results are missing.

docs.title: ARR Links
docs.text: Open a movie or series in Sonarr, Radarr, or Bazarr from its Jellyfin detail page. Sonarr and Radarr links appear only for servers that contain the title.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open Jellyfin Enhanced → *arr.
  2. Use + Add Sonarr instance or + Add Radarr instance and enter URL and API Key. The URL must be reachable from the Jellyfin server.
  3. Optionally enter Bazarr URL.
  4. Turn on Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages and choose the link presentation below.
  5. Click Save Settings, then reload the Jellyfin web client.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Sign in as an administrator and open a movie or series detail page.
  2. Look beside the TMDB external link.
  3. Click a service icon, text link, or dropdown entry to open a new browser tab.

With Show links as text and Show status badge for single-instance on, a Sonarr link shows downloaded/total episode counts and a colored status border.

Detail-page requirements

The detail page must show a TMDB link. These service links do not appear on individual season or episode pages. Bazarr opens the series or movies overview rather than the specific title.

docs.title: Link settings
docs.text:
These are admin (server) settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages Off Adds administrator-only service links. Show links as text Off Uses text labels instead of icons. Show status badge for single-instance Off Adds status styling to one matching instance; visible badges also require text mode.

Metadata icons override text links

Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) under Extras forces service links into icon mode. It overrides Show links as text.

Title matching and request-card links

Sonarr also requires a TVDB provider ID; Radarr uses the movie's TMDB ID. Bazarr opens /series/ or /movies/.

Administrators can also get Open in Sonarr and Open in Radarr icons on Seerr request cards when Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages is on. Movie cards require TMDB; TV cards require both TMDB and TVDB. These use the first matching instance, with no dropdown or Bazarr link. See Seerr features for request-card actions and View on Seerr.

Shoko's Open in Shoko link is on anime Calendar events; see Anime Calendar Events (Shoko).

docs.title: Multi-Instance Support
docs.text:
Add separate servers (instances) for TV, anime, HD, or 4K libraries. Give them distinct names so you can tell them apart. Each has its own connection and browser URL mappings.

  1. Add an instance under Sonarr or Radarr.
  2. Give it a distinct name.
  3. Click Save Settings.

Use the checkbox in a card's summary to enable or disable that instance. Click Save Settings after changing the checkbox, adding a card, or confirming Remove.

With one matching instance, you get a direct link. With multiple matches, click the service button to open a dropdown containing instance names, download status, and available sizes. Sonarr includes episode-file counts.

Color Meaning Green Sonarr's reported episode-file total is complete, or Radarr has a movie file. Amber Sonarr has some episode files, but fewer than its reported episode total. Gray The title exists in the instance, but reports no downloaded episode files or movie file. Missing Sonarr statistics also use this color.

Instances without the title are omitted. For one match, turn on both Show status badge for single-instance and Show links as text to see the episode count or Downloaded/Missing badge.

Instance names, disabled connections, and status details

Names appear in links, Calendar badges, and tooltips on source icons for ordinary download cards. Grouped Season cards show only Sonarr.

Disabled instances keep their credentials. JE skips them for lookups, Calendar, queue/history retrieval, and tag sync.

If Sonarr reports no statistics, the badge reads 0/0 with gray status. Icon-mode tooltips retain available status details.

docs.title: URL Mappings
docs.text:
Use mappings when the server connects to an internal service address but your browser needs a public address. The left side is the Jellyfin address used by the client; the right side is the service address to open.

  1. Open that instance's URL Mappings (optional).
  2. Enter one pair per line, as in the example below.
  3. Use Validate Mappings to check URL syntax and that the two addresses differ.
https://jellyfin.example.com|https://sonarr.example.com
http://192.168.1.10:8096|http://192.168.1.20:8989
How mappings are matched

Matching ignores case and trailing slashes, but otherwise compares the full Jellyfin server address, including its base path. The first matching pair wins. If none matches, the browser link uses the instance's URL. Each instance's mappings are independent; they do not inherit a global mapping.

Bazarr and Shoko have their own mapping fields with the same format.

Keep the server connection address

Mappings change browser links only. Keep URL reachable from Jellyfin, especially when the public address requires an interactive proxy login. Validate Mappings does not test connectivity or API authentication.

docs.title: Legacy Single-Instance Fields
docs.text:
Keep a configuration backup if you may need to restore an earlier setup.

Compatibility and recovery

An explicitly empty instance list can fall back to the legacy connection fields. Saving cards copies the first complete card into the legacy URL, API key, and mappings, even if that card is disabled. Removing all cards and saving clears the legacy fields.

An unreadable instance list does not fall back to legacy fields; see instance recovery.

docs.title: ARR Tags
docs.text: Copy Sonarr and Radarr tags into Jellyfin metadata, then display them as clickable links on detail pages. Clicking a tag opens Jellyfin's list of items carrying that full prefixed tag.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Configure at least one complete, enabled Sonarr or Radarr instance under *arr.
  2. In Tags Sync, turn on Enable Tags Sync, choose a nonempty Tag Prefix, and review cleanup and filters.
  3. Click Save Settings.
  4. Open Jellyfin's Scheduled Tasks and run Sync Tags from *arr to Jellyfin, in the Jellyfin Enhanced category.
  5. Add a task trigger if you want recurring synchronization, then reload item pages to see the updated tags.

Run or schedule the task yourself

Saving does not run the task, and it has no default triggers. Tag sync does not require Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages.

docs.title: Tag Settings
docs.text:
These are admin (server) settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Tags Sync Off Allows the scheduled task to update metadata. Tag Prefix JE Arr Tag: Prepends this text to each source tag, including the trailing space. Clear old tags before sync On Removes metadata tags starting with the current prefix before adding replacements. Show synced tags as links On Shows existing matching metadata tags as detail-page links for viewers. How tags are matched

Radarr matches movies by TMDB ID; Sonarr tag sync matches series by IMDb ID. Sync updates movies and series in your library, excluding virtual placeholders, combines tags from enabled instances, and avoids duplicates regardless of letter case. Bazarr and Shoko do not supply tags.

Cleanup can remove tags without replacements

Clear old tags before sync also affects unmatched items and runs where upstream tag results are empty or failed. Check connectivity before running cleanup. Turning cleanup off preserves stale tags; changing Tag Prefix leaves tags bearing the previous prefix in place.

Prefix behavior

Keep Tag Prefix nonempty and its spelling/case consistent. The factory default is JE Arr Tag:, but settings replace a blank value with Requested by:. When the prefix is blank, displayed tag links use JE Arr Tag:; sync uses Requested by: only if the stored prefix is unset, rather than empty. Links require matching prefix capitalization; cleanup ignores capitalization.

docs.title: Tag Filtering
docs.text:
Choose which tags to sync or show as links. Link filters change what you see without changing stored metadata.

  1. Open Tag Filters under Tags Sync.
  2. Enter source tag names without the prefix. Matching is exact and ignores letter case.
  3. Use commas or semicolons for Sync to Jellyfin Filter, and one name per line for the two link filters.
Setting Default What it does Sync to Jellyfin Filter Empty Limits metadata writes to listed tags; empty syncs all source tags. Use commas or semicolons. Show as Links Filter Empty Limits clickable links to listed tags; empty allows all tags with the prefix. Use one name per line. Hide Specific Links Filter Empty Hides listed tag links and takes priority over the show filter. Use one name per line.

For Sync to Jellyfin Filter, use:

in-netflix,in-disney,4k-upgrade

Use commas or semicolons for the sync filter

The form says one per line, but putting each name on a new line does not work for Sync to Jellyfin Filter.

For Show as Links Filter, use:

in-netflix
in-disney
4k-upgrade

For Hide Specific Links Filter, use:

internal-tag
do-not-show
Existing metadata tags

Existing prefixed tags can appear as links without enabling sync or running another task. The visible link text includes the prefix.

docs.title: Custom Styling
docs.text:
Use custom CSS to rename a visible tag label, hide a link, or change its color. The examples below show the supported hooks.

CSS hooks and examples

Tag links expose .arr-tag-link, .arr-tag-link-text, and .arr-tag-link-icon, plus data-tag (full tag), data-tag-name (unprefixed name), data-tag-prefix, and data-id (slugified name).

Rename a visible label:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-tag-name="1 - n00bcodr"] .arr-tag-link-text {
  display: none !important;
}
.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-tag-name="1 - n00bcodr"]::after {
  content: " N00bCodr";
}

Hide a link or give it a service color:

.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="internal-tag"] {
  display: none !important;
}
.itemExternalLinks a.arr-tag-link[data-id="in-netflix"] {
  background: #d81f26;
  color: #fff;
}

See CSS customization for more recipes.

docs.title: Calendar Page
docs.text:
See upcoming episodes and cinema, digital, and physical movie releases in one Calendar. Enabled Sonarr and Radarr instances and a configured Shoko server supply events independently.

This example uses Month with Monday first; the default view is Agenda.

Agenda lists releases by date across a 30-day range. Use Today to start the range at the current date.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Configure an enabled Sonarr or Radarr instance, or enter Shoko URL and Shoko API Key, under *arr.
  2. Open Pages → Calendar Page and turn on Enable Calendar Page.
  3. Choose a navigation mode, then click Save Settings and reload the web client.

Calendar data needs no companion plugin

Calendar data does not require Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages or a companion plugin. Placement through Plugin Pages or Custom Tabs requires the corresponding plugin.

Navigation and plugin requirements

By default, JE adds Calendar where its navigation section is available. With placement modes off, you can also open /web/index.html#/calendar, prefixed by your Jellyfin base path.

For a Home tab, enable Add Calendar as a native Home tab; this requires no companion plugin. Alternatively use Use Plugin Pages or Use Custom Tabs with the corresponding installed plugin. Native and Custom Tabs modes cannot both be enabled for Calendar. Use the generated navigation link rather than a fixed Home tab index. On Jellyfin 12's experimental layout, header access can open a tab whose tab-strip button is hidden.

Plugin Pages 3.0+ supports live registration on save; older versions or a failed live update need a server restart. When a detected Plugin Pages integration is selected, use its page entry instead of the standalone URL. Entry locations depend on layout and viewport; the Modern Layout sidebar is mobile-only. See JE pages and tabs for placement instructions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Open Calendar from your configured entry point.
  2. Choose Day, Week, Month, or Agenda.
  3. Use the previous/next arrows to move by a day, week, month, or 30-day Agenda period. Click Today to return to the current date.
  4. Click legend chips to filter events. On phones, expand the initially collapsed filter panel to see the legend.

Week shows seven days of releases. Use the previous/next arrows to move one week at a time.

For one date, choose Day and use the previous/next arrows to change dates. In List and Backdrop presentation, timed releases are grouped by hour.

Choose List, Backdrop, or Cards to change presentation in Day, Week, or Month. These controls are disabled in Agenda.

Colors represent Cinema Release, Digital Release, Physical Release, Episode, and Anime. Badges identify service/instance names. There is no source-service selector or text search.

Click legend chips to select release categories or Available, plus Requests when Seerr is enabled. Watchlist and Watched appear when their highlight settings are on. With no selected chips, all otherwise eligible monitored events appear.

Switch from Month to Week to Agenda, then select and clear the Episode filter.

Event times use your browser's local timezone. Click a series event to open the matching series in Jellyfin. A movie event needs a file in Radarr before you can open it. The Available arrow and available time labels open episode or movie details without starting playback.

Your controls have personal defaults, saved through Calendar itself:

Setting Default What it does Day / Week / Month / Agenda Agenda Chooses the view and saves it in your personal settings; Agenda covers 30 days. List / Backdrop / Cards List Chooses presentation and saves it in your personal settings; disabled in Agenda. Unmonitored Off Includes otherwise excluded unmonitored events; saved per user in this browser's local storage. Combine Calendar filters
  • OR matches any selected chip; AND requires every selected chip. These controls need at least two selected chips.
  • NOT inverts the combined match and needs at least one selected chip.
  • Unmonitored is a separate inclusion toggle. NOT does not override it, library access, or forced requested-only filtering.

For example, select Episode and Available, then AND to show available episodes. Selecting mutually exclusive release categories with AND can yield no events. Your selected filter chips are not saved as personal preferences.

Event availability and duplicate releases

Time labels have different styles for upcoming unavailable events, past unavailable events, and those at least 24 hours late. Available files have their own styling. A source file may exist before Jellyfin has scanned or matched it, so clicking may do nothing yet.

Duplicate Sonarr events merge by TVDB ID, season, episode, and UTC date; Radarr events merge by TMDB ID, release category, and UTC date. Titles are the fallback when provider IDs are missing. JE prefers an accessible match, then one with a file, and retains distinct instance names in the badge. Cinema/digital/physical releases stay separate, as do Shoko events from Sonarr events.

docs.title: Calendar Settings
docs.text:
These are admin (server) settings; users cannot override them as personal defaults:

Setting Default What it does First Day of Week Monday Chooses any of the seven weekdays for the grid. Time Format 5pm/5:30pm Selects 12-hour or 17:00/17:30 24-hour formatting. Highlight Favorites/Watchlist Off Adds watchlist indicators and a Watchlist filter. Highlight Watched Series Off Adds watched indicators and a Watched filter for the matched played/started episode or movie. Filter by Library Access On Filters releases by your library access; access checks for titles not yet in Jellyfin may be incomplete. Show Requested Only (Default) Off Initially selects Requests; you can change filters. Force Only Requested Items Off Always limits the displayed Calendar to your requested titles and hides the Requests chip.

To show watchlisted episodes on a phone, expand the filter panel, select Episode and Watchlist, then choose AND. The Watchlist chip requires Highlight Favorites/Watchlist.

Highlighting, library access, and requested-only limits

Watchlist highlighting uses Jellyfin's like (Likes) flag, not the favorite (heart) flag. Under Seerr, Add requested media to Watchlist and Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin set this flag for matching library items; see Seerr settings. Watching another episode of a series does not mark an upcoming episode watched.

Library filtering infers unmatched-title access from matched Calendar events sharing an upstream root folder. Unknown roots remain visible; unmatched Shoko events have no root folder for this inference. Turning the option off broadens Calendar results without granting playback access.

Requested-only modes need Seerr request data for your linked account, matched by media type and TMDB ID. Missing request data can leave an empty Calendar; Shoko events lack TMDB IDs and are excluded. These options only change what you see in Calendar; they do not restrict access to Calendar data from the server.

docs.title: Anime Calendar Events (Shoko)
docs.text:
Shoko adds pink Anime events from its server collection. Use it to include anime in Calendar.

  1. Configure the one supported Shoko connection under *arr → Shoko.
  2. Enable Calendar under Pages.
  3. Under Episode Types to Show on Calendar, enable the types you want.
Setting Default What it does Episodes On Includes regular episodes. Specials Off Includes specials. Credits (OP/ED) Off Includes opening/ending credits. Trailers Off Includes trailers. Parodies Off Includes parodies. Other Off Includes other episode types. Anime event limits, matching, and air dates

With all six off, no anime events appear. Missing and restricted Shoko content is excluded; selecting episode types does not include restricted content.

Jellyfin matches use the Shoko Series and Shoko Episode provider IDs, normally supplied by Shokofin. Matched events can use Jellyfin poster artwork. Unmatched events may lack artwork and cannot open a matched Jellyfin detail page, but administrators can use Open in Shoko on the source icon when a Shoko series ID and URL are available. This opens /webui/collection/series/<id> using Shoko URL and Shoko URL Mappings. These connection details and links are available only to administrators.

A Shoko event is Available when Shoko reports an episode file. Shoko air dates are converted to your browser's local time, so depending on your timezone an event can show a time or appear on the previous day.

docs.title: Downloads Page
docs.text: Downloads are part of the shared Requests page, alongside Seerr Requests, optional Issues, and History. Sonarr and Radarr provide queue/history data; see Seerr features for request lists, request actions, issues, and request statuses such as Coming Soon and Orphaned.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Configure complete, enabled Sonarr/Radarr instances under *arr.
  2. Open Pages → Requests Page and turn on Enable Requests Page.
  3. Keep Show Downloads in Requests Page on and review ownership and History controls below.
  4. Choose standalone, native Home tab, Plugin Pages, or Custom Tabs placement, then click Save Settings and reload.
Placement and connection requirements

With placement modes off, open Requests from JE navigation or /web/index.html#/downloads, including any Jellyfin base path. Add Requests as a native Home tab needs no companion plugin. Use Plugin Pages for Requests and Use Custom Tabs for Requests require their respective plugins. Native and Custom Tabs modes are mutually exclusive for Requests; Plugin Pages live registration/restart rules are the same as Calendar. See JE pages and tabs.

Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages is not required for queue/history data. Seerr is optional for administrator queue monitoring, but default viewer ownership filtering needs enabled/configured Seerr and a linked account. Configure the Seerr connection under Seerr; it does not create a second Requests page.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Download cards show title, progress, downloaded/total size, ETA where available, and status. Use them to follow a transfer through to import.

How to use

  1. Open Requests from your configured entry point.
  2. Check the cards under Downloads.
  3. When multiple statuses are present, use the status tabs or All. Click the search icon to search title, subtitle, and instance name; matching ignores letter case. The search toggle appears only in this multiple-status layout.

Statuses include Downloading, Queued, Paused, Importing, Completed, Warning, Failed, and Unknown.

docs.title: Downloads settings
docs.text:
Admin (server) section and refresh settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Requests Page Off Enables the shared page. Show Downloads in Requests Page On Shows the queue; turning it off also hides History in the page. Filter Downloads by User Requests On Restricts non-admin queue/history results to titles they requested through Seerr. Show Seerr Issues Section Off Adds Seerr issues when Seerr is enabled. Show Download History Section On Shows recently imported/failed downloads. Restrict Download History to Admins Off Enforces administrator-only History access on the server. Enable Auto-Refresh On Refreshes enabled sections. See Refresh behavior. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 Sets the refresh interval; the form accepts 30–300 seconds. Card details, status priority, and queue limits

Hover the source icon on an ordinary card to see the instance name. Grouped Season cards show only Sonarr. Cards do not show quality.

An upstream tracked warning takes priority. Tracked import/failure states override transfer status. A completed transfer can still be importing or require intervention before Jellyfin can show it.

Three or more Sonarr entries sharing title, season, progress, and instance name collapse into a Season card. Grouped entries may still be separate downloads. Sizes are counted once only if every grouped entry has identical total and remaining sizes; otherwise they are summed. JE reads one queue page of up to 1,000 records per instance.

docs.title: Download History
docs.text:
History shows recent import results so you can check what reached your library. Cards show source/instance, title, relative time, and Imported, Import Failed, or Partially Imported.

  1. Open History below the other sections.
  2. Use its pagination to browse recent results; History has no search control.

Mixed Sonarr groups include imported/total counts.

History limits

JE reads the latest 200 history records per enabled instance, keeps import/failure records, groups Sonarr records by download ID, and retains at most 200 merged cards before viewer filtering. Pagination covers this bounded pool, not the complete upstream archive. Other history events, such as grabs, renames, and deletions, are omitted. History errors appear in server logs rather than the named instance errors shown for the queue.

docs.title: Who sees downloads
docs.text:
Administrators see downloads without request-ownership filtering. With Filter Downloads by User Requests on, other viewers see titles they requested through Seerr.

How request ownership is matched

Titles match by TMDB ID and media type. This is title-level filtering, not downloader ownership. Missing Seerr configuration, an unlinked account, no requests, or queue/history entries lacking usable TMDB IDs can yield no results.

Turning off ownership filtering shares download titles

Turning off Filter Downloads by User Requests exposes other users' queue/history titles to signed-in viewers, subject to the independent administrator-only History option.

Seerr request-list and issue permissions remain separate. For differences caused by hidden items, see Hidden Content filtering.

docs.title: Refresh behavior
docs.text:
Requests loads data when you open it, even with auto-refresh off. Use the refresh icon beside Downloads to reload all enabled sections.

Polling and caching

Polling stops when you leave the standalone page or switch away from its native Home or Custom Tabs tab. With Plugin Pages, it can keep refreshing after you navigate away, until you reload or close the browser page. Hidden browser tabs are always skipped.

Queue and History use separate shared server caches. Their lifetime follows the configured poll interval, clamped internally to 5–300 seconds; even a manual refresh may return cached data.

If a transfer has finished but the item is missing from Jellyfin, check upstream import and library scanning. Reaching 100% progress does not mean the item is available in your library.

docs.title: *arr Settings
docs.text:
Use Jellyfin Enhanced → *arr for connections, item links, and tag sync, and Pages → Calendar Page or Requests Page for page controls.

Administrator settings apply server-wide unless marked personal. For workflows, see *arr features; for missing links, data, or navigation, see troubleshooting.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Connect only the services you need for the features you want. The table below shows what each feature requires.

  1. Configure your services under Jellyfin Enhanced → *arr.
  2. Choose the features you want to enable.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the web client.

Back up your connections

Keep a configuration backup before replacing connections.

Feature Connection needed Item links Enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance with URL/key, or a Bazarr URL; administrator account and detail-page metadata prerequisites. Tag sync Enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance with URL/key and a scheduled-task run. Calendar Enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance with URL/key, or both Shoko URL and key. Downloads and History Enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance with URL/key; default non-admin ownership filtering also needs Seerr and account linkage. How API keys are used

API keys are stored in Jellyfin's plugin configuration and used for server requests. Administrators can view and edit them in settings. JE's browser features receive Sonarr/Radarr connection details without the API keys.

docs.title: CSS Customization
docs.text: See tag-link styling and CSS customization for supported hooks and examples.

docs.title: Multi-Instance Configuration
docs.text: Add one card per Sonarr or Radarr server so you can manage each connection separately. Open *arr → Sonarr or Radarr to get started.

docs.title: Adding an Instance
docs.text:
1. Click + Add Sonarr instance or + Add Radarr instance.
  2. Expand the card and enter its name, URL, and API Key.
  3. Optionally add URL Mappings (optional).
  4. Click Test to check the current URL and API Key.
  5. Click Save Settings.

Complete both connection fields

Only cards with both URL and API Key are saved. Incomplete cards are omitted; a card with a URL but no key produces a warning.

docs.title: Instance Fields
docs.text:
Use a distinct name to recognize each server in links and pages. The checkbox beside the collapsed card's name enables or disables the instance.

Setting Default What it does Instance name (unlabeled input) Empty Optional. Distinct names make sources easier to identify. Summary enable checkbox On Includes the instance in service lookups, Calendar, queue/history, and tag sync. URL Empty Required with the key to save a card. Server-side API address, including the service base path if needed. API Key Empty Required with the URL. Get it from the service's Settings → General → Security → API Key. URL Mappings (optional) Empty Maps Jellyfin access addresses to this instance's browser address. Instance defaults and connection testing

Both instance lists default to empty ([]). Saving a blank name substitutes Sonarr or Radarr. The summary checkbox's accessible label is Enable <name> instance.

Test checks unsaved values against /api/v3/system/status without saving them. A successful test confirms that the service answered, but does not guarantee that queue, Calendar, or title lookups will work.

docs.title: Import from Seerr
docs.text:
Copy Sonarr/Radarr connections from Seerr to save entering them manually. This is a one-time copy, not ongoing synchronization.

Seerr key permission

The configured Seerr key needs Administrator permission to read service settings.

  1. Save an enabled, complete Seerr connection under Seerr. It needs Enable Seerr integration (default off), Seerr URL(s) (One per line) (default empty), and Seerr API Key (default empty). See Seerr settings.
  2. Under Sonarr or Radarr, click Import from Seerr.
  3. Select the instances and review the Internal and External Jellyfin addresses used for mapping rows.
  4. Click Import Selected, review the resulting cards, then click Save Settings. Cancel closes the picker without importing.
What the import copies

Import uses the first nonempty newline-separated Seerr URL. It copies name, hostname/port/base-path URL, API key, and mapping rows into enabled cards. Exact URL duplicates are marked already imported and cannot be selected.

docs.title: Disabling an Instance
docs.text:
Disable an instance to skip it while keeping its connection.

  1. Uncheck the summary checkbox.
  2. Click Save Settings.
Editing and removing a disabled instance

The card body becomes disabled. Re-enable the checkbox to edit it or use Remove. Removal asks for confirmation and takes effect only after Save Settings.

docs.title: URL Mappings (per-instance)
docs.text:
Use mappings when your browser needs a different service address from the Jellyfin server.

  1. Open URL Mappings (optional) on the instance.
  2. Enter one jellyfin_url|service_url pair per line. Put the Jellyfin address on the left and the browser-facing service address on the right.
  3. Click Validate Mappings, then Save Settings.

For example:

https://jellyfin.example.com/jellyfin|https://sonarr.example.com
http://192.168.1.10:8096|http://sonarr:8989
Mapping rules and validation

The left side must match the Jellyfin server address used by the client, including the base path. Matching ignores case and trailing slashes; the first match wins. If nothing matches, the instance's URL becomes the browser address. Mappings are independent per instance, with no inherited global mapping.

The server continues using URL for API calls. Validate Mappings checks syntax and that both sides differ; it does not test network access or credentials. See URL mapping usage.

docs.title: Link Behaviour
docs.text:
Add service links so you can open a title in Sonarr, Radarr, or Bazarr from Jellyfin. These links are for administrators.

  1. Open *arr → *arr UI Links.
  2. Turn on Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages and choose icons or text.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the web client.
Setting Default What it does Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages Off Adds administrator-only Sonarr/Radarr/Bazarr links on Movie/Series detail pages and Sonarr/Radarr icons on request cards. Show links as text Off Uses text instead of service icons. Show status badge for single-instance Off Adds status styling for a single Sonarr/Radarr match. Visible badges also require Show links as text. Title-matching requirements

The detail page must show a TMDB external link. Sonarr additionally needs TVDB; Radarr uses the movie's TMDB ID. Unmatched titles have no Sonarr/Radarr link.

docs.title: Single Instance
docs.text:
One matching instance opens directly. Enable Show status badge for single-instance and Show links as text to see Sonarr episode-file counts or Radarr Downloaded/Missing badges.

Hover the link for its instance name, status, file size, and root folder when supplied, even with Show status badge for single-instance off.

Icon mode and missing statistics

Icon-mode tooltips retain available details. If Sonarr reports no statistics, the badge reads 0/0 with gray status.

docs.title: Multiple Instances (Dropdown)
docs.text:
Multiple matching instances produce a dropdown with names, status dots, counts/download status, and file sizes when supplied. Green means complete, amber means partially downloaded Sonarr episodes, and gray means a matching title with no downloaded files. Instances that do not contain the title are omitted.

Metadata icons override text links

Under Extras, Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) defaults off. Turning it on forces Show links as text off. It is a server setting, not a personal service-link override.

docs.title: Legacy Single-Instance Fields
docs.text:
JE keeps older connection fields for compatibility. Restoring an older configuration requires a backup; downgrading alone does not restore it.

Stored fields and compatibility

Legacy SonarrUrl, SonarrApiKey, SonarrUrlMappings, RadarrUrl, RadarrApiKey, and RadarrUrlMappings all default empty. These are stored compatibility fields, not separate controls in the current tab.

Explicitly empty instance lists can use complete legacy URL/key pairs. Saving a readable list mirrors its first collected instance into the legacy fields, including a disabled first instance. Saving no instances clears them. Unreadable stored lists and their legacy fields are preserved on ordinary save, without legacy fallback.

docs.title: Bazarr
docs.text:
Bazarr adds links to its movie and series overviews so you can manage subtitles. You can configure one Bazarr connection.

  1. Open *arr → Bazarr.
  2. Enter Bazarr URL and, if needed, Bazarr URL Mappings.
  3. Click Save Settings.
Setting Default What it does Bazarr URL Empty Base browser address for Movie/Series overview links. Bazarr URL Mappings Empty Uses the same Jellyfin-address-to-service-address format as instance mappings. Bazarr link requirements and limits

Bazarr has no API-key input, tag sync, Calendar source, queue, or History integration. Its detail links require administrator service links and a visible TMDB link. They open /movies/ or /series/, not a specific item.

docs.title: Shoko
docs.text:
Connect Shoko to include anime events in Calendar. You can use Shoko as the only Calendar source.

Enter both Shoko connection fields

Both Shoko URL and Shoko API Key must be present. Partial configuration produces a Calendar error.

docs.title: Generating a Shoko API Key
docs.text:
1. In Shoko's web UI, open Settings → API Keys → Add API Key.
  2. Copy the key into Shoko API Key.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open *arr → Shoko and enter Shoko URL and Shoko API Key.
  2. Optionally configure Shoko URL Mappings.
  3. Click Save Settings.
  4. Enable Calendar under Pages. No Sonarr/Radarr connection is needed for a Shoko-only Calendar.

docs.title: Instance Fields
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Shoko URL Empty Server-side Shoko address; also the browser-link fallback. Shoko API Key Empty Key for Shoko API v3 requests. Shoko URL Mappings Empty Browser-link mappings under Advanced URL Mappings. Episodes On Includes regular anime episodes on Calendar. Specials Off Includes special episodes. Credits (OP/ED) Off Includes opening/ending credits. Trailers Off Includes trailers. Parodies Off Includes parodies. Other Off Includes other AniDB episode types.

The six type switches are under Episode Types to Show on Calendar.

Shoko matching and event limits

Shoko supports one server and has no instance-name or enable-checkbox control. Connections use Shoko API Key and time out after 15 seconds. With all six episode types off, no anime events appear. Missing and restricted Shoko content is excluded; selecting episode types does not include restricted content.

Matching uses Shoko Series and Shoko Episode provider IDs, normally supplied by Shokofin. Unmatched anime may lack Jellyfin artwork and navigation, but administrators can still get Open in Shoko on the Calendar source icon. See anime event limits.

docs.title: Tag synchronization
docs.text:
Copy Sonarr/Radarr tags into Jellyfin metadata and show them as clickable links. Run the scheduled task to sync them.

  1. Open *arr → Tags Sync and turn on Enable Tags Sync.
  2. Choose a nonempty Tag Prefix and review cleanup. Filters are under Tag Filters.
  3. Click Save Settings.
  4. Run Sync Tags from *arr to Jellyfin from Scheduled Tasks.
  5. Add your own trigger for recurring runs; there are no default triggers.
Setting Default What it does Enable Tags Sync Off Permits Sync Tags from *arr to Jellyfin to update Movie/Series metadata. It does not run or schedule the task. Tag Prefix JE Arr Tag: Prepended to source tags; preserve the trailing space and use a nonempty value. Clear old tags before sync On Removes tags starting with the current prefix before adding replacements. Show synced tags as links On Shows existing prefixed metadata tags as links for viewers, independently of sync and administrator service links. Sync to Jellyfin Filter Empty Comma/semicolon-separated unprefixed names to sync; empty syncs all. Show as Links Filter Empty Newline-separated unprefixed names to show; empty shows all tags with the prefix. Hide Specific Links Filter Empty Newline-separated names to hide; hiding wins over the show filter.

Review cleanup and filter format

Clear old tags before sync also removes tags on unmatched items or failed/empty source results. Use commas or semicolons for Sync to Jellyfin Filter, even though the form says one per line.

Prefix and matching details

Settings replace a blank Tag Prefix with Requested by:. When the prefix is blank, displayed tag links use JE Arr Tag:; sync uses Requested by: only if the stored prefix is unset, rather than empty. Avoid blank prefixes. Changing the prefix leaves previously prefixed metadata in place.

Filters ignore capitalization in tag names, but displayed links require matching prefix capitalization. Movies match by TMDB, series by IMDb. See ARR Tags for cleanup limits, working filter examples, and styling.

docs.title: Calendar Page Settings
docs.text:
Choose how Calendar looks and which releases it shows. These are admin (server) settings.

  1. Open Pages → Calendar Page and turn on Enable Calendar Page.
  2. Choose page placement and display options.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the web client.

Setting Default What it does Enable Calendar Page Off Enables the Calendar surface using configured Sonarr/Radarr/Shoko sources. Add Calendar as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab without a companion plugin. Use Plugin Pages Off Uses the installed Plugin Pages integration. Use Custom Tabs Off Embeds Calendar in a Custom Tabs tab. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates a matching entry on save when the page and Custom Tabs mode are also enabled. First Day of Week Monday Selects any weekday as the grid's first column. Time Format 5pm/5:30pm Chooses 12-hour or 17:00/17:30 24-hour format; times use the browser timezone. Highlight Favorites/Watchlist Off Adds watchlist indicators and a Watchlist filter. Highlight Watched Series Off Marks the event's matched played/started episode; movie events also use played/started state. Filter by Library Access On Filters releases by your library access, with best-effort checks for future titles. Show Requested Only (Default) Off Initially selects Requests; viewers can change filters. Force Only Requested Items Off Always limits the displayed Calendar to your requested titles and hides the Requests chip. Highlighting and access limits

Watchlist highlighting uses Jellyfin's like (Likes) flag, not the favorite (heart) flag. Library filtering checks matched-item access and infers unmatched-title access from Calendar root folders. Unknown roots remain visible.

Under Seerr, Add requested media to Watchlist and Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin set the like flag for matching library items; see Seerr settings.

Requested-only display requires Seerr data for the linked viewer and matches TMDB ID plus media type. It excludes Shoko events and can be empty when request data is unavailable. These options only change what you see in Calendar; they do not restrict access to Calendar data from the server. Library filtering is best-effort for future titles; unmatched Shoko events have no root folder to check. Broader Calendar visibility does not grant playback access.

Standalone address: /web/index.html#/calendar, including your Jellyfin base path. Use the Plugin Pages entry when that installed integration is selected. See Calendar usage and page placement.

docs.title: Requests Page Settings
docs.text:
Use one shared Requests page to follow downloads, requests, and import results. Sonarr/Radarr supply Downloads and History; Seerr supplies Requests and optional Issues.

  1. Open Pages → Requests Page and turn on Enable Requests Page.
  2. Choose sections, access rules, placement, and refresh options.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the web client.

These are admin (server) settings:
