Setting Default What it does Enable Requests Page Off Enables the shared Requests surface. Show Downloads in Requests Page On Shows the queue; turning it off also hides History on the page. Filter Downloads by User Requests On Filters non-admin queue/history results to titles they requested through Seerr. Administrators bypass it. Show Seerr Issues Section Off Adds Issues when Seerr is enabled. Show Download History Section On Shows recent import/failure results. Restrict Download History to Admins Off Hides History from non-admins, enforced on the server. Add Requests as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab without a companion plugin. Use Plugin Pages for Requests Off Uses the installed Plugin Pages integration. Use Custom Tabs for Requests Off Embeds Requests in a Custom Tabs tab. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates a matching entry on save when the page and Custom Tabs mode are also enabled. Enable Auto-Refresh On Refreshes enabled sections; hidden browser tabs are skipped. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 Editable when Enable Auto-Refresh is on; form range 30–300 seconds. Save enforces a minimum of 30.

Download sources and viewer access

Queue/history require complete enabled Sonarr/Radarr credentials, not Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages. Default viewer filtering also requires enabled/configured Seerr, a linked account, and matching requests. Without them, viewers can receive empty results.

Turning off ownership filtering shares download titles

Turning off Filter Downloads by User Requests exposes all queue/history titles to authenticated viewers, subject to the History administrator restriction.

Opening the page loads data independently of polling. Use the Downloads refresh icon to reload enabled sections.

Ownership, refresh behavior, and History limits

Ownership matches use TMDB ID and media type. History retains at most 200 merged cards before user filtering and pagination.

Auto-refresh stops when you leave the standalone page or switch away from its native Home or Custom Tabs tab. Plugin Pages can keep refreshing after navigation until you reload or close the browser page. Hidden browser tabs are skipped.

Queue and History have separate shared caches whose lifetimes follow the interval, clamped to 5–300 seconds internally. Manual refresh may return cached results.

Standalone address: /web/index.html#/downloads, including your Jellyfin base path. Use the configured integration entry in Plugin Pages mode. See downloads and History, Seerr features, and page placement.

docs.title: Page placement
docs.text: Choose where you open each enabled page. Native Home tabs need no companion plugin; Plugin Pages and Custom Tabs need their corresponding plugins.

docs.title: Native Home tabs
docs.text: Use Add Calendar as a native Home tab or Add Requests as a native Home tab for navigation without a companion plugin. See JE Pages & Tabs for setup, layout behavior, and generated Home links.

docs.title: Plugin Pages
docs.text: Use Use Plugin Pages for Calendar or Use Plugin Pages for Requests with the companion installed. Follow Plugin Pages setup and fallback for registration, restart requirements, and navigation.

docs.title: Custom Tabs
docs.text: Use Use Custom Tabs for Calendar or Use Custom Tabs for Requests to embed the page on Home. Follow Custom Tabs setup for prerequisites, managed entries, manual HTML markers, and detection recovery.

docs.title: Personal settings
docs.text:
Choose your preferred Calendar view and presentation directly in Calendar. These controls save personal preferences; they are not admin defaults or settings-panel toggles.

  1. Open Calendar.
  2. Choose a view and presentation, or turn on Unmonitored to include unmonitored events.
Setting Default What it does Day / Week / Month / Agenda Agenda Saves your preferred Calendar view in your personal settings. List / Backdrop / Cards List Saves your preferred presentation in your personal settings; unavailable in Agenda. Unmonitored Off Includes unmonitored events; remembered for your account in this browser, without syncing to other browsers. What personal preferences cover

Your selected filter chips are not saved as personal preferences. Service connections, service-link settings, tag-sync settings, and Calendar access/highlight options are controlled by the administrator.

docs.title: Hidden Content settings
docs.text:
Hide matching items from Calendar, Downloads, and Requests. The administrator sets starting values, and you can change your personal filters.

  1. As an administrator, enable Enable Hidden Content and review defaults under Pages → Hidden Content → More Settings.
  2. In your personal Hidden Content settings, enable Enable Content Hiding and choose the surface filters.

Admin (server) settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Hidden Content Off Enables the feature server-wide, including personal filters. Hidden Content enabled by default On Sets the starting personal hiding state for new users. Filter Calendar On Sets the starting personal Calendar filter; users can override it. Filter Requests page On Sets the starting personal Requests filter; users can override it.

Both hiding switches must be on

Enable Hidden Content and your personal Enable Content Hiding must both be enabled for filtering. Ordinary saves preserve existing personal choices.

Personal controls in Hidden Content:

Setting Default What it does Enable Content Hiding On Enables your own hiding and surface filters when the server feature is enabled. Filter Calendar On Starts with the admin default. Hides matching hidden items in Month, Week, and Agenda; hidden items remain visible in Day. Filter Requests On Starts with the admin default. Hides matching hidden items in Downloads and Requests; History and Issues remain unchanged.

See Hidden Content filtering for these surface differences and Enhanced features for the full Hidden Content workflow.

docs.title: *arr Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the symptom you see, then work through the checks. See *arr settings for controls and *arr features for expected behavior.

docs.title: Links Not Appearing
docs.text:
Service links let you open a title in Sonarr, Radarr, or Bazarr. Check your account, connection, and detail page if they are missing.

  1. Sign in as a Jellyfin administrator. Sonarr/Radarr/Bazarr links and request-card service icons are administrator-only.
  2. Under Jellyfin Enhanced → *arr → *arr UI Links, turn on Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages and click Save Settings.
  3. Check that the relevant Sonarr/Radarr card is enabled and has both URL and API Key. Use Test to check the current connection.
  4. Open a movie or series detail page with a visible TMDB external link. Season and episode pages do not get these service links.
  5. Confirm the title exists in that upstream instance. Instances without a matching title are omitted.
  6. Hard-reload the web client after changing connection settings.
Matching, browser addresses, and badges

Sonarr needs a TVDB provider ID; Radarr uses the movie's TMDB ID. Detail-link lookups are cached for the session.

Bazarr needs Bazarr URL and the same detail-page prerequisites, but no API key. Its links open a movie/series overview. Shoko's Open in Shoko link appears on anime Calendar events, rather than item detail pages.

If a link appears but opens the wrong address, check URL Mappings (optional), Bazarr URL Mappings, or Shoko URL Mappings. The left side must be the Jellyfin server address used by the client, including any base path. The right side is the browser-facing service address. A successful API test does not establish browser reachability; mappings do not change the server's API destination.

If the single-instance status badge is missing, enable Show status badge for single-instance and Show links as text. If Sonarr reports no statistics, the badge reads 0/0 with gray status. Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) under Extras forces icon mode, where visible badges are omitted and details remain in tooltips.

docs.title: Connection errors and instance recovery
docs.text:
Check each connection before investigating individual features. Test helps you find which server needs attention.

  1. Open the affected Sonarr/Radarr card.
  2. Click Test to check the current URL and API Key.
  3. Use the result to choose a check below.
Symptom What to check Authentication failure Confirm the service API key. Check whether a reverse proxy is rejecting the request before it reaches the service. Timeout or network error Check DNS, port, scheme, TLS, and reachability from the Jellyfin server/container. A working browser URL does not establish server connectivity. Invalid response Inspect upstream/proxy logs. A public URL may return an HTML login or Cloudflare page instead of JSON, even after an HTTP-success test. URL rejected Use an absolute HTTP(S) service URL. Check the URL limits in the details below. One source missing, others working Inspect the named instance error and that card's enable checkbox, URL, and key. Healthy instances can still supply results. Connection testing, URL limits, and error reporting

Test checks the unsaved URL/key against /api/v3/system/status without saving. Validate Mappings checks syntax only. Authentication failures can return 401/403.

For services behind interactive login proxies, use an internal API address in URL, Shoko URL, or the relevant connection field, and put the public address in browser mappings. Loopback addresses are allowed, but localhost refers to the Jellyfin server/container, not your browser's machine. LAN addresses are not generally prohibited.

The URL guard rejects specified cloud-metadata hosts/IPs, unspecified addresses such as 0.0.0.0, and IPv4 169.254.0.0/16. The container aliases host.containers.internal and host.docker.internal have limited exceptions for host mappings in that range; metadata ranges remain blocked. Use the alias rather than a literal link-local IP where your container runtime provides it.

Queue, Calendar, and title-lookup errors identify the affected instance. The same error notification will not keep repeating until the connection recovers, so check the browser console and server logs even if you see no new notification. History errors appear in server logs rather than the named instance errors shown for the queue.

If settings show an unreadable Sonarr/Radarr instance list, ordinary Save Settings preserves its stored value. Corrupt lists do not trigger legacy fallback. Recover from a backup where possible.

Reset replaces the unreadable configuration

Reset Sonarr instances (clears stored value) or Reset Radarr instances (clears stored value) asks for confirmation. Saving afterward clears the unreadable entries. Recreate the cards and save only when you are ready to replace that configuration.

docs.title: Tags Not Syncing
docs.text:
Tag sync copies source tags into Jellyfin metadata. Check the task first, then distinguish missing metadata from missing tag links.

  1. Under *arr → Tags Sync, turn on Enable Tags Sync, configure complete enabled Sonarr/Radarr instances, then click Save Settings.
  2. Run Sync Tags from *arr to Jellyfin from Scheduled Tasks. Saving alone does not run it, and the task has no default triggers. Add your own trigger for recurring runs.
  3. Check that source tags exist.
  4. If Sync to Jellyfin Filter is set, use comma- or semicolon-separated source names without the prefix. Putting each name on a new line does not work for sync, even though the form suggests it.
  5. Inspect the Jellyfin item's metadata tags. Tag Prefix is added during sync; source tags do not need to contain it.
  6. Check task/server logs for a failed or disabled instance and review cleanup before running again.

Preserve tags while investigating

Clear old tags before sync removes tags starting with the current prefix even on unmatched items or empty/failed source results. Turn it off if you need to preserve existing tags. Changing the prefix does not remove tags bearing the old prefix.

If tags are present in metadata but missing as links:

  1. Check Show synced tags as links, the exact prefix spelling/case, and Tag Filters.
  2. Use one unprefixed name per line for Show as Links Filter and Hide Specific Links Filter. The hide filter wins.
  3. Reload the web client after updating metadata or filters.

Seeing existing tag links does not require administrator status or Enable Tags Sync.

Tag matching and prefix behavior

Movie sync matches TMDB IDs; series sync matches IMDb IDs, not the TVDB ID used by Sonarr item links. Sync updates movies and series in your library, excluding virtual placeholders.

Keep Tag Prefix nonempty. Settings replace a blank value with Requested by:, while displayed tag links use JE Arr Tag: for a blank prefix. Sync uses Requested by: only if the stored prefix is unset, rather than empty. See tag settings and examples.

docs.title: Calendar Not Loading
docs.text:
A blank Calendar page and a Calendar with no events need different checks. Start by confirming the page is enabled and opens from the right place.

  1. Under Pages → Calendar Page, turn on Enable Calendar Page, click Save Settings, and reload the web client.
  2. Verify at least one source: a complete enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance, or both Shoko URL and Shoko API Key. A Shoko-only Calendar needs neither Sonarr nor Radarr. Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages is not required.
  3. Check how you are opening it: standalone, Plugin Pages, native Home tab, or Custom Tabs. Use the matching entry point; see page placement.
  4. Distinguish a blank/unready page from No upcoming releases. The former points to client injection or placement; the latter can be successful loading with no visible events.
Page entry points and loading diagnostics

For standalone mode, use /web/index.html#/calendar, including the deployment's Jellyfin base path. When a detected Plugin Pages integration is selected, open its registered Calendar entry instead. Plugin Pages 3.0+ supports live registration; restart for older versions or if logs say live registration failed.

Plugin Pages loads an authenticated Calendar fragment from /JellyfinEnhanced/calendarPage, registered as Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced.CalendarPage. Requests uses /JellyfinEnhanced/downloadsPage, registered as Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced.DownloadsPage. These fragments are not replacements for the standalone hashes. They wait up to five seconds for the JE module before showing Jellyfin Enhanced not ready. Check script injection, failed asset loads, and browser-console errors separately from service credentials.

For Custom Tabs, use your browser's developer tools to check the active Home tab for .jellyfinenhanced.calendar or .jellyfinenhanced.requests. A missing marker means the tab needs its Calendar or Requests HTML; a present but empty marker means JE has not loaded or displayed the page. If automatic creation failed, use Retry on the plugin detection banner or reload and save again. A saved JE configuration does not guarantee that the companion tab was created.

Native tabs use generated Home links containing a current tab index and stable jeTab=calendar or jeTab=requests. Do not reuse a fixed tab index. Jellyfin 12's experimental layout can hide the tab-strip button; use header access. Companion-plugin navigation depends on layout and viewport; Modern Layout sidebar access is mobile-only.

docs.title: Empty or incomplete Calendar results
docs.text:
Filters can hide events even when a source loads successfully. Check the visible controls first, then access and source settings.

  1. Return to Today, change the view, and clear selected chips and NOT. AND between mutually exclusive release categories can show nothing.
  2. Turn on Unmonitored if the missing upstream event is unmonitored; it is excluded by default.
  3. Check Filter by Library Access and your Jellyfin library permissions. Future-title root-folder inference is best-effort; unknown roots and unmatched Shoko events can remain visible.
  4. Review Show Requested Only (Default) and Force Only Requested Items. These need request data for your linked Seerr account; they exclude Shoko events. Forced mode hides the Requests chip.
  5. For Shoko, verify the six episode-type switches; only Episodes defaults on. Enter both Shoko URL and Shoko API Key. A URL without a key, or a key without a URL, produces an error. Check Shoko API v3 access and server logs.
  6. Check Hidden Content filtering and named source failures.
Highlighting, matching, and event times

Watchlist highlighting uses Jellyfin's like (Likes) flag, not the favorite (heart) flag. Under Seerr, Add requested media to Watchlist and Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin set this flag for matching library items; see Seerr settings. Watched markers reflect whether you have played or started the matched episode or movie; watching other episodes does not mark an upcoming episode.

If an available event does nothing when clicked, confirm Jellyfin has scanned and matched it. The Available arrow opens details rather than starting playback. A Shoko event is Available when Shoko reports an episode file. Shoko matching needs Shoko Series/Shoko Episode provider IDs. Unmatched anime may still offer an administrator's Open in Shoko link. Event dates use your browser's local time. Shoko air dates are also converted to your browser's local time, so depending on your timezone an event can show a time or appear on the previous day.

docs.title: Blank screen / Cannot find module error
docs.text:
If Calendar or Requests is blank and the console shows Cannot find module './', Cloudflare Rocket Loader may be interfering with JavaScript module loading. This symptom alone does not prove the cause.

  1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, select your domain.
  2. Open Speed → Settings → Content Optimization and turn Rocket Loader off. Use a configuration rule for your Jellyfin hostname if you need to limit the change.
  3. Reload and compare the result.

See Cloudflare's Rocket Loader instructions and issue #570.

docs.title: Requests Page Issues
docs.text:
The shared Requests page combines Downloads, Seerr Requests, optional Issues, and History. For request-list permissions, approval/decline, issues, or Coming Soon/Orphaned states, see Seerr features.

There is no independently enabled second Seerr Requests page.

docs.title: Downloads Not Showing
docs.text:
Check the queue source and your access rules if Downloads is empty. Administrators and viewers can get different results.

  1. Under Pages → Requests Page, enable Enable Requests Page and Show Downloads in Requests Page, then save and reload.
  2. Verify complete enabled Sonarr/Radarr cards and use Test. Confirm the upstream queue contains records.
  3. Compare administrator and viewer results. With Filter Downloads by User Requests on, administrators bypass filtering. Viewers need enabled/configured Seerr, a linked account, and requested titles.
  4. Clear download search/status selections and check Hidden Content filtering.
  5. Inspect named queue errors and server logs. Healthy instances can return data despite another source failing.

Auto-refresh is not required for the initial load. Neither queue nor History requires Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages.

Turning off ownership filtering shares download titles

Turning off Filter Downloads by User Requests exposes other users' queue/history titles to authenticated viewers, subject to the independent History administrator restriction.

Queue limits and ownership matching

JE reads one queue page of up to 1,000 records per instance. Viewer requests match by TMDB ID and media type. No linkage/requests or missing upstream TMDB IDs can produce empty results.

docs.title: Status Not Updating
docs.text:
Requests can refresh itself while you follow a download. If its status looks stale, check refresh settings and the upstream service.

  1. Check Enable Auto-Refresh and Poll Interval (seconds).
  2. Use the refresh icon beside Downloads to reload enabled sections.
  3. If the upstream queue is stale too, investigate the downloader or upstream import.
Setting Default What it does Enable Auto-Refresh On Refreshes enabled sections. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 Sets the refresh interval; form range 30–300 seconds. Polling and server caching

Polling stops when you leave the standalone page or switch away from its native Home or Custom Tabs tab. With Plugin Pages, it can keep refreshing after you navigate away, until you reload or close the browser page. Hidden browser tabs are always skipped.

Queue and History have separate shared server caches with a lifetime tied to the interval, clamped to 5–300 seconds internally. A manual refresh may still return cached data.

Completed describes transfer completion; Importing, Warning, and Failed come from upstream tracking. Check Sonarr/Radarr's import errors and Jellyfin scanning when 100% progress does not become library availability. Seerr availability updates are separate; see Seerr settings for its library-sync controls.

docs.title: History missing or shorter than expected
docs.text:
History shows recent import results, rather than a full archive. Check section and access settings if it is missing.

  1. Keep Show Downloads in Requests Page and Show Download History Section on.
  2. Check Restrict Download History to Admins. It hides History from ordinary viewers and is enforced server-side.
  3. Check ownership filtering; it also applies to History.
History record limits

JE reads the latest 200 history records per instance, retains import/failure events, groups Sonarr records by download ID, and keeps at most 200 merged cards before viewer filtering and pagination. Imported, Import Failed, and mixed Partially Imported groups are shown; grabs, renames, and deletions are omitted. This is a recent window, not a full archive. Check server logs for History errors; these do not appear as the named instance errors shown for the queue.

docs.title: Hidden Content filtering
docs.text:
Hidden Content filters remove matching hidden items from selected parts of Calendar and Requests. You can change your personal filters.

  1. Check that the server's Enable Hidden Content and your personal Enable Content Hiding are both on.
  2. Open your personal Hidden Content settings and review Filter Calendar and Filter Requests.
  3. Reload the relevant page after changing these options.
Setting Default What it does Filter Calendar On Admin starting value; you can override it with personal Filter Calendar. Filter Requests page On Admin starting value; you can override it with personal Filter Requests.

Filter Calendar hides matching items in Month, Week, and Agenda; hidden items remain visible in Day. Filter Requests hides matching items in Downloads and Requests, while History and Issues remain unchanged. See Hidden Content.

docs.title: Diagnostic endpoints
docs.text:
Use the signed-in web client's network panel to inspect responses when the checks above do not explain the problem. The routes and limits below help identify where a request fails.

Authenticated routes and response limits

These routes use the /JellyfinEnhanced prefix and Jellyfin authentication. Inspect responses from the signed-in web client's network panel; use the API reference for broader API details.

Endpoint Access / diagnostic use GET arr/validate/sonarr?url=…, GET arr/validate/radarr?url=… Administrator; the Test action sends the service key in X-Arr-ApiKey, not the URL. GET arr/identify-url?url=… Administrator; probes a supplied URL to identify its service, not an owning instance. GET arr/series-slug?tvdbId=… Administrator; one title against the first enabled Sonarr instance. GET arr/series-slugs?tvdbId=… Administrator; one title across enabled Sonarr instances, with matches/errors. GET arr/movie-instances?tmdbId=… Administrator; one movie across enabled Radarr instances, with matches/errors. GET arr/links?tmdbIds=…&tvdbIds=… Administrator; batches comma-separated positive IDs, ignoring malformed/duplicate entries; requires at least one and permits at most 100 distinct parsed IDs combined. GET arr/queue Signed-in viewer; applies request-ownership filtering. GET arr/history?take=…&skip=… Signed-in viewer; applies History enablement, administrator restriction, and ownership gates. take defaults 20, capped at 50; skip defaults 0 and cannot be negative. GET arr/requests?take=…&skip=…&filter=…&userOnly=… Signed-in linked viewer with configured Seerr for data; take defaults 20, capped at 200, skip defaults 0/nonnegative, userOnly defaults false. See Seerr features for visibility permissions. POST arr/requests/{requestId}/approve, POST arr/requests/{requestId}/decline Linked Jellyfin administrator or Seerr user with ADMIN/MANAGE_REQUESTS; missing identity/link/permission can fail separately. GET arr/calendar?start=…&end=… Signed-in viewer; library filtering applies. Defaults to today UTC through 90 days; invalid dates keep defaults, reversed ranges swap, and ranges over 365 days are capped. POST arr/calendar/user-data Signed-in viewer; reads caller-specific watchlist/watched flags for supplied events, without saving preferences.

Enabling or disabling a page controls its display and navigation; it does not turn off every data-reading API. Batch links return per-ID matches/errors; absent instances yield empty results, while all-disabled or corrupt configuration can report errors. Bazarr has no dedicated integration endpoint; Shoko data is available through Calendar.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
Check the FAQ and issue-reporting guide. You can report issues on GitHub.

Include:

  • Plugin and Jellyfin versions.
  • Layout and page-placement mode.
  • Affected service and instance.
  • Differences between administrator and viewer results.
  • Relevant browser, server, and upstream errors.

Remove credentials before sharing

Remove API keys and authentication tokens from logs or screenshots.

docs.title: Elsewhere & Reviews
docs.text: Find subscription streaming providers, read reviews, and see release or air dates on item detail pages in Jellyfin. These features work in compatible Jellyfin web clients.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You can set up provider lookup, TMDB reviews, release dates, and reviews from your Jellyfin users in the admin Elsewhere & Reviews tab. Start with Elsewhere & Reviews Settings for setup, defaults, and troubleshooting.

API key requirements

Provider lookup, TMDB reviews, and release dates share the TMDB API Key. User-written reviews stay on your server and need no API key.

docs.title: Streaming Provider Lookup
docs.text: See which subscription services carry a movie or series in your default search country. Provider badges let you scan the results, and manual searches let you compare other countries.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. After an admin completes setup, open a movie or series detail page with a TMDB external link.
  2. Find the provider panel, normally just below the external links.
  3. Read Also available in {region} on: and its provider badges, or Not available on any streaming services in {region}. An admin can replace the unavailable heading with a custom message and optional icon.
  4. Use the gear icon to open Search Settings, choose countries and providers, and click Save. Reload or revisit the page to update automatic results.
  5. Use the magnifying-glass icon to search manually. Available countries get separate blocks; unavailable countries share one block. Use the close icons to dismiss blocks. Searching again replaces the previous manual results.

An admin's Custom Branding Message replaces the unavailable heading; the red box is a manual search result.

Admin settings in Elsewhere & Reviews:

Setting Default What it does Enable Elsewhere On Enables the detail-page provider panel with a configured TMDB key. TMDB API Key Empty Supplies the shared key for server-side TMDB requests. Default Region US Sets the automatic country until you choose a personal default. Default Providers Empty Allows all subscription providers when empty; otherwise allows only exact provider names. Ignore Providers Empty Hides matching provider names after Default Providers is applied.

Provider badges show names and logos. Available headings open a regional availability link in a new tab when TMDB supplies one, with the JustWatch tooltip. These links and badges do not start playback or verify your subscriptions.

Subscription availability only

Rental, purchase, free, and ad-supported categories are not shown separately. An unavailable result means no matching subscription providers for the country and filters you used. It does not mean the title is exclusive to your server.

How automatic and manual results differ

Ignore Providers uses case-insensitive regular expressions after Default Providers. Automatic results use the admin provider filters and your Default Search Country. Manual searches use Search Other Countries (leave empty to use default), falling back to your default country only when that list is empty. They use your Providers (leave empty to show all available) selection and bypass both admin provider lists. See Search Settings and provider filtering.

Availability comes from TMDB's subscription (flatrate) category. If a badge logo fails to load, its name remains. Without an external-links container, the panel is added to the detail section.

docs.title: Per-season providers
docs.text: See which services carry each part of a series. When seasons have different providers, a series page groups them under labels such as Seasons 1–6 and Season 7; a season page shows its own providers.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open a series in its default aired order, or one of its numbered seasons, with a parent-series TMDB ID.
  2. Keep the admin Per-season providers setting on.
  3. In the panel's Search Settings, keep Show providers per season (when seasons differ) on. This personal setting appears only when the admin permits it.
Setting Default What it does Per-season providers On (admin) Enables automatic season lookup for default/aired-order series. Show providers per season (when seasons differ) On (per user) Lets you turn off season lookup for your account. Grouping and fallbacks

Grouping uses integer-numbered Jellyfin seasons returned for you. Admin filtering happens first. Regular seasons without matching providers fall back to filtered series providers; specials without matching providers are left out of grouping. If every considered season has the same provider set, the display stays at series level.

Alternate orders, manual searches, and Seerr cards use title-level availability. See Per-season providers for the requirements for showing the panel and its fallbacks.

docs.title: Custom Branding
docs.text: Give the unavailable-provider heading your own message and optional icon. It appears when no filtered automatic providers or season groups remain.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. As an admin, open Custom Branding in the Elsewhere & Reviews tab.
  2. Enter a message and optional image URL, then click Save Settings.
  3. Reload the detail page.
Setting Default What it does Custom Branding Message Empty (admin) Replaces the automatic unavailable heading; empty keeps the standard heading. Custom Branding Icon URL Empty (admin) Adds an optional icon beside a nonempty custom message; empty supplies no icon. Country, filters, and controls

The message reflects the current country and filters. In this state, search and gear controls appear when you hover over the panel. See Custom Branding for image paths and touch-device considerations.

docs.title: User Reviews
docs.text: Share your thoughts and star ratings with other viewers on your Jellyfin server. You can review movies, series, and their numbered seasons and episodes.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. An admin opens Elsewhere & Reviews, turns on Enable User Written Reviews, and clicks Save Settings. Reload the client after changing the configuration.
  2. Open an eligible item and expand Reviews ({count}).
  3. Click Write a Review (shown only when you have no review for this item), enter text and/or choose a rating, then click the save icon. Click a star's left half for a half-star value or its right half for a full value. Use the close icon beside the stars to clear a rating, or the form's close icon to cancel.
  4. Use your card's Edit icon to update the review or Delete to remove it after confirmation. You have one review per movie, series, season, or episode; saving again updates it.

Admin settings in Elsewhere & Reviews:

Setting Default What it does Enable User Written Reviews Off Enables the local review panel and writing controls, independently of provider lookup and TMDB reviews. Hide reviews from hidden users On Hides these authors' reviews from other non-admin viewers. Hide reviews from disabled users On Hides these authors' reviews from other non-admin viewers. Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating Off Copies movie/series review stars to the author's Jellyfin rating at twice the star value. Show average user rating on poster cards Off Adds visible local-review averages to eligible posters when rating tags are enabled. Show "—" on posters for unrated items On Shows a dash when no visible rated-review average exists, if poster averages are enabled.

Your server's review cards appear before TMDB cards. They have green borders, author names and avatars, update dates, and star ratings when supplied. Use Read More and Read Less for long text.

Review requirements and limits

Movies and series need TMDB IDs. Season and episode pages need the parent series' TMDB ID and the relevant season/episode numbers. Reviews accept up to 2,000 characters and/or a rating from 1–5 stars in half-star increments.

Choose at least 1 star

The picker offers 0.5 on the left half of the first star, but the server rejects that value. Choose at least 1 star or clear the rating for a text-only review.

Visibility, moderation, and averages

Reviews are stored locally. The admin's author-visibility settings and your Spoiler Guard settings control which reviews you see. Existing authors see their own reviews even when author filters apply; admins bypass those filters. Deleted-author reviews are hidden from non-admins while either filter is on. Filtering keeps reviews stored and also applies to averages.

Admins can use Delete as admin on other authors' cards. The web UI does not let them edit another author's review. Failed deletions show feedback. Each review is stored under its movie, series, season, or episode key. Duplicate library items with the same TMDB identity and child numbering share reviews. Hidden authors are identified by Jellyfin account policy, independently of your Hidden Content list; these author filters also apply to stored Activity Feed entries.

Detail pages show the average of visible rated local reviews out of ten. Poster averages also need effective Show Rating Tags; a stored personal value overrides the admin Enable Rating Tags default. Rating-tag type and row exclusions also suppress review chips; see Tags. See User Reviews settings for visibility, poster controls, and the effects of copying ratings to Jellyfin.

docs.title: TMDB Reviews
docs.text: Read TMDB community reviews on movie and series detail pages. You can browse the cards alongside reviews from your own server.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced, then the Elsewhere & Reviews tab.
  2. Enter and test the shared TMDB API Key. Keep Enable Elsewhere on to edit the TMDB-review controls in the admin UI.
  3. Turn on Show TMDB Reviews, optionally turn on Expand reviews by default, and click Save Settings.
  4. Reload the client, open a movie or series with a TMDB ID, and expand Reviews ({count}). Scroll horizontally through the cards; use Read More or Read Less for long text.

Admin settings in Elsewhere & Reviews:

Setting Default What it does TMDB API Key Empty Supplies the same server-side key used for provider lookup and release dates. Show TMDB Reviews Off Displays TMDB reviews for movies and series. Expand reviews by default Off Sets the starting expansion preference, which you can override by opening or closing the section.

TMDB cards have blue borders and show the author, review date, supplied rating, and a TMDB logo that links to the original review. Text over 350 characters starts as a preview. Opening or closing the section saves your preference for future pages; opening a writing form also opens the section. There is no separate expansion toggle in the personal Enhanced panel.

With local reviews disabled, the panel has no Write a Review button.

How TMDB reviews load

Jellyfin Enhanced retrieves reviews through your Jellyfin server and caches the responses. Your browser does not call the TMDB API directly. Your expansion preference is stored in your account's settings.json.

Requests fetch the first page in en-US, and the panel shows at most ten TMDB cards. Reviews ({count}) counts fetched TMDB reviews plus visible local reviews, so the count can exceed the TMDB cards shown. Empty or failed lookups can leave Reviews (0). Seasons and episodes support local reviews only.

Loading TMDB reviews needs the key and Show TMDB Reviews, independently of Enable Elsewhere. The admin controls have the extra UI dependency described in TMDB Reviews settings.

Spoiler Guard and reviews

Spoiler Guard can hide both review sources on guarded movies, series, and child pages in the web client. See Spoiler Guard settings.

Spoiler Guard defaults and overrides

Enable Spoiler Guard is off by default; Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series is on by default. The personal Reviews override inherits the admin policy until changed. Turning it off allows reviews after Spoiler Guard state loads successfully. If state loading fails, reviews are hidden before that override is checked.

docs.title: AniList Reviews
docs.text: Read the top AniList user reviews for anime on movie and series detail pages. The cards appear in the same Reviews ({count}) section, after any TMDB reviews.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Make sure AniList is a metadata provider for your anime library (for example with the Jellyfin AniList plugin), so each item has an AniList ID.
  2. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced, then the Elsewhere & Reviews tab, turn on Show AniList Reviews, and click Save Settings.
  3. Reload the client, open an anime movie or series that has an AniList ID, and expand Reviews ({count}).
Setting Default What it does Show AniList Reviews Off Displays the top AniList user reviews for movies and series that have an AniList ID.

AniList cards have a lighter blue border and show the author, review date, the reviewer's score out of ten, the AniList logo and a link to the original review. The review summary appears in bold above the text. Text over 350 characters starts as a preview with Read More and Read Less.

Requires AniList as a metadata provider

Items are matched by their AniList ID, so this only works for items that have one. Items without an AniList ID show no AniList cards. No API key is needed.

How AniList reviews load

Jellyfin Enhanced retrieves reviews through your Jellyfin server from AniList's public API, so your browser does not call AniList directly. The server keeps results in memory for 12 hours (2 hours when an anime has no reviews) to stay well inside AniList's rate limit.

The panel shows up to ten reviews, ordered by how many AniList users found them helpful. Spoiler sections of a review are replaced with "[spoiler hidden]", and embedded images and videos are removed. Seasons and episodes support local reviews only. Reviews ({count}) includes the AniList cards.

Spoiler Guard hides AniList reviews on guarded series the same way it hides TMDB and local reviews.

docs.title: Release Dates
docs.text: See movie release dates or television air dates beside the item's other metadata. Each date chip has an icon and uses your locale's date format.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. In Elsewhere & Reviews, configure the shared TMDB API Key.
  2. Under Release Dates, turn on Show Release/Air Date and click Save Settings.
  3. Reload the client and open a movie, series, season, or episode with the required TMDB metadata. Hover over a movie chip to see Cinema Release, Digital Release, or Physical Release; television chips use Episode.

Admin settings in Elsewhere & Reviews:

Setting Default What it does Show Release/Air Date Off Adds release/air-date chips with a configured TMDB key and available dates. Default Region US Sets the preferred country for movie release dates. TMDB API Key Empty Enables TMDB-backed date lookups.

No available date means no chip. There is no personal enable switch. This feature does not require Enable Elsewhere. See Release Dates settings.

Which dates are shown Item Date selection Movie Separate cinema, digital, and physical dates. Each category prefers the admin country, then US, then the first other region containing that category. It uses the earliest date within the chosen country/category. Series Next episode's air date, falling back to the last episode's air date. Season First dated episode in TMDB response order airing today or later, falling back to the last dated episode in that response. Episode Jellyfin's episode premiere date when present, otherwise its TMDB air date.

Movies and series need their own TMDB IDs. Child pages need the parent series' TMDB ID and numbering for TMDB lookups. Even an episode using Jellyfin's premiere date needs that parent ID. Your personal Default Search Country does not change movie release-date preference.

docs.title: Integration with Seerr
docs.text: Provider logos on Jellyfin Enhanced's Seerr cards help you check subscription availability before requesting a title. These cards appear inside Jellyfin, including Seerr results in Jellyfin search.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Complete Seerr connection setup.
  2. Configure the shared TMDB API Key in Elsewhere & Reviews.
  3. Open Seerr, turn on Show Streaming Providers on Posters, and click Save Settings.
  4. Reload the client and browse JE's Seerr cards.
Setting Default What it does Show Streaming Providers on Posters Off (admin, Seerr) Shows up to four valid subscription-provider logos on JE's Seerr cards. Show Seerr Results in Search On (admin, Seerr) Enables JE's Seerr results in Jellyfin search, when the integration is configured and enabled.

Requirements

Provider logos need working Seerr cards and a TMDB key. They do not require Enable Elsewhere. See Integration with Seerr settings for all prerequisites.

Country, filters, and logos

Cards use the admin Default Region and provider filters, with title-level data. They can differ from personal or season-specific detail-page results and have no personal country-search controls.

Logos have provider-name tooltips. Failed images are removed.

docs.title: Elsewhere & Reviews Settings
docs.text: Configure providers, TMDB reviews, release dates, and local reviews in Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Elsewhere & Reviews. Settings on this page are admin settings for the server unless marked per user. For viewer workflows, see Elsewhere Integration.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Use a compatible Jellyfin web client with Jellyfin Enhanced loaded. See Compatibility to check your client.

A compatible web client is required

These panels depend on the web client's detail-page elements. Installing the server plugin does not add them to every native or third-party app.

TMDB key and internet access

Provider lookup, TMDB reviews, and release dates need a TMDB API key and outbound internet access from your Jellyfin server. Get the v3 API key from your TMDB account's API settings. Local reviews need no key, but the item still needs a TMDB identity.

How items are identified

Ordinary provider lookup finds a title through a TMDB external link in the detail section. A metadata ID alone is not enough to show this panel. Eligible season pages have a parent-series exception described under Per-season providers. Reviews and release-date chips use IDs from Jellyfin item metadata instead.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Set up the shared TMDB key first, then choose the Elsewhere features you want. The same key also serves JE's TMDB-dependent Seerr features.

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced, then Elsewhere & Reviews.
  2. Enter your TMDB API Key. Click Test beside it and read the feedback. This checks the entered key through Jellyfin, including an unsaved key; it does not save configuration.
  3. Turn on Enable Elsewhere. Enter the key first if this checkbox is disabled.
  4. Choose Default Region, such as US, GB, DE, or AU. Optionally configure Default Providers, Ignore Providers, and Custom Branding.
  5. Turn on any review or release-date features you want, then click Save Settings.
  6. Reload the client and open a supported item detail page.
Configured key versus tested key

Enable Elsewhere ships on, but providers cannot work until a key is configured. Its checkbox depends on that key requirement. The server's configured-key flag only means the key is nonempty and non-whitespace; it does not mean the key passed Test.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
Use Elsewhere (Streaming Providers) to choose what appears in automatic detail-page results. The country and provider filters also affect logos on JE's Seerr cards.

Follow Setup to apply these server settings, then use the sections below to adjust countries and filters.

Setting Default What it does Enable Elsewhere On Enables the detail-page provider panel with a configured TMDB key. TMDB API Key Empty Supplies the server-side key shared by TMDB-backed features. Default Region US Sets the automatic search country unless the viewer chooses a personal default. Empty falls back to US. Default Providers Empty Shows all subscription providers when empty; otherwise permits only exact provider names. Ignore Providers Empty Hides matching provider names after Default Providers is applied. Per-season providers On Enables automatic season lookup for default/aired-order series; users can opt out. Custom Branding Message Empty Replaces the unavailable heading when no filtered automatic providers or season groups remain. Custom Branding Icon URL Empty Adds an optional icon beside a nonempty custom message.

docs.title: Default Region
docs.text:
Choose the main country for your server's provider results.

Choose Default Region and click Save Settings. Viewers inherit it until they save Default Search Country in the provider panel's Search Settings.

Country defaults and suggestions

Seerr provider logos and movie release-date preference use the admin country. Your personal country override does not affect them.

The admin selector and personal suggestions offer country names and codes. The linked region suggestion list helps you select a country; it does not guarantee provider data in every country.

docs.title: Default Providers
docs.text:
Limit automatic results and Seerr poster logos to the services you want. Leave Default Providers blank to allow all TMDB subscription providers.

  1. Enter provider names, separated by commas or newlines. Copy names exactly, including capitalization.
  2. Click Save Settings.

For example:

Netflix,Amazon Prime Video,Disney Plus

The provider suggestion list can help you find names. Availability and names depend on the TMDB data returned.

Exact matching and list handling

Default Providers uses case-sensitive full-name equality, rather than a regular expression or a partial-name match. A list with no matching names removes every provider.

Both admin lists accept comma-separated or newline-separated entries. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, empty entries are discarded, and apostrophes are removed. A pattern containing a comma is split into multiple entries and cannot remain one pattern.

Manual searches bypass Default Providers and Ignore Providers. They use your personal Providers (leave empty to show all available) selection instead, so a manual search in the same country can show different services.

docs.title: Ignore Providers
docs.text:
Hide services from automatic results and Seerr poster logos. Ignore Providers applies after Default Providers, so an exclusion wins even if you allowed that service.

  1. Enter names or patterns in Ignore Providers, separated by commas or newlines.
  2. Click Save Settings.

For simple exclusions:

Apple TV,Google Play Movies
Pattern matching and invalid patterns

Each entry becomes a case-insensitive regular expression. Simple patterns match anywhere in a name. For full-name matches, anchor the patterns:

^Apple TV$,^Google Play Movies$

To match a literal name containing regex metacharacters such as +, ., or parentheses, escape them with a backslash. For example, \+ matches a literal plus sign. A pattern such as .*with Ads hides matching subscription-provider names; it does not filter a separate ad-supported availability category.

If any entry is an invalid regex, the entire ignore step is skipped and an error is logged in the browser console. Default Providers still applies. With Default Providers set to Netflix,Amazon Prime Video and Ignore Providers set to ^Netflix$, only Amazon Prime Video survives when both services are returned.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The provider panel shows services for your saved Default Search Country, or the admin Default Region until you set one. Automatic lookup uses the admin provider lists and, when enabled, season lookup.

docs.title: On Item Detail Pages
docs.text:
Read provider badges to see which subscription services carry a title. The badges show names and logos; they do not link to playback.

  1. Open a supported movie or series page. Find the provider panel, normally directly below external links.
  2. Look for Also available in {region} on: or Not available on any streaming services in {region}. Custom branding can replace the unavailable heading.
  3. Click an available heading to open TMDB's regional availability URL in a new tab, when supplied. Both automatic and manual-country headings use the JustWatch tooltip.
Other display states

When raw providers exist but an active Default Providers list leaves no matching automatic providers, the panel can also show No configured services available. Broken badge logos are hidden while names remain.

docs.title: Manual country searches
docs.text:
Compare subscription availability in other countries using your personal provider selection. Manual searches check the whole title, including when you start from a season page.

  1. Open the gear icon's Search Settings and choose countries and providers.
  2. Click Save, then use the panel's magnifying-glass icon. It shows Searching… while fetching.
  3. Read the available-country blocks and the combined unavailable-country block. Use their close icons to dismiss them; searching again replaces all previous manual blocks.
Which countries and providers are searched

A nonempty Search Other Countries (leave empty to use default) list replaces the fallback country list. Your default country is not automatically added. With that list empty, the search checks your effective default country only.

Personal provider selection uses case-sensitive full-name matching. Empty shows all available subscription providers. Manual results bypass both admin lists.

docs.title: Search Settings
docs.text: Use the provider panel's gear icon to choose your country and manual-search preferences. These settings belong to your Jellyfin account and are saved on the server, so they are not limited to one browser.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open Search Settings and choose Default Search Country from the dropdown. Its Reset to plugin default icon selects the current admin country.
  2. Type in the country or provider autocomplete field, then select a suggestion to add a removable chip. While suggestions are open, use Up or Down to navigate, Enter to add, and Esc to dismiss suggestions. Remove a chip with its × control.
  3. Set Show providers per season (when seasons differ) if available.
  4. Click Save to submit your selections. Cancel or a click on the backdrop closes the dialog without saving.
  5. Reload or revisit the page to update automatic results for your new country and season preference.
Save Canada, Australia, and Netflix in Search Settings, then search for matching providers.

Per-user settings:

Setting Default What it does Default Search Country Empty; inherits admin country Sets your automatic country and the manual-search fallback country. Search Other Countries (leave empty to use default) Empty list Replaces the manual-search country list when nonempty. Providers (leave empty to show all available) Empty list Selects exact provider names for manual searches only. Show providers per season (when seasons differ) On Enables your automatic season lookup; shown only when the admin permits it. Saving, resetting, and reopening the dialog

Preferences are saved in elsewhere.json. Save updates the manual-search variables and closes the dialog, but does not rebuild automatic results already on the page.

Closing without saving does not reset the dialog's unsaved controls; they can still be present when you reopen it. The country reset selects the admin country rather than clearing your saved override back to an inherited empty value.

Save failures are logged without an error shown in this dialog. If preferences do not persist after reloading, check the browser console and Jellyfin logs.

docs.title: Per-season providers
docs.text:
Show which services carry different parts of a series. A series page groups different provider sets under labels such as Seasons 1–6 and Season 7; a season page shows that season's filtered providers.

Top: series groups; bottom: the Season 3 page.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Use a default/aired-order series with a TMDB ID and numbered Jellyfin seasons visible to your account, or an eligible season page with its parent-series ID and season number.
  2. Keep the admin Per-season providers on.
  3. In the panel's Search Settings, leave Show providers per season (when seasons differ) on and click Save.
  4. Reload or revisit the series or season page.
Setting Default What it does Per-season providers On (admin) Permits automatic season lookup. Show providers per season (when seasons differ) On (per user) Lets you opt out when the admin permits season lookup. Grouping, display orders, and fallbacks

Grouping considers integer-numbered Jellyfin seasons returned for you, rather than every season TMDB knows about. If all considered seasons have the same provider set, the display stays at series level.

Admin filters run before grouping and fallback. A regular season with missing data or no matching providers falls back to the filtered series providers. In series grouping, specials (season 0) without matching providers are omitted; they do not inherit series providers. A specials detail page with no usable season result can still fall back to the title-level panel. Different raw season data can collapse to the same set after filtering.

DVD, absolute, and other alternate display orders keep title-level results because their numbers may not match TMDB's aired order. Manual searches and Seerr cards are always title-level. A season page without a TMDB external link can show the panel through its parent series only when both season settings permit lookup and the parent uses default/aired order.

docs.title: Custom Branding
docs.text: Show your own heading when no filtered automatic providers or season groups remain. The message describes the current country and filters; it does not establish that the title is exclusive to your server.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Expand Custom Branding in Elsewhere & Reviews.
  2. Enter a message and optional icon URL. Use an image viewers can access, such as an HTTPS URL or a root-relative path like /web/assets/img/icon.png.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the client.
Setting Default What it does Custom Branding Message Empty Replaces only the automatic unavailable heading. Empty keeps the standard unavailable heading. Custom Branding Icon URL Empty Adds a 24 × 24 CSS-pixel icon beside the custom message. Empty supplies no icon.

Check your touch devices

With a custom message in the unavailable automatic state, search and settings controls appear on hover. Test this state on the touch devices you use before relying on hover instructions.

Icons, headings, and hidden controls

An icon URL without a message has no effect. Failed icons are hidden. There is no default branding logo. Manual-country results retain their own availability headings.

With a custom message in the unavailable automatic state, search and settings controls initially have zero opacity. Pointer entry reveals them and pointer exit hides them; their click handlers remain.

docs.title: TMDB Reviews
docs.text: Read TMDB community reviews on movie and series pages. See TMDB Reviews for card behavior and limits.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Configure and test TMDB API Key. Keep Enable Elsewhere on to edit the review controls.
  2. Turn on Show TMDB Reviews and, optionally, Expand reviews by default.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload the client.
Setting Default What it does Show TMDB Reviews Off Enables TMDB review cards for movies and series with TMDB IDs and a configured key. Expand reviews by default Off Sets the admin default for opening the shared reviews section. A stored viewer preference overrides it.

Opening or closing Reviews ({count}) saves your expansion choice, including for local-only reviews. Opening a writing form also opens the section.

Control dependencies and loading limits

The admin UI disables both controls when Enable Elsewhere is off. It also disables expansion when Show TMDB Reviews is off. This dependency applies to the admin UI: loading TMDB reviews does not require Enable Elsewhere. Local reviews are independent of both toggles.

Your expansion choice is stored in settings.json. TMDB requests use en-US, page 1, and show at most ten TMDB cards. The count includes all fetched TMDB reviews plus visible local reviews and can exceed the cards shown. Failed or empty lookups can leave Reviews (0).

docs.title: AniList Reviews
docs.text: Show the top AniList user reviews for anime on movie and series pages. See AniList Reviews for card behavior and limits.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Make sure AniList is a metadata provider for your anime library, so items have an AniList ID.
  2. Turn on Show AniList Reviews, click Save Settings, and reload the client.
Setting Default What it does Show AniList Reviews Off Enables AniList review cards for movies and series that have an AniList ID. Dependencies and privacy

This needs no API key and is independent of Enable Elsewhere, the TMDB key and Show TMDB Reviews. Items without an AniList ID show no AniList cards.

Your Jellyfin server sends the item's AniList ID to AniList's public GraphQL API (graphql.anilist.co) and caches the response in memory. No user information is sent.

docs.title: User Reviews
docs.text: Let viewers share text reviews and/or star ratings on your server. Local reviews need no TMDB API key or enabled provider panel.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Turn on Enable User Written Reviews in Elsewhere & Reviews, click Save Settings, and reload the client.
  2. On an eligible detail page, expand Reviews ({count}) and click Write a Review if you have no review for that item, or Edit on your existing review.

See User Reviews for writing, editing, deletion, character limits, and the picker limitation.

Setting Default What it does Enable User Written Reviews Off Enables local review UI independently of provider lookup and TMDB reviews. Hide reviews from hidden users On Hides reviews by hidden Jellyfin authors from other non-admin viewers. Hide reviews from disabled users On Hides reviews by disabled Jellyfin authors from other non-admin viewers. Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating Off Copies movie/series review stars to the author's Jellyfin rating at twice the star value. Show average user rating on poster cards Off Adds visible local-review averages to eligible posters when rating tags are enabled. Show "—" on posters for unrated items On Uses a dash when no visible rated-review average exists and poster averages are enabled.

Item requirements

Movies and series need TMDB IDs. Seasons and episodes need the parent-series TMDB ID and the relevant numbering.

Admin control dependency

The admin UI disables the five subordinate local-review controls when Enable User Written Reviews is off.

docs.title: Author visibility and moderation
docs.text:
Choose whose reviews other viewers can see, and remove reviews when needed. Local reviews are shared server data, rather than private personal notes.

  1. Use Hide reviews from hidden users and Hide reviews from disabled users to set author visibility.
  2. Authors can Edit or Delete their own cards. Admins can use Delete as admin on other authors' cards, with confirmation and failure feedback. The web UI does not let admins edit another author's review.
Visibility rules and deleted accounts

The two author-hide settings filter reviews for other non-admin viewers. They use Jellyfin account policies for hidden/disabled users, rather than your Hidden Content list. Existing authors always see their own reviews, and admins bypass author filtering.

Reviews whose authors were deleted are hidden from non-admins while either filter is enabled. With both filters off, those reviews are visible. These rules also govern review averages. Hiding an author leaves the review stored. Deleting a Jellyfin account does not erase its stored reviews.

Account updates, deletion, and lockout invalidate cached authors for subsequent requests.

docs.title: Averages and poster controls
docs.text:
Detail pages show the average of visible rated local reviews out of ten. For example, 3- and 4-star reviews average to 7; text-only reviews do not contribute.

  1. Keep Enable User Written Reviews on and turn on Show average user rating on poster cards.
  2. Enable rating tags: use the admin Enable Rating Tags in Display, or your personal Show Rating Tags preference.
  3. Choose whether Show "—" on posters for unrated items should show a dash when no visible rated-review average exists.

See Tags for rating-tag placement and supported card contexts.

Rating-tag defaults and the dash

Poster averages require local reviews, poster averages, and effective rating tags to be enabled. The admin Enable Rating Tags defaults off. A stored per-user Show Rating Tags value overrides that default, including a saved off value.

The dash means there is no visible rated-review average. It does not mean the current viewer has not rated the item.

docs.title: Jellyfin rating mirroring
docs.text:
Copy movie and series review stars to the author's Jellyfin rating. The Jellyfin value is twice the star value; seasons and episodes are excluded.

To use this, turn on Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating. Saving movie/series stars then copies the rating.

Existing Jellyfin ratings are overwritten

Saving review stars with this setting on replaces a Jellyfin rating set elsewhere.

Removing stars, deleting reviews, and failures

Removing stars or deleting the review clears the Jellyfin rating only while mirroring is enabled and the current rating still matches the previous review stars ×2. A value changed elsewhere is preserved.

A mirroring failure is logged and does not undo the review save or deletion.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard
docs.text:
Hide both local and TMDB review panels on guarded items in the web client. This includes guarded movies and a guarded series' child pages.

  1. Use the admin Enable Spoiler Guard and Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series settings in Display.
  2. Set your personal Reviews preference in Spoiler Guard to override the admin policy, or leave it unset to inherit that policy.
Setting Default What it does Enable Spoiler Guard Off (admin, Display) Enables Spoiler Guard, including its review-suppression checks. Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series On (admin, Display) Permits suppression of local and TMDB review panels for guarded items. Reviews Unset; inherits admin policy (per user) Controls personal review hiding in Spoiler Guard preferences. Off allows reviews once state loads successfully.

See Spoiler Guard settings.

State-loading failures and API access

If Spoiler Guard state fails to load, reviews are hidden before your personal override is checked. Hiding the panel is a web-client behavior; it does not make local reviews inaccessible through the review API.

docs.title: Release Dates
docs.text: Show movie release dates and television air dates beside detail-page metadata. See Release Dates for how each item's date is chosen.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Configure the shared TMDB API Key.
  2. Turn on Show Release/Air Date under Release Dates, then click Save Settings.
  3. Reload the client and open an identifiable movie, series, season, or episode.
Setting Default What it does Show Release/Air Date Off Enables release/air-date chips with a configured key and resolvable date data. Default Region US Sets movie release-date country preference, followed by US and then other available regions.

Dates use your locale's format and preserve the calendar day. Missing dates leave out the chip. This feature does not require Enable Elsewhere.

Country preference and child items

Your personal Default Search Country does not affect movie release dates. Child pages need a parent-series TMDB ID, even when an episode uses its Jellyfin premiere date.

docs.title: Integration with Seerr
docs.text: Show subscription-provider logos on JE's Seerr cards inside Jellyfin, including Seerr results in Jellyfin search. This setting does not configure the external Seerr website.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Complete Seerr connection setup.
  2. Configure the shared TMDB API Key in Elsewhere & Reviews.
  3. Open Seerr, turn on Show Streaming Providers on Posters, and click Save Settings.
  4. Reload the client and browse JE's Seerr cards. For Jellyfin search cards, keep Show Seerr Results in Search on.

Admin settings in Seerr, except the TMDB key:

Setting Default What it does Enable Seerr integration Off Enables JE's Seerr features. Seerr URL(s) (One per line) Empty Supplies the Seerr instance addresses used by JE. Seerr API Key Empty Authenticates JE's requests to Seerr. TMDB API Key Empty (Elsewhere & Reviews) Enables server-side watch-provider lookups. Show Streaming Providers on Posters Off Adds at most four valid subscription-provider logos to JE's Seerr cards. Show Seerr Results in Search On Enables JE's Seerr results in Jellyfin search when connection and access requirements are met. Country, filters, and logos

Cards use the admin Default Region, Default Providers, and Ignore Providers, with title-level availability. They can differ from personal or season-specific item-page results. These cards have no personal country-search/settings panel.

Logos have provider-name tooltips; failed logos are removed. The logo setting does not require Enable Elsewhere.

docs.title: Privacy & Data
docs.text:
TMDB lookups send the queried title identifiers and your server's API key to TMDB over HTTPS. User-written reviews stay in Jellyfin's local storage and are not posted to TMDB.

The plugin does not upload your full library inventory or viewing history to TMDB. Individual TMDB IDs identify the titles being looked up. Encryption between your browser and Jellyfin depends on your deployment's HTTPS configuration.

Request handling and external images

Jellyfin handles TMDB API requests through authenticated JE routes. Watch-provider responses contain all available regions. Ordinary detail requests select the country in the browser; Seerr batches send the country to Jellyfin for server-side extraction. The selected country is not added to ordinary upstream watch-provider requests.

Browsers load provider logos from image.tmdb.org and custom branding images from the host in the configured URL. Country/provider suggestions use JE's local CDN route, backed by jsDelivr, with hardcoded fallbacks if loading fails. Clicking an external availability heading opens the URL supplied by TMDB.

docs.title: Cache freshness and storage
docs.text:
Cached results can take time to reflect changes on TMDB. Reloading clears results temporarily saved in your browser, but your Jellyfin server may still return its saved results.

Cache lifetimes and requests

Title-level provider and TMDB-review requests use a shared 30-minute client cache. Successful JSON server lookup responses have a six-hour lifetime; JSON 404 responses are cached for ten minutes. Non-JSON responses and HTTP 401, 429, and 5xx outcomes are not stored in that server response cache.

Concurrent identical lookups share upstream work. Eligible title requests without cached data can bundle providers, reviews, and other title data. Each upstream attempt has a 30-second timeout budget; that does not guarantee a 30-second limit for the entire browser operation.

Season-provider and TMDB season-number promises stay cached for the lifetime of the initialized Elsewhere script, across detail-page navigation, without time-based expiry. Failed entries are removed. Release-date results have a separate one-hour client cache.

Stored files and backups

JE stores these files under <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/:

File Contents <userId>/elsewhere.json Personal country, manual-search countries/providers, and season preference. <userId>/settings.json Personal Enhanced settings, including review expansion. reviews.json Shared local reviews; back this up separately from per-user preferences. tmdb-cache.json Persistent shared TMDB response cache; not the local-review store.

User-directory IDs are normalized lowercase GUIDs without dashes. See Settings Overview for the broader settings and backup reference.

docs.title: API access
docs.text:
You can use authenticated JE routes to access provider data, preferences, and reviews. See the API reference for integration examples.

Provider, settings, and review routes

All routes below use the /JellyfinEnhanced prefix and require authentication. Admin-only actions check administrator status in their handlers.

Method and route Access and limits GET tmdb/{**apiPath} Authenticated TMDB proxy; missing configured key returns 503. Parental restrictions can refuse lookups. GET tmdb/validate?apiKey=… Admin-only test of the supplied key, including an unsaved key. GET watch-providers?items=movie:603,tv:1399&region=US At most 100 distinct valid titles; items at most 2,048 characters. IDs are positive, one to nine digits. An explicit nonempty region must be two uppercase letters. Omitted/empty uses normalized admin country, falling back to US if invalid. GET user-settings/{userId}/elsewhere.json Own preferences, or another user's preferences for an admin. POST user-settings/{userId}/elsewhere.json Same access rules; saves personal preferences. GET reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Returns reviews visible to the authenticated viewer. POST reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Creates or updates the caller's review. DELETE reviews/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Deletes the caller's review. GET reviews/ratings?keys=… Averages and counts of visible rated reviews; at most 200 distinct valid keys. GET reviews/admin/all Admin list/export; supports since, userId, limit, and offset. Limit defaults to 500, accepts 1–1,000; offset defaults to 0 and must be nonnegative. POST reviews/admin/{userIdN}/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Admin upsert on another author's behalf. DELETE reviews/admin/{userIdN}/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Admin moderation deletion.

Review media types are movie and tv. Season keys use <seriesTmdbId>:s<n>; episode keys use <seriesTmdbId>:s<n>:e<n>. Reviews are keyed by author, media type, and item key. POST accepts content and/or rating, with the same 2,000-character and 1–5 half-star limits as the UI.

Provider batches return a region and a results map. An empty array means no usable regional subscription entries after server extraction, which also validates names and logo paths. null can mean a blocked/failed lookup or an unusable response. Parental restrictions apply to TMDB proxy and provider-batch requests. A missing TMDB key returns 503 for provider batches too.

The review-ratings response maps keys to {average, count} or null when no visible rated review exists; its API average is on the five-star scale. Enable User Written Reviews governs the client UI, not authorization or availability of the review endpoints. Show average user rating on poster cards governs poster inclusion, not access to the direct ratings endpoint.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If the whole client enhancement is absent, start with installation troubleshooting. Elsewhere's panels are added to the web client.

docs.title: Elsewhere Not Showing
docs.text:
Check the key and the item's TMDB link first. The server also needs a working connection to TMDB.

  1. Check Enable Elsewhere, test TMDB API Key, click Save Settings, and reload.
  2. Confirm the detail section has a matching TMDB movie/TV external link. A metadata ID alone is not enough.
  3. For a season without that link, check the parent TMDB ID, aired/default order, season number, and both season settings.
  4. Check DNS, internet connectivity, and firewall rules on the server or inside its container. TMDB API access starts from Jellyfin.
  5. Check parental restrictions, the browser console, and Jellyfin logs.
Client layouts and device VPNs

A web-client layout without the expected detail elements can prevent the panel from appearing. A VPN applied only to your viewing device does not change the server's outbound connection.

docs.title: No Providers Showing
docs.text:
Check the country and filters before assuming a title has no subscription providers. TMDB data can also be incomplete or outdated, and cached results can delay changes.

  1. Check your effective default country and both admin lists. Default Providers can remove everything through unmatched names or capitalization; Ignore Providers can exclude all matches.
  2. Try a manual search with an empty personal provider list to compare unfiltered subscription data in another country.
  3. If names show without logos, check browser access to image.tmdb.org. For a missing branding icon, check the configured image host.
Subscription categories

No matching subscription (flatrate) providers does not mean the title is unavailable to rent, buy, or watch through another category.

docs.title: Provider errors
docs.text:
Use the message shown in the panel to choose your next check.

Message What to check Invalid TMDB API Key. Re-enter the v3 key and use Test before saving. The requested item could not be found on TMDB. Verify the item's TMDB identity and metadata match. Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again. Allow the rate limit to recover before retrying. The TMDB service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later. Check Jellyfin logs and server/container connectivity; retry after the temporary failure. Received an unexpected response from the server. Check your reverse proxy or Jellyfin configuration. Inspect reverse-proxy/middleware responses for a non-JSON error page. TMDB API is unreachable. Check the browser-to-Jellyfin request as well as the server's outbound TMDB connection. Missing keys and other errors

The missing-key proxy response is 503, so the temporary-service message can also mean no key is configured. Other errors can show their underlying HTTP message, including parental-policy refusals.

Review retrieval failures are logged and can appear as an empty review section rather than a provider error.

docs.title: Reviews or dates missing
docs.text:
Check the feature's own setting and the item's metadata. Local reviews need no key; TMDB reviews and dates do.

  1. Check the relevant feature toggle and TMDB API Key for TMDB reviews or dates. For local reviews, check Enable User Written Reviews.
  2. Verify item IDs and child numbering. If the review panel is absent, check Spoiler Guard.
  3. Check author filtering, which can reduce reviews and averages. Poster average chips also need rating tags enabled; check Show Rating Tags and see Averages and poster controls for the admin default and your personal override.
  4. If a preference change has not appeared, reload or revisit after Search Settings → Save.

Missing release data simply leaves out date chips.

Preferences that do not persist

If changes do not persist, inspect the logged save failure. The search dialog does not display that error.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Availability depends on TMDB's data quality, country coverage, and update timing. Displays use subscription-provider data only, and your filters can narrow it further.

Availability is informational

Logos and headings do not verify your subscriptions or start playback. TMDB lookups and external images require internet access. Local reviews remain local, and cached results can lag behind upstream changes.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
Check the FAQ, installation troubleshooting, and your browser/Jellyfin logs. For an unresolved issue, use the issue-reporting guide or GitHub issues.

Include the client, item type, country, and relevant settings. Redact API keys.

docs.title: Enhanced Features
docs.text:
Use Jellyfin Enhanced's shortcuts, browsing tools, and player controls to make Jellyfin fit the way you watch. You can also catch up on unwatched titles, see server activity, and add information to detail pages.

Client requirements

These controls need a client running JE's injected web scripts. Server-side hidden-content filtering can also affect supported list responses in native clients. See Compatibility.

Open your personal settings:

  1. Press ? outside a text field to open the Enhanced panel. You can also choose Enhanced Panel under the Jellyfin Enhanced drawer heading, Jellyfin Enhanced in Jellyfin 12's avatar menu, or Jellyfin Enhanced - User Settings in user preferences. During playback in mobile or TV web layouts, use the tune button titled Jellyfin Enhanced when the player controls are available. Desktop layouts hide this button.
  2. Use Search settings… or select the section named in the feature below. On phones, use the back arrow to return to the section list.
  3. Close with ×, Esc, or ?.

Open admin settings: Go to Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced. Tables below show stock defaults for a new installation.

Personal defaults and saving changes

Where an admin setting supplies a personal default, existing users keep their saved choices. Personal settings and shortcut overrides save automatically on the server for each account. Reload another open client to load changes.

See Enhanced Settings and Settings Overview for the default/override workflow, including Overview → Quick Actions → Overwrite everyone's personal settings.

Choose where JE pages appear

Choose either a native Home tab or Custom Tabs; Plugin Pages can coexist with either. Native tabs need no companion plugin and are recommended for Jellyfin 12's experimental layout. Plugin Pages and Custom Tabs require their respective plugins.
