Under More Settings, these admin values supply starting values for the matching personal Hidden Content controls. Saving new defaults leaves existing personal copies intact.

Setting Default What it does Hidden Content enabled by default On Sets Enable Content Hiding. Show "Hide" buttons by default On Sets Show Hide Buttons. Show confirmation dialog before hiding On Sets Show Confirmation Dialog. Show "Hide" button on Seerr search results On Sets Show on Seerr Items. Show "Hide" button on item details pages On Sets Show on Detail Pages. Show "Hide" button on library / home cards Off Sets Show in Library Views. Show "Hide" button on cast / actor cards Off Sets Show on Cast/Actors. Filter Library & details pages On Sets Filter Library. Filter Search results Off Sets Filter Search. Filter Continue Watching On Sets Filter Continue Watching. Filter Next Up On Sets Filter Next Up. Filter Upcoming episodes On Sets Filter Upcoming. Filter Suggestions / recommendations On Sets Filter Recommendations. Filter Discovery On Sets Filter Discovery. Filter Calendar On Sets Filter Calendar. Filter Requests page On Sets Filter Requests. Allow hiding collections, libraries, and playlists (experimental) Off Sets Hide Collections & Libraries. Experimental container hiding can disrupt browsing. Details

The server master defaults to Off even though personal hiding defaults to On. The personal controls and browsing limits are separate from the row-removal preference in Display → UI Preferences.

docs.title: Activity Feed
docs.text:
Activity shows watching history, favorites, and reviews, with an optional live-stream section. You can open titles or artwork to view their details.

  1. Enable the feature under Pages → Activity Feed and configure an entry point.
  2. Open Activity and browse Active Streams, Watch History, and Reviews. Favorites share Reviews.
  3. Use Refresh to reload stored activity. Partial watches show progress; completed watches use completion wording.

All settings below are admin server settings, with no personal-panel counterparts.

The disabled Use Plugin Pages and Use Custom Tabs controls require their companion plugins.

Setting Default What it does Enable Activity Feed Off Enables the feed and its watched/favorite collection. Turning it off retains saved activity. Show recently watched On Collects and shows qualifying stopped or completed playback. Show recently favorited On Collects and shows favorites. Unfavoriting removes the saved entry. Show recently reviewed On Includes reviews from the current User Reviews store. Non-admins only see their own activity Off Regular users only see their own watched, favorited and reviewed entries; administrators still see everyone. Show Active Streams section On Adds live sessions when the separate Active Streams feature and viewer permissions allow them. Add Activity as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Activity Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Exposes Activity through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off Enables the Activity Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save.

For the live section, also configure these admin server settings under Extras → UI Tweaks:

Setting Default What it does Active Streams Header Widget Off Enables the header widget and live-session data used by the feed. Show widget to non-admins Off Permits authenticated non-admins to read live sessions.

Stored watched/favorite/review entries respect viewer library access. Active Streams has separate access rules and can show sessions for items outside a viewer's library access. See Other settings for the widget's full behavior.

How it works

Show recently watched collects playback stopped at a position of at least 5% of known runtime, plus playback Jellyfin reports completed. The 5% threshold measures stopped playback position, not time spent watching.

The usual request returns up to 50 merged entries with no UI pagination. Watched/favorite storage in activity.json is capped at 500 entries. Rewatches update the timestamp while retaining maximum progress and completion.

Elsewhere & Reviews → User Reviews → Hide reviews from hidden users and Hide reviews from disabled users both default to On. They also filter activity authors, with admin/self exceptions. User Reviews runs independently. Disabling Activity Feed stops watched/favorite collection, but reviews written while it is off can appear when the feed returns. See Elsewhere & Reviews Settings for those shared review controls.

Active Streams Header Widget enables the Active Streams data endpoint as well as the header widget. The feed's live section refreshes every 15 seconds while the document is visible. Stored history does not use that polling. The header widget refreshes on initialization, opening, and manual refresh.

docs.title: Catch Up
docs.text:
Catch Up gives you swipeable cards for unwatched movies and shows. Use them to mark items watched, dismiss them, add them to your watchlist, or open their details.

  1. Enable the feature under Pages → Catch Up and configure an entry point.
  2. Open Catch Up and choose Movies or Shows.
  3. Swipe right to mark watched, left to dismiss, up to add to the watchlist, or down to open details. Buttons and arrow keys provide the same actions.
  4. Press Backspace to rewind when an undo is available.

All settings below are admin server settings.

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up Off Enables decks of unwatched items accessible to each user. Add Catch Up as a native Home tab Off Adds the built-in Catch Up Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Exposes Catch Up through Plugin Pages. Use Custom Tabs Off Enables the Catch Up Custom Tabs embed. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching managed Custom Tabs entry on save. Record Catch Up activity On Saves reported actions for administrators while Catch Up is enabled. Turning it off stops new records; existing history remains readable.

Dismissals stay in this browser for your account, separate from server-synced Hidden Content. Reloading keeps them. Clear their browser storage or use an available rewind to reverse them.

Administrators can open Activity to view Feed or Summary, even with recording disabled. Use All users, Search titles, and action chips to filter Feed; those filters do not affect Summary. Refresh reloads the selected view and Hide closes it.

See Enhanced features for the full gesture workflow and API reference for event routes.

How it works

The watchlist uses Jellyfin's Likes flag. Decks sample random batches of 40 items, excluding dismissed, already-seen, and imageless cards. They do not sort newest first. Nothing more to show here. can mean a batch produced no eligible new cards.

A show's season picker appears only with at least two regular seasons; specials are excluded. Shows with fewer regular seasons are marked watched directly.

The selected deck mode is remembered locally for the browser. Switching decks or restarting resets the queue, seen set, and undo history.

The open admin activity panel refreshes every ten seconds and docks at widths of at least 1100 pixels. Narrower screens use a dialog.

Logs contain open, undo, and failed actions as well as swipes. They are client-reported actions, not proof of viewing. Feed requests up to 300 matching events. Summary counts distinct surviving user/title actions not marked failed, removes recorded undos, and lists up to 15 top titles per action.

The server retains catchup-log.jsonl and catchup-log.1.jsonl in the plugin configuration folder. It rotates before the next append once the live file exceeds 5 MiB.

docs.title: Tags: Quality, Genre, Language, Rating, Age Rating, People
docs.text: All tag settings have moved to Tags & Badges: personal UI Settings controls, admin Display → Media Tags defaults, quality categories/order, language preferences, rating scopes, people/review badges, hover behavior, and Tag Styles.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: For personal tag choices, open UI Settings. Administrators use Display → Media Tags. See Tags & Badges for exact labels, defaults, and configuration instructions.

docs.title: Server-Side Tag Cache
docs.text: Server cache settings, library exclusions, browser fallback persistence, Clear All Client Caches, and Admin → Tag Cache → Rebuild Server Tag Cache are covered in Tags & Badges.

docs.title: Audio Language Tags
docs.text: The controls under Display → Audio Language Tags and the Sync Audio Language Tags to Jellyfin task are covered in Tags & Badges.

docs.title: Native Poster Tags (Experimental)
docs.text: Admin Display → Media Tags controls and personal Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) are covered in Tags & Badges, including eligible clients, exclusions, and refresh requirements.

docs.title: Settings in other areas
docs.text:
Use these references for settings owned by other feature areas:

  • Seerr and Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page: Seerr settings.
  • *arr, Pages → Calendar Page, and the download parts of Pages → Requests Page: *arr settings. Request controls are also covered in Seerr settings.
  • Elsewhere, TMDB Reviews, Release Dates, and User Reviews: Elsewhere & Reviews Settings. Written reviews have no separate personal review-tag switch.
  • Display → Spoiler Guard: Spoiler Guard settings.
  • Display → Awards / MDBList Ratings, other Extras options, and Admin maintenance, analytics, developer, and cache controls: Other settings.

docs.title: Documentation in the dashboard
docs.text:
Read the hosted documentation from the dashboard's Docs tab. This tab has no enable switch.

Open Docs to load Documentation from the GitHub Pages site, or choose Open in new tab.

Details

The tab needs connectivity from your browser; it is not an offline copy bundled with the plugin. It loads the document when first opened and retains it when you switch tabs.

If no iframe load event arrives within eight seconds, a fallback message and link replace it. Open in new tab is always an alternative.

docs.title: Tags & Badges
docs.text:
See quality, genres, audio languages, scores, and age classifications while browsing your library. You can choose which badges appear, move them between corners, and change their colors. People Tags add age and birthplace information to cast cards.

The optional tag groups are enabled for this example; all six groups start off.

docs.title: Set up your tags
docs.text:
You can choose tags for your own account. If you administer the server, you can also set the starting values for users.

How to use — personal preferences:

  1. Open the Jellyfin Enhanced panel from the user profile menu on Jellyfin 12 or the sidebar on 10.11. You can also press ?.
  2. Select UI Settings and choose your tags. Changes save automatically to your Jellyfin account on the server.
  3. Refresh another open client to load changes you made elsewhere.

How to use — admin defaults:

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Display → Media Tags.
  2. Choose your settings and click Save Settings.
  3. Refresh affected web clients to load the changes.

Tables below show factory defaults. Rows marked “Admin / personal” give both exact labels for the same preference. Most admin defaults become the starting values for new personal settings. Saved personal values take precedence, so changing a server default does not overwrite a user's choice.

Hover hiding starts off

Hide Tags on Hover follows the admin value for new users, and overwriting personal settings applies it too.

Replacing everyone's preferences

Overview → Quick Actions → Overwrite everyone's personal settings replaces saved personal preferences with the current admin values. It also replaces other Enhanced display/playback preferences, so each user would need to reapply their customizations. Read Settings Overview before using it.

docs.title: Where tags appear
docs.text:
You'll see poster badges in library grids, home rows, Jellyfin search results, and supported rows on detail pages. People Tags appear on cast cards instead.

Feature What you see Where it appears Quality Tags Resolution, source, HDR, special format, video codec, sound Supported library cards; series/season quality describes a representative episode Genre Tags Up to three genre icons, with names on hover Supported library cards with genre metadata Language Tags Up to three distinct flags or a no-dialogue symbol Supported library cards; cached series/season flags cover their episodes, collection flags cover linked movies Rating Tags Community star score and critic percentage Supported library cards, subject to item-type and row scopes User-review chips Average visible review rating, or an optional dash Movie, series, season, and episode cards with a usable review identity Age Rating Tags Official parental/content classification Supported library cards with classification metadata People Tags Age, age at release, birthplace, deceased styling Cast and guest-cast cards on web item detail pages Audio language links Named audio languages linking to Jellyfin tag lists Movie, series, season, and episode detail pages Player badges Scores in the controls; optional age/advisory badge at playback start Jellyfin web video player

Native Poster Tags draw supported poster groups into images for eligible native clients. Their page and row limits differ from web overlays.

Tags need metadata

Each badge needs suitable metadata. A supported card does not guarantee every tag will appear.

Supported cards and locations

Web poster overlays apply to supported movie, series, season, episode, collection (BoxSet), and video cards, including videos in Home Videos/Photos libraries. Detail-page rows include season/episode cards and the series Next Up shelf. Large episode list images can also carry overlays.

The web overlays skip the large artwork in the detail page's information area, cast cards, chapter/scene cards, My Media, modal dialogs, small list images, and plugin/catalog/device/library administration cards. Seerr search and discovery cards do not receive these library tags.

docs.title: Positions and shared controls
docs.text:
You can place each poster group in a corner and hide badges on hover to make card buttons easier to see.

How to use:

  1. In UI Settings, click the small four-corner selector beside a group's toggle. Administrators use Position for each poster group.
  2. Choose Top Left, Top Right, Bottom Left, or Bottom Right.

Setting Default What it does Position — Quality Tags Top Left Admin default and personal corner choice for quality badges Position — Genre Tags Top Right Admin default and personal corner choice for genre icons Position — Language Tags Bottom Left Admin default and personal corner choice for flags Position — Rating Tags Bottom Right Admin default and personal corner choice for score and review chips Position — Age Rating Tags Bottom Right Admin default and personal corner choice for classification badges Admin / personal: Hide Tags on Hover Off Fades web poster overlays when you hover over a card, making its buttons easier to see; new and overwritten personal settings take the admin value Admin: Disable Tags on Search Page Off Suppresses the poster overlays on Jellyfin web search results, including age-rating and review chips; useful for compatibility with Gelato

Groups sharing a corner stack with a small gap rather than overlap. Top-right groups move below Jellyfin's watched or unplayed-count indicator. People Tags have their own cast-card layout and no corner selector.

With Hide Tags on Hover off, genre names expand beside their icons on hover. Turn it on to fade poster tags instead.

Genre names expand with Hide Tags on Hover off; turning it on fades the tags instead.

docs.title: Quality Tags
docs.text:
Quality badges help you identify a file's picture and sound format before opening it. They read Jellyfin's media metadata and naming signals.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Show Quality Tags in UI Settings.
  2. Expand Choose what to show and select categories.
  3. Use Move up / Move down to change their stacking order.

Administrators configure the same defaults under Categories and sound language in Media Tags.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Quality Tags / personal: Show Quality Tags Off Enables the quality group Admin: Show resolution (4K, 1080p, ...) / personal: Resolution (4K, 1080p, ...) On; first Shows resolution from the first video stream Admin: Show source (BluRay, DVD, HDTV, VHS, ...) / personal: Source (BluRay, DVD, HDTV, ...) On; second Shows the source of a physical-media stub Admin: Show HDR (HDR10+, Dolby Vision) / personal: HDR (HDR10+, Dolby Vision) On; third Shows detected dynamic-range labels Admin: Show special format (IMAX, 3D) / personal: Special format (IMAX, 3D) On; fourth Shows detected IMAX/3D labels Admin: Show video format (HEVC, H264, AV1, ...) / personal: Video format (HEVC, H264, AV1, ...) On; fifth Shows video codec labels Admin: Show sound (Atmos, DTS, 5.1, 7.1, ...) / personal: Sound (Atmos, DTS, 5.1, 7.1, ...) On; sixth Shows recognized audio format/channel information Admin: Preferred Audio Language for Sound Tags No preference (best track overall) Chooses a fixed language whose audio tracks determine the sound tag Admin: Use Each User's Jellyfin Audio Language Off Uses each user's Jellyfin preferred audio language; users without one retain the fixed admin language Personal: Preferred audio language for the sound tag Server default Inherits server policy, uses My Jellyfin audio language, selects No preference (best track overall), or chooses a specific language Badge examples Category Examples the detector can produce Resolution 8K, 4K, 1440p, 1080p, 720p, 576p, 480p, LOW-RES Source BluRay, HD DVD, DVD, VHS, HDTV, Physical Dynamic range Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HDR Special format IMAX, 3D Video codec AV1, HEVC, H265, VP9, H264, VP8, XVID, DIVX, WMV, MPEG2, MPEG4, MJPEG, THEORA Sound ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS, Dolby Digital+, 7.1, 5.1; codec labels can include channels, such as ATMOS 7.1

docs.title: Detection limits
docs.text:
Series and season quality describes one representative episode, not every episode or media version. Missing streams or naming information can leave categories empty. Collections have no streams of their own and normally have no quality badges.

Detection and sound-language details

Resolution: JE first checks recognized video display-title hints, then dimensions. It rejects a misleading 4K/2160p hint when the known height is below 1250 pixels.

Dimension fallback recognizes 8K at height ≥3000 or width ≥7000, and 4K at height ≥1550 or width ≥3500. A 3840×1600 ultrawide file can therefore show 4K. PAL-sized video can show 576p. Sorting and styling support SD, but the current web resolution detector does not produce it.

Source and special format: Source badges require a .disc media stub and select one source. An ordinary download's release name alone does not identify it as BluRay.

IMAX detection uses title/name/path signals and excludes NON-IMAX. 3D requires a path containing 3d and a recognized format signal such as hsbs, fsbs, htab, ftab, or mvc.

Sound: JE takes the first recognized candidate display title, then checks technical metadata if no title matched. It detects channels separately. It does not rank every track by richness, despite the No preference (best track overall) option wording. Standalone channel fallback produces 5.1 or 7.1; 2.0 can be appended to a recognized codec.

A sound-language preference tries language plus region, then the base language, then all tracks if no match exists. For example, selecting a German AC3 5.1 dub can replace an English Atmos badge with 5.1; the detector does not emit AC3 as a codec label. These choices change the badge, not the audio selected for playback.

docs.title: Genre Tags
docs.text:
Genre Tags show up to three genres as compact Material Design icons, so you can recognize them while browsing. You can hover to see names beside the icons.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Show Genre Tags in UI Settings and choose a corner.
  2. Leave Hide Tags on Hover off to see expanded names.
Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Genre Tags / personal: Show Genre Tags Off Shows up to three genre icons on supported cards Genre sources and hover behavior

Genres come from Jellyfin metadata. Unfamiliar names use a generic icon.

With Server-Side Tag Cache on, series and season cards keep their own genres when present and use episode or parent-series genres only when their own are missing. In batch fallback, season cards prefer the parent series' genres whenever available, even if the season has its own. Series cards without genres use the first episode.

With Hide Tags on Hover on, hover-name spans are omitted and the overlays fade out instead. There is no genre-name expansion in a static native poster image.

docs.title: Language Tags
docs.text:
Language Tags show available audio as flags, helping you find a dub while browsing. Audio with no linguistic content uses a crossed-out speech-bubble symbol labeled No dialogue.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Show Language Tags in UI Settings.
  2. For readable language names, enable Show Audio Languages and use the detail-page audio-language row.

Administrators can favor particular languages under Priority languages.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Language Tags / personal: Show Language Tags Off Shows up to three distinct flags/symbols on supported cards Admin: Priority Languages Empty Comma-separated language names or codes; use names such as English, Japanese to avoid differences between two- and three-letter codes. Matching flags appear first in list order Admin: Only Show Priority Languages Off With a nonempty priority list, removes flags that do not match; an item can show fewer than three or none Admin: Merge Regional Variants Off Regional and script variants such as en-GB, pt-BR or zh-Hant share their base language's flag, so tracks Jellyfin lists as one language show one flag

docs.title: Grouping, regions, and partial dubs
docs.text:
With Server-Side Tag Cache enabled, series and season cards show audio languages across their episodes. A dub missing from some episodes has a dimmed flag with a dashed outline and “not on all episodes” in its title/alt text.

Flag grouping, coverage, and regions

Flags come through Jellyfin Enhanced's asset service. Tracks marked zxx (no linguistic content) use the No dialogue symbol.

Languages sharing a flag are grouped before the three-flag limit. Their names are stored in the flag's title/alt text. Poster flags do not show hover tooltips.

Priority filtering also operates on grouped flags: a matching flag can represent additional languages sharing it. An empty priority list leaves flags unchanged even with strict filtering on. Language priorities are server policy, with no personal priority-list setting.

Priority matching uses the flag's language code, its base code, or its displayed language names. It does not equate two- and three-letter codes: ja does not match jpn, but Japanese matches the displayed name.

The cached flags use the union of audio languages across episodes. Full-coverage flags normally come first, but administrator priorities can put a partial flag ahead of them. A grouped flag is partial only when all its represented languages are partial.

Specials do not count against a series' full-coverage languages. Tracks with no usable language tag are ignored. Equivalent tags such as eng/en or fre/fr-FR can count as the same dub. Regional variants that coexist in one episode, such as es-419 and es-ES, are assessed separately.

In batch fallback mode, series/season poster flags reflect a representative episode and do not show partial coverage.

Cached collection flags combine languages from linked movie members. A collection containing an English movie and a Japanese movie can therefore show both flags; it does not mean every member has both languages.

Regional flags require explicit regional metadata. For example, pt-BR shows Brazil, pt/pt-PT show Portugal, es-419/es-MX show Mexico, and zh-Hant shows Taiwan. A base language such as pt, es, or zh keeps its default flag; JE does not guess a region.

Tagging matters

Region detection depends on the language metadata in the media file. Poster Language Tags and the detail-page audio-language row have separate switches; enabling one does not enable the other.

docs.title: Audio language links
docs.text:
The detail-page audio-language row shows language names and flags. You can also sync languages to Jellyfin metadata tags, so clicking a matching language opens a list of items with that tag.

How to use:

  1. Keep Show Audio Languages on in UI Settings to display the row.
  2. As an administrator, open Display → Audio Language Tags and turn on Enable Audio Language Tags Sync and Link audio languages to their tag page. Click Save Settings.
  3. Run Sync Audio Language Tags to Jellyfin under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks → Jellyfin Enhanced to tag existing movies and series.

Admin settings below are under Display; the row's default is in UI Preferences, and synchronization controls are in Audio Language Tags.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Show available audio languages on item detail page / personal: Show Audio Languages On Displays the audio-language row on movie, series, season, and episode detail pages Admin: Enable Audio Language Tags Sync Off Writes audio languages as Jellyfin tags on movies and series Admin: Tag Prefix JE Language: (trailing space) Prefixes synchronized language tags Admin: Link audio languages to their tag page On Turns a displayed language into a link when a matching synchronized tag exists on the item

Schedule language synchronization

Sync Audio Language Tags to Jellyfin has no default schedule. Add a trigger or run it manually, especially with the server cache off.

Language matching and synchronization

A regional track gets a base tag, such as JE Language: English, and a regional tag, such as JE Language: English (United States). A regional chip tries the matching regional tag first, then its base tag. Without a match it remains plain text.

The synchronized series tags combine languages across episodes. The detail-page row itself uses a representative episode for series/seasons. It can therefore show fewer languages than cached poster flags or synchronized series tags.

For playable items, changing the selected media version can change the row. More than three languages can scroll horizontally; missing usable data shows a dash.

Synchronization directly tags movies and series, not seasons or episodes. With the server cache on, cache updates can sync new or changed items after library changes. Cache-excluded items skip that update path but can still be processed by the standalone task.

Updates remove stale tags only under the current prefix. Changing the prefix leaves old-prefix tags behind. Disabling synchronization does not delete existing tags.

docs.title: Rating Tags
docs.text:
Rating Tags show Jellyfin's community score as a yellow-star chip and its critic score as a percentage. You can choose which item types and home rows show them.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Show Rating Tags in UI Settings.
  2. Expand Choose where to show and select item types and home rows.

Administrators set defaults under the same heading in Media Tags.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Rating Tags / personal: Show Rating Tags Off Enables poster score chips and, when configured, user-review chips Admin: Show on movies / personal: Movies On Allows rating and review chips on movie cards Admin: Show on series / personal: Series On Allows rating and review chips on series cards Admin: Show on seasons / personal: Seasons On Allows rating and review chips on season cards Admin: Show on episodes / personal: Episodes On Allows rating and review chips on episode cards Admin: Show in the Continue Watching row / personal: Continue Watching row On Allows rating and review chips in that row Admin: Show in the Next Up row / personal: Next Up row On Allows rating and review chips in home Next Up and the series-page shelf

Your item-type and row choices both apply. Turn off Episodes to hide these chips on every episode card, including Next Up and Continue Watching. Turn off a row to hide them only in that row. These choices do not hide quality, genre, language, or age-rating badges.

Score sources and fallback

Collections and videos are not governed by the four type switches. Critic scores below 60% use the rotten icon; 60% and above use the fresh icon. Built-in chip colors are fixed rather than a score gradient.

Scores come from Jellyfin's CommunityRating and CriticRating. Their sources depend on your metadata providers or synchronization, including MDBList settings. The overlays do not fetch TMDB or Rotten Tomatoes scores directly. A community score displayed as 0.0 becomes a dash; absent scores do not produce their respective chips.

Season/episode score fallback differs by data path. The server cache substitutes both series scores when the child's community score is null. Batch fallback and player scores use the series only when neither child score is truthy. A child with only a critic score can therefore display differently between the cache and fallback paths.

Spoiler Guard and scores

Spoiler Guard can suppress score data on protected items. Age classifications have a separate policy, described below.

docs.title: User-review chips
docs.text:
A pink person-with-heart chip shows the average star rating from reviews visible to you. It converts the 1–5 average to a /10 display: a four-star average appears as 8.

How to use:

  1. As an administrator, open Elsewhere & Reviews → User Reviews.
  2. Turn on Enable User Written Reviews and Show average user rating on poster cards, then click Save Settings.
  3. Each viewer must also enable Show Rating Tags. There is no separate personal review-chip switch.

To contribute, open an eligible detail page and click Write a Review. Choose stars, enter review text, or both.

Setting Default What it does Enable User Written Reviews Off Enables JE's stored user reviews; independent of Elsewhere and TMDB Reviews being enabled Show average user rating on poster cards Off Adds the average-review chip to eligible cards with Rating Tags enabled Show "—" on posters for unrated items On Shows a dash when no visible aggregate star rating exists; off removes that chip Hide reviews from hidden users On Hides those authors' reviews from other non-admin viewers; self-view and admin exceptions apply Hide reviews from disabled users On Applies the same visibility rule to disabled accounts Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating Off Mirrors movie/series review stars to Jellyfin's personal /10 rating, independently of the displayed average

The optional dash means there is no visible average star rating, even if you have written a text-only review.

Mirroring replaces your Jellyfin rating

Also save review star ratings as the user's Jellyfin rating overwrites an existing personal Jellyfin rating.

Review identities, limits, and mirrored ratings

Movies and series require a TMDB ID. Seasons and episodes require the parent series' TMDB ID and their season/episode numbers.

Matching identities share reviews across duplicate library items. Collections and generic videos do not have these review chips. The chips follow the same corner and scope exclusions as Rating Tags and respect applicable Spoiler Guard review restrictions.

Stars range from 1–5 in half-star increments. Review text is limited to 2,000 characters, and a review needs stars or nonblank text. Only reviews with stars contribute to the poster average.

Deleting a review or removing its stars clears the mirrored rating only if it still matches. A rating changed elsewhere is preserved. Season/episode reviews are not mirrored. Writing and moderating reviews is covered in User Reviews.

docs.title: Age Rating Tags
docs.text:
Age Rating Tags show the official parental/content classification Jellyfin already has, such as PG-13, R, TV-MA, FSK 12, or BBFC 15. Supported rating-board labels receive predefined colors, with a fallback for other labels.

How to use: Turn on Show Age Rating Tags in UI Settings and choose a corner.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Age Rating Tags / personal: Show Age Rating Tags Off Shows the item's official classification on supported cards Admin: Colored Ratings Backgrounds Off Under Extras → UI Tweaks, colors official classification boxes on detail pages and applicable player elements

The default bottom-right position stacks with Rating Tags. Seasons and episodes normally show their own nonblank classification, or their series' classification if they have none.

Poster age badges use classification colors independently of Colored Ratings Backgrounds. That separate switch controls detail/player classification boxes.

Classification labels and colors

Equivalent labels share colors. For example, DE-12 and FSK 12 become FSK-12, and supported unrated labels become NR. Color support includes international boards, US TV descriptors, and ESRB classifications. These are classification colors, not gradients for community/critic scores.

Spoiler Guard and classifications

Age classifications remain visible. When score stripping protects unwatched episodes or unstarted seasons, the badge can deliberately use the series classification instead of the child's own rating, avoiding a hint from an unusually high episode classification.

docs.title: People Tags
docs.text:
People Tags add age and birthplace facts to cast and guest-cast cards on item detail pages. They support rectangular and round portraits.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Show People Tags in UI Settings.
  2. Open a title's detail page and view its cast.

Administrators can set the starting value in Media Tags.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable People Tags / personal: Show People Tags Off Adds age chips, birthplace information, and deceased styling to cast cards Admin: Tags Cache Duration (days) 30 Sets the lifetime of cached person facts in the browser; allowed range 1–365

You'll see green current-age chips, red age-at-death chips, and blue age-at-release chips near the top of a rectangular portrait. Birthplace appears along the bottom, with a country flag when the place can be resolved. Deceased people receive a cross and grayscale styling; round portraits use an adjusted layout.

Optional TMDB enrichment

To add facts from TMDB, the person needs a TMDB ID and your administrator must set TMDB API Key under Elsewhere & Reviews.

Person metadata and caching

Facts come from Jellyfin person metadata. Failed or unavailable TMDB enrichment keeps usable Jellyfin facts. Missing birth/death dates or birthplace omit the corresponding details. Age at release also needs the viewed item's visible premiere date; hidden or stripped dates cannot supply it.

Age at release is calculated from birth to premiere without a death-date limit. For a posthumous release, that chip can show an age the person never reached.

Birthplace flags require the last comma-separated part of the place to match a recognized country name. A place ending in England UK can therefore show its text without a flag.

The separate browser facts cache holds at most 3,000 people. Ages are calculated from cached dates for the current visit rather than kept as stale age numbers. People Tags are web cast overlays and are not drawn by Native Poster Tags. Spoiler Guard can remove protected guest-cast/cast cards before these overlays appear.

docs.title: Player badges
docs.text:
You can show scores in the web video player's controls and an age-classification badge when playback starts. These are independent server settings; neither has a personal control in the panel.

How to use:

  1. Configure score chips under Display → Media Tags.
  2. Configure the playback-start classification badge under Playback → Playback & Tab Switch.
  3. Click Save Settings, then refresh the web client.
Setting Default What it does Show Rating in Video Player On Shows community and critic score chips near the time information in the on-screen controls, before Ends at Show Age Rating When Playback Starts Off When an official classification is available, shows it with up to three recognized advisory tags and up to three genres when playback starts

Neither setting requires poster Rating Tags or Age Rating Tags. Poster scope switches do not control player score chips.

Player score and classification behavior

Player score chips use Jellyfin's rating fields and can fall back to series scores when a season/episode has neither score.

The playback-start badge needs an official classification. It uses the series' classification when an episode has none. It displays for five seconds, followed by a 400 ms fade.

Advisories are selected from matching Jellyfin metadata tags. Episodes also use series genres when their own are missing and incorporate series tags. Missing advisories or genres omit only their respective lines. Colored Ratings Backgrounds can color its classification box.

docs.title: Server-Side Tag Cache
docs.text:
The server cache prepares tags for supported items in included libraries, so each page avoids repeating metadata requests. You receive only data allowed by your library access and Spoiler Guard policy.

How to use:

  1. Leave Server-Side Tag Cache on under Display → Media Tags. Choose library exclusions if needed.
  2. After changing exclusions, or after a plugin update that changes tag computation, click Save Settings and open Admin → Tag Cache.
  3. Click Rebuild Server Tag Cache and confirm the full rebuild.
  4. Check server logs for progress and completion. The existing cache keeps serving while the new one builds in the background.

Browser fallback controls appear only with Server-Side Tag Cache off.

Setting Default What it does Server-Side Tag Cache On Loads, builds, and maintains the server cache; off uses per-page batch fallback Exclude libraries from the tag cache Off Reveals library selection for omitting libraries from precomputation Libraries to exclude Empty Selects libraries to skip on the next full rebuild; an empty selection excludes nothing Tags Cache Duration (days) 30 Lifetime of browser fallback entries and People Tags facts, not the server cache's refresh schedule; range 1–365 Persist Tag Fallback Cache in Browser Storage Off in configuration Visible only with Server-Side Tag Cache off; saving in that mode forces it on. See Browser storage and fallback below Clear All Client Caches Action Visible here only with Server-Side Tag Cache off; signals clients to invalidate JE caches on their next load. Does not rebuild the server snapshot or reset server-stored personal preferences

docs.title: Builds, refreshes, and exclusions
docs.text:
The retained cache grows with the number of included items. Exclude large libraries or disable server mode if its memory cost is unsuitable.

Cache lifecycle and excluded libraries

When poster review chips are enabled, visible review averages travel with the filtered cache data.

At startup, JE restores tag-cache.json from <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/. If no usable cache is available, it queues Refresh Tag Cache to build one. Library item additions, updates, and removals keep entries current. The scheduled task normally reconciles changes rather than recomputing every item. Its default daily trigger is 03:00.

Excluded libraries do not lose access or forcibly lose their web tags. Cards without a server entry can use per-page batch fallback. Exclusions also bypass the normal cache-update audio-language synchronization path; the standalone language-sync task can still process those items.

Builds load item data in small pages to reduce peak memory.

Turning server mode off releases the in-memory cache and stops loading, building, monitoring, and scheduled refresh work. The saved snapshot remains on disk. Clients pick up the switch on their next load.

Re-enabling from the dashboard restores the snapshot and catches up on missed changes in the background, without a restart.

If you edit the configuration file by hand instead, restart Jellyfin and run Refresh Tag Cache to catch up.

docs.title: Browser storage and fallback
docs.text:
Turn off Server-Side Tag Cache to reveal Persist Tag Fallback Cache in Browser Storage and Clear All Client Caches in Media Tags.

Browser storage and fallback details

The first web load downloads the server payload and saves an IndexedDB copy scoped to that server and user. Later loads restore that copy and request changes since the saved cursor. Tags wait for confirmation that the stored version and access/Spoiler Guard revision still match. A rebuild or changed filtering replaces the copy, including changes made from another device. Navigation also checks for updates, with requests spaced during rapid browsing.

The stored copy is invalidated when server mode is switched off, by Clear All Client Caches, or when another account signs in in the same browser. Each copy contains that user's filtered, spoiler-safe data.

Without usable IndexedDB, including some private modes or storage failures, the client downloads the payload again on each page load and uses memory only.

Saving with the server cache off forces Persist Tag Fallback Cache in Browser Storage on. The client enables localStorage fallback whenever server mode is off.

Batch fallback fetches the items needed for the current page and keeps frequently used entries in memory. With server mode off, it also persists fallback entries in localStorage, using Tags Cache Duration (days). This is separate from the full server-payload copy in IndexedDB. Browser storage failures leave tags able to fetch data again. Average-review lookups in fallback mode are batched separately.

docs.title: Related routes
docs.text:
Diagnostic routes

These routes are useful when diagnosing a cache problem; routine setup uses the dashboard controls above. All require authentication. See the API reference for broader API use.

Route Access and behavior GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-cache/{userId} Own account or administrator; filtered cache payload. Returns 404 when server mode is off. Optional since is a Unix-millisecond cursor; use the returned generation timestamp, not servedAt POST /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-data/{userId} Own account or administrator; per-page fallback for accessible items. Body is a nonempty array of at most 200 item-ID strings; optional mediaSourceId selects a media version POST /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-cache/rebuild Administrator only; starts a full background rebuild. Returns 400 with server mode off, or 409 if a rebuild is already running GET /JellyfinEnhanced/audio-language-tags?codes=… Returns base/regional synchronized tag names for the supplied comma-separated language codes; empty mapping when sync is off

docs.title: Native Poster Tags (Experimental)
docs.text:
Native Poster Tags add your enabled poster groups to images shown in eligible native apps, without changing the original artwork files. The feature is built into JE, so you need no companion plugin or client modification.

Server preview; this is not a native-app screenshot.

How to use:

  1. Enable suitable tag groups and ensure the items have the required metadata.
  2. Under Display → Media Tags, turn on Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental) and click Save Settings.
  3. Each user can opt out with Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) in UI Settings.
  4. Reopen the native app's library or restart the app to pick up changed poster addresses.

Setting Default What it does Admin: Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental) Off Server-wide master switch; off serves original posters and stops native tag composition Admin: Additional Excluded Clients Empty Adds web-wrapper client names that should retain original posters; newline- or comma-separated Personal: Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) On while allowed Shows tags in native clients; hidden while the master switch is off, retaining the saved choice Stored native preferences

The admin configuration uses NativePosterTagsEnabled and NativePosterTagsWebClientNames for the master switch and additional client exclusions. The personal UseNativePosterTags value permits native tags when null or true; false opts out while retaining the preference when the master switch is off.

Enable the tag groups too

The master switch alone does not produce visible tags: each user's applicable groups start off.

Supported groups and preferences

JE draws tags into Primary images for movies, series, seasons, episodes, collections, and videos. Supported groups are quality, genre, language, community/critic rating, user-review, and age-classification. People Tags are not a native group.

It uses personal tag switches, corners, quality categories/order, sound-language preference, and rating item-type scopes, together with the administrator's language-priority policy.

docs.title: Eligible clients and requests
docs.text:
Examples of native clients include Jellyfin for Android TV, Tizen, Swiftfin, Findroid, and Streamyfin.

The built-in exclusions are Jellyfin Web, Jellyfin Media Player, Jellium Desktop, Jellyfin Desktop, Jellyfin for WebOS, and Jellyfin for Android (the phone app). These load web overlays and retain original poster images. Jellyfin for Android TV is a different client name and is eligible.

If a custom web wrapper shows tags twice, add its name as shown under Dashboard → Devices to Additional Excluded Clients.

Client matching and image requests

Native tags depend on the app retaining Jellyfin's personalized image tag in its poster request. Requests that omit it, or ask Jellyfin to draw its own watched/progress/unplayed-count indicators into the image, retain original artwork.

Exclusion matching trims whitespace and compares exact names without case sensitivity. Unidentified clients are excluded.

docs.title: Limits and caching
docs.text:
Layout, Spoiler Guard, and image caching
  • Static layout: genre hover names and Hide Tags on Hover do not apply. Size follows the image width rather than the app's final display size; landscape episode images use an adjusted layout.
  • No page or row context: Disable Tags on Search Page and the Continue Watching row / Next Up row rating scopes do not apply. Item-type scopes still apply. Tags can appear anywhere the app reuses that Primary image, including search and detail pages. If an episode card uses a series poster, its tags describe that image's owner.
  • Spoiler-safe data: native composition applies the user's Spoiler Guard stripping policy. Artwork follows the configured stock-card/blur policy, rather than always using blur. Spoiler-scoped responses use no-store so an old poster is not retained under a changed policy.
  • First-view cost: the server draws a poster the first time a particular variant/size is requested. Rendered images are cached with a 128 MiB memory budget and approximately 1 GiB disk budget under Jellyfin's cache directory, jellyfin-enhanced/poster-tags.
  • Refreshes: settings changes can change poster addresses. With the server tag cache on, tag-data changes also change addresses for cached items. Apps can need a library refresh or restart to use them. With the cache off, tag-data changes keep the same URL; apps can show the old composite for up to an hour before revalidating that URL.
  • Fallback: unsupported identity/token requests, missing renderable tags, decode/render failures, sources over 32 MiB, or decoded image sides outside 32–4096 pixels can yield original artwork. These are implementation limits, not adjustable settings.
Signing key and backups

JE stores a 32-byte signing secret in <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/native-poster-tags.key, separately from rendered-image caches. Preserve it in backups to retain personalized URL-signing continuity. JE recreates a missing or invalid key. Older URLs can then serve original artwork until clients refresh.

If the key cannot be persisted, JE logs a warning and uses a process-lifetime key that changes after restart.

On Unix, new keys use owner-only read/write permissions. There is no setting for this internal key.

Administrator preview route

Administrators can diagnose composition with GET /JellyfinEnhanced/native-poster-tags/preview/{itemId}. It requires an accessible supported item, an existing target user, and a local Primary image.

Optional userId defaults to the caller. width defaults to 360, and width/optional height are clamped to 32–2048. Optional topRightOffset controls indicator clearance.

The JPEG response uses no-store and includes X-JE-Poster-Tags-* diagnostics.

The preview attempts composition even with the master/personal native switch off. It strips tag data for Spoiler Guard but uses original, unblurred artwork. It therefore does not preview image protection.

docs.title: Tag Styles and CSS
docs.text:
Use Tag Styles to change supported tag colors without writing CSS. The server editor can apply colors to web overlays, native poster images, or both.

How to use:

  1. Open Display → Media Tags and turn on Enable Tag Styles.
  2. Choose Apply Tag Styles To.
  3. Click a tag to edit its colors and opacity (0–100%), or choose a preset and click Apply Preset.
  4. Click Save Settings and refresh clients as needed.

Use Reset This Tag to restore a tag's defaults, or Reset All Tag Styles to remove all overrides.

Apply a preset, edit a tag's color and opacity, then reset the styles. Setting Default What it does Enable Tag Styles Off Enables saved color overrides; disabling it preserves edits Apply Tag Styles To Both (Jellyfin Web and poster images) Alternatives: Jellyfin Web only or Poster images only (apps without web overlays) Preset Default colours Selects Glass, Outline, Dark, Light, or Default colours for Apply Preset Apply to All tags Applies a preset or bulk colors to all editable groups, or This tab only Colours Background #000000 at 60%; Border #ffffff at 50%; Text #ffffff at 100%; application boxes unchecked Selects bulk colors and opacity; check the fields to include, then use Apply Colours Editor tab Editable fields Quality Background, Border, Text Age ratings Background, Border, Text Rating chips Background, Text and star Genre Background, Border, Icon

Saved overrides start empty. The bulk color pickers do not apply themselves automatically. Language flags and People Tags are not editor tabs.

Stored style configuration

The saved fields are TagStylesEnabled, TagStyleTarget (both, web, or native), TagStylePreset (default initially), TagStyleApplyScope (all or tab), and TagStyleOverrides (an empty string initially). Applying bulk colors sets the preset value to custom.

Check the style scope

Apply to returns to its saved value after you switch editor tabs, select a tag, or apply a preset or bulk colors. Select This tab only immediately before each application if you want to limit changes to the current tab.

Styles change colors, not size, shape, position, or visibility. For web layout, sizing, hiding, and more detailed styling, see CSS Customization.

Style requirements

Native colors require Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental). Enable the tag feature and supply metadata first: CSS cannot create missing tags or restyle pixels already drawn into an image.

Web CSS behavior

On the web, critic-chip styling also reaches user-review chips because they share that chip class.

Saved Tag Styles use stronger important color rules than simple CSS recipes, but sufficiently specific important custom CSS can override them. Prefer the corner controls to transforms that can disrupt shared-corner stacking. Genre-name styling requires Hide Tags on Hover off. Hiding a displayed flag with CSS does not make a fourth flag appear.

Style API routes

The effective web color overrides are available through authenticated GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-styles (empty when disabled or targeting native only). The shipped defaults catalog is administrator-only GET /JellyfinEnhanced/tag-styles/catalog.

Other integrations have separate badge systems: see Seerr for request/availability/provider badges and *arr for service status and synchronized tag links. Those are configured independently of these poster groups.

docs.title: Contributing Translations
docs.text: Help translate JE's interface into your language or improve existing strings. You can contribute through Weblate without a local development setup.

docs.title: Translate on Weblate (Recommended)
docs.text:
Weblate keeps translation work in one place and provides quality checks.

  1. Open the Jellyfin Enhanced project on Weblate.
  2. Choose your language, or request a new language through the project.
  3. Translate or improve strings using the English source and available context.
  4. Review the validation feedback and save your changes.

Use the project engagement page to find languages that need help.

docs.title: Preserve functional text
docs.text:
Translate the visible wording while keeping the parts the interface needs to work. Use consistent wording across related controls. Check long strings in context where possible, especially buttons, notifications, and dialogs.

Note

Translate values, not JSON keys. Do not replace a missing translation with an empty string.

Details

Preserve these parts exactly:

  • Variables such as {count}, {query}, or {userName}. They may move within a sentence, but must retain their names and braces.
  • Icon tokens such as {{icon:search}}.
  • Functional HTML, such as <kbd>, <br>, and links. Translate visible text without breaking the markup or changing required attributes.
  • Escape sequences and valid JSON syntax. For example, a newline inside a JSON string is written as \n.

docs.title: Maintainer Fallback: Manual JSON Changes
docs.text:
When Weblate is unavailable, maintainers can update locale JSON in the repository. Prefer the Weblate workflow for normal contributions so edits stay coordinated.

  1. Work in Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/js/locales/.
  2. For an existing language, edit its JSON file. For a new language, copy en.json and name the file with its language code, such as es.json; follow the existing naming convention for regional variants.
  3. Translate string values while preserving keys, placeholders, icon tokens, and functional markup.

  4. From the repository root, validate the changed language:

    node scripts/validate-translations.js validate es

    Replace es with your language code. To validate every locale:

    node scripts/validate-translations.js validate

  5. Fix errors and review warnings, then submit a pull request describing the language and changes.

A passing check does not replace reviewing grammar, meaning, or layout.

How it works

The validator compares locales with en.json. Missing keys are errors; extra keys and empty strings produce warnings. For source strings that contain placeholders, missing placeholders are errors and extra placeholders produce warnings.

It does not detect added placeholders in a string whose English source has none, so review those manually. Validation errors return a nonzero exit status.

docs.title: Translation Updates
docs.text:
Merged translations normally reach your installed plugin with a plugin release. They do not immediately replace translations included with the version you already have.

  1. To select a language, open personal Settings → Language Settings → Display Language.
  2. Choose your language. JE saves your choice to your account and browser, then reloads the page.

Clear Translation Cache removes this browser's saved translations and reloads. It normally loads the translation included with your installed plugin again.

How it works

When you open JE, it looks for translations in this order:

  1. A copy saved in your browser for the installed plugin version, valid for 24 hours.
  2. The translation included with your installed plugin, using the base language if the selected regional translation is not included.
  3. A translation from the repository, downloaded through your Jellyfin server, if your installed translation is unavailable.

JE uses English if it cannot load your selected language.

For a regional choice such as fr-CA, JE uses included French (fr) if Canadian French is not included. If no matching included translation can be loaded, JE tries the regional translation from the repository and may then use English without trying the repository's base-language translation.

The language menu lists translations included with your plugin and checks GitHub for newly added languages. Seeing a new language in the menu does not mean the translations you already have were updated from the repository.

Refresh Translation Cache asks all clients to clear their saved translations on their next page load. This scheduled task runs when Jellyfin starts by default.

See How do I change the plugin's language? for administrator defaults and personal overrides.

If a translated string is wrong, report it through Weblate. Include the language, affected screen, English source or string key, and suggested correction. Use Support & Community if you need help finding the string.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Use these answers to find the right settings or troubleshooting guide. For installation failures, start with Troubleshooting installation.

docs.title: What is Jellyfin Enhanced?
docs.text: Jellyfin Enhanced (JE) adds personal controls, playback enhancements, media tags, pages, and optional service integrations to Jellyfin. Start with Quick start, then use Settings Overview to find the administrator and personal controls.

docs.title: Can I customize the keyboard shortcuts?
docs.text:
Yes. You can change shortcut combinations for your account, and changes save automatically.

  1. Open your Enhanced Panel with ? while you are not typing in an input or text area.
  2. Select Shortcuts.
  3. Click a binding and press your new combination.

While the binding is listening, Backspace restores the administrator binding and Del disables that action for you.

Administrators control shortcut availability under Keyboard:

Setting Default What it does Disable Keyboard Shortcuts Off Stops ordinary JE shortcuts and hides Shortcuts in the personal panel.

You can still open the panel with ?, and you cannot change that key. See Enhanced settings for the controls and Settings Overview for alternative panel entry points.

Details

Changes save to your account's server-side shortcuts.json. Modifier-only keys are ignored. Duplicate combinations are rejected; player actions also reject keys reserved by Jellyfin's player. A rejected binding flashes red and shakes. Percentage jumping is read-only.

docs.title: Does this work on mobile apps?
docs.text: To use JE's web controls, your app must load the web interface served by your Jellyfin server. Playback enhancements also need a browser player that JE can control. Check Compatibility for your app and playback mode.

docs.title: Does this work on Android TV or other TV platforms?
docs.text: Native apps do not receive JE's web controls, but enabled server features can still affect them. Examples include Spoiler Guard, hiding content from supported lists and Home rows, automatic requests, experimental Native Poster Tags, and data synchronized into Jellyfin. Each has its own switches and limits on the screens and clients it supports. See Compatibility.

docs.title: Is this plugin affiliated with Seerr?
docs.text: JE is an independent project that integrates with Seerr. Report JE integration problems through JE's bug-report process. If the same problem occurs directly in Seerr, investigate that service separately.

docs.title: How do I change the plugin's language?
docs.text:
You can choose a JE language independently of Jellyfin's language.

  1. In your personal Settings, open Language Settings → Display Language.
  2. Select a language. JE saves your preference and reloads the page.
Setting Default What it does Display Language (per user) Auto Follows Jellyfin's language unless your administrator sets a starting language or you choose your own. Default UI Language (admin, Display) System Default Sets the starting JE language for new users; they can change it in their personal settings. How it works

With Auto in your personal settings, JE follows Jellyfin's language and uses English if that translation is unavailable. Clear Translation Cache clears this browser's saved translations and reloads. It normally reloads the translation included with your installed plugin. See Contributing Translations for languages, loading order, and release timing.

docs.title: Where is the userscript version?
docs.text: The userscript is discontinued. An archived userscript remains for the old basic shortcut implementation; it is not a substitute for the current plugin.

docs.title: Does JE send usage statistics?
docs.text:
Usage reporting is opt-in and off by default.

  1. As an administrator, open Admin → Usage Statistics.
  2. Turn on Share Anonymous Usage Statistics if you want to participate.
  3. Use Preview to see what you would share before you save.
Setting Default What it does Share Anonymous Usage Statistics Off Enables optional analytics reporting. Feature toggle states (on/off only) On Includes feature-switch states and selected text settings when reporting is enabled. Feature usage counts On Includes usage counts when reporting is enabled. Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) On Includes only the total size of the custom branding directory, without file names or contents, when reporting is enabled. Reporting interval (days) 15 Sets the interval, clamped to 7–30 days. How it works

Reports always include an anonymous installation ID, plugin and Jellyfin versions, and the Jellyfin build target, even with all three categories off. Turning reporting on schedules a report right away. Turning it off asks the analytics service to exclude your registered installation from public statistics.

Optional analytics is separate from requests needed for enabled integrations, assets, or hosted documentation. See Community Analytics for the full privacy and reporting details.

docs.title: Plugin Compatibility
docs.text: See Compatibility for Jellyfin versions, clients, layouts, companion plugins, and integration requirements. Use the shared manifest in the Installation Guide to get the matching server build.

docs.title: Plugin not appearing after installation?
docs.text: Check whether the server plugin is loaded before diagnosing the panel. Follow Plugin Not Appearing After Installation.

docs.title: Scripts not loading after installation
docs.text:
Check whether the page includes JE's script and whether the scripts load. Follow Scripts Not Loading.

Details

Normal injection is not repaired simply by running the startup task.

docs.title: Update not working properly?
docs.text: Compare the running version and build target, then check client and proxy caching. Follow Update Not Working.

docs.title: I see "permission denied" errors in logs!
docs.text:
Find the path and operation in the full error, then use Permission Issues.

Details

Normal injection needs no writable web directory. User data, branding, caches, logs, and old-tag cleanup have different storage requirements.

docs.title: Auto-skip intros not working?
docs.text:
Check that the item has Intro or Outro segments, then enable the matching auto-skip control.

Required

JE reads Jellyfin's stored Intro and Outro media segments; it does not detect them. A segment provider such as Intro Skipper must supply usable start and end boundaries.

  1. Check that the item has segments before changing JE settings. The details below explain how to check them with a request.
  2. In the Enhanced panel's Auto-Skip Settings, enable the relevant control.
Setting Default What it does Automatically Skip Intro Off Seeks to the end of a stored Intro segment. Automatically Skip Outro Off Seeks to the end of a stored Outro segment.

See Playback controls for the workflow and Enhanced settings for administrator defaults.

Details

An authenticated request to Jellyfin's /MediaSegments/{itemId} can confirm the item's segments; a signed-out request may return 401. Do not share API keys in reports. JE does not need a visible native skip button or English button text.

Direct play/stream and HLS support the intended local seek. Progressive transcodes can stall or fail to seek ahead, and this local seek does not synchronize a SyncPlay group. Seeking backward into a skipped segment suppresses immediate re-skipping.

docs.title: Seerr integration not connecting?
docs.text:
Test the connection from Jellyfin first, then check account import and permissions separately.

  1. In administrator Seerr, configure Enable Seerr integration, Seerr URL(s) (One per line), and Seerr API Key.
  2. Select Test beside the key.
  3. For a linked account, use Permission Audit → Run Audit to check permissions needed by enabled features.

Required

Jellyfin's server must be able to reach Seerr. In a container, localhost means that container.

Use Seerr settings for setup, defaults, sign-in/import instructions, and connection diagnosis; use Permission Audit for authorization checks.

These screenshots show external account management. They do not show JE feature permissions:

An imported account still needs the permissions required by the enabled features.

Manual import is an alternative when automatic import is not enabled; this dialog does not demonstrate access denial.

docs.title: Tags not showing on posters?
docs.text: Open UI Settings in the Enhanced panel, enable the tag groups you want, and check the item's metadata; your saved choices override administrator defaults. See Tags & Badges for setup, scopes, and native posters, and the score sources and fallback rules for season/episode differences between server-cache, batch, and player paths. For stale data, use targeted cache troubleshooting.

docs.title: Bookmarks not syncing across devices?
docs.text:
Sign in with the same Jellyfin account and reload the other device. JE saves bookmarks, main Enhanced preferences, and shortcut overrides on the server for that account.

  1. Reload the page to pick up changes to bookmarks and other saved data. Reopen the personal panel to reload your main settings.
  2. If a bookmark still does not save or appear, check its failed request and the server log for storage errors.

See Smart Bookmarks for bookmarks and Settings Overview for user-data storage and backups.

How it works

Reopening the personal panel reloads your main settings from settings.json. Browser storage also holds caches and local UI state.

docs.title: Why did changing an administrator default not change my settings?
docs.text:
Saved personal preferences take precedence over administrator defaults. Ordinary administrator saves do not continually replace your choices.

To deliberately replace existing preferences:

  1. Save the desired administrator defaults.
  2. Use administrator Overview → Quick Actions → Overwrite everyone's personal settings.

Warning

This action replaces personal choices. Back up first and have users reload their clients afterward. See Settings Overview for its scope and recovery instructions.

Details

The action also saves the current form. It replaces settings.json for known user directories, resets Hidden Content settings while keeping hidden items, and resets existing Spoiler Guard preference overrides while keeping their lists. It does not reset shortcuts.json.

docs.title: What should I back up, and does uninstalling erase my data?
docs.text:
Back up the plugin XML configuration and JE's data, including personal data, shared records, and uploaded branding. Uninstalling JE leaves your saved user data in place.

Follow Settings Overview for storage, backup, and restoration instructions.

Details

Back up the plugin XML configuration and JE's data, including personal settings.json, shortcuts.json, bookmark.json, elsewhere.json, hidden-content.json, and spoilerblur.json. User directories live beneath <PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/<lowercase-user-id-without-hyphens>/.

Keep shared records, uploaded branding, and native-poster-tags.key too. You can find custom_branding inside a folder beside the plugin XML configuration file, with the same name minus .xml. JE can download cdn-cache again. Keep native-poster-tags.key so your restored server can still use existing personalized poster links; losing it can leave clients showing original artwork until they refresh metadata.

Uninstalling JE attempts to remove any old script added to the web files and leaves your saved user data in place. Deleting a Jellyfin account can also leave its personal settings, reviews, and activity records behind.

docs.title: Pause screen not appearing?
docs.text:
Turn on your personal pause screen and stop interacting with the player for the configured delay.

  1. Open personal Settings → Playback Settings and make sure Custom Pause Screen is on.
  2. Pause a video in a browser player JE can control.
  3. Stop interacting for the configured delay. Fullscreen and theater mode are optional.

Personal controls:

Setting Default What it does Custom Pause Screen On Shows the overlay during paused browser playback. Delay before showing (seconds): 5 Sets how long you must stop interacting before the overlay appears. Details

Moving the mouse, touching the screen, or pressing a key postpones the overlay. If you dismiss it, it stays hidden until you resume and pause again.

See Playback controls and CSS Customization for use and styling.

docs.title: Reviews, Elsewhere, or Seerr icons not working?
docs.text:
Identify what failed before treating it as a TMDB problem:

  • TMDB-backed reviews or availability: check the configured JE TMDB key, provider IDs, the relevant proxy request, and server connectivity. See Elsewhere & Reviews Settings.
  • Seerr search or requests: check service connectivity, account linking, and permissions through Seerr settings.
  • Stored poster ratings: check Jellyfin rating metadata using Media tags.
  • Static icons: check local CDN asset requests using installation troubleshooting.
  • Local user-written reviews: check the JE review request and server log; these are separate from fetching external TMDB reviews. See User Reviews.

docs.title: Is "Remove from Continue Watching / Next Up" destructive?
docs.text:
It preserves playback progress and watched state.

  1. Enable your personal Add Remove from Continue Watching & Next Up Buttons preference.
  2. For lasting row filtering, your administrator must enable Enable "Remove from Continue Watching" or Enable Hidden Content.
  3. Enable your personal Enable Content Hiding and the filter for the affected row.

Administrator settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable "Remove from Continue Watching" Off Turns on server row filtering and sets the starting value of the personal removal-button preference. Enable Hidden Content Off Enables the broader Hidden Content feature and its management page; row removal works without this switch.

Personal settings start with administrator defaults; you can change them for your account:

Setting Default What it does Add Remove from Continue Watching & Next Up Buttons Off Adds the removal controls to item menus, even with both server switches off. Enable Content Hiding On Enables your hidden-item filters. Filter Continue Watching On Hides removed items from this row. Filter Next Up On Hides removed items from this row.

On the Hidden Content management page, Continue Watching-only entries use Add back to Continue Watching; other scopes use Unhide.

See Content management and Enhanced settings for scopes, prerequisites, and restoration.

How it works

Starting playback clears a matching Continue Watching-only hide. A combined home-sections hide becomes Next Up-only; Next Up-only and global hides remain.

docs.title: How do I customize tag appearance?
docs.text: Use the built-in tag settings first. For selectors and CSS examples, see Media tags and CSS Customization.

docs.title: How do I upload custom branding?
docs.text:
Upload images to replace Jellyfin's branding assets.

  1. As an administrator, open Jellyfin Enhanced → Extras → Custom Image Assets.
  2. Select or drop an image into a slot.
  3. Check its preview, reported dimensions, and upload status.
  4. Refresh the web client.
Asset slot Recommended dimensions Icon Transparent 536×536 pixels Favicon 256×256 pixels Banner Dark 1302×378 pixels Banner Light 1302×378 pixels Apple Touch Icon 180×180 pixels

Upload requirements

Use an image file no larger than 10 MiB in a format suitable for the slot. You need administrator access, and Jellyfin must be able to write to the branding folder.

Warning

Uploads and deletions persist immediately. They do not wait for a configuration save.

The separate URL-based override has these administrator settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Splash Screen Override Off Shows the configured logo on a temporary black loading overlay until Jellyfin is ready or the 20-second timeout expires. Splash Screen Image URL /web/assets/img/banner-light.png Selects the splash image when the override is enabled.

See Other settings for formats and limits.

How it works

Slots initially have no uploaded file. JE saves each image in its original format without converting it. JE's image replacements are enabled by default (DisableBrandingMiddleware=false); File Transformation is not required.

docs.title: Why aren't my subtitles using the Jellyfin Enhanced styling?
docs.text:
JE can style text subtitles drawn by Jellyfin's web player. For Position, select Custom in Jellyfin's subtitle settings so Jellyfin draws the captions instead of your browser.

Note

These controls cannot style subtitles burned into the video, image-based tracks, or subtitles drawn by a different player.

See Playback controls for supported playback modes and Compatibility for client limits.

docs.title: How do I turn off subtitle styling and use Jellyfin's own?
docs.text:
Enable Disable Custom Styles to use Jellyfin's own subtitle styles.

  1. Open personal Settings → Subtitle Settings.
  2. Turn on Disable Custom Styles and reload.

Personal setting:

Setting Default What it does Disable Custom Styles Off Stops JE's subtitle styling so Jellyfin's own styles apply.

Administrators set the starting preference under Playback:

Setting Default What it does Disable Custom Subtitle Styles by default Off Starts users without saved preferences with JE's subtitle styling disabled.

Saved personal choices take precedence over the administrator default. See Enhanced settings for the full subtitle controls, or Settings Overview if you intend to overwrite preferences for everyone.

docs.title: Can I change tag positions?
docs.text: Yes. Open personal Settings and choose the position for the relevant tag type. See Media tags for controls and CSS Customization for advanced styling.

docs.title: How do I gather logs for bug reports?
docs.text:
Reproduce the problem once and note the time. This helps you match browser and server log entries.

  1. Open developer tools with F12 and select Console. Filter for Jellyfin Enhanced and copy the relevant error, stack trace, and nearby messages that explain it.
  2. In Network, filter for JellyfinEnhanced and reproduce the failure. Record the request path, method, status code, and useful response body.
  3. Open Jellyfin's server logs from its administration tools or configured log directory. Include the relevant error and nearby lines rather than an unrelated full log. The details below explain which JE logs to look for.

Warning

Before sharing logs, screenshots, or network exports, redact API keys, access tokens, cookies, passwords, private URLs, usernames, and other personal information.

Collect evidence promptly. Then follow Report issues for the environment details to include.

Details

Look for the Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced logger category and the dedicated JellyfinEnhanced_yyyy-mm-dd.log file. JE's dedicated logs are in Jellyfin's configured log directory; its messages also appear in Jellyfin's main log.

When JE starts, it removes dedicated log files created more than three days ago. It checks the file's creation time, not the date in its name, and only performs this cleanup when starting.

A proxy login page returned instead of JSON or a script is useful evidence. Leave Dev Mode off unless you need to check which individual script fails to load. See Scripts Not Loading for that diagnostic option.

docs.title: Common error messages and solutions
docs.text: Error or symptom Next step BUILD/HOST MISMATCH Install the matching build. index.html access denied Check whether JE was removing an old script or writing a new one. Plugin loaded but panel missing Inspect HTML and client requests. Bookmarks/settings fail to save Check the failing storage operation. Seerr search/account/permission failure Check Seerr setup and Permission Audit. Calendar or Requests is blank Use *arr troubleshooting, including source and proxy checks. Administrator tabs do nothing Compare local and proxy access. Tags or translation text are stale Target the affected cache.

docs.title: Native Home tabs and the Custom Tabs plugin
docs.text:
JE can show Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Requests, Calendar, Recommendations, Activity, and Catch Up as native Home tabs without a companion plugin.

  1. Choose either a native Home tab or Custom Tabs for each JE page using JE Pages & Tabs.
  2. If you let JE add a Custom Tabs entry, remove any duplicate you added yourself.
  3. If you choose Plugin Pages, restart Jellyfin when using an older version or when updating its entries fails.

Check Compatibility for layout and companion requirements. If detection fails, follow Plugin detection issue.

How it works

Native JE tabs can coexist with external Custom Tabs; JE tabs follow those tabs. Generated links include a current numeric index and stable identity, such as #/home?tab=4&jeTab=bookmarks or jeTab=catchup.

With a compatible Plugin Pages 3.0+ version, JE tries to update its entries when you save. Restart Jellyfin if you use an older version or that update fails. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me works when JE supports your Custom Tabs configuration.

docs.title: What is Catch Up?
docs.text:
Catch Up is a page for marking titles watched, dismissing them, or adding them to your watchlist.

  1. As an administrator, enable it under Pages → Catch Up and choose its placement.
  2. Open it from the chosen location. For Plugin Pages, use its registered entry.

Catch Up can record activity. You need administrator access to view its activity feed and summary. See Enhanced features for the workflow, Enhanced settings for settings and logging limits, and JE Pages & Tabs for navigation.

Details

A native link uses jeTab=catchup.

docs.title: Plugin conflicts?
docs.text:
Test with a clean browser profile, then check custom CSS, browser extensions, and companion plugins one at a time.

Details

The Enable Splash Screen Override help warns that it might cause strange behavior with Media Bar. This is a conditional warning, not a guarantee that the plugins always conflict.

For nonworking administrator tabs, compare local/proxied access through installation troubleshooting. Include the theme and relevant companion versions in a bug report.

docs.title: Performance issues?
docs.text:
