Find where the delay happens before changing unrelated settings.

  1. Check whether the browser takes a long time to display the page, a request waits for a response, or a server task takes too long.
  2. Compare with a clean profile and temporarily disable the affected feature to narrow it down.
  3. Check request timing and server logs.

For tags, check cache mode and exclusions in Media tags. For service pages, use Seerr settings or *arr troubleshooting. Routine browser-cache clearing is not a performance fix.

docs.title: Where can I get help?
docs.text: Use Support & Community for questions, Report issues for reproducible bugs, Feature Requests for proposals, and Contributing Translations for language work.

docs.title: Related Projects
docs.text: See Related Projects for other projects and Compatibility for companion plugins.

docs.title: Still Have Questions?
docs.text: Search the support channels and existing issues first. When asking for help, include the versions, client, reproduction steps, and relevant redacted logs described in Report issues.

docs.title: Feature Requests
docs.text: Describe the problem you want to solve and how a change would help you use Jellyfin. You do not need to design the implementation.

docs.title: Before requesting
docs.text:
The feature may already exist behind a server switch or personal preference. A matching request may also have useful discussion you can build on.

  1. Check the relevant feature guides and Settings Overview.
  2. Search existing enhancement requests.
  3. If a matching request exists, add your use case and useful details there.

Use GitHub Discussions for an early idea or an open-ended conversation about possible approaches.

docs.title: Submit Feature Requests
docs.text:
Use the feature request template for a concrete proposal.

The template asks for:

  1. Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Explain the current workflow and where it falls short.
  2. Describe the solution you'd like. Describe the behavior you want and how you would use it.
  3. Additional context. Include relevant screenshots, mockups, or examples.
Details

If it does not open directly, use the issue chooser and select the feature request template.

docs.title: Good Feature Requests
docs.text:
A concrete example helps others understand the behavior you want: “When I open this page, I want to filter these results because…”.

Include:

  • The client and layout you use.
  • Whether the change is for administrators or viewers.
  • Any service it depends on.
  • The limitation of any existing setting or workaround you have tried.

Keep separate ideas in separate requests unless they form one workflow. Be open to a different solution that addresses the same problem.

Note

A submitted request starts a discussion. It does not guarantee implementation or a release date.

If an existing feature is failing, use Report issues instead.

docs.title: Report issues
docs.text: Show how to reproduce the problem so the JE project can investigate it. Your report helps identify whether the failure is in JE, Jellyfin, your client, or an integration.

docs.title: Before Reporting
docs.text:
Check for an existing report and rule out common setup problems before opening an issue.

  1. Search existing issues for the same symptom. Add useful reproduction details to a matching report rather than opening a duplicate.
  2. Check your running JE version and Jellyfin build target using installation troubleshooting. If you can update, retest with the current matching release.
  3. Check Compatibility and the relevant feature/settings guide. For installation, use Troubleshooting installation; for integrations, use Seerr settings or *arr troubleshooting.
  4. Test with a clean browser profile or temporarily disable browser extensions/custom CSS. Record whether the problem remains.
  5. If you normally access Jellyfin remotely, compare your remote URL with direct local access and record the result.

If you need help narrowing down a problem before it is reproducible, use Discussions or Discord.

docs.title: Gather evidence
docs.text:
Collect the logs and images that show the failure.

  1. Follow How do I gather logs for bug reports? for console, Network, and server logs.
  2. Note the reproduction time. Include the failed request, its status, and the surrounding error lines.
  3. Attach screenshots or a short recording when the behavior is visual.

Warning

Redact credentials and personal information before sharing. Check request URLs, headers, response bodies, logs, and screenshots for API keys, tokens, cookies, passwords, private addresses, and usernames. Review a network export before uploading it.

Details

Do not turn on Dev Mode just to submit a report. Use it only when checking which individual script fails to load, as described in Scripts Not Loading.

docs.title: Create Issue
docs.text:
Use the bug report template to keep the information in one place.

  1. Open the bug report template. If it does not open directly, use the issue chooser and select the bug template.
  2. Give the issue a title that identifies the affected feature and failure.
  3. Complete the template with the information below.

Include:

  • A clear description, numbered reproduction steps, and expected versus actual behavior.
  • Exact Jellyfin server and JE versions, including the JE build target if a mismatch is possible.
  • Installation method, such as a container image, Linux package, or Windows service.
  • Device, operating system, exact app/browser name and version, and playback mode when relevant.
  • Theme and relevant custom CSS.
  • External access method when the issue occurs remotely, such as a reverse proxy, tunnel, or VPN; say whether local access also fails.
  • Relevant companion and upstream service versions. See the details below for what to include.
  • Relevant administrator switches and personal overrides, redacted logs, failed request details, and screenshots.

State how often it happens and whether other accounts, devices, or library items reproduce it. Keep one distinct problem per report unless the symptoms clearly share the same reproduction.

Details

State whether FileTransformation is installed, as the template asks. Include versions of other relevant companions, such as Plugin Pages or Custom Tabs, and upstream service versions when relevant.

docs.title: After submitting
docs.text:
Reply with requested details and test results in the same issue. If you find a workaround or a version where it stops happening, include that result so others can reproduce the comparison.

For proposed functionality rather than a bug, use Feature Requests.

docs.title: Support & Community
docs.text:
Choose the channel that fits what you need. Search existing questions and reports first so you can build on the information already available.

You need Where to go Help installing or loading JE Installation Guide and Troubleshooting installation An answer about settings or behavior FAQ, Settings Overview, and the relevant feature guide A general question or an early idea GitHub Discussions Community conversation and help Discord Community A reproducible bug Report issues and GitHub Issues A concrete feature proposal Feature Requests Translation work Contributing Translations

docs.title: Asking for help
docs.text:
Give enough context for someone else to understand and try the same steps.

  1. Describe what you were trying to do, what happened, and how to reproduce it.
  2. Include your Jellyfin and JE versions, installation method, exact client/browser and device, and theme or relevant companions.
  3. If it happens remotely, say how you access the server and whether direct local access works.
  4. Add useful screenshots and relevant logs.

Warning

Redact credentials and personal information before sharing screenshots or logs.

Keep follow-up details in the same discussion or issue, and allow time for community members to respond.

docs.title: Other ways to contribute
docs.text:
You can help by testing the steps in a report, explaining a workaround, improving documentation, or translating strings.

For code contributions, use the GitHub repository and Project Structure to find the relevant code area.

docs.title: Support the project
docs.text:
JE is free and open source. You can use the plugin and participate in the community without donating.

If you want to support its development financially, use Ko-fi or Buy Me a Coffee. Donations are optional.

For related plugins, themes, and projects, see Related Projects.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Get Jellyfin Enhanced running, choose a few settings, and try it in your browser. You don't need Seerr, *arr services, or companion plugins to open the Enhanced panel and use the basic playback tools.

docs.title: 1. Install and reload
docs.text:
1. Follow the installation guide to add the repository and install Jellyfin Enhanced. Choose the build for your server: Jellyfin 12.x or 10.11.x.
  2. Restart Jellyfin.
  3. Open the web interface served by your Jellyfin server and refresh it.
How it works

JE normally adds its scripts while the server serves the web page. Normal script loading and custom branding don't require File Transformation or a writable web directory.

Plugin Pages adds page navigation through its own integration; Custom Tabs embeds JE pages on Home. Install their prerequisites if you choose either integration. JE's native Home tabs need no companion plugin. Intro Skipper and In-Player Episode Preview support additional playback tools. See compatibility.

docs.title: 2. Set up the server
docs.text:
Choose the starting preferences for accounts that haven't loaded JE yet. You can connect optional services now or later.

  1. As an administrator, open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced. This is the server configuration page; your personal panel is separate.
  2. In Overview, check Service Status and Optional Dependencies for integrations you plan to use.
  3. In Display and Playback, choose starting preferences.
  4. In Pages, enable the pages you want and choose how users reach them. JE pages & tabs explains the options.
  5. If you use Seerr, Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr, Shoko, or TMDB-based features, connect them now; see Connect optional services below.
  6. Click Save Settings, then refresh affected web clients.

These are administrator defaults for a new configuration. Where a setting supplies a personal starting value, users can change it for their account.

Setting Default What it does Enable Custom Pause Screen On Shows the pause overlay after your personal delay, initially 5 seconds. Enable Bookmarks Feature On Lets you save playback timestamps. Enable Random Button On Adds random library browsing. Auto-pause on tab switch On Sets the starting value for your personal Auto-pause preference. Show available audio languages on item detail page On Sets the starting value for your personal language display preference.

Main media-tag preferences start off, including quality, genre, language, rating, and people tags. Seerr, Spoiler Guard, Activity, Requests, Calendar, Hidden Content, Catch Up, and Active Streams also start off. Some suggestions in What to try first need features that start off, so enable them first.

Elsewhere needs a key

Elsewhere starts on, but needs a TMDB API key. No key is configured initially.

Existing personal preferences

JE saves starting preferences when an account first loads JE. Saving admin defaults doesn't replace those saved preferences, even for users who never customized them. To replace them for everyone, save the defaults first, then use Overview → Quick Actions → Overwrite everyone's personal settings. See settings overview for its scope, storage, and backups.

Connect optional services
  • Seerr: Open Seerr, turn on Enable Seerr integration, enter Seerr URL(s) (One per line) and Seerr API Key, then click Test beside the key. Follow the Seerr setup guide to link/import Jellyfin accounts. In Users, click Import Users Now to import unblocked users. Then use Permission Audit → Run Audit to check linked accounts; it doesn't import missing ones.
  • Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr, or Shoko: Configure them in *arr. Use addresses reachable from the Jellyfin server. Configure public browser links separately with URL mappings when needed.
  • TMDB: Add TMDB API Key in Seerr or Elsewhere & Reviews if your chosen features need it. Both fields edit the same key. Basic poster tags don't require it.

Click Save Settings and refresh affected clients after configuring services. Test each optional service separately. Opening the personal panel confirms that JE's client interface loaded; it doesn't confirm that every integration is ready.

docs.title: 3. Open your personal panel
docs.text:
Use the Enhanced panel to make JE feel right for your account. Your main preferences and shortcut overrides save to your account on the server.

  1. Open the panel using an entry below.
  2. Use Search settings… or select a section to find a preference.
Open the panel and select a settings section. Where you are How to open the panel Desktop Press ? while you're outside an input field. Jellyfin 12 Modern Layout Open your avatar menu and select Jellyfin Enhanced. Visible navigation drawer, including on a phone Choose Jellyfin Enhanced → Enhanced Panel. Jellyfin's user settings menu, including on a phone Select Jellyfin Enhanced - User Settings. Mobile or TV web player Select the tune button titled Jellyfin Enhanced when the player controls are available; desktop layouts hide it.

Reload any other device to pick up your changes.

See settings overview for all sections and entry points.

docs.title: What to try first
docs.text:
• Open Shortcuts and try Go to Home with Shift+H. Click a displayed key to customize it; Backspace restores the administrator's binding.
  • Start a browser video and press B to save a bookmark. Open Bookmarks to return to that timestamp later.
  • In UI Settings, enable a poster tag category and browse a library. Tags & badges explains their data requirements and scopes.
  • Pause a browser video and wait without interacting to try the pause screen. Adjust playback preferences in Playback Settings.
  • If your administrator enabled them, open Calendar, Requests, or Seerr Recommendations (Recommendations in Plugin Pages or JE-managed Custom Tabs) to try the connected services.

docs.text:

  • Check your setup

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: JE supports Jellyfin Server 12.x and 10.11.x with separate builds. You'll get the web features in clients that load your server's web interface. Native apps can use some server features too.

docs.title: Jellyfin versions
docs.text:
Use the build that matches your Jellyfin server. Both versions support the seven JE pages, tags, and automatic requests.

  1. Install the matching build from the shared plugin repository.
  2. Restart Jellyfin. See installation for the full steps.
Area Jellyfin 12.x Jellyfin 10.11.x Plugin build Jellyfin 12.x build Jellyfin 10.11.x build Script loading and branding Supported Supported JE pages and native Home tabs Supported; Modern Layout has navigation limits below Supported, including native Home tabs Personal Enhanced panel Drawer, user settings menu, player button, shortcut, and Modern Layout avatar-menu entry Drawer, user settings menu, player button, and shortcut

Older Jellyfin servers

Jellyfin 10.10 needs the historical plugin line, frozen at 10.11.1.0.

Wrong build installed

If Wrong plugin build for this Jellyfin version appears on the admin page, reinstall the matching build and restart. See troubleshooting.

Build and API details Server Build file Runtime target Jellyfin 12.x Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced_12.0.0.zip .NET 10 Jellyfin 10.11.x Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced_10.11.0.zip .NET 9

Script loading and branding use built-in request-time middleware on both versions. The conditional server code adapts Activity library access and item statistics. Jellyfin 12 uses access-scoping and batch APIs; 10.11 uses compatible access queries and individual user-data reads. These differences don't reserve the seven JE pages, tags, or automatic requests for Jellyfin 12.

The startup log reports a wrong build as BUILD/HOST MISMATCH. The authenticated, administrator-only /JellyfinEnhanced/host-compat diagnostic identifies the expected artifact. There is no setting to turn off this check.

docs.title: Clients and playback
docs.text:
For the panel, tags, and browser playback tools, open the web interface served by your Jellyfin server. Check the table below if you prefer an app or a separate player.

Client What to expect Jellyfin web served by your server The injected panel, page navigation, tags, search integration, and browser playback tools are available when their settings and requirements are met. Official Android and iOS apps using the embedded web interface Web enhancements can run when the app loads the server's injected web page. Playback tools need browser playback. Jellyfin Desktop and other desktop web wrappers Web enhancements depend on loading the server's web interface. JE's browser playback tools aren't available in an external or native player. Android TV, Roku, Swiftfin, and other native clients JE's injected panel, pages, buttons, and shortcuts aren't added to their native interface. Enabled server features can still affect their Jellyfin requests, images, and saved user data. Independently hosted web clients Connecting to a JE server alone doesn't add JE's web enhancements to a separately hosted client.

Browser playback tools include the pause screen, subtitle styling, long-press speed changes, automatic skipping, and picture-in-picture. What you can use also depends on your browser's playback capabilities.

Playback limits

JE's playback tools control a browser video element. External and native players don't provide that element. Independently hosted web clients don't automatically pass through JE's injection middleware; connecting to a JE server alone doesn't install JE's client scripts in a separately served web shell.

Auto-skip seeks a browser video element. Progressive transcoding can limit seeking, and the seek isn't synchronized to other SyncPlay members.

docs.title: What works for native clients
docs.text:
Native apps can benefit from JE's server features even though they don't show its panel or buttons. Set your personal policies in the web interface first.

Server feature What can work in native clients Automatic requests Season and movie requests triggered by qualifying playback activity, plus server-side watchlist monitoring when enabled. Native Poster Tags Personalized supported artwork for identified native clients when admin Enable Native Poster Tags (Experimental) and personal Show Tags in Native Clients (Experimental) are on. Hidden Content Filtering on supported item, search, and Home-row responses when the server feature and your applicable filters are on. Spoiler Guard Filtering of supported images and Jellyfin metadata. Saved Jellyfin data Watched status and configured MDBList community/critic rating synchronization. Watchlist synchronization also stores Jellyfin data. Native-client limits

Image caching can delay Native Poster Tag changes. A native app's locally cached Hidden Content results may also need refreshing.

JE's Reviews panel is additionally suppressed by injected web code. Server protection doesn't promise review suppression in a separate client. Displaying a synchronized watchlist requires a suitable client interface.

These effects don't guarantee that every native screen uses a filtered endpoint. The tag guide, Hidden Content guide, Spoiler Guard guide, and Seerr guide describe the switches and limits.

docs.title: Modern and Legacy layouts
docs.text:
Your layout changes where you'll find JE's settings and pages. Native Home tabs work on Jellyfin 12's Modern and Legacy layouts, and on 10.11.

Layout How to reach JE Jellyfin 12 Modern Layout, desktop Open your avatar menu's Jellyfin Enhanced entry for personal settings. Use Home tabs for pages, or JE's header shortcut tray if a native tab button is hidden. Jellyfin 12 Modern Layout, mobile Use sidebar links, including Plugin Pages links.

Modern Layout has no desktop sidebar links

Its header and drawer differ from the Legacy layout. Sidebar links are only visible on mobile. JE adds header shortcut-tray links when Modern Layout hides native Home tab buttons.

See page placement to choose navigation that suits your layout.

How native links stay usable

Generated links carry a stable jeTab identity as well as the current numeric tab index. This lets them recover when other tabs change position.

docs.title: Companion plugins
docs.text:
Companion plugins add optional navigation and playback tools. You don't need File Transformation for normal JE script loading or branding.

  1. Install and activate the companion for the feature you want, along with its prerequisites.
  2. Check Overview → Optional Dependencies for detection status.
  3. If Plugin detection issue appears, use Retry. A failed probe isn't proof that a plugin is missing.
Companion Used for Without it File Transformation Prerequisites of other web modifications, including page/tab companions shown by JE's dependency dashboard Normal JE script loading and branding still work. Plugin Pages The Use Plugin Pages variants under Pages Its registered navigation entries aren't available. JE's standalone implementations for Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Requests, Calendar, and Recommendations can provide navigation when their other placement settings permit it; Activity and Catch Up need a tab or Plugin Pages. Custom Tabs The Use Custom Tabs variants under Pages It can't create the Home containers those options expect. Custom Tabs mode can suppress JE's standalone sidebar links, so turn it off and select a native Home tab or another available placement. Intro Skipper Timestamp source and admin dependency check for Auto-Skip Auto-skip controls are unavailable in the admin UI when the plugin is known to be absent. In-Player Episode Preview Open Episode Preview player shortcut JE can't open the companion's preview interface. KefinTweaks Watchlist interface for Seerr/Jellyfin watchlist features Server-side watchlist data and monitoring don't provide a built-in JE watchlist browser. KefinTweaks is detected as a web modification, rather than a normal server plugin. How script loading and auto-skip work

Intro Skipper is also detected as SkipIntro. The playback engine reads Jellyfin Media Segments and needs valid intro/outro boundaries.

JE doesn't automatically switch to an on-disk rewrite when File Transformation is absent. The hidden configuration flag DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware defaults to false. Setting it to true explicitly selects legacy startup injection into WebPath/index.html, which needs write access there. This is separate from File Transformation detection. Normal injection and branding need writable JE configuration/data storage, not a writable web directory. Startup may still clean an old JE script tag from index.html.

docs.title: External services by feature
docs.text:
Connect only the services your chosen features need. The table shows where to set each one up.

  1. Open the admin page and enter credentials and instance settings in the relevant tab.
  2. Use addresses reachable from the Jellyfin server for API calls. Set browser-facing URL mappings separately.
  3. Click Save Settings and refresh your client.

Addresses inside containers

In a container, localhost means that container.

Feature Requires Where to configure Seerr search, requests, issues, and discovery Enabled Seerr integration, reachable Seerr URL and API key; a linked, unblocked user with the relevant Seerr permissions Seerr → Seerr Connection Setup and Users; Seerr settings and permission audit Automatic season requests Configured Seerr and the automatic request switches, eligible playback, and permitted linked users Seerr → Automatic Requests; Seerr features Automatic movie requests Configured Seerr plus TMDB API Key for movie discovery, eligible playback, and permitted linked users Seerr → Seerr Connection Setup and Automatic Requests Requests page Enable Requests Page; Seerr for requests/issues, enabled Sonarr/Radarr instances with API keys for downloads/history Pages → Requests Page, Seerr, and *arr; *arr settings Calendar Enable Calendar Page and at least one configured source: enabled Sonarr/Radarr instance with API key, or Shoko URL and API key Pages → Calendar Page and *arr → Sonarr / Radarr / Shoko; *arr features Sonarr/Radarr item links and tag synchronization Enabled instances with URL and API Key. Item links also need a Jellyfin administrator account and Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages. Sync needs Enable Tags Sync and its scheduled task. *arr → Sonarr / Radarr, *arr UI Links, and Tags Sync Bazarr link A Jellyfin administrator account, one Bazarr URL, and Enable *arr Links on Detail Pages; optional Bazarr URL Mappings. No API key is needed. *arr → Bazarr; *arr settings Shoko anime Calendar entries Shoko URL, Shoko API Key, and selected episode types; Sonarr/Radarr aren't required *arr → Shoko Recommendations page Enable Recommendations Page, enabled/configured Seerr, and a linked user; studio-produced TV discovery also needs a TMDB key Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page and Seerr; Seerr features Elsewhere streaming providers and TMDB reviews TMDB API Key, the relevant switches, and appropriate TMDB item IDs Elsewhere & Reviews; Elsewhere & Reviews Settings MDBList ratings and rating synchronization MDBList API Key and the relevant display/fetch/sync switches; fetching depends on the account's available allowance Display → MDBList Ratings; MDBList settings Standalone Letterboxd links Enable Letterboxd Links; movies need an IMDb ID. No Letterboxd account/API key is configured in JE Extras → External Links; Other settings Ordinary poster rating tags Stored Jellyfin community or critic ratings; no JE TMDB/MDBList key merely to display those values Display → Media Tags or personal UI Settings; Tags & badges Service and network details

Show synced tags as links displays existing prefixed tags for viewers independently of service connections, synchronization, and administrator item links.

Bazarr links open the movies/series overview, rather than a specific item. Letterboxd links for people use a name-derived actor link; JE has no TV-series Letterboxd link. Ordinary poster rating tags display Jellyfin's stored CommunityRating or CriticRating.

JE also fetches allow-listed assets through its server-side CDN cache. A fresh installation needs upstream connectivity for uncached assets. The admin Docs tab loads this hosted documentation in your browser. Optional Share Anonymous Usage Statistics is off by default and is separate from service and asset requests; see Community Analytics.

docs.title: JE Pages & Tabs
docs.text: JE adds seven pages for bookmarks, upcoming releases, requests, and more. Choose which ones to enable and where you want users to find them. Page content and navigation have separate settings.

docs.title: Choose a placement
docs.text:
Native Home tabs are a quick way to make pages easy to reach. They need no companion plugin and work on Jellyfin 12 and 10.11.

  1. Open admin Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Pages.
  2. Enable the feature and its Add … as a native Home tab option.
  3. Click Save Settings and refresh the user's web client.

You can also choose one of the other placements below.

Placement Requires How users reach it JE standalone page JE's injected web interface; available for Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Requests, Calendar, and Recommendations JE's navigation drawer link where the layout exposes it, or the supported standalone route below. Native Home tab JE's injected web interface and that page's native-tab setting The named Home tab. If the layout hides its button, use JE's fallback header shortcut-tray link. Plugin Pages Active Plugin Pages companion and that page's Plugin Pages setting The companion's registered page entry. On Jellyfin 12's Modern Layout, sidebar entries are mobile navigation. Custom Tabs Active Custom Tabs companion, its prerequisites, that page's Custom Tabs setting, and a matching tab entry The configured tab on Home. JE can create its entry automatically or you can add it manually.

Choose one Home-tab mode per page

Native Home tabs and Custom Tabs can't be enabled together for the same page; selecting one deselects the other. JE's native tabs can coexist with unrelated Custom Tabs. Plugin Pages is a separate option and can be enabled alongside a native tab.

Modern Layout on Jellyfin 12

Desktop has no visible sidebar page links in this layout. JE's native tab button can also be hidden, so JE adds a header shortcut-tray fallback. On phones, use the drawer or Home/header links. The avatar-menu Jellyfin Enhanced entry opens personal settings; it isn't a replacement menu for every JE page.

All page-placement switches and Add the Custom Tabs entry for me start Off. Of these seven pages, only the Bookmarks feature starts On.

The automatic-entry option is hidden here because Custom Tabs isn't installed.

Activity and Catch Up need navigation

Activity and Catch Up have no JE standalone sidebar page. Enabling either feature without a tab or Plugin Pages doesn't create a navigable page.

docs.title: Bookmarks
docs.text:
Save a moment while watching so you can return to the scene later. Your timestamps are saved per account on the server.

  1. During browser playback, press B with the default binding or use the bookmark button.
  2. Open Bookmarks to play, edit, or organize saved timestamps. You don't need a companion plugin to manage them.

Use Series for episode bookmarks; each episode has its own card.

For library maintenance, see Enhanced features.

Admin Pages → Bookmarks:

Setting Default What it does Enable Bookmarks Feature On Enables bookmarking and the library. Add Bookmarks as a native Home tab Off Adds a JE-managed Home tab. Use Plugin Pages for Bookmarks Library Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs for Bookmarks Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the matching companion entry on save. Details

Without a selected tab or active Plugin Pages integration, the standalone library uses #/bookmarks.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Bookmarks Feature BookmarksEnabled Add Bookmarks as a native Home tab BookmarksUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages for Bookmarks Library BookmarksUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs for Bookmarks BookmarksUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me BookmarksAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Hidden Content
docs.text:
Keep titles or other supported items off selected surfaces, then review or unhide them in one place.

  1. Set your personal filters in the Enhanced panel's Hidden Content section.
  2. Hide items from the supported surfaces you use.
  3. Open Hidden Content to review or unhide them. Administrators can also manage other users' lists when Let admins view and manage other users' hidden content is on.

See content management and Enhanced settings.

Admin Pages → Hidden Content:

Setting Default What it does Enable Hidden Content Off Enables hide controls, filtering, management, and personal settings. Add Hidden Content as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages for Hidden Content Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs for Hidden Content Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry. Let admins view and manage other users' hidden content On Allows administrators to select another user's hidden list and use Edit to add or unhide items for that user. Details

The standalone route is #/hidden-content. Disabling the server feature preserves saved hidden items. Hiding filters supported responses and web surfaces; it doesn't revoke library access.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Hidden Content HiddenContentEnabled Add Hidden Content as a native Home tab HiddenContentUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages for Hidden Content HiddenContentUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs for Hidden Content HiddenContentUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me HiddenContentAutoCreateCustomTab Let admins view and manage other users' hidden content HiddenContentAdmin

docs.title: Requests and downloads
docs.text:
Requests brings together Seerr requests and issues with Sonarr/Radarr downloads and download history. Use it to check progress in one place. Scroll through the stacked Downloads, Requests, Issues, and History sections when their content is enabled and available.

Scroll through the combined Requests page to see downloads, requests, issues, and history.
  1. Configure Seerr for requests/issues, and enabled Sonarr/Radarr instances with API keys for downloads/history.
  2. Enable the page and choose its placement.
  3. Open Requests to inspect status. Your available actions depend on the linked Seerr user's permissions.

See *arr features, *arr settings, and Seerr permissions.

Admin Pages → Requests Page:

Setting Default What it does Enable Requests Page Off Enables the combined page. Add Requests as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages for Requests Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs for Requests Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry.

Show Downloads in Requests Page, Show Seerr Issues Section, and Show Download History Section control the page's content separately.

Details

The standalone route is #/downloads. There isn't a separate JE Downloads page, even though internal properties and this route use that name.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Requests Page DownloadsPageEnabled Add Requests as a native Home tab DownloadsUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages for Requests DownloadsUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs for Requests DownloadsUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me DownloadsAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
Browse upcoming movies and episodes from your configured Sonarr, Radarr, or Shoko sources. Shoko can be your only source.

  1. Open Calendar and select a view and filters.
  2. Open an event to see its details.

See *arr features and *arr settings for source setup and access filters.

Admin Pages → Calendar Page:

Setting Default What it does Enable Calendar Page Off Enables the Calendar. Add Calendar as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Registers the Calendar companion page. Use Custom Tabs Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry. Details

The standalone route is #/calendar. When Calendar detects its active Plugin Pages integration, its standalone page yields to that integration. Use the registered page entry rather than relying on the direct route.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Calendar Page CalendarPageEnabled Add Calendar as a native Home tab CalendarUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages CalendarUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs CalendarUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me CalendarAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
Find something to watch in trending, popular, and upcoming feeds, or browse studios, networks, and genre tiles. This discovery page is separate from recommendations on an individual item's details.

  1. Open Seerr Recommendations from its standalone link or native Home tab, or Recommendations from Plugin Pages or a JE-managed Custom Tabs entry.
  2. Open a row or category to explore it.

Seerr is required

Enable and configure Seerr, and link your user. Studio-produced TV feeds also require TMDB API Key.

See Seerr features.

Admin Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page:

Setting Default What it does Enable Recommendations Page Off Enables discovery. Add Recommendations as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry. Details

The standalone route is #/recommendations. Changing placement can't repair disabled integrations or missing upstream permissions.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Recommendations Page RecommendationsPageEnabled Add Recommendations as a native Home tab RecommendationsUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages RecommendationsUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs RecommendationsUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me RecommendationsAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
See recent watched, favorited, and reviewed activity from people on your server. Library access and author-visibility rules control what you can see.

Open Activity from a configured tab or Plugin Pages entry. See Enhanced features and Enhanced settings.

Admin Pages → Activity Feed:

Setting Default What it does Enable Activity Feed Off Enables activity recording and display. Add Activity as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry.

Choose activity types in this admin section.

Active Streams needs data collection

Show Active Streams section also needs active-stream data collection enabled in Extras. This is independent of showing the header widget.

Details

Watched activity includes qualifying partial playback, as well as completions. JE provides no standalone #/activity route.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Activity Feed ActivityFeedEnabled Add Activity as a native Home tab ActivityFeedUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages ActivityFeedUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs ActivityFeedUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me ActivityFeedAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Catch Up
docs.text:
Work through unwatched titles as a card deck. You'll see only titles you can access.

  1. Open Catch Up from a configured tab or Plugin Pages entry.
  2. Use buttons or swipe gestures to mark a title watched, dismiss it, or add it to your watchlist.

See Enhanced features for the deck and its actions.

Admin Pages → Catch Up:

Setting Default What it does Enable Catch Up Off Enables the deck. Record Catch Up activity On Records deck actions when Catch Up is enabled; admins can read the page's Activity panel. Add Catch Up as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab. Use Plugin Pages Off Registers the companion page. Use Custom Tabs Off Shows the page in a Custom Tabs container. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Manages the companion entry. Details

JE provides no standalone #/catchup route. The activity log retains the current file and one rotated file; settings and data covers its location and backups.

Internal setting names:

Setting Property Enable Catch Up CatchUpEnabled Record Catch Up activity CatchUpLogEnabled Add Catch Up as a native Home tab CatchUpUseNativeTab Use Plugin Pages CatchUpUsePluginPages Use Custom Tabs CatchUpUseCustomTabs Add the Custom Tabs entry for me CatchUpAutoCreateCustomTab

docs.title: Plugin Pages setup and fallback
docs.text:
Plugin Pages adds registered page entries through its companion plugin. Use it when you want that plugin to handle page navigation.

  1. Install and activate Plugin Pages with its prerequisites.
  2. Enable the JE feature and its Plugin Pages option above.
  3. Click Save Settings.
  4. Refresh users' web clients.

Some registration changes need a restart

Plugin Pages 3.0+ supports live registration/removal on save. Older interfaces need a Jellyfin restart after registration changes. If the server log says live registration failed, restart even with a newer version, then refresh clients.

Registration and fallback details

JE registers embedded pages with the companion, including /JellyfinEnhanced/catchUpPage. These registration URLs aren't standalone JE controller routes to substitute for web navigation.

If Plugin Pages is missing, its registered link isn't available. Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Requests, Calendar, and Recommendations have standalone implementations, with fallback navigation when no other selected placement suppresses it. Activity and Catch Up need a native tab or working Custom Tabs integration instead.

A failed companion detection probe doesn't guarantee fallback. Resolve Plugin detection issue with Retry, then save and refresh.

docs.title: Custom Tabs: automatic or manual entries
docs.text: Custom Tabs embeds JE pages on Home through its companion plugin. You can let JE manage the matching entry or add it yourself.

docs.title: Let JE manage the entry
docs.text:
Let JE create a matching companion entry when you save.

  1. Install and activate a compatible Custom Tabs version with its prerequisites, including File Transformation.
  2. Enable the JE feature, its Custom Tabs option (for example, Use Custom Tabs for Bookmarks), and Add the Custom Tabs entry for me.
  3. Click Save Settings.

The automatic control depends on detection

Add the Custom Tabs entry for me appears only when JE recognizes the installed companion's configuration structure and the page is enabled with its Custom Tabs option ticked, such as Use Custom Tabs for Bookmarks. An unrecognized structure requires manual setup. The content switch alone doesn't create a companion tab.

Entry ownership and detection details

JE creates a missing matching entry. If one already exists, JE leaves it in place and doesn't claim a manually created entry. On later saves, turning off the feature, its Custom Tabs option, or automatic management removes a matching entry only if JE owns it. Re-enabling all three creates it again.

The internal ownership flags are BookmarksCustomTabJeOwned, HiddenContentCustomTabJeOwned, DownloadsCustomTabJeOwned, CalendarCustomTabJeOwned, RecommendationsCustomTabJeOwned, ActivityFeedCustomTabJeOwned, and CatchUpCustomTabJeOwned. All default to false. They have no user-facing setting label and record ownership rather than another placement choice.

If Custom Tabs is absent, JE skips synchronization and retains stored intent for a later installation. If detection or its configuration read fails, automatic controls are hidden and an intended create can be skipped. JE settings can also save without creating the tab if the companion configuration cannot be saved. Check the save feedback, then use Retry or reload and save again.

docs.title: Add the entry yourself
docs.text:
Create your own companion entry using the matching title and content below.

  1. Leave Add the Custom Tabs entry for me off.
  2. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Custom Tabs, add a tab, and paste the matching content into HTML Content. You can use Copy beside the marker on JE's admin page or copy it from the table below.
  3. Turn on the JE feature and its Custom Tabs option too.
  4. Save both configurations and refresh the client.
Page/title Content to paste Bookmarks <div class="sections bookmarks"></div> Hidden Content <div class="jellyfinenhanced hidden-content"></div> Requests <div class="jellyfinenhanced requests"></div> Calendar <div class="jellyfinenhanced calendar"></div> Recommendations <div class="jellyfinenhanced recommendations"></div> Activity <div class="jellyfinenhanced activity"></div> Catch Up <div class="jellyfinenhanced catchup"></div> Missing or inactive Custom Tabs

Custom Tabs mode can suppress JE's standalone links without creating the expected Home container if the companion is missing or inactive. Disable that mode and choose a native tab or another available placement.

docs.title: Reach the pages on desktop and phone
docs.text:
In a layout with a visible drawer, use its page links. On Jellyfin 12 Modern Layout desktop, use Home tabs or JE's fallback header shortcut tray; on phones, use the drawer, Home, or header tray. Plugin Pages and Custom Tabs supply their own entries only when their integration is working.

Jellyfin 12 Legacy layout shows the enabled JE pages beside Home and Favorites.

On Jellyfin 12's Modern Layout, JE adds header icons when native tab buttons are hidden. When space is limited, extra actions move into the More from Jellyfin Enhanced (•••) launcher.

Use the native Home links JE generates so they keep working when other tabs move. All these page interfaces require the injected web client; native-client server effects are separate.

Administrators can open Docs → Documentation on the JE configuration page to browse the hosted docs inside the dashboard, or select Open in new tab.

Direct routes and native link identities

For enabled standalone pages, append the route below to your server's /web/index.html, including any base-URL prefix. For example, Calendar is /web/index.html#/calendar and Requests is /web/index.html#/downloads. Direct navigation opens the standalone page only when the conditions below are met.

Page Standalone route When standalone navigation is available Native link identity Bookmarks #/bookmarks Native Home tab and Custom Tabs options off; no detected Plugin Pages integration jeTab=bookmarks Hidden Content #/hidden-content Native Home tab and Custom Tabs options off; no detected Plugin Pages integration jeTab=hidden-content Requests #/downloads No detected Plugin Pages integration jeTab=requests Calendar #/calendar No detected Plugin Pages integration jeTab=calendar Recommendations #/recommendations No detected Plugin Pages integration jeTab=recommendations Activity Use a tab or Plugin Pages No standalone route jeTab=activity Catch Up Use a tab or Plugin Pages No standalone route jeTab=catchup

A detected Plugin Pages integration means the page's Plugin Pages option is enabled and JE detects its registered page entry. Use that sidebar entry instead of the standalone route. For Bookmarks or Hidden Content with native-tab placement enabled, use the generated Home link; with Custom Tabs placement enabled, open the configured Home tab. These guards prevent the standalone page from opening; they don't automatically redirect you to the selected placement.

Use the native links JE generates: they include both tab=<current index> and the stable jeTab identity. Don't hard-code a numeric tab index, because other tabs can move it.

docs.title: Settings overview
docs.text: Use the admin configuration page for server features, service connections, and starting preferences. Use the personal Enhanced panel for your account's preferences and shortcut overrides.

docs.title: The admin configuration page
docs.text:
The admin page controls server features, service connections, and starting preferences for users. Use its tabs to set up the parts of JE you want.

  1. Sign in as an administrator and open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced. On Jellyfin 12, plugin navigation can take you directly to the configuration page. On 10.11, open the installed plugin's configuration.
  2. Use Search settings... or the section shortcuts within a tab to find a control. Use Descriptions to show or hide explanatory text.
  3. Check the unsaved indicator, then click Save Settings.
  4. Refresh affected web clients.

Tab What you'll find Detailed guide Overview Service Status, Optional Dependencies, Features, and Quick Actions for connection tests, overwriting personal settings, and clearing client tag caches Defaults and resets, compatibility Display Watch progress, file information, poster/detail tags and their styles, native poster tags, Spoiler Guard, icons/theme, random-button defaults, language, awards, and MDBList ratings Enhanced settings, Tags & badges, Spoiler Guard settings Playback Tab-switch playback behavior, pause screen, long-press speed, automatic intro/outro skipping, subtitle defaults, and panel/toast timing Enhanced settings Pages Enablement, content options, and placement for Bookmarks, Hidden Content, Requests, Calendar, Recommendations, Activity, and Catch Up JE pages & tabs Seerr Connection and shared TMDB key, URL mappings, search/discovery, automatic requests, recently-added scan, watchlist sync, user import/blocking, permission audit, and response-cache diagnostics Seerr settings, permission audit *arr Sonarr/Radarr instances, one URL-only Bazarr endpoint, Shoko Calendar source, browser URL mappings, item links for administrators, and tag synchronization *arr settings Elsewhere & Reviews Streaming providers, regions, shared TMDB key, provider branding, TMDB reviews, release dates, and user reviews Elsewhere & Reviews Settings Extras UI tweaks, header shortcuts, active streams, plugin icons, Letterboxd links, and Custom Image Assets Other settings Keyboard Disable Keyboard Shortcuts and the server's shortcut bindings; click a key to edit it Enhanced features and personal shortcut controls Admin Optional usage statistics, maintenance mode, tag-cache operations, and Dev Mode Other settings, Community Analytics, Tags & badges Docs Documentation embedded from the hosted site, with Open in new tab Quick start

Select a tab to see it on the admin page.

DisplayPlaybackPagesExtrasKeyboardAdmin

In Overview, the What's New notice links to the settings groups that contain controls added since the last dismissal. Use the release-notes link for the full changelog.

Admin page details

The page uses the same route on both versions: /web/index.html#/configurationpage?name=Jellyfin%20Enhanced. Include your Jellyfin base-URL prefix if configured.

Tabs scroll when they don't fit. Search, section jumps, and links in the What's New notice don't save changes. API fields are masked when unfocused and revealed while editing.

The Docs tab loads the hosted documentation when you first select it. It isn't an offline copy bundled with the plugin; your browser needs access to the hosted site. JE retains the loaded page across tab switches. If it doesn't receive a load event within eight seconds, it replaces the frame with a message and external link. Open in new tab is available independently.

docs.title: The personal Enhanced panel
docs.text:
You can change your own preferences without administrator access. Open the panel using whichever entry fits your layout:

Where How to open it Desktop keyboard Press ? outside an input or textarea. Visible desktop or phone drawer Select Jellyfin Enhanced → Enhanced Panel. Jellyfin 12's Modern Layout exposes these drawer links on mobile. Jellyfin 12 Modern Layout avatar menu Select Jellyfin Enhanced. Jellyfin user settings menu, including on phones Select Jellyfin Enhanced - User Settings. Mobile or TV web player Select the tune button titled Jellyfin Enhanced beside the player's settings button when those controls are available; desktop layouts hide it.

  1. Use Search settings… to filter the section list by the text inside each pane, or select a section from the navigator. On desktop, the sections and selected pane sit side by side.

  2. On a phone, select a section to open its pane. Use the back arrow to return to the navigator.

    Open Jellyfin Enhanced from the avatar menu, then use the back arrow between sections.

  3. Change a preference using its control. Personal changes save as you make them; there is no admin-style Save Settings button here.

Section What you can change Detailed guide Shortcuts View bindings, record a personal key combination, disable a binding, or restore the admin binding Enhanced features Playback Settings Auto-pause, auto-resume, picture-in-picture, long-press speed, and pause screen Enhanced settings Auto-Skip Settings Personal intro/outro skipping preferences Enhanced settings Subtitle Settings Disable Custom Styles, style/color, size, font, text effect, and position Enhanced settings Random Button Settings Enablement, unwatched-only selection, item types, and random source Enhanced settings UI Settings Watch progress, file size, tag categories/order/positions, native poster preference, and other display choices Enhanced settings, Tags & badges Hidden Content Personal hide controls and surface filters, plus access to the hidden list; present when the server feature is enabled Enhanced settings Spoiler Guard Personal overrides for admin-enabled categories and Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off; present only when admin Enable Spoiler Guard is on Spoiler Guard settings Language Settings Display Language and Clear Translation Cache Enhanced settings About Version, release notes, and the repository contribution link About

Open About to check your JE version or select Release Notes or Contribute.

Some sections need an enabled feature

Controls and sections depend on enabled features. Disable Keyboard Shortcuts hides Shortcuts and stops ordinary JE shortcut handling. Auto-skip needs supported segments and playback; see compatibility.

Panel shortcut and device refresh

The panel-opening ? listener remains available even when ordinary shortcuts are disabled. Saved shortcut overrides don't change it.

Opening the panel fetches fresh settings.json. For a full update of scripts, feature availability, and other user documents on another device, refresh that client.

docs.title: Admin defaults and personal overrides
docs.text:
JE saves your starting preferences the first time your account loads JE. Changing admin defaults later doesn't replace those saved preferences, even if you never customize anything. To push new defaults to existing users, use Apply defaults to existing users.

To set starting preferences for accounts that haven't loaded JE yet, change them on the admin page and click Save Settings. To customize your own account, use the personal Enhanced panel.

Server features control availability

A personal preference can't enable a page or integration that's disabled on the server. If a child control is disabled, turn on or configure its required parent switch, key, or companion plugin first.

Setting Default What it does Admin Default UI Language System Default Starting language for a new personal settings document; doesn't force existing users to change language. Personal Display Language Starting value from Default UI Language; Auto on a fresh server Overrides JE's display language for your account; changing it saves and reloads. Admin Disable Keyboard Shortcuts Off Disables ordinary shortcut handling and hides the personal shortcut pane. Personal Disable Custom Styles Starting value from admin Disable Custom Subtitle Styles by default (Off on a fresh server) Uses Jellyfin's default subtitle styles for your account. How starting values are chosen

JE creates a missing settings.json using current admin defaults. Settings without admin defaults use built-in defaults.

Client fallbacks fill in missing values. An ordinary Save Settings updates the server configuration. Default UI Language → System Default stores an empty value.

docs.title: Apply defaults to existing users
docs.text:
Use this action when you want existing users to start over with the current defaults. It replaces saved personal preferences.

Back up before overwriting preferences

There is no per-user undo. Restore a backup or have users reapply their choices.

  1. Open Overview → Quick Actions → Overwrite everyone's personal settings.
  2. Confirm the action to save the current form and reset existing users' preferences.
  3. Have users refresh their clients.
What the overwrite action changes Data Effect of the overwrite action settings.json Replaced with current admin defaults, except watch progress mode/time format reset to Percentage / h:m regardless of Watch Progress Default / Watch Progress Time Format. Personal subtitle colors/position and random source selections reset to built-in defaults; audio language and native poster preferences return to inheriting server settings. Internal panel/Calendar view state also resets. hidden-content.json Personal filter settings reset; hidden items retained. Existing spoilerblur.json Preference overrides reset to inherit admin policy; protection lists retained. A missing file isn't created just for this reset. shortcuts.json Personal shortcut overrides retained. Bookmarks, Elsewhere settings, shared reviews/activity Not reset by this action.

Before resetting preferences, the action synchronizes managed Custom Tabs entries. It resets users with existing canonical JE user directories. A Jellyfin user without a JE directory receives the defaults when JE first creates their settings instead. If an individual reset fails, check the server log. The endpoint reports skipped settings/Hidden Content users; Spoiler Guard preference failures are logged separately. The admin success dialog isn't a per-file audit.

Clear all client tag caches and Clear Translation Cache clear caches, not personal preferences.

docs.title: Reset a shortcut
docs.text:
You can change a shortcut for your account or return to the administrator's binding.

  1. Open Shortcuts and click a displayed key.
  2. While it is listening, press your new combination. Press Backspace to remove your override and restore the current administrator binding, or Del to disable the shortcut for your account.
Shortcut rules and admin bindings

Conflicting combinations and reserved browser-player bindings are rejected. These edits save to shortcuts.json.

In admin Keyboard, the same keys edit server bindings: Backspace restores the plugin's built-in binding, and Del disables the server binding. Users with saved personal overrides can still have their own bindings. The personal panel doesn't offer a single button to reset every preference.

docs.title: Settings and data on disk
docs.text:
Your server stores JE's configuration and personal data in Jellyfin's configured directories. These paths vary by installation, so don't assume one Docker mount or operating-system path.

Use the file reference below to locate the data you want to back up. Follow Backup and restore for the copying steps.

Storage must be writable

JE needs writable configuration/data and log storage.

File locations and storage details

The admin XML is <PluginConfigurationsPath>/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced.xml (Jellyfin's ConfigurationFilePath for this plugin). The user/shared data root is:

<PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/

User directories use the Jellyfin user ID in lowercase with hyphens removed, for example a 32-character GUID, rather than the username.

Location Contents <user-id>/settings.json Main personal Enhanced preferences, including panel and Calendar view state. <user-id>/shortcuts.json Personal shortcut overrides. <user-id>/bookmark.json Saved video bookmarks. <user-id>/elsewhere.json Personal Elsewhere preferences. <user-id>/hidden-content.json Hidden items and personal filters. <user-id>/spoilerblur.json Spoiler Guard lists and preference overrides. <user-id>/processed-watchlist-items.json Watchlist-monitor processing state. reviews.json Shared user reviews. activity.json Shared watched/favorite activity records. catchup-log.jsonl, catchup-log.1.jsonl Catch Up activity log and one rotated copy, when recording is enabled. Rotation occurs after the current file exceeds 5 MiB. native-poster-tags.key Internal 32-byte secret signing personalized poster URLs. Preserve it for URL-signing continuity. cdn-cache/ Downloaded asset cache; regenerable when upstream assets are reachable.

Custom branding uses <directory containing the plugin XML>/<plugin XML filename without .xml>/custom_branding/. With the normal XML filename, that is <PluginConfigurationsPath>/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/custom_branding/. This is derived from ConfigurationFilePath; don't assume it is always the same physical root as the user documents.

Some browser state remains local, including theme selection, caches, and UI state. A server backup doesn't copy that browser storage. If the poster signing key is missing or has the wrong length, JE recreates it; previously issued personalized URLs can return original artwork until clients refresh. If the key can't be persisted, JE logs a warning and uses a key lasting only for that server process.

docs.title: Upgrade migration
docs.text:
At startup, JE updates old uppercase or hyphenated user-directory names to lowercase names without hyphens. Keep its recovery files if you're investigating preferences that changed after an upgrade.

Downgrading doesn't restore data

Installing a different plugin build doesn't automatically restore an earlier version of your data.

How migration handles existing files

JE skips already canonical names and unrelated directories.

  • If the canonical directory is absent, JE renames the old directory.
  • In the code's case-only rename branch, it renames through <directory>.case-rename-<suffix> before assigning the canonical name.
  • When it merges distinct directories, it chooses files individually by modification time; the canonical copy wins a tie. It doesn't merge settings fields or bookmark records within those files.
  • A canonical file replaced by a newer source is preserved as <file>.pre-case-merge-<suffix>. After a successful directory merge, the source is preserved as <directory>.migrated-<suffix>.

Stored JSON fields with null are skipped during deserialization so model defaults can fill those fields without discarding the rest of the document.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
A file backup lets you restore preferences and saved data after a move or a reset. JE has no general settings backup/export/import interface or bookmark export/import UI.

  1. Stop Jellyfin for a consistent copy.
  2. Back up the admin XML and the entire user/shared data root listed above. Include every user directory, shared files, the poster signing key, and any migration recovery files you want to keep.
  3. Back up the derived custom_branding directory if it is outside that root. The cdn-cache directory can be regenerated.
  4. If you use Plugin Pages or Custom Tabs, preserve their configuration as part of your Jellyfin backup too. Their entries live outside JE's XML.

To restore:

  1. While Jellyfin is stopped, copy the files to the equivalent configured paths. Retain write access for the Jellyfin service account.
  2. Install the build matching the restored server, then start Jellyfin.
  3. Refresh your clients.

Include accounts when moving the server

User documents follow Jellyfin user IDs. Restoring JE data alone doesn't recreate accounts or give a new account its old ID. Include Jellyfin's own account/server backup when moving the whole installation.

Overwrite everyone's personal settings resets preferences; it doesn't restore a backup.

docs.title: Account deletion and retained data
docs.text:
Deleting a Jellyfin user leaves that user's JE directory and shared records in place. Uninstalling JE also leaves user data behind.

For intentional cleanup, back up first. Account for the personal directory and shared stores separately; removing one personal directory doesn't remove shared records.

What deletion and uninstall do

JE's deletion handlers invalidate identity, tag-access, and review-author caches. They don't purge personal documents or the user's shared reviews, activity, or Catch Up log records. Hiding an unresolved review author doesn't erase that author's data.

JE's uninstall hook removes legacy script injection; it doesn't implement a user-data purge.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Install Jellyfin Enhanced (JE) through Jellyfin's plugin manager, then restart the server and reload the web client.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you install

  • You need Jellyfin Server 12.x or 10.11.x and administrator access.
  • Use a browser with the web interface served by that Jellyfin server.
  • The account running Jellyfin needs write access to plugin configuration/data storage and Jellyfin log storage.

See Compatibility for supported clients, layouts, historical Jellyfin releases, companion plugins, and external services.

How it works

JE normally adds its script when the server serves the web page. It does not need to modify the web directory or require File Transformation.

If you host the web interface separately from Jellyfin, check that it loads JE's scripts. JE cannot automatically add them to a page served elsewhere.

docs.title: Standard Installation
docs.text: Add the repository so Jellyfin can offer the JE build that matches your server. Then install the plugin and restart Jellyfin.

docs.title: Step 1: Add Plugin Repository
docs.text:
1. Sign in as an administrator and open Jellyfin's plugin repository management screen.

  2. Add a repository named Jellyfin Enhanced with this URL:

    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n00bcodr/jellyfin-plugins/main/manifest.json

  3. Save the repository.

Details

The shared manifest lets Jellyfin select the build that matches your server. The plugin version and its Jellyfin build target are separate: one JE release supplies builds for both supported server lines.

docs.title: Step 2: Install Plugin
docs.text:
1. Open the plugin catalog and select Jellyfin Enhanced.
  2. Install the release offered for your server.
  3. Wait for installation to finish.

docs.title: Step 3: Restart Server
docs.text: Restart the Jellyfin server to load the plugin. A browser refresh alone cannot load a newly installed server plugin.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Installation
docs.text:
1. Confirm Jellyfin Enhanced appears in Jellyfin's installed plugins and open its administrator configuration page.
  2. Reload the web client with Ctrl+F5 on Windows/Linux or Cmd+Shift+R on macOS.
  3. Open your personal panel using one of these entries:

    - Press ? while focus is outside an input or text area. - In a layout with a sidebar, select Jellyfin Enhanced → Enhanced Panel. - In the Jellyfin 12 profile menu, select Jellyfin Enhanced. - In the user preferences menu, select Jellyfin Enhanced - User Settings. - In mobile or TV web layouts, use the player button titled Jellyfin Enhanced when the player controls are available. Desktop layouts hide it.

If the panel opens, JE's client interface loaded successfully.

Details

Configure and test optional integrations separately. Opening the panel does not verify service connectivity, account permissions, background tasks, or library metadata.

If the plugin appears but the panel does not open, use Scripts Not Loading. If the plugin itself is missing, use Plugin Not Appearing After Installation.

docs.title: First settings
docs.text:
The administrator configuration page controls server features and the starting values for personal preferences. Your Enhanced Panel controls your account's personal preferences. See Settings Overview for the distinction and Quick start for what to try first.

You can also read Documentation in the administrator Docs tab. It loads the hosted docs site, so your browser needs access to that site. Select Open in new tab if it cannot load inside the settings. See Settings Overview for the admin tabs.

docs.title: Optional integrations
docs.text: Install companions or configure services only for the features you want. Check Compatibility for requirements and JE Pages & Tabs for page placement. Follow the Seerr settings, *arr settings, and Elsewhere & Reviews Settings guides for their integrations.

docs.title: Updates and backups
docs.text:
Back up JE's configuration and data before an update or server migration. Follow Settings Overview for backup instructions.

  1. Update through Jellyfin's plugin manager.
  2. Restart the server.
  3. Hard-refresh your web clients.

If the running version or behavior is still wrong, see Update Not Working.

docs.title: Troubleshooting installation
docs.text: Use this page when JE is missing, its web scripts fail to load, or an update leaves old behavior behind. For the installation sequence, use the Installation Guide. Check Compatibility before diagnosing a client or layout issue.

docs.title: Plugin Not Appearing After Installation
docs.text:
Check that Jellyfin has loaded the server plugin first. If it has, troubleshoot the personal panel next.

  1. Check Jellyfin's installed plugins for Jellyfin Enhanced. Confirm it is enabled and that you restarted Jellyfin after installation or an enable/disable change.
  2. Check the Jellyfin server log for plugin-loading errors. Record the running Jellyfin version and the build you installed.
  3. Check the loaded JE version using the address in the details below.
  4. If the server plugin loads, continue with Scripts Not Loading.
Details

Open /JellyfinEnhanced/version on the same server. Include your Jellyfin base URL prefix if configured. A successful response reports the loaded JE version; you do not need to sign in. A 404 can mean the plugin did not load or your proxy did not send the request to Jellyfin.

Clearing browser caches cannot repair a server plugin that failed to load.

docs.title: Wrong plugin build
docs.text:
Install the build that matches your Jellyfin version, then restart the server. See Compatibility for version requirements.

  1. Back up your configuration.
  2. Replace the mismatched installation using the shared repository in the Installation Guide.
  3. Restart Jellyfin.
How it works

The administrator page can show Wrong plugin build for this Jellyfin version. The startup log reports BUILD/HOST MISMATCH and the expected release asset: Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced_12.0.0.zip for Jellyfin 12, or Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced_10.11.0.zip for Jellyfin 10.11.

These filenames identify the build target, not the JE release version.

For administrator diagnostics, authenticated GET /JellyfinEnhanced/host-compat reports the build target, host target, expected asset, and manifest URL. It also checks administrator access; a signed-out request or an ordinary user cannot use it. There is no configuration switch to disable the compatibility check.

The same JE version number on two ZIP files does not make their build targets interchangeable.

docs.title: Scripts Not Loading
docs.text:
Check the page Jellyfin sends to your browser, then check whether JE's scripts load.

  1. Open browser developer tools with F12.
  2. Select the Network tab and reload the web client.
  3. Follow the page and request checks below.

Note

Keep your server's base URL prefix on all requests below.

docs.title: Check the served page
docs.text:
Look for JE's script in the original page response. Scripts may change the page after it loads, so inspect the response in Network.

  1. Inspect the HTML response and look for /JellyfinEnhanced/script?v=….
  2. If it is missing, compare direct Jellyfin access with access through your proxy. The proxy may serve an old saved page or a separately hosted web interface.
  3. Check server logs and the loading setting described below.

An independently served web client does not automatically receive JE's injection. See Compatibility for the client requirements.

How it works

Normal injection applies to GET requests whose paths end in /web, /web/, or /web/index.html, including a base URL prefix. The response must be HTTP 200 with an HTML content type and a closing </body>. JE skips injection if a JE script reference is already present.

Check server logs for Script injection middleware error. Also check whether DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware was deliberately changed in the configuration file. Its default is false. Setting it to true makes JE add its script to index.html when Jellyfin starts. There is no control for it on the administrator settings page. See Permission Issues for this older loading method.

docs.title: Check client requests
docs.text:
Check the script requests for a failed download or a response that contains the wrong kind of content.

  1. Filter Network requests by JellyfinEnhanced.
  2. Check the status, response type, and response body of the script request and /JellyfinEnhanced/bundle.js?v=….
  3. Check browser messages for blocked scripts, browser extensions, content-security-policy errors, or failed assets.

Administrator diagnostic setting, under Admin → Developer Settings:

Setting Default What it does Dev Mode Off Stops reusing saved scripts and loads them individually so you can diagnose loading errors.

Leave Dev Mode off for normal use. If you change it for diagnosis, save and reload the client. After an update, start with a hard refresh. Use the targeted controls below if only scripts, translations, tags, or images remain out of date.

How it works

JE normally loads its scripts together from /JellyfinEnhanced/bundle.js?v=…. If that request fails, JE can try loading the scripts individually. If you see individual requests, check the console for the original failure and whether loading recovered. You do not need to sign in to request the bundle or its diagnostic source map at /JellyfinEnhanced/bundle.js.map.

A 404 suggests a missing route or proxy path problem. An HTML login page returned for a JavaScript request suggests proxy authentication or rewriting.

docs.title: Background tasks are separate
docs.text:
Run Jellyfin Enhanced Startup manually after fixing an error that stopped JE's background services from starting. For a missing script with normal settings, use the page and request checks above.

How it works

Jellyfin Enhanced Startup runs when Jellyfin starts. It starts JE's background services and runs Refresh Tag Cache if the server tag cache is enabled and empty. JE normally adds its script when Jellyfin serves the web page.

If you deliberately chose the older method that writes to index.html, running the task also retries that operation.

docs.title: Update Not Working
docs.text:
Confirm Jellyfin restarted with the updated plugin, then check for an old page or script in your browser or proxy cache.

  1. Compare /JellyfinEnhanced/version with the version shown by the installed plugin. Confirm the server restarted after the update.
  2. Check Wrong plugin build if you changed Jellyfin server lines.
  3. Hard-refresh the browser, then compare the served script tag and script/bundle responses using Scripts Not Loading. Check proxy caching if local access works but remote access does not.
  4. If the installed plugin files are still wrong, back up configuration/data, remove the affected JE installation through the plugin manager, and restart. Use the Installation Guide to install the matching build again.
Details

Uninstalling JE attempts to remove any old script added to the web files and leaves your saved user data in place. Reinstalling or downgrading the plugin does not restore earlier settings; restore a backup separately if you need them. See Settings Overview for backups and restoration.

docs.title: Preferences changed after an upgrade
docs.text:
If your preferences changed after an upgrade, check for a user-folder migration error before trying to recover the data. The recovery steps below apply to a failed migration that left a .case-rename-… folder.

To recover from this failure:

  1. Find Failed to migrate user dir in the server log and identify the affected user folder.
  2. Stop Jellyfin and back up both the lowercase folder and the leftover .case-rename-… folder.
  3. Compare their files and copy the versions you want to keep into the lowercase folder. Replacing a file replaces all the settings or bookmarks inside it; keep the backups.
  4. Start Jellyfin and reload your client to check the restored data.
How it works

JE stores each user's data in a folder named with their lowercase ID, without hyphens. When Jellyfin starts, JE checks older uppercase or hyphenated folders and renames them if the lowercase folder is missing. If a hyphenated old folder and the lowercase folder both exist, JE tries to keep the newer copy of each file; the lowercase folder's copy wins when modification times match. It chooses whole files rather than combining the bookmarks or settings inside them. Keep .pre-case-merge-… file backups and .migrated-… copies of old folders when investigating unexpected changes.

On a case-sensitive filesystem, such as a typical Linux installation, you can have separate uppercase and lowercase folders for the same user. If their names differ only in capitalization, JE can move the uppercase folder to a .case-rename-… name and then fail because the lowercase folder already exists. The old data stays in that .case-rename-… folder without a file merge. JE checks old ID-named folders again on later starts, but skips folders with the .case-rename-… suffix, so restarting does not recover that data automatically.

docs.title: Wrong Plugin Build or Restart Required
docs.text:
If the configuration page shows Wrong plugin build for this Jellyfin version or the logs contain BUILD/HOST MISMATCH:, the running plugin build targets a different Jellyfin version. If the warning names a zip to install, install it from the plugin repository, then stop and start the Jellyfin service or container.

Both builds share the same plugin version number and installation path. Jellyfin's Dashboard → Restart restarts the server inside the same process and keeps the previous build loaded in memory, even after the correct file is installed. If the warning says the plugin file on disk was replaced after Jellyfin loaded it, or shows Plugin restart required (STALE PLUGIN BUILD: in the logs), start with a full process restart:

  • Linux service: sudo systemctl restart jellyfin
  • Docker: docker restart <container>
  • Windows: stop and start the Jellyfin service

Refresh the configuration page after Jellyfin starts again. If the wrong-build warning is still there, the file on disk is the wrong build too: install the zip it names, then restart the process again.

docs.title: Permission Issues
docs.text:
Find the path and operation in the full error before changing permissions. The account running Jellyfin needs write access to plugin configuration/data and log storage.

Normal script loading does not need a writable web directory. Use the table to check the affected storage.

Failing path or operation What to check User document, such as settings.json or bookmark.json Write access to JE's user-data directory for the account running Jellyfin. custom_branding upload Administrator access and write access to branding storage. cdn-cache Write access to JE's asset-cache storage. JellyfinEnhanced_yyyy-mm-dd.log Write access to Jellyfin's configured log directory. index.html Whether the operation is old-tag cleanup or deliberately enabled legacy injection.

See Settings Overview for actual storage locations and backup boundaries.

docs.title: Old-tag cleanup and the legacy fallback
docs.text:
Check whether JE was removing an old script tag or using the older method that writes a new one. An index.html error does not mean every installation needs that older method.

  1. Find Jellyfin's configured web directory and inspect its index.html for the old JE tag.
  2. Identify whether the error is reading the file or writing the cleaned version.
  3. Back up the file before removing an old tag or making a narrowly scoped permission change.
How it works

JE can attempt to remove an old JE script tag from the configured web directory's index.html. An error such as Error during cleanup of old script from index.html does not mean every installation needs on-disk injection.

JE only writes its script to index.html at startup if you deliberately set DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware=true. To return to normal script loading, restore the default false and restart. File Transformation is not required for JE's normal loading method; see Compatibility for companion-plugin roles.

docs.title: Platform-Specific Permission Issues
