docs.text: These checks apply to the failing storage path, or to web-file cleanup/legacy injection when those operations are actually involved. Paths and service identities vary by installation.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Check the container's actual Jellyfin UID/GID, the affected bind mount or volume, host ownership, and whether the mount is read-only.

Normal JE installations do not require an index.html bind mount.

Details

A path such as /jellyfin/jellyfin-web/index.html is an example, not a requirement for every image.

If you deliberately maintain an index.html bind mount for the older script-loading method, update it when you upgrade the container's web interface. An old copied page can break after a Jellyfin upgrade. To return to normal loading, set DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware=false and restart Jellyfin.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Identify the account that actually runs the Jellyfin service or process. Check that account's permissions on the specific failing configuration, log, or web file. Do not assume the account is NETWORK SERVICE or grant write access to the entire installation tree.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text: Identify the service user and configured data, log, and web paths. Check ownership, parent-directory access, mount flags, and any service or security-policy restrictions for the failing operation. Avoid recursive ownership or permission changes across system installation directories.

docs.title: Stale caches or missing assets
docs.text:
Use the action that matches the stale or missing content. Clearing all browser storage is not routine maintenance and does not replace saved server preferences.

Symptom Targeted action Old scripts after an update Hard-refresh; inspect the script version and proxy cache using Scripts Not Loading. Stale translation strings Personal Language Settings → Clear Translation Cache reloads this browser. Refresh Translation Cache signals clients to refresh translations on their next page load. See Translation Updates for bundled-locale limits. Stale browser tag data With Server-Side Tag Cache off, use administrator Overview → Quick Actions → Clear all client tag caches, or Display → Clear All Client Caches, then reload affected clients. Stale server tag data Refresh Tag Cache updates changed entries and rebuilds the cache when needed. Admin → Tag Cache → Rebuild Server Tag Cache starts a full rebuild. Missing locally mirrored icons or other CDN assets Check asset requests and server logs; run Refresh CDN Assets after repairing upstream connectivity. See the details below for the request path.

The admin Display controls for tag caching are:

Setting Default What it does Server-Side Tag Cache On Enables the server cache and its background maintenance. Exclude libraries from the tag cache Off; no libraries selected Excludes the selected libraries when the switch is on. Both the switch and a selection are needed. Persist Tag Fallback Cache in Browser Storage Off Saves tag data in your browser when the server cache is off.

See Media tags if tags are missing or show incorrect information.

Details

Clear all client tag caches and Clear All Client Caches are both hidden while server caching is on. Use the server-cache actions instead.

Turning off Server-Side Tag Cache checks Persist Tag Fallback Cache in Browser Storage automatically. Saving enables it whenever the server cache is off.

Refresh Tag Cache runs daily at 03:00 by default. Starting background services, updating the server cache, rebuilding it completely, and clearing browser caches are separate actions. Choose the one that matches your problem.

For missing CDN assets, check /JellyfinEnhanced/cdn/{source}/{path} and server logs.

docs.title: CDN connectivity and limits
docs.text:
Restore your server's internet connection, then run Refresh CDN Assets if locally served images or icons are missing. JE serves saved copies through Jellyfin, but it still needs internet access to fetch assets it has not saved yet.

Note

A fresh offline installation may be missing those files. Material Symbols fonts are included with the plugin.

How it works

JE downloads supported external images and other assets, stores copies, and serves them through your Jellyfin server.

Refresh CDN Assets runs at startup and every 24 hours. JE and your browser keep downloaded assets for 24 hours before checking for updates. If JE cannot download an asset and has no saved copy, it waits five minutes before trying again. It can keep serving an older saved copy if the download fails. Each asset can be up to 8 MiB; JE removes older files to keep its saved copies within 512 MiB. These limits are fixed. If one download times out, the task continues with the remaining files unless you cancel it.

docs.title: Admin Config Page Tabs Not Switching
docs.text:
Compare direct local access with your remote URL. If the tabs work locally, check your proxy before changing plugin settings.

  1. If you use Cloudflare Rocket Loader, try disabling it for your Jellyfin hostname and reload. It modifies script execution and can interfere with the admin page.
  2. If the problem remains, check browser console and Network errors.
Details

The current tabs are Overview, Display, Playback, Pages, Seerr, *arr, Elsewhere & Reviews, Extras, Keyboard, Admin, and Docs.

A proxy authentication page returned in place of JSON or JavaScript is a different failure from an unreachable service. For Seerr and *arr, server connection URLs must be reachable by Jellyfin without an interactive browser sign-in; user-facing URL mappings are separate. Follow Seerr settings or *arr troubleshooting for service-specific diagnosis.

docs.title: Plugin detection issue
docs.text:
Fix the failed plugin-list request, then click Retry. Plugin detection issue means JE could not reliably check optional plugins; it does not by itself prove a companion is missing.

After enabling or disabling a companion, restart Jellyfin so detection reflects the running plugins. See JE Pages & Tabs for placement and registration requirements.

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text: Collect the failed request, console error, and relevant server log using How do I gather logs for bug reports?. Then report an issue or use the support channels.

docs.title: Other Features
docs.text:
Personalize Jellyfin's web interface, inspect active streams, add external ratings, and manage maintenance windows. These features come with Jellyfin Enhanced; you do not need to install the optional UI scripts separately. See Other Settings for the settings reference.

Where to find these controls

“Other” is a documentation category. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced; administrator controls are spread across Display, Playback, Extras, Pages, and Admin.

Web enhancements need supported Jellyfin page layouts and markup. See Compatibility for clients and layouts.

docs.title: Custom Branding
docs.text: Replace Jellyfin's logos, banners, browser favicon, and touch icon with your own images. You do not need to edit jellyfin-web files or install another branding plugin.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open the admin Extras tab → Custom Image Assets.
  2. Click a slot or drop an image onto it. Upload starts immediately; wait for ✓ Uploaded.
  3. Check the preview and measured dimensions where available, then reload Jellyfin. Use Ctrl+F5 if the old asset remains cached.
  4. To replace a file, upload again. To remove it, use that slot's trash button; deletion acts immediately and restores stock-asset fallback.
Upload an icon, refresh to see it, then delete it and refresh to restore the stock logo.

Uploads apply immediately

Save Settings applies configuration fields such as the splash override. Uploaded files do not wait for Save Settings. Replacing them normally needs a browser reload rather than a server restart.

docs.title: Asset slots
docs.text:
All slots are administrator uploads under Extras → Custom Image Assets.

Setting Default What it does Icon Transparent Stock icon Top-left logo beside the server version; recommended 536×536 transparent PNG. Favicon Stock favicon Browser tab icon; UI recommends 256×256 for PNG and lists ICO, PNG, or SVG. Prefer ICO. Banner Dark Stock banner Light-mode loading banner; recommended 1302×378. Banner Light Stock banner Dark-mode loading banner; recommended 1302×378. Apple Touch Icon Stock touch icon iOS Home Screen and supported PWA touch icons; recommended 180×180 PNG.

Formats and limits

Use PNG for the PNG slots and ICO for the favicon. Uploads accept image MIME types up to 10 MiB; dimensions are recommendations.

How it works

JE's middleware serves the uploaded files without converting them. PNG slots are stored and served as .png, and the favicon as .ico. Use matching content even though the banner UI also lists JPG/WebP and the favicon UI lists PNG/SVG. See the asset reference for fixed filenames.

docs.title: Storage and troubleshooting
docs.text:
Keep the branding directory writable and persistent. If branding does not appear, confirm upload success, reload, and check server logs and storage permissions.

Details

Files are stored in:

<JE configuration-file directory>/<JE configuration-file basename>/custom_branding/

The absolute path varies by Jellyfin installation. Assets survive server/web updates when the configuration storage is retained; deleting custom files removes the overrides.

JE's middleware handles supported hashed branding filenames and Jellyfin 12's sized touch icons. If a custom file is absent or cannot be served, Jellyfin serves its stock asset. JE does not rewrite every arbitrary image URL.

The configuration-only DisableBrandingMiddleware property defaults to false; true bypasses the overrides. There is no visible settings-page switch for it. It does not disable the separate JavaScript splash.

docs.title: Icon Settings
docs.text: Choose the icons you see in JE's panel headings and ordinary toast notifications.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Display → Icons & Theme and enable Use Icons in UI.
  2. Choose Icon Style.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload.
Setting Default What it does Use Icons in UI On Displays helper icons in supported JE UI regions. Icon Style Emoji Chooses Emoji, Lucide Icons, or Material UI Icons. Requires Use Icons in UI. Details

This does not replace every Jellyfin icon or every extra's own icons. Unsupported helper entries fall back to emoji. Metadata Icons controls a separate stylesheet for item metadata and external links.

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
Customize the dashboard, login screen, and user-preferences menu with these optional enhancements.

How to use: Most switches are under admin Extras → UI Tweaks. Turn on the switch you want, click Save Settings, and reload the affected page.

Details

The user Activity Feed is a separate feature under Pages → Activity Feed. See Enhanced Features and Enhanced Settings for its watch, favorite, review, and page-delivery controls. Dashboard icon coloring does not change that feed.

Its Active Streams section needs the stream-widget switch and, for non-admins, the viewer-access switch. It polls every 15 seconds while its container and document are visible. The header widget described below refreshes on demand.

docs.title: Colored Activity Icons
docs.text:
Give matching events in the dashboard Home activity list predefined Material icons and colors, making them easier to distinguish.

These icons belong to dashboard activity, separate from the JE Activity Feed.

How to use: Enable Colored Dashboard Icons under admin Extras → UI Tweaks, save, and open the dashboard Home page. The full Activity page is unchanged.

Setting Default What it does Colored Dashboard Icons Off Applies predefined replacements to supported dashboard event entries. Details

There is no color picker. Matching depends on supported event wording and expected dashboard markup; unmatched text receives no mapped replacement. This is separate from the user Activity Feed.

docs.title: Colored Ratings
docs.text:
Color official age/content classifications, including PG-13, TV-MA, and supported international boards. This feature does not color TMDB, IMDb, or Rotten Tomatoes numerical review scores.

How to use: Enable Colored Ratings Backgrounds under admin Extras → UI Tweaks, save, and open a detail page with an official rating.

Setting Default What it does Colored Ratings Backgrounds Off Applies classification-specific backgrounds to supported official-rating chips.

No ratings API key is needed.

How it works

Supported styling includes country-prefixed ratings, bare classifications, US TV descriptors, and ESRB labels. German forms such as DE-12 and FSK 12 normalize to FSK-12, with FSK-specific colors. Unknown classifications use a neutral blue-grey background. This is separate from MDBList Ratings and poster tags.

docs.title: Login Image Display
docs.text:
Select a user card on the login screen to show that user's profile picture above the password field. The picture replaces the username area while it is shown.

How to use: Enable Profile Picture on Login under admin Extras → UI Tweaks, save, and reload the signed-out login page. Select a user with a profile picture.

Setting Default What it does Profile Picture on Login Off Displays the selected login card's avatar above the password field on supported markup. Details

JE matches the selected username to an available login user card. If no matching card or image is available, or the image fails to load, JE restores the ordinary form. Hidden users entered through Manual Login have no matching public card, so their avatar is not shown.

docs.title: Plugin Icons
docs.text:
Replace supported dashboard plugin-menu icons with a mixture of Material icons and image logos. You can also add links to existing plugin configuration pages.

How to use:

  1. Enable Custom Plugin Menu Icons under admin Extras → UI Tweaks.

  2. To add a configuration-page link, open Extras → External Links → Sidebar Custom Links. Enter one pair per line, using the exact decoded page name, including spaces:

    Configuration Page Name | Material Icon Name

    For example:

    Jellyfin Enhanced | tune

  3. Click Test Links to preview the entered links in the current window until refresh.

  4. Click Save Settings to persist the configuration, then reload the dashboard sidebar.
Setting Default What it does Custom Plugin Menu Icons Off Replaces matching plugin-link icons and enables saved custom configuration-page links. Sidebar Custom Links Empty Under Extras → External Links; adds one configuration-page name/icon pair per line. How it works

Built-in replacements are:

Plugin link Replacement Jellyfin Enhanced Jellyfish image/favicon JavaScript Injector JavaScript image logo Intro Skipper redo Reports insert_chart_outlined JellySleep dark_mode (matches Jellysleep in the route) Home Screen Sections dashboard_customize File Transformation file_open Newsletters newspaper Segment Editor content_cut Jellyfin Helper Image logo Moonbase Image logo

These replacements require matching rendered plugin links. They do not install plugins, and layouts without the supported dashboard sidebar markup may not show them.

JE builds a #/configurationpage?name=... link. The second field is an icon name, not a URL. Saved custom links depend on Custom Plugin Menu Icons.

docs.title: Plugin revision display
docs.text:
JE makes supported dashboard plugin-detail pages easier to scan by hiding repeated version rows. It keeps the first row for each version within each revision list.

How to use: Open a plugin's detail page. This runs automatically, with no dedicated setting.

Details

This only changes presentation. It does not delete packages, reorder rows, change installation handlers, or install a version. It relies on Jellyfin 12-style MUI accordion markup; do not expect the same presentation on every 10.11 layout.

docs.title: Theme Selector
docs.text:
Choose a color palette from Jellyfin's user-preferences menu. Install the Jellyfish base theme natively first; the selector imports color palettes for that theme.

How to use:

  1. Enable Theme Selector (Jellyfish) under admin Extras → UI Tweaks, click Save Settings, and reload.
  2. Open Jellyfin's user-preferences menu and choose a palette under Theme. Choosing one fades and reloads the page.
  3. For a daily random palette, use the shuffle button with the tooltip Random daily theme. It shows Daily while daily randomization is enabled. Enabling it can immediately choose a palette and reload the page.
Choose Coral and Forest, then enable Daily to apply a random palette. Setting Default What it does Theme Selector (Jellyfish) Off Admin switch that makes the selector available. Theme Default Personal, browser-stored palette selection. Default removes the imported palette. Random daily theme Off Personal, browser-stored daily randomization choice. Details

The 16 choices are Default, Aurora, Banana, Coal, Coral, Forest, Grass, Jellyblue, Jellyflix, Jellypurple, Lavender, Midnight, Mint, Ocean, Peach, and Watermelon.

Selections use user-prefixed browser storage rather than JE's server-stored personal settings. Daily selection uses a UTC date and is evaluated during initialization; an already-open page does not necessarily switch at midnight. This selector changes native Jellyfish colors and is not a KefinTweaks theme selector.

docs.title: Active Streams Widget
docs.text:
See who is watching, what they are playing or have paused, and how Jellyfin is delivering each stream. Administrators can also broadcast a native Jellyfin message.

How to use:

  1. Enable Active Streams Header Widget under admin Extras → UI Tweaks, click Save Settings, and reload.
  2. Click the stream icon in the Jellyfin header to open the panel. Its title shows the active-stream count, or No Active Streams when none are playing.
  3. Click the Refresh sessions icon with the tooltip Refresh for current data. The footer shows the last update time.
Setting Default What it does Active Streams Header Widget Off Adds the counter and sessions panel, available to administrators by default. Show widget to non-admins Off Gives signed-in non-admin viewers access to current sessions. How it works

The widget fetches at initialization, opening, and Refresh, without continuous background polling. Cards can show:

  • Item/episode title and navigation to its detail page.
  • Playing/paused state, position, runtime, and playback progress.
  • Direct-play/transcoding badges, codecs, bitrate, and dimensions/frame rate when supplied.
  • Transcoding reasons, supported codec-conversion details, and an amber transcode-buffer progress layer when reported.
  • User name/avatar, client, device, and — for administrators only — IP address.

During playback, JE also places the control in supported player-overlay header markup and positions the panel beneath it. Technical details depend on the session data supplied by Jellyfin; dimensions and frame rate are not guaranteed for Direct Play.

The Direct Play badge checks whether video is being transcoded. It can appear alongside audio-transcode reasons and codec-conversion badges when the video is copied but the audio is converted.

Header appearance Meaning Play icon, no badge No active streams. Person icon with 1 One playing stream. Group icon with count Multiple streams, including mixed playing/paused states. Pause icon with count All streams paused. Red icon Session retrieval failed.

Non-admin session visibility

Show widget to non-admins exposes other users' current titles, names, clients, devices, and playback information. It does not apply the historical Activity Feed's library-access filtering. IP addresses and broadcasting remain admin-only.

docs.title: Broadcast messages
docs.text:
Send a native Jellyfin message to signed-in sessions, including idle sessions.

How to use (administrators):

  1. Click the megaphone button with the tooltip Broadcast message.
  2. Fill in the form below and click Send. Use Cancel to close the form.
Field Default What it does Title (optional) Empty Optional heading; the browser input limits it to 200 characters. Some clients, including web presentations, may not show it. Message (required) Empty Nonblank body; the browser input limits it to 1000 characters. Put the important information here. Timeout (s): 10 seconds Message duration; the input declares 1–3600 seconds. Zero uses 10 seconds. How it works

Broadcasting attempts delivery to signed-in sessions with usable user names, including idle sessions. The result reports sent/skipped sessions and errors. Delivery and display depend on the client supporting Jellyfin messages.

The UI character limits are not equivalent server validators. The send handler does not clamp the timeout to the input bounds.

docs.title: Timeout Settings
docs.text: Adjust how long the Enhanced panel and ordinary JE toasts remain visible.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Playback → Shortcuts Panel & Toast Timing.
  2. Enter durations in milliseconds and try Preview autoclose or Preview toast.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload to use the new durations.
Setting Default What it does Shortcuts Panel Autoclose Delay (ms) 15000 ms (15 seconds) Inactivity delay before the Enhanced panel closes. Toast Notification Duration (ms) 1500 ms (1.5 seconds) Duration of ordinary JE toast notifications. Details

Hover clears the panel timer; leaving restarts it. Movement, clicks, scrolling, and dragging reset timing. The number inputs have no declared minimum/maximum. Zero uses the corresponding client default and does not disable panel auto-close.

The admin toast help text says 3000 ms, but this release's server default and client fallback are 1500 ms. Previews have their own fallback/cap behavior, described in Other Settings. Hidden Content's eight-second Undo toast and broadcast timeouts are independent.

docs.title: Letterboxd Integration
docs.text: Add a Letterboxd external link to supported movie and person detail pages.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Extras → External Links and turn on Enable Letterboxd Links.
  2. Optionally enable Show link as text, then click Save Settings and reload.
  3. Open a movie with an IMDb ID, or a person detail page, and click Letterboxd.
Setting Default What it does Enable Letterboxd Links Off Adds supported movie/person links. Show link as text Off Uses Letterboxd text instead of an icon.

Metadata Icons uses icon links

Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) disables the text option and forces it off on save.

How it works

Movie links use an IMDb redirect (https://letterboxd.com/imdb/<IMDb ID>), not TMDB mapping. Movies without IMDb IDs are skipped. Person links use a name-derived actor slug. Ambiguous names or names that cannot produce a usable slug may fail.

Series do not receive this standalone link treatment. The page needs a supported external-links area.

docs.title: Metadata Icons
docs.text: Show supported item metadata and external links as icons using Druidblack's metadata-icon stylesheet.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Extras → External Links and turn on Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack).
  2. Click Save Settings and reload.
  3. Open an item detail page to see its metadata and external links.
Setting Default What it does Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) Off Styles supported metadata and external links, and forces Letterboxd and *arr links into icon mode. How it works

JE loads public-icon.css through its local asset service. The stylesheet determines which metadata it can style. This is separate from Use Icons in UI, Icon Style, and poster tags.

docs.title: MDBList Ratings
docs.text: Show ratings from multiple sources on detail pages. You can also fill Jellyfin's own Community/Critic Rating fields, using either feature or both.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Get an API key from MDBList preferences.
  2. Open admin Display → MDBList Ratings and turn on Enable MDBList Ratings.
  3. Enter MDBList API Key and click Check to test it and inspect quota/reset information. This works before saving.
  4. Leave Show Ratings Row on Item Details on for badges. Expand Configure ratings shown to choose sources and reorder them with the arrows.
  5. Click Save Settings, reload, and open a supported item with a TMDB ID.
Setting Default What it does Enable MDBList Ratings Off Master switch. MDBList API Key Empty Account key used by the server. Show Ratings Row on Item Details On Enables source badges when the master is on. Configure ratings shown All returned sources (empty list) Selects and orders detail-page badges independently of synchronization sources. Show % Symbol Off Adds % only to normalized badge scores.

These controls apply server-wide under admin Display → MDBList Ratings. They are not personal settings.

How it works

Based on xroguel1ke's original script.

MDBList ratings requests are proxied through JE, so ordinary viewers do not need the key. Administrators can view, edit, and test it in plugin configuration.

docs.title: The ratings row
docs.text:
See badges from your chosen rating sources on supported detail pages.

TMDB IDs are required

Movies and series need TMDB IDs. Seasons and episodes use their parent series' TMDB ID and series ratings. Missing IDs, no usable rating data, or unsupported page markup can leave the page without a row.

To hide the row, turn off Show Ratings Row on Item Details. An empty source list shows all returned sources, including when every badge checkbox is unchecked.

How it works

JE prefers placement before external links, then uses metadata or other detail-page anchors. Placement varies with layout and theme. The default order prioritizes TMDB, RT Critic, RT Audience, IMDb, Trakt, and Metascore, followed by remaining returned sources. You can also select Metacritic User, Letterboxd, Roger Ebert, MAL, AniList, and Master; see the source reference.

Badges use source logos or text, show vote-count tooltips when available, and link to source pages where enough information exists. Some links are derived; some badges, such as Master without a source URL, stay unlinked. There are no numerical red/yellow/green score bands.

Normalized Score values are shown on a 0–100 scale, optionally with %. Raw Value fallbacks keep their source scale and precision, such as 3.5, without %. RT Critic uses a red tomato for normalized scores of 60 or higher and a green splat below 60; without a normalized score, it falls back to MDBList's Fresh/Rotten flag.

docs.title: Filling in Jellyfin's own ratings
docs.text:
Fill Jellyfin's Community/Critic Rating fields from MDBList data. Fetching ratings and writing them to Jellyfin are separate tasks.

How to use:

  1. Under admin Display → MDBList Ratings, enable the MDBList master and the matching task switches.
  2. Choose your sources, fallbacks, reserve, and overwrite behavior below, then click Save Settings.
  3. For initial library-wide synchronization, open Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks. Run Fetch Ratings from MDBList, then Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin.
  4. Add your own triggers for recurring runs; neither task has a default trigger.
Task Default trigger What it does Fetch Ratings from MDBList None Fetches missing/stale movie/series data into the MDBList cache. Makes API calls, without changing Jellyfin rating fields. Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin None Writes Jellyfin rating fields from available cache data. Makes no MDBList API calls.

All controls below are under admin Display → MDBList Ratings.

Setting Default What it does Fetch Ratings from MDBList Off Allows the Fetch task to run. Fetch Task Reserve 400 Stops Fetch when the remaining account quota is at or below the reserve. Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin Off Allows the Sync task to run. Star Rating Source (Community Rating) TMDB Primary source for Community Rating. Star Rating Fallback Source None Used when the primary source has no usable score. Tomato Rating Source (Critic Rating) RT Critic Primary source for Critic Rating. Tomato Rating Fallback Source None Used when the primary source has no usable score. Overwrite Existing Jellyfin Ratings Off Preserves existing fields when off; replaces fields with usable selected-source data when on. How it works

Both tasks are registered regardless of their switches. Browsing can also populate data usable by Sync, so Fetch does not have to be enabled for Sync to use already-cached ratings.

Sync considers non-virtual movies/series with numeric TMDB IDs. It prefers normalized scores; only TMDB and RT Critic may fall back to raw values. Community Rating divides the selected result by ten; Critic Rating uses it directly. Roger Ebert is available for badges, not synchronization. Source selectors and fallback choices are listed in Other Settings.

With overwrite off, each populated field is preserved independently. A missing Community or Critic Rating can still be filled later; an item is skipped entirely only when both are populated. With overwrite on, usable cached values can replace existing provider or manually edited ratings. Missing source data does not erase fields. These Jellyfin fields are also what JE's community/critic poster and player tags read; the detail-page MDBList badges remain independent.

docs.title: Batching
docs.text:
Fetch skips fresh ratings on later runs.

Batch requests and retries

Fetch requests up to 150 distinct TMDB IDs of the same media type per batch. Each matched title's response includes its available rating sources, so the same server cache supports both badges and Sync. A failed batch preserves existing stale entries or missing entries for a later retry; it does not turn the entire batch into one-hour failure records.

docs.title: How refreshing works
docs.text:
JE caches ratings for found MDBList titles for seven days. A later detail lookup or Fetch run can refresh them after expiry.

Other caches and saved Jellyfin ratings Data Refresh behavior Confirmed no match Cached for three days. Failed individual lookup Retry placeholder lasts one hour. Browser display results Additional response-cache layer for revisits; cleared on a user switch. Jellyfin Community/Critic fields Updated only by Sync here, from available cached data. They are persisted metadata, not another expiring display cache.

Server MDBList data is stored in mdblist-ratings.json under <Jellyfin plugins directory>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/. Running Sync frequently does not fetch newer upstream values. With overwrite off, already-populated fields remain unchanged even after the MDBList cache refreshes.

docs.title: Account quota
docs.text:
JE uses your MDBList account status to track limits, remaining quota, and reset time.

Quota checks and safeguards

Server status is cached for about three minutes, and JE adjusts its cached remaining count after requests. Check can test an unsaved key without replacing the saved key's quota cache.

Both individual and batch requests stop at a five-request safety margin when status is known. Fetch additionally observes Fetch Task Reserve and stops conservatively if account status cannot be read. Individual lookups may proceed when status is unavailable. These checks do not reserve capacity against other applications using the same MDBList account. Consult MDBList's API documentation for account-plan and short-window limits rather than assuming a fixed allowance.

If no badges appear, check the master/display switches, key status, TMDB metadata, and available source data. If Jellyfin's own fields stay unchanged, check the Sync switch, cached data, chosen sources, and overwrite setting. Failed batches are logged and can be retried on a later Fetch run.

docs.title: Content Warnings
docs.text: Show community-voted content warnings, such as "a dog dies", gore or flashing lights, on movie and series pages. The data comes from DoesTheDogDie, and each user chooses which triggers matter to them.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Create a DoesTheDogDie account and copy the API key from your profile page.
  2. Open admin Display → Content Warnings (DoesTheDogDie) and turn on Show Content Warnings.
  3. Paste the key into DoesTheDogDie API Key, click Save Settings, and reload the web client.
  4. Open a movie or series that DoesTheDogDie knows about. A Content Warnings section appears above Reviews.
  5. Click the gear icon on the section to choose your own triggers.
Setting Default What it does Show Content Warnings Off Master switch. The section also needs a saved key. DoesTheDogDie API Key Empty Account key used by the server. Viewers never see it.

docs.title: Reading the section
docs.text:
Each chip is one trigger with the share of votes that say it happens in the title and the total number of votes, for example A dog dies 91% · 1,509. Hover a chip to see the yes/no split.

Colour Share of "yes" votes Red 90% and above Orange 75% to 89% Yellow 50% to 74% Green One of your picked triggers, reported as not happening

Before you pick anything, the section lists every trigger that most voters say is present, most-voted first. Topics with fewer than three votes are left out so a single stray vote cannot headline the list.

docs.title: Choosing your triggers
docs.text:
The gear icon opens a searchable list of all DoesTheDogDie topics, grouped by category. Tick the ones you care about and click Save. The choice is personal and stored server-side with your other settings, so it follows you between devices.

After you have picked triggers:

  • Your triggers are shown first, with a summary such as "2 of your 5 triggers reported for this title".
  • A picked trigger that voters say does not happen shows as a green "not reported" chip.
  • A picked trigger nobody has voted on for this title is not shown, because no data is not the same as "does not happen".
  • Everything else is folded behind + N other triggers. Click it to expand and click again to fold.

docs.title: Request budget
docs.text:
DoesTheDogDie's free tier allows 5,000 requests a month for the whole server and is for non-commercial use only. JE keeps requests low:

  • One shared cache serves every user, and your personal trigger filter is applied in the browser, so it costs nothing.
  • A title that has not been opened before costs two requests. After that it costs none: results are kept for 30 days, and a title DoesTheDogDie does not know is remembered for 14 days.
  • Several people opening the same new title at once share one lookup.
  • JE reads the remaining monthly and per-minute allowance from every response, stops looking up new titles when about 100 requests remain for the month, and pauses all lookups when DoesTheDogDie reports a rate limit.
  • The topic list for the picker is refreshed about once a month.

Attribution

DoesTheDogDie requires the text "Powered by DoesTheDogDie.com" next to its data. JE shows it under the section and links it to the title's page on their site. The wording is fixed and is not translated.

If nothing appears, check that the master switch is on and a key is saved, that the item has a TMDB ID, and that DoesTheDogDie has the title. Seasons and episodes use their parent series. Lookups that fail are retried after an hour.

docs.title: Hidden Content
docs.text:
Hide and restore content with JE's per-user tools.

How to use: Follow Content Management, the canonical guide for usage, filtering limits, page placement, and administrator management. See Enhanced Settings for the server controls and personal defaults.

docs.title: Splash Screen
docs.text: Show your logo on a black full-screen loading overlay while Jellyfin starts. The logo fits inside the screen, with a decorative progress bar; this is a loading screen rather than a persistent login background.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Extras → Custom Image Assets and turn on Enable Splash Screen Override.
  2. Enter Splash Screen Image URL and check that the URL opens an image in your browser.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload.
Setting Default What it does Enable Splash Screen Override Off Enables JE's loading overlay. Splash Screen Image URL /web/assets/img/banner-light.png Supplies the logo from a browser-reachable URL or suitable same-origin path. Details

Use a logo that remains legible within approximately 250×250 px. A remote URL is supported; you do not need to copy files into jellyfin-web. For same-origin paths, include your configured application base where needed: the default /web/... path assumes Jellyfin is served at the origin root.

JE uses the image URL as entered; it does not discover Jellyfin's current hashed banner filename for you. Test the URL instead of assuming the default path exists.

Progress is decorative, not a measured percentage of server work. JE detects application readiness and fades the overlay out, with a 20-second fallback timeout. If the UI is already ready, the overlay may appear only briefly. It suppresses a competing Media Bar splash while active; test combinations of loading-screen customizations if the presentation looks wrong.

docs.title: Internationalization
docs.text: Use community translations for JE's interface, with an administrator default and a personal language choice.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
• Administrator default: Open Display → Default Language, choose Default UI Language, and click Save Settings.
  • Personal choice: Open Enhanced Panel from the sidebar. Under Language Settings → Display Language, select a language or Auto. Your choice saves to the server and browser language key, then reloads the page.
Setting Default What it does Default UI Language System Default (empty) Admin default for users without a saved personal selection. Display Language Auto (empty before the admin default supplies a starting value) Per-user override in Language Settings, including an explicitly saved Auto.

The admin setting is a dropdown, not an arbitrary-code text field. It does not force users who already have a saved language choice to change.

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text:
You can choose from these bundled languages; pr is Pirate:

ar, bg, ca, cs, da, de, en-GB, en-US, es, et, fa, fi, fr, gsw,
he, hu, it, ko, ml, nl, no, pl, pr, pt, pt-BR, ru, sk, sv, tr,
uk, zh-CN, zh-HK

Bundled files and language choices

Version 12.12.0.0 bundles 33 locale files. The bundled server list excludes base en, giving 32 locale entries; regional English variants are selectable.

The admin selector adds System Default, and the personal selector adds Auto. Both selectors can discover additional upstream locale choices. Translation completeness varies by locale.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Your saved personal language choice takes precedence over the admin default, even when that choice is Auto.

Translation loading and cache

Automatic loading uses the browser's user language key when populated, then Jellyfin's resolved document language, with English as fallback. A server-saved choice supplies the starting browser value only when that key is absent; changing language on another device does not replace an existing browser choice.

JE reuses a valid versioned browser translation cache for up to 24 hours. When loading fresh data, it tries the bundled locale first and uses remote fallback through the server's local asset route when needed. Old-version browser entries are removed after a plugin update.

The loader builds regional, base-language, and English candidates, but an individual candidate's internal English fallback can succeed before the outer loop reaches the base language. Do not assume every unsupported regional code resolves to its base translation.

docs.title: Contributing Translations
docs.text:
Help translate JE through Contributing Translations.

To clear your browser's cached translations, use Clear Translation Cache under personal Language Settings. This reloads the page without resetting your feature preferences or language choice.

Details

Loading still prefers bundled data. Upstream changes do not immediately replace a usable bundled locale in this release. The server Refresh Translation Cache task under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks → Jellyfin Enhanced is a separate signal for clients on their next load and runs at startup.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text: Warn users during server work, optionally restrict non-admin accounts or remote connections, and restore JE's recorded changes when the window ends.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Admin → Maintenance Mode.
  2. Enter Login Page Banner Message and Active Session Notification.
  3. Under Action, choose Disable user accounts, Disable remote connections, both, or neither.
  4. Choose Affected Users: All non-admin users or Select specific users.
  5. Set Duration (minutes); 0 means until disabled.
  6. Turn on Enable Maintenance Mode and click Save Settings.
  7. To end manual maintenance, turn off Enable Maintenance Mode and save. Check logs/status if policies do not restore as expected.

Saving can restrict access immediately

The default manual action disables non-admin accounts. Leave both Action boxes unchecked for a banner/notification-only window. Administrators are excluded from policy changes. An empty specific-user selection means all eligible non-admin users; Deselect All does not mean “affect nobody.”

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
All settings are server controls under admin Admin → Maintenance Mode.

Setting Default What it does Enable Maintenance Mode Off Applies a manual maintenance window on save. Duration (minutes) 0 Sets the manual end time; 0 is open-ended. Login Page Banner Message This server is currently undergoing maintenance. Please try again. Plain-text web banner. Active Session Notification Server undergoing maintenance. Native message attempted after successful manual Enable on applicable saves. Remind on playback start Off Reminds affected non-admin sessions, with a five-minute cooldown. Disable user accounts On under Action Disables affected accounts' login. Disable remote connections Off under Action Disables affected users' remote access; LAN remains available if accounts stay enabled. Affected Users All non-admin users Shared target selection for manual and scheduled windows.

See Other Settings for input bounds, action encodings, and blank-message behavior.

docs.title: What maintenance does
docs.text:
JE shows a plain-text banner on login and signed-in pages, including for administrators.

Account policies and session messages

The injected web client adjusts page/header offsets for the banner's height. Account restrictions use Jellyfin's user policies on the server. JE changes only the selected account/remote-access permissions; it does not promise to disconnect an already-playing session immediately.

After a successful manual Enable request, each applicable configuration save attempts a 30-second native message to signed-in sessions with known users, including idle sessions and administrators. Scheduled opening also attempts a 30-second message. Blank notification text falls back to the banner, then built-in notification text. This messaging is independent of the Active Streams widget; client support and delivery failures can affect what users see.

docs.title: Countdown and message tokens
docs.text:
Add time remaining or an end time to your maintenance messages.

How to use: Put {countdown} or {ends_at} in a banner or notification message. Click × (Close) to dismiss the banner for the current document.

Details

Banner and notification messages accept case-insensitive {countdown} and {ends_at}:

  • {countdown} is time remaining, rounded up to the next minute, such as 1h 05m or 12m.
  • {ends_at} is the end time: viewer-local time in the banner, server-local time in native messages.

With a known end and no {countdown} token, JE appends English Time remaining: …. text. For open-ended maintenance, it removes the time tokens.

The banner updates the countdown every 15 seconds using the message and end time originally loaded. It removes itself when that known end passes. It does not poll for early cancellation or later message/end-time changes. Reload to reliably obtain changed server state.

Closing the banner restores page offsets for the current document. It does not end maintenance or change restrictions, and no dismissal preference is saved. Reloading can show the banner again.

How it works

Re-saving an existing manual window preserves its end only when action, affected-user selection, and requested duration are unchanged. Changing action or targets reconciles restrictions and applies a fresh window. Changing the duration restarts the manual clock. The background service handles timed expiry and turns the manual switch off.

docs.title: Reminders on playback start
docs.text:
Remind affected non-admin users about maintenance when they start playback. This is most useful when accounts remain enabled.

How to use: Enable Remind on playback start.

Details

JE attempts a 15-second native message, with a five-minute per-session cooldown. It uses the active manual/scheduled notification, with the same text fallbacks and time tokens. Display depends on the client's Jellyfin-message support.

docs.title: Scheduled window
docs.text:
Run maintenance at the same time each day using the server's local clock.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Enable daily maintenance window.
  2. Set Start time and End time. Check the displayed server time and UTC offset, particularly for containers. An end earlier than the start crosses midnight.
  3. Choose the scheduled messages and Scheduled Action, then click Save Settings.
  4. To end a scheduled window early, turn off Enable daily maintenance window and save. This also attempts restoration.
Setting Default What it does Enable daily maintenance window Off Runs a daily window using server-local time. Start time / End time 00:00 / 08:00 Daily window bounds; supports crossing midnight. Scheduled Banner Message The library is updating; slowdowns are normal. Time remaining: {countdown} Banner for the daily window. Scheduled Session Notification The library is updating; slowdowns are normal. Opening notification and, if enabled, playback reminder text. Disable user accounts / Disable remote connections Both Off under Scheduled Action Scheduled policy changes; default is banner/notification-only.

Choose valid, different times

Equal or invalid start/end times make JE ignore the schedule. Manual maintenance takes precedence while active.

How it works

The daily window uses the shared Affected Users selection and its own messages/action. Saving unrelated settings with the manual toggle off does not end a running scheduled window.

Checks begin roughly 15 seconds after startup and repeat about every 30 seconds. Open/close transitions and expiry are not guaranteed at the exact second. Users already browsing get changed banner state on their next load; opening notifications are attempted separately.

docs.title: Maintenance recovery
docs.text:
Check that maintenance has restored the account access you expected.

How to use: Check server logs, administrator status, and actual account/remote-access policies. A saved toggle alone does not prove restoration succeeded.

Check that access is restored

Disabling maintenance or reaching its end restores only JE's recorded changes. Previously disabled accounts and previously restricted remote access remain restricted. Removing the journal alone does not restore users.

Details

JE journals successfully applied policy changes and absolute end times in maintenance-state.json under <Jellyfin plugins directory>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/.

Restoration can partially fail. JE retries with backoff capped at one hour. It continues restoration on the disable/expiry path even if a journal write fails.

If the journal is unreadable or corrupt, enabling is blocked. JE attempts to preserve corrupt content in a .corrupt-<timestamp> backup, but backup creation can fail. Preserve the journal and any backup, inspect logs and affected user policies, and reconcile outstanding restoration before repairing or removing the file.

docs.title: Administrator routes
docs.text:
You can script maintenance using these routes with an authenticated administrator account.

Maintenance API reference

Prefix paths with your Jellyfin application base if applicable. See API for the wider API reference.

Method and route Purpose GET /JellyfinEnhanced/MaintenanceMode/Status Current window state, source, recorded change counts, end time, and server-local time/offset. GET /JellyfinEnhanced/MaintenanceMode/Users Lists all eligible non-admin accounts for the selector, not just currently affected users. POST /JellyfinEnhanced/MaintenanceMode/Enable Applies a manual window. POST /JellyfinEnhanced/MaintenanceMode/Disable Ends maintenance and attempts restoration. includeScheduled=true also ends the current scheduled occurrence without immediately reopening it. POST /JellyfinEnhanced/MaintenanceMode/Broadcast Attempts a native message independently of the Active Streams widget.

docs.title: Cache Management
docs.text: Refresh stale JE data without resetting personal preferences.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
Choose the action below that matches the data you need refreshed. Confirm Clear All Client Caches when prompted.

The client-clear shortcut appears with Server-Side Tag Cache off; the server-rebuild button appears with it on.

Action Location What it does Clear All Client Caches Admin Display → Media Tags, with Server-Side Tag Cache off; Overview → Quick Actions labels the shortcut Clear all client tag caches Clears targeted JE client caches on the next load, after confirmation. Rebuild Server Tag Cache Admin Admin → Tag Cache, with Server-Side Tag Cache on Rebuilds library tag data on the server. Clear Translation Cache Per-user Enhanced panel → Language Settings Clears this browser's translation entries and reloads.

Cache actions do not wipe unrelated browser storage, reset server-stored personal settings, or delete the MDBList server cache. Clearing/rebuilding tag data can make the next load slower. For tag-cache setup and defaults, see Tags & Badges.

How it works

Clear All Client Caches sets a server signal to invalidate targeted JE client caches on the next load.

Under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks, Refresh Translation Cache signals clients to refresh translations on their next load and runs at startup by default. Refresh CDN Assets refreshes local copies of external assets at startup and every 24 hours. Both are separate from the personal translation-clear button; fresh translation loading still prefers bundled locales. See Scheduled Tasks for requirements and triggers.

docs.title: Usage Statistics
docs.text: Choose whether your server shares usage statistics. Reporting is off by default.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Admin → Usage Statistics and turn on Share Anonymous Usage Statistics.
  2. On first enabling it, the form selects feature-toggle states, usage counts, and data-file sizes. Adjust the categories you want to share.
  3. Use Preview, then click Save Settings to opt in.
Setting Default What it does Share Anonymous Usage Statistics Off Opts the server into reporting after saving. Feature toggle states (on/off only) On Includes feature enable/disable states when reporting is on. Feature usage counts On Includes usage counts when reporting is on. Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) On Includes file sizes when reporting is on. Reporting interval (days) 15 Sets the reporting interval, within 7–30 days.

See the settings reference and Community Analytics for preview, collection, privacy, and reporting details.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: If something does not work, verify its switch and requirements, reload the client, and check the browser console and Jellyfin logs. See FAQ for common solutions, Troubleshooting Installation for injection/loading problems, or report an issue on GitHub.

docs.title: Other Settings
docs.text:
Use these controls to personalize Jellyfin and manage your server. Unless marked per-user, they are administrator settings. See Other Features for usage and Settings Overview for personal defaults and overrides.

Admin tab reference

“Other” is a documentation category, not a plugin tab. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced and use the locations below.

After changing configuration fields, click Save Settings and reload the web client. Branding uploads and cache actions apply separately.

Admin tab Settings covered here Display Icons & Theme, Default Language, MDBList Ratings, Content Warnings, client tag-cache clearing Playback Shortcuts Panel & Toast Timing Extras UI Tweaks, External Links, Custom Image Assets Pages Hidden Content and Activity Feed — links to their canonical guides below Admin Usage Statistics, Maintenance Mode, Tag Cache, Developer Settings

docs.title: Custom Branding
docs.text: Replace Jellyfin's branding with your own logos and icons. You do not need another branding plugin.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Extras → Custom Image Assets.
  2. Click a slot or drop an image onto it. Upload starts immediately; wait for ✓ Uploaded.
  3. Check the preview and measured dimensions where available, then reload. Use Ctrl+F5 if an old image remains cached.
  4. Upload again to replace a slot, or use its trash button to delete the custom file immediately. Reload after either action.

Save Settings applies configuration fields; uploads do not wait for it.

Setting Default What it does Icon Transparent Stock icon Replaces the top-left logo beside the server version. UI recommendation: 536×536 PNG with transparency. Favicon Stock favicon Replaces the browser tab icon. UI suggests 256×256 for PNG and lists ICO, PNG, or SVG. Prefer ICO. Banner Dark Stock banner Replaces the light-mode loading banner. UI recommendation: 1302×378, PNG, JPG, or WebP. Prefer PNG. Banner Light Stock banner Replaces the dark-mode loading banner. UI recommendation: 1302×378, PNG, JPG, or WebP. Prefer PNG. Apple Touch Icon Stock touch icon Replaces the iOS Home Screen icon and supported PWA touch-icon assets, including Jellyfin 12's sized variants. UI recommendation: 180×180 PNG.

Accepted uploads are not converted

Use PNG for .png slots and ICO for the favicon, even when the UI lists other formats. Uploads accept image MIME types up to 10 MiB. Recommended dimensions are not enforced.

How it works

These slots are uploaded files, not configuration properties. JE serves them through its own middleware and uses Jellyfin's stock asset when no replacement file exists. It keeps the original bytes without converting them, under these fixed filenames. The served MIME type follows the filename extension.

Slot Filename Icon Transparent icon-transparent.png Favicon favicon.ico Banner Dark banner-dark.png Banner Light banner-light.png Apple Touch Icon apple-touch-icon.png Details

Files live in <JE configuration-file directory>/<JE configuration-file basename>/custom_branding/. The absolute path depends on your installation. Keep that storage writable and persistent to retain branding across updates. See Custom Branding for middleware behavior and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Icon Settings
docs.text:
Choose the icons you see in JE's panel headings and toast notifications.

How to use: Open admin Display → Icons & Theme, turn on Use Icons in UI, and choose Icon Style. Click Save Settings and reload.

Setting Default What it does Use Icons in UI On Enables icons in JE regions that use its icon helper, including toasts and panel headings. Icon Style Emoji Chooses Emoji, Lucide Icons, or Material UI Icons. Available when Use Icons in UI is on. How it works

These controls apply to JE regions that use its icon helper. They do not replace every Jellyfin icon or every icon supplied by an extra. Unsupported helper entries fall back to emoji. Metadata Icons is a separate feature.

Stored style values are Emoji (emoji), Lucide Icons (lucide), and Material UI Icons (mui).

docs.title: Extras
docs.text: Customize the dashboard, login screen, and user-preferences menu with these optional switches.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Extras → UI Tweaks and turn on the switches you want.

  2. For Sidebar Custom Links, open Extras → External Links. Enter one configuration-page name/icon pair per line, using the decoded page name, including spaces:

    Jellyfin Enhanced | tune

  3. Use Test Links to preview entered links in the current window until refresh.

  4. Click Save Settings to persist your configuration, then reload.
Setting Default What it does Colored Dashboard Icons Off Replaces matching icons in the dashboard Home activity list with predefined Material icons and colors. Colored Ratings Backgrounds Off Colors official age/content classifications, such as PG-13, TV-MA, and FSK-12. Does not color numerical review scores. Profile Picture on Login Off Shows the selected public login card's avatar above the password field and hides the username area. Hidden users entered through Manual Login have no matching card. Custom Plugin Menu Icons Off Replaces supported plugin-link icons in the dashboard sidebar. Also enables saved custom configuration-page links. Theme Selector (Jellyfish) Off Adds Theme to Jellyfin's user-preferences menu. Requires the Jellyfish base theme installed natively to use its color palettes. Sidebar Custom Links Empty Adds configuration-page links when Custom Plugin Menu Icons is enabled. One Configuration Page Name \| Material Icon Name pair per line. Details

The second Sidebar Custom Links field is an icon name, not a destination URL. See Extras for supported plugin mappings, theme choices, and login limitations.

docs.title: Activity Feed
docs.text:
Use the user Activity Feed to see activity separately from dashboard icon coloring.

How to use: Open Pages → Activity Feed. Follow Enhanced Settings and Enhanced Features for setup and use.

Active Streams section requirements

Enable Enable Activity Feed, Show Active Streams section, and Active Streams Header Widget. Non-admin viewers also need Show widget to non-admins.

How it works

The feed's stream section polls while visible. The header widget below refreshes on demand.

docs.title: Active Streams Widget
docs.text:
See who is watching and open their current session details from Jellyfin's header.

How to use: Open admin Extras → UI Tweaks and turn on Active Streams Header Widget. Click Save Settings, reload, and open the widget; use Refresh for current data.

Setting Default What it does Active Streams Header Widget Off Adds a header counter and a sessions panel. Administrators have access by default. Show widget to non-admins Off Allows signed-in non-admin users to read current sessions when the widget is enabled.

What non-admin viewers can see

Enabling Show widget to non-admins exposes other users' stream titles, names, clients, devices, and playback details. This session list does not use the historical Activity Feed's library-access filtering. IP addresses and broadcasting remain admin-only.

How it works

The widget fetches at initialization, when opened, and with Refresh; it does not continuously poll. See Active Streams Widget for cards, player placement, and broadcast fields.

docs.title: Timeout Settings
docs.text: Adjust how long the Enhanced panel and ordinary JE toast messages stay visible.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Playback → Shortcuts Panel & Toast Timing and enter durations in milliseconds.
  2. Try Preview autoclose and Preview toast. They use your unsaved inputs.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload.
Setting Default What it does Shortcuts Panel Autoclose Delay (ms) 15000 ms Sets the Enhanced panel's inactivity timer. Hover keeps it open; interaction restarts the timer. Toast Notification Duration (ms) 1500 ms Sets the duration of ordinary JE toast messages. Details

Previews fall back for invalid values or values below 200 ms and cap at 120000 ms. These preview limits do not constrain the saved settings. Preview fallbacks are 15000 ms for the panel and 3000 ms for the toast; the latter differs from the actual client default. The number inputs declare no minimum or maximum. Zero uses the client default and does not disable auto-close.

The toast field's help text says 3000 ms, but the server default and client fallback are 1500 ms. Hidden Content's Undo toast lasts eight seconds independently; broadcasts use their own timeout.

docs.title: Letterboxd Integration
docs.text:
Add a Letterboxd link to supported movie and person detail pages.

How to use: Open admin Extras → External Links, turn on Enable Letterboxd Links, and optionally enable Show link as text. Click Save Settings and reload.

Setting Default What it does Enable Letterboxd Links Off Adds external links on supported movie and person detail pages. Show link as text Off Displays Letterboxd text instead of the normal icon.

Requirements and text links

Movies need an IMDb ID. Show link as text depends on Enable Letterboxd Links. Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) disables the text option and forces it off when saved.

Details

Person links use name-derived actor slugs and can be ambiguous or fail to resolve. This standalone feature does not add series links. See Letterboxd Integration.

docs.title: Metadata Icons
docs.text:
Show supported metadata and external links as icons on item detail pages.

How to use: Open admin Extras → External Links and turn on Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack). Click Save Settings, reload, and inspect an item's metadata and external links.

Setting Default What it does Enable Metadata Icons (Druidblack) Off Styles supported metadata and external links. Forces Letterboxd and *arr links into icon mode. How it works

JE loads Druidblack's metadata-icon stylesheet through its local asset service and applies supporting external-link styling. This is separate from Use Icons in UI, Icon Style, and poster tags. See Metadata Icons.

docs.title: MDBList Ratings
docs.text: Show ratings from several sources on detail pages, or fill Jellyfin's own Community/Critic Rating fields. Displaying ratings, fetching data, and writing Jellyfin fields have separate controls.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Display → MDBList Ratings and turn on Enable MDBList Ratings.
  2. Enter MDBList API Key and click Check. This tests the entered key before saving and shows account quota/reset information.
  3. Leave Show Ratings Row on Item Details on for badges. Open Configure ratings shown to select and reorder them with the up/down controls.
  4. Click Save Settings and reload.

docs.title: Fetch, then sync
docs.text:
After setting up the master switch and key above:

  1. Enable Fetch Ratings from MDBList, choose a reserve, and enable Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin if you want Jellyfin fields populated.
  2. Choose primary/fallback sources, review overwrite behavior, and click Save Settings.
  3. Under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks, run Fetch Ratings from MDBList, then Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin. Add your own triggers for recurring runs; neither supplies one by default.

docs.title: Display controls
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Enable MDBList Ratings Off Master switch for ratings requests, display, and both rating tasks. MDBList API Key Empty Key from MDBList preferences. Administrators can view, edit, and test it; ordinary viewer requests go through JE. Show Ratings Row on Item Details On Displays source badges on supported movie/series detail pages; seasons and episodes use their parent series. Requires the master switch. Configure ratings shown Empty source list: all returned sources Expands checkboxes and up/down controls to select and order detail-page badges independently of sync sources. Show % Symbol Off Adds % to normalized badge scores; raw-value fallbacks retain their source scale and precision.

To hide the entire row, turn off Show Ratings Row on Item Details. Clearing every badge checkbox saves an empty list, which shows all usable returned sources.

docs.title: Fetch controls
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Fetch Ratings from MDBList Off Allows the corresponding scheduled task to fetch missing/stale MDBList data without changing Jellyfin rating fields. Fetch Task Reserve 400 Stops Fetch when the remaining account quota is at or below this value. Details

Fetch uses the cached live remaining quota. Fetch Task Reserve input bounds are 1–100000.

docs.title: Sync controls
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin Off Allows the corresponding scheduled task to write Jellyfin's Community/Critic Rating fields from cached data, without MDBList API calls. Star Rating Source (Community Rating) TMDB Selects the source written to Community Rating. Star Rating Fallback Source None (empty) Used when the primary star-rating source has no usable score. Tomato Rating Source (Critic Rating) RT Critic Selects the source written to Critic Rating. Tomato Rating Fallback Source None (empty) Used when the primary critic-rating source has no usable score. Overwrite Existing Jellyfin Ratings Off Off: preserves each populated field independently. On: replaces each field for which the selected primary/fallback source has usable cached data. Missing data does not erase existing values. How it works

Based on xroguel1ke's original script.

The master switch gates operation; display/fetch/sync choices are stored independently. Source changes do not replace populated Jellyfin fields unless Overwrite Existing Jellyfin Ratings is on.

Both tasks are registered even when their switches are off. Execution checks the master switch and the corresponding task switch. Sync needs usable cache data, not an enabled Fetch switch: viewing detail pages can also populate the cache, despite the configuration help saying Fetch must be enabled first.

docs.title: Sources and fallbacks
docs.text:
All four sync selectors offer TMDB, RT Critic, RT Audience, IMDb, Trakt, Metascore, Metacritic User, Letterboxd, MAL, AniList, and Master. The two fallback selectors also offer None. Roger Ebert is available only for badges.

How it works Source label Stored value TMDB tmdb RT Critic tomatoes RT Audience popcorn IMDb imdb Trakt trakt Metascore metacritic Metacritic User metacriticuser Letterboxd letterboxd MAL myanimelist AniList anilist Master master Roger Ebert rogerebert

Sync prefers MDBList's normalized Score; only TMDB and RT Critic may fall back to raw Value. Community Rating converts the chosen result to the 0–10 scale by dividing by ten; Critic Rating uses it directly on the 0–100 scale.

The default order prioritizes TMDB, RT Critic, RT Audience, IMDb, Trakt, and Metascore, then the others. A nonempty list selects only those sources in that order.

See MDBList Ratings for batching, expiry, quota safeguards, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Content Warnings
docs.text: Show community content warnings from DoesTheDogDie on movie and series pages. See the feature guide for what users see and how the request budget works.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Display → Content Warnings (DoesTheDogDie) and turn on Show Content Warnings.
  2. Enter DoesTheDogDie API Key, from your account profile on doesthedogdie.com.
  3. Click Save Settings and reload.
Setting Default What it does Show Content Warnings Off Master switch. Needs a saved key to take effect. DoesTheDogDie API Key Empty Used by the server only. Never sent to clients.

These controls are server-wide. Each user picks their own triggers from the gear icon on the section, so there is no admin trigger list.

Free tier limits

The free API tier is for non-commercial use and allows 5,000 requests a month and 30 per minute for the whole server. A commercial server needs their Commercial tier. Results are cached for weeks, so usage depends mostly on how many different titles are opened.

docs.title: Hidden Content
docs.text:
Manage Hidden Content's server settings and personal options.

How to use: Open Pages → Hidden Content for server controls, or the Enhanced panel for personal controls. See Content Management for hiding, restoration, delivery modes, and administrator management. Enhanced Settings covers all defaults and personal options.

docs.title: Splash Screen
docs.text:
Show your logo on JE's loading overlay, with a decorative progress bar.

How to use: Open admin Extras → Custom Image Assets, turn on Enable Splash Screen Override, and enter Splash Screen Image URL. Check that the URL opens an image in your browser, then click Save Settings and reload.

Setting Default What it does Enable Splash Screen Override Off Shows JE's loading overlay with a contained logo and decorative progress bar. Splash Screen Image URL /web/assets/img/banner-light.png Browser-reachable logo URL or suitable same-origin path. Available when the override is enabled. Details

Use a logo legible within approximately 250×250 px. Include your Jellyfin application base in a same-origin path if needed; the default /web/... path assumes Jellyfin is served at the origin root.

JE uses the image URL as entered; it does not discover Jellyfin's current hashed banner filename. Test the URL instead of assuming the default path exists.

JE suppresses a competing Media Bar splash while its override is active. Combinations of custom loading screens may still need testing. See Splash Screen.

docs.title: Default UI Language
docs.text:
Choose a starting language for JE's interface. Users can save a personal choice that overrides the admin default.

How to use:

  • Administrator default: Open Display → Default Language, choose Default UI Language, and click Save Settings.
  • Personal choice: Open the Enhanced panel → Language Settings and choose Display Language. A change saves your preference and browser language key, then reloads.

Administrator setting:

Setting Default What it does Default UI Language System Default (empty) Supplies the initial JE display language for users without a saved personal choice. Choose a listed language; this is a dropdown, not a free-text language-code input.

Per-user location: Enhanced panel → Language Settings.

Setting Default What it does Display Language Auto (empty before the admin default supplies a starting value) Overrides the admin default with a saved personal selection. How it works

A saved personal selection, including an explicitly saved Auto, takes precedence over the admin default. Automatic resolution uses the browser's user language key, then Jellyfin's document language, with English as fallback. See Internationalization for bundled languages and loading behavior.

docs.title: Cache Management
docs.text:
Refresh cached JE data when it becomes stale. These actions do not reset all preferences or delete the MDBList server cache.

How to use: Choose the action below for the data you want to refresh. Clear All Client Caches asks for confirmation.

Action Location What it does Clear All Client Caches Admin Display → Media Tags, with Server-Side Tag Cache off; Overview → Quick Actions labels the shortcut Clear all client tag caches Clears targeted JE client caches on their next page load. Keeps server-stored personal preferences and unrelated browser storage. Rebuild Server Tag Cache Admin Admin → Tag Cache, with Server-Side Tag Cache on Rebuilds cached tag data for the library. This may take time on a large server. Clear Translation Cache Per-user Enhanced panel → Language Settings Clears this browser's translation entries and reloads. Does not signal other clients or reset the language selection. How it works

After confirmation, Clear All Client Caches updates the server's client-cache signal.

ClearLocalStorageTimestamp and ClearTranslationCacheTimestamp both start at 0. They are invalidation markers, not durations or switches. The latter is set by Refresh Translation Cache, a scheduled task; there is no separate admin button with the personal cache-clear label.

For tag-cache configuration, see Tags & Badges. A translation reload still prefers a usable bundled locale; refreshing the CDN cache does not force the loader to replace it with an upstream translation.

docs.title: Scheduled Tasks
docs.text:
Run JE's background jobs manually or choose when they run.

How to use: Open Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks and run a task or manage its triggers. Enabling a feature does not add a trigger where the task's default is none.

Task Default trigger Requirements and effect Fetch Ratings from MDBList None MDBList master, Fetch switch, valid key, and available quota. Fetches missing/stale movie/series ratings in batches and updates the server cache. Sync Ratings from MDBList to Jellyfin None MDBList master, Sync switch, and usable cached data. Writes Jellyfin's rating fields locally. Refresh Translation Cache Server startup Signals clients to refresh translation caches on their next load. Can be run manually. Refresh CDN Assets Server startup and every 24 hours Refreshes server-local copies of external assets; no enable switch. *Sync Tags from arr to Jellyfin None Requires Enable Tags Sync and configured *arr integration. See *arr Features and *arr Settings for prefixes, filters, and tag removal options before running. Details

Refresh Translation Cache sets a server timestamp to signal clients. The asset service also uses a 24-hour cache policy.

The daily maintenance window uses a background service, not a Jellyfin scheduled task.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text:
Warn users during server work and optionally restrict non-admin accounts or remote connections. Read Maintenance Mode before enabling.

Saving can restrict access immediately

Saving can immediately change account and remote-access policies. The manual default disables non-admin accounts. For a banner/notification-only window, leave both Action boxes unchecked.

Admin location: Admin → Maintenance Mode.

docs.title: Manual maintenance
docs.text:
Keep maintenance on until you disable it, or set a duration.

How to use:

  1. Enter the banner and session messages, then choose Action and Affected Users.
  2. Set Duration (minutes) and turn on Enable Maintenance Mode.
  3. Click Save Settings. To end the window, turn off Enable Maintenance Mode and save again.

The capture has both manual Action boxes unchecked; Disable user accounts is on by default.

Setting Default What it does Enable Maintenance Mode Off Applies the manual window on save. Turning it off attempts restoration of changes JE recorded. Duration (minutes) 0 0 means until disabled. Positive values set an absolute end time. Input bounds: 0–525600. Login Page Banner Message This server is currently undergoing maintenance. Please try again. Plain-text web banner. Supports {countdown} and {ends_at}. Active Session Notification Server undergoing maintenance. Native message attempted on applicable saves with manual maintenance enabled. Blank text falls back to the banner, then built-in notification text. Remind on playback start Off Sends a 15-second reminder to affected non-admin sessions starting playback, with a five-minute per-session cooldown. Also applies to scheduled maintenance. Disable user accounts On Under Action; disables login for affected non-admin accounts. Disable remote connections Off Under Action; disables remote access for affected non-admin users. With accounts enabled, LAN access remains available. Affected Users All non-admin users Choose All non-admin users or Select specific users. Shared with scheduled maintenance. Administrators are excluded from policy changes.

An empty user selection affects all non-admins

An empty selection means all eligible non-admin users. Deselect All does not mean “affect nobody.”

How it works

Both Action boxes unchecked stores none; account-only stores disable_accounts, remote-only stores disable_remote, and both stores both.

Affected Users stores all or a JSON array of selected user IDs.

The configuration's banner default above differs from the deliberately blank banner's client fallback: This server is currently undergoing maintenance. Please try again later. Blank fields do not reliably suppress the banner or notifications.

docs.title: Scheduled window
docs.text:
Run a daily maintenance window using the server's local clock. Manual maintenance takes precedence while active.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Enable daily maintenance window and choose Start time and End time.
  2. Check the server time and UTC offset shown under the time fields.
  3. Choose scheduled messages and Scheduled Action, then click Save Settings.
Setting Default What it does Enable daily maintenance window Off Opens/closes maintenance daily using server-local time. Manual maintenance takes precedence while active. Start time 00:00 Start of the window; must differ from the end. End time 08:00 End of the window. Earlier than the start means the window crosses midnight. Scheduled Banner Message The library is updating; slowdowns are normal. Time remaining: {countdown} Plain-text banner during scheduled maintenance. Scheduled Session Notification The library is updating; slowdowns are normal. Native message attempted when the window opens; also used for playback reminders. Disable user accounts Off Under Scheduled Action; scheduled account restriction. Disable remote connections Off Under Scheduled Action; scheduled remote-access restriction.

Choose valid, different times

Invalid or equal times make JE ignore the schedule.

How it works

The default Scheduled Action is none, with both boxes unchecked. The same action encodings apply as in manual maintenance.

Checks begin about 15 seconds after startup and repeat about every 30 seconds. Transitions are not guaranteed at the exact second.

Restoration and recovery

JE restores only policy changes it recorded as applied. Accounts already disabled, or remote access already restricted before maintenance, stay that way. Partial failures can leave restoration pending. Preserve maintenance-state.json, check logs and actual user policies, and follow Maintenance recovery if the journal is unreadable. Deleting it alone does not restore users.

docs.title: Usage Statistics
docs.text: Choose whether your server shares usage statistics. See Community Analytics for what is collected and how it is used.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
1. Open admin Admin → Usage Statistics and turn on Share Anonymous Usage Statistics. On first enabling it, the form selects all three categories.
  2. Uncheck any categories you do not want and inspect Preview.
  3. Click Save Settings to opt in.
Setting Default What it does Share Anonymous Usage Statistics Off Opts the server into usage reporting after saving. Feature toggle states (on/off only) On Includes feature-switch states and selected text settings when reporting is enabled. Feature usage counts On Includes usage counts when reporting is enabled. Data file sizes (bytes only, never contents) On Includes only the total size of the custom branding directory, without file names or contents, when reporting is enabled. Reporting interval (days) 15 Sets the reporting interval, constrained to 7–30 days.

The page shows the last-sent time, or that no report has been sent. Preview shows your current selections without registering the installation or transmitting a report.

Details

Later enable/disable changes preserve your configured category choices. To preview while saved reporting remains off, check the master temporarily without saving.

How it works
