Reporting also maintains internal state, not additional editable controls. AnalyticsHasBeenConfigured starts at false; AnalyticsLastReportedAt and AnalyticsForbiddenSinceLastSuccess start at 0. AnalyticsInstallId, AnalyticsInstallSecret, AnalyticsLastPayloadJson, AnalyticsLastReportedPluginVersion, AnalyticsLastReportedJellyfinTarget, and AnalyticsLastReportedJellyfinVersion start empty. These track registration, configured choices, and report history; see Community Analytics for their role.

docs.title: Developer Settings
docs.text:
Use Dev Mode when developing JE scripts. Leave it off for normal use.

How to use: Open admin Admin → Developer Settings, change Dev Mode, click Save Settings, and reload.

Setting Default What it does Dev Mode Off Disables normal script caching for development. Details

In Dev Mode, clients load individual scripts and the bundle is rebuilt with no-store responses.

The following configuration-only troubleshooting properties have no visible admin controls:

Property Default What it does DisableScriptInjectionMiddleware false Bypasses JE's request-time script-injection middleware. DisableBrandingMiddleware false Bypasses uploaded branding overrides and lets stock assets pass through.

See Troubleshooting Installation before changing configuration-only properties.

docs.title: Related Projects
docs.text: Explore companion plugins, scripts and themes by n00bcodr. For Jellyfin Enhanced itself, start at the documentation index or installation guide.

docs.title: Jellyfin Tweaks
docs.text: Jellyfin Tweaks adds controls for Jellyfin playback, display and user defaults. Use its own documentation to decide which settings to manage alongside JE. Check its releases for current compatibility.

docs.title: Jellyfin JavaScript Injector
docs.text:
JavaScript Injector lets you add your own JavaScript to Jellyfin's web interface. Use it for standalone customizations and script testing. Follow that project's setup instructions and release requirements.

Note

JE already loads its own scripts as the server serves the web interface. You do not need JavaScript Injector to install JE. Avoid loading another copy of JE's client through an injector.

docs.title: Jellyfin Elsewhere
docs.text:
Jellyfin Elsewhere is the standalone streaming-provider lookup project. JE includes Elsewhere functionality with regional and per-season provider lookup; use the JE Elsewhere guide when running the plugin.

Consult the standalone repository for its maintenance status, setup and limits.

Note

Do not run both versions of Elsewhere on the same web interface.

docs.title: Jellyfish
docs.text:
Jellyfish is a Jellyfin CSS theme with color stylesheets. JE's color selector lets you choose a color in the web interface.

How to use:

  1. Follow Jellyfish's installation instructions for the base theme and any optional components.
  2. Open JE's administrator configuration and select Extras.
  3. Turn on Theme Selector (Jellyfish) and save. Users can then choose a color from the web interface.

Administrator setting:

Setting Default What it does Theme Selector (Jellyfish) Off Adds a Jellyfish color selector. How it works

The selector loads color CSS through JE's local CDN route. Your choice is saved in browser storage under your Jellyfin user ID and does not synchronize across devices. The random daily color preference starts off.

See customization & extras and settings.

Note

Turning on the color selector does not install the base Jellyfish theme. CSS themes and custom rules can change the appearance of JE. Check the theme's own compatibility guidance, and use the CSS customization guide when adjusting JE's styles.

docs.title: Installing plugins
docs.text:
Install JE, Jellyfin Tweaks and JavaScript Injector from the shared repository.

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Repositories and click ➕.

  2. Enter a name, paste this repository URL, then save:

    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n00bcodr/jellyfin-plugins/main/manifest.json

  3. Open Catalog, select the desired plugin and click Install.

  4. Restart Jellyfin and refresh the web interface.

See JE installation for the full workflow and compatibility for dependencies. Install File Transformation when an optional companion requires it; JE itself does not need it.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Choose the JE build for your Jellyfin version. Current builds target Jellyfin 12.x and 10.11.x.

Project Jellyfin 12.x Jellyfin 10.11.x Older servers Jellyfin Enhanced Current build Current build 10.10: archived at JE 10.11.1.0 Jellyfin Tweaks Check release requirements Check release requirements Use that project's release information JavaScript Injector Check release requirements Check release requirements Use that project's release information Jellyfish Check theme documentation Check theme documentation Use the theme's own compatibility guidance Details

The shared manifest contains separate builds; one DLL does not serve every Jellyfin version. The Jellyfin 10.10 build is archived at JE 10.11.1.0.

docs.title: Support & community
docs.text:
Report a problem to the project that owns the feature:

  • Jellyfin Enhanced issues.
  • Jellyfin Tweaks issues.
  • JavaScript Injector issues.
  • Jellyfish issues.
  • Discord community.

Use each project's releases for updates and its contribution guide before submitting changes. JE is GPL-3.0; consult each companion repository's own license rather than assuming they all share the same license.

docs.title: Seerr Permission Audit
docs.text: Check whether your Jellyfin users are linked to Seerr and have the permissions needed for enabled JE features. The audit helps you find account and access problems before users try to request media.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The audit checks account linkage and selected permission gaps. It does not show a complete inventory of each account's permissions.

Administrator check

Run Audit is a read-only administrator action. It does not change accounts, settings, or permissions, and never imports users. There is no persistent audit setting.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Run the check from JE's Seerr settings.

How to use: Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Seerr → Permission Audit, then press Run Audit.

docs.title: Quick steps
docs.text:
Use the audit after connecting Seerr or changing feature access.

How to use:

  1. Configure and enable Seerr with saved URLs and API key. Use Test under Seerr Connection Setup to check connectivity with the entered credentials.
  2. Save changes to feature switches and Blocked Users.
  3. Open Seerr → Permission Audit, press Run Audit, and wait.
  4. Review missing-permission cards against your intended access policy. Adjust permissions in Seerr, or use user import if an account is genuinely missing.
  5. Run the audit again after changes, then verify the relevant request/issue workflow as that user.

Save before auditing

Run Audit uses the saved server configuration. It does not save pending form changes. Many users or failed upstream addresses can make the check slow.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The audit checks Jellyfin users against Seerr's stored account links. It honors Blocked Users.

How it works

The audit iterates Jellyfin users and attempts to resolve each account using Seerr's stored jellyfinUserId. It bypasses JE's user lookup cache and explicitly disables automatic import for the audit, even when automatic import is enabled elsewhere.

User lookup reads the first take=1000 users from each attempted Seerr URL. Large Seerr user lists can therefore leave a valid account unresolved.

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text:
Each result tells you whether an account was linked and whether the selected checks passed.

How to use: Review Not linked and Permissions Missing cards, then check the limits below before treating OK as proof of access.

Result What it means What to do Not linked No Seerr account was resolved. Check logs before assuming an import is needed. Permissions Missing A linked account fails one or more checks below. The card lists those selected gaps, rather than every permission held. Review the gaps against your intended access policy. OK Linkage and the checks performed passed. Verify the relevant workflow as that user. Details

Not linked can mean an absent account, a JE-blocked user, an upstream HTTP failure, an exception, or an unexpected response shape.

In mixed results, passing users appear in a collapsed list. If everyone passes, the UI shows an all-OK summary without individual names.

docs.title: Checks performed
docs.text:
The enabled features determine which permissions the audit checks. A linked Seerr administrator passes automatically.

How to use: Expand the table to see which saved feature switches caused a warning. Feature switches are admin settings documented in Seerr settings; the defaults below come from JE's server configuration.

How it works

These checks apply to linked accounts without Seerr ADMIN.

Check When checked Passing Seerr permission Request capability Every linked non-Seerr-admin account Any of REQUEST, REQUEST_MOVIE, REQUEST_TV 4K movies Enable 4K Requests is on (default off) REQUEST_4K or REQUEST_4K_MOVIE 4K series Enable 4K TV Requests is on (default off) REQUEST_4K or REQUEST_4K_TV Advanced options Show advanced request options is on (default off) and request capability is present Specifically REQUEST_ADVANCED Other users' requests Enable Requests Page is on (default off) REQUEST_VIEW or MANAGE_REQUESTS Create issues Show "Report Issue" button on items is on (default off) CREATE_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES Issue indicator Show open issue indicator is on (default off) VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES

Own requests may be enough

An own-requests-only warning can be intentional. Ordinary linked users can still use the Requests page for their own requests without permission to view other users' requests. Grant broader access only if that is your intended policy.

docs.title: Limits of an OK result
docs.text:
An OK result confirms only the checks performed. It does not validate quotas, Sonarr/Radarr setup, parental policy, or every media/quality-specific permission.

How to use: Test the request or issue workflow as the user after reviewing the audit.

Details

Passing the generic request check with movie-only permission does not prove TV request access.

The advanced-options audit specifically checks REQUEST_ADVANCED. Actual advanced-option authorization also accepts MANAGE_REQUESTS and linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators, so the audit can warn about a user whose advanced options work.

More generally, the audit does not apply the linked Jellyfin-administrator bypass used by actual proxy permission checks. It evaluates the linked Seerr account's permissions.

Show Seerr Issues Section does not independently activate an audit check. An OK result does not prove a user can read that section: ordinary linked users still need VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES. See issue permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & notes
docs.text:
A failed account lookup can look like a missing account. Check the connection and account link before importing again.

How to use:

  1. For Not linked, inspect JE's preceding warning/error log lines.
  2. Check Blocked Users and the stored Jellyfin ID. Matching usernames are insufficient.
  3. If import is needed, use Import Users Now. This saves configuration and performs a separate action that imports accounts. See import prerequisites, throttling, and email conflicts.
How it works

The administrator endpoint is GET /JellyfinEnhanced/jellyseerr/permission-audit. It rejects non-admins and returns HTTP 503 if the saved integration is disabled or URLs/key are missing. It uses saved credentials, unlike Test, which uses entered form values.

An unreachable Seerr server, a reverse proxy returning HTML, or a response-shape mismatch can look like a missing account. A working connection test does not prove every user's linkage.

Bypassing the user lookup cache makes this audit fresher than a cached account check. It does not clear all browser caches or guarantee every upstream state is current. Saving JE configuration clears its Seerr server caches. See Debug and caching and connection troubleshooting.

docs.title: Seerr Integration
docs.text:
Search, request, and discover media from Jellyfin using your Seerr instance. Start with Seerr setup, then check your accounts with Permission Audit.

Client and connection requirements

These interfaces run in the Jellyfin web client. Server playback automations can also react to native clients. External Seerr links need to be accessible from your device.

How it works

JE proxies API calls through the Jellyfin server, keeping the Seerr API key out of the browser and avoiding browser CORS requirements.

JE is independent of Seerr. Report integration problems to the Jellyfin Enhanced project.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Search and requests, including seasons, 4K, collections, advanced destinations, and quotas.
  • More Info, item-specific recommendations, discovery, and the Recommendations page.
  • Issue reporting and the shared Requests page.
  • Watchlist sync and automatic requests.

docs.title: Search Integration
docs.text: Seerr adds movies and series you can request alongside Jellyfin's own search results. Cards show request and availability status; person results are excluded.

docs.title: Requesting:
docs.text:
How to use:

  1. Enter a query in Jellyfin search. Discover on Seerr appears alongside library results; Seerr-only mode uses Seerr Results.
  2. Hover a card on desktop, or use its touch/keyboard controls, to reveal the overview and request actions. Press Request for an unrequested title; TV opens season selection. Movie requests open Request Movie when advanced options are enabled for your account; otherwise they submit immediately.
  3. Open a poster for details. Title links for library matches open Jellyfin, including partially available series. Other results open More Info or Seerr, depending on the admin settings.
  4. Scroll the Seerr row sideways to load more results. Use the refresh icon beside its heading to reload the row.
The demonstration stops before submission.

To show only Seerr results, double-click or double-tap the active Seerr icon. With the active icon focused, you can also press Enter or Space to toggle this mode. You need a linked account.

To narrow results by year, search for Title (YYYY), including the closing parenthesis.

Admin settings under Seerr → Search & Requests (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show Seerr Results in Search On Adds Seerr search when the integration is enabled and the viewer is linked. Exclude search items already in library Off Removes library matches, including partially owned series and movies owned in lower quality. Show Collections in Seerr Results On Adds collections derived from matching movies when Seerr search is on.

Search exclusions

Search exclusion can hide a movie you want in 4K or a series with missing seasons. Use Request More on the series detail page or request directly in Seerr. Discovery/recommendation exclusion is a separate setting. Hidden Content can also affect which cards you see.

How it works

A library match needs a Jellyfin media ID and available/partially available status, with TV season data also considered.

The year filter uses a movie's release year or a series' first-air year. Unknown or nonmatching years are excluded. Jellyfin's native results are unaffected.

docs.title: Season selection
docs.text:
Choose which seasons to request when Seerr allows partial TV requests.

How to use:

  1. Open a TV request to see season selection.
  2. Choose requestable seasons or Select All Seasons. With Only Allow Requesting One Season at a Time on, Select All Seasons is removed and each request is limited to one season (needs partial requests enabled in Seerr).
  3. Press Request to submit your selection.

Seerr controls season selection

TV requests depend on Seerr's partial-request and special-episode settings. Without partial requests, the checkboxes are disabled, and submission requests every regular season number returned by Seerr, or the whole series if none are returned.

How it works

Specials appear only when enabled upstream and are excluded from Select All Seasons. Seasons with zero episodes are hidden. The request dialog refreshes status every ten seconds while retaining your selections.

If upstream settings cannot be read, JE uses its last successful settings. Without those, it treats partial requests and specials as disabled.

Library season-presence checks can make deleted seasons requestable again even while Seerr still reports them available. Request eligibility also depends on the selected quality's status and Seerr's authorization.

docs.title: 4K TV Requesting:
docs.text:
Request series in 4K when your Seerr setup supports it.

How to use:

  1. Turn on the admin setting Enable 4K TV Requests.
  2. Choose Request in 4K from a TV request dropdown.
  3. In Request Series - 4K, choose seasons and submit with Request in 4K.

Movie cards also offer Request in 4K when Enable 4K Requests is on. Choose 4K from the dropdown before opening an advanced movie request dialog.

Admin settings under Seerr → Search & Requests:

Setting Default What it does Enable 4K Requests Off Exposes 4K movie requests. Requires a suitable Seerr 4K Radarr destination and permissions. Enable 4K TV Requests Off Exposes 4K series requests. Requires a suitable Seerr 4K Sonarr destination and permissions.

Normal and 4K statuses are separate. These switches expose actions; Seerr still decides whether a request is accepted. See 4K settings.

Details

In More Info, unrequested series can show Request, follow-up requests can show Request More, and Request in 4K can be a dropdown choice or a standalone button when normal requests are unavailable.

docs.title: Series without a TVDB match:
docs.text:
You can match a series manually when its TMDB metadata has no TVDB ID.

How to use:

  1. In the season dialog, select the correct series from the Sonarr search candidates.
  2. If needed, enter TVDB ID: the numeric ID in the series' thetvdb.com address.
  3. Request normally.
Details

When neither upstream metadata nor Seerr's stored media record supplies a match, the season dialog offers Sonarr search candidates. Manual entry also works when candidates cannot be retrieved or Sonarr is not configured in Seerr.

Series with an existing TVDB match do not show this block. This matching workflow has no separate JE setting.

docs.title: Advanced request options
docs.text:
Choose where and how Seerr downloads a request when your account has access to advanced options.

How to use: In the request dialog, choose Destination Server, Quality Profile, and Root Folder. Fill every required choice before submitting.

Admin settings under Seerr → Search & Requests (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show advanced request options Off Shows destination choices to authorized linked users. How it works

Linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators and users with REQUEST_ADVANCED or MANAGE_REQUESTS can use advanced options. Other users' advanced fields are hidden and stripped if sent.

Servers are sorted alphabetically. JE selects the matching normal/4K default and any supplied profile/folder defaults. Folder labels can include free space. Explicit selections bypass JE's client-side override-rule evaluation.

docs.title: Request quotas
docs.text:
Quota information helps you see how many requests you have left and when another slot may become available.

How to use: Check the quota chip when requesting a title. It shows the movie or series quota for that title. A next-slot estimate can appear while you still have requests left.

Admin settings under Seerr → Search & Requests (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show request quota info On Shows finite Seerr quota usage, window, and estimated next-slot timing, and enables detailed quota-error handling. Details

Unlimited quotas show no chip. One or two remaining slots show a warning; exhausted quotas show a restricted state.

A recognized quota-exceeded HTTP 403 opens Request limit reached with recovery guidance. Turning quota information off gives simpler errors without changing the upstream limit.

docs.title: Collection requests
docs.text:
Request several movies from a collection in one place.

How to use:

  1. Open a collection card or a movie's collection membership badge to use Request Collection.
  2. Choose movies individually or with Select All Movies.
  3. Press Request Selected Movies.

Admin settings under Seerr → Search & Requests:

Setting Default What it does Show Collections in Seerr Results On Adds search collection cards from matching movies. Depends on Show Seerr Results in Search. Details

Available movies and entries with normal-quality Pending/Processing media status are disabled. Other entries start checked, including partially available or blocklisted entries whose requests may fail upstream. Requests are sequential and normal quality; feedback reports successful and failed counts. A quota error recognized while quota information is enabled stops the remaining batch. A separate TMDB key supplies fallback collection metadata if Seerr returns no collection.

docs.title: Request Status Indicators:
docs.text:
Status labels help you see whether a title is available or a request needs attention. Cards, More Info chips, season rows, and Requests cards summarize related but different Seerr states.

How to use: Read the label on the card or season row using the guide below.

Status Meaning Available Seerr reports availability. Partially Available Some series content is available; season rows use Partial. Pending Approval A request is waiting for approval. Requested A request is in progress without active transfer information. Processing Active download activity on shared cards/season displays. The Requests page filter has the broader meaning described below. Declined The request was declined. This is separate from blocklisting the media. Blocklisted Seerr has blocked the media. Deleted Previously tracked media was removed; it can become requestable again. Not Requested No request recorded, used in season/collection displays. Details

These are fetched/cached snapshots, not a continuous live feed. Local checks can correct stale availability. An upgrade download can retain Available while showing activity. A pending request can coexist with partially available media. Season rows also use Requested for Pending/Processing media without active downloads.

Request, Request Missing, and Request More are actions, not status names. Series controls can include counts of available/requested seasons. More Info displays normal and 4K chips independently. Request actions update their interface; the season request dialog polls, the Requests page can auto-refresh, and More Info has manual refresh. See cache settings when a state looks stale.

docs.title: Item Details
docs.text: Find more to watch in Similar and Recommended rows on movie and series detail pages. You can open details and request titles just as you do in search.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
How to use:

  1. Turn on either row under Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras → Item Pages Discovery.
  2. Open an eligible movie or series detail page and browse the rows.
  3. To request more seasons, press Request More beside the season list when it is available. On Jellyfin 12, this list is headed Series. This opens season selection.

Admin settings (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show similar items On Adds Similar. Show recommended items On Adds Recommended independently. Show "Request More" button on Series On Adds follow-up season requesting when eligible. Exclude items already in library On Filters shared discovery/recommendation cards. Exclude blocklisted items Off Filters media with Seerr's blocked media status, rather than declined requests.

Requirements

The rows need a TMDB-identified movie or series and working Seerr user access.

How it works

JE places the rows after Jellyfin's More Like This region. Each row has up to 20 items before filtering, without unlimited additional pages.

Request More appears for requestable additional regular seasons containing episodes. Local season-presence and Seerr status checks can make deleted seasons eligible again.

JE also adds a Seerr link to the External Links row independently of *arr links. It opens More Info when enabled, otherwise Seerr in a new tab; the detail-link settings control its visibility and icon/text appearance.

docs.title: More Info
docs.text:
More Info lets you read about a title, check its availability, and request it without leaving Jellyfin.

How to use:

  1. Open a result poster or the Seerr detail link.
  2. Choose a request action. Where a season availability badge links to Jellyfin, use it to open that library season.
  3. Press the refresh icon (Refresh status) to update request, status, download data, and seasons.

Admin settings under Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Open results in "More Info" modal On Uses JE's modal for result details and the Seerr detail link. Link available items' posters straight to Jellyfin Off Makes available posters open Jellyfin directly; available title links already do. Show Seerr link on item detail pages On Adds a link for TMDB-identified movies/series. Show as text instead of icon Off Changes the enabled detail link to text. Show Streaming Providers on Posters Off Adds up to four subscription-provider icons using the admin Elsewhere region/provider filters; requires TMDB configuration. Details

More Info shows metadata, content rating, overview, requester names/avatars, and normal/4K status. Depending on upstream data, it includes download bars, cast/crew, trailers, keywords, collection membership, external links, and TV seasons with availability badges that link to the library when a Jellyfin season ID is resolved.

It does not continuously poll. It shows up to 20 cast entries, 20 keywords, and six trailers. View on SIMKL is available when an IMDb ID exists, with no separate switch.

The modal's Streaming section is independent of poster icons. With TMDB configured, it shows up to six unique subscription providers using your per-user Elsewhere region, then the server region (US by default). If the selected region is absent from supplied data, it tries US and then the first supplied region. See provider settings.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard before library arrival
docs.text:
Protect a title from spoilers before it arrives in your library. This is a per-user choice.

How to use: Press Enable Spoiler Guard in More Info. The button becomes Spoiler Guard (pending); you can disable it again from there.

Related admin settings (Spoiler Guard reference):

Setting Default What it does Enable Spoiler Guard Off Enables protection and the More Info toggle. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request Off Arms successful JE requests for their requester, within the configured content-type scope. Manual arming does not require this switch.

Requires Spoiler Guard

Your admin must enable Spoiler Guard. Your choice is stored with your pending protected titles.

docs.title: Hidden Content on Seerr results
docs.text:
Hide a title for your Jellyfin account, even before it reaches your library.

How to use: Use Hide on an enabled Seerr card. Use Unhide or restore it through Hidden Content. See Hidden Content for management and its settings for personal overrides.

The server master switch is under Pages → Hidden Content. The following are admin defaults that users can override, except for the master switch:

Setting Default What it does Enable Hidden Content Off Server master switch; required for the feature. Show "Hide" button on Seerr search results On Default visibility of Seerr hide buttons. Your personal Hidden Content enablement and hide-button visibility must also be on (both default on). Filter Search results Off Default removal of hidden titles from search. Filter Discovery On Default removal from discovery. Filter Suggestions / recommendations On Default removal from recommendation rows. Filter Requests page On Default removal from the Requests page. Details

These personal defaults also apply in new user configuration. Hiding a title and filtering it out of a particular surface are separate choices.

docs.title: Discovery Pages
docs.text:
Find related movies and series beyond your library on Jellyfin genre, studio/network, tag, person, and collection pages. You can request them from the same cards used elsewhere in Seerr integration.

How to use:

  1. Enable the relevant discovery switch below.
  2. Open the corresponding page from your library.
  3. Where both media types are available, choose All, Movie, or Series. Use Popular, Top Rated, Newest, or Oldest where supported.

docs.title: Available Discovery Types
docs.text:
Admin settings under Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras → "More" Discovery (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show "More from Network" On Adds discovery for known networks and production companies. Show "More Genre" On Adds genre discovery. Show "More Tag" On Adds tag discovery using a matched TMDB keyword. Show "More from Actor" On Adds actor/crew credits using a TMDB ID or name search. Show missing collection movies On Shows missing movies with request buttons on BoxSet pages that have a TMDB collection ID.

Network/studio pages can combine movies and series. Studio-produced series come from TMDB and require the separate TMDB key; those cards initially show status only for series already in the library, so open a card for fuller status. Some networks have no matching movie-company feed. Seerr-backed genre, keyword, and person discovery do not require a separate TMDB key.

Open a person page to find more titles featuring that actor or crew member.

Tag discovery prefers an exact TMDB keyword match, otherwise the first keyword result. No match gives no discovery results; a non-exact match can represent a different keyword. Arbitrary Jellyfin tags do not automatically define TMDB catalogs.

Collection details show Missing from followed by the collection name and availability counts. Fully available movies are excluded and remaining parts are sorted by release date. This is a fixed set without the general discovery filter/sort controls. Use its cards to request missing movies. Collection parts remain subject to shared exclusions, Hidden Content, and parental filtering.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Discovery and recommendation cards share these admin filters under Item Pages Discovery:

Setting Default What it does Exclude items already in library On Removes library matches from shared discovery/recommendation cards. Exclude blocklisted items Off Removes Seerr blocklisted media from those cards.

These are separate from Exclude search items already in library. Availability still depends on matching metadata, configured services, and linked user access.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
How it works

Sort scope varies: Recommendations categories sort fetched pages locally, rather than the entire upstream catalog. Person credits are deduplicated and shown in chunks of 40.

Discovery is added to these Jellyfin routes:

Page Route Studio/network #/list?studioId=<Jellyfin studio ID> Genre #/list?genreId=<Jellyfin genre ID> Tag #/list?type=tag&tag=<encoded tag> Person #/details?id=<Jellyfin person ID> Collection #/details?id=<Jellyfin BoxSet ID>

docs.title: Recommendations page
docs.text:
Browse trending, popular, and upcoming titles in Seerr Recommendations. This dedicated discovery page is separate from item-specific Similar/Recommended rows.

How to use:

  1. Open the configured Recommendations navigation entry.
  2. Select a row heading or tile to open a category.
  3. Use its filters and sort controls, then scroll for further pages.
  4. Use the category's own back arrow to return.

Admin settings under Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page (full navigation reference):

Setting Default What it does Enable Recommendations Page Off Enables the page for linked viewers with configured, enabled Seerr. Add Recommendations as a native Home tab Off Adds a Home tab without a companion plugin. Use Plugin Pages Off Uses Plugin Pages integration. Use Custom Tabs Off Embeds Recommendations with Custom Tabs; incompatible with its native tab. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates/removes the managed Custom Tabs entry with that mode.

Returning to a category

Categories have no independent URL or history entry. Refreshing the page does not restore the category.

How it works

The built-in page URL is /web/index.html#/recommendations; preserve your web/base path.

The landing page previews are Trending, Popular Movies, Popular TV Shows, Upcoming Movies, and Upcoming TV Shows. It also has Movie Genres, TV Show Genres, Studios, and Networks tiles.

Landing rows are page-one previews; only category views load further pages. Search and Recommendations insert results after their initial fetches complete. Studio and network logos are bundled, so they show with or without a TMDB key and fall back to the styled name if one fails to load; studio-produced TV requires the separate TMDB key.

docs.title: Seamless Scrolling
docs.text:
JE loads results ahead to reduce gaps as you scroll, while keeping their feed order. This works in search rows, paged discovery sections, and Recommendations categories.

How to use: Scroll horizontally in search or down a category to load more. If loading pauses, press the circular-arrow button to continue or Tap to retry after a failed load.

More genre results appear as you scroll.

There is no separate setting. Active search/discovery/page settings and their exclusions determine the feed.

How it works

Recommendations landing previews and item-detail rows do not gain unlimited paging.

  • The client shows cards ahead and prefetches further pages; posters load as cards approach the screen.
  • Empty filtered pages advance automatically. After 40 consecutive empty pages, loading pauses with a circular-arrow button. Press it to continue from the same position. Other stalled-buffer pauses can also occur.
  • Failed loads retry with backoff, then offer Tap to retry.
  • Upstream pagination limits apply, including TMDB's 500-page cap. Filtering, pauses, and failures can still produce gaps or fewer results.

docs.title: Parental Ratings
docs.text:
JE applies your Jellyfin parental policy to protected Seerr browsing and request paths. You do not need a separate JE switch.

How to use: Configure the user's parental policy in Jellyfin.

How it works

These rules apply the current user's parental rating, movie/series unrated policy, and blocked/allowed tags. They filter search, discovery, recommendations, person credits/known-for entries, collection parts, request lists, watchlist responses, and issues. They also gate protected title details, seasons, requests, and TMDB helper access.

Users without a maximum rating, movie/series block-unrated preference, or blocked/allowed tags need no additional parental metadata lookups.

  • Certifications use the server's metadata country, with US only when none is configured, and Jellyfin's rating table. Other countries' ratings are not substituted. More Info can display another region's rating through your Elsewhere preference without changing enforcement.
  • Successfully fetched titles without a recognized local rating follow the user's unrated policy for that media type. Failed/unresolved lookups remain hidden until verified. Search/discovery can re-fetch once delayed lookups finish.
  • Resolved ratings/keywords are cached server-wide for 24 hours; failed lookups retry after five minutes. With a TMDB key, certification lookups use TMDB; otherwise JE uses Seerr title details.
  • Blocked tags match TMDB keywords and genre names. Allowed tags form an allow-list against keywords only; blocked tags win. Matches compare the full value, ignoring case: Sci-Fi matches sci-fi, but not sci fi. Community keyword coverage can be incomplete.
  • Collection cards remain visible without a rating; their movies are filtered when opened.

Server automation boundary

Automatic movie/season requests go directly to Seerr. They bypass JE's parental-request checks and do not check the Blocked Users list. Scheduled watchlist matching is not limited to each user's library access. Review automation limits and watchlist access limits before relying on parental filtering for them.

docs.title: Issue Reporting
docs.text: Report video, audio, subtitle, or other media problems to Seerr without leaving an eligible Jellyfin detail page. The modal also shows existing reports and comments grouped by type.

docs.title: How to Report
docs.text:
How to use:

  1. Open a movie, series, regular season, or episode detail page and press the report icon (Report issue).
  2. Select Issue Type. Optionally enter Description (Optional).
  3. For TV, use Season/Episode as appropriate. Selectors use local library entries; season/episode pages attempt to preselect and lock the corresponding fields.
  4. Press Submit Report.
The demonstration fills an episode report and cancels before submission.

Admin settings under Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Show "Report Issue" button on items Off Adds reporting to eligible detail pages. Show open issue indicator Off Shows an orange report icon and open-issue count, capped at 9+; requires the report-button switch.

Reporting requirements

You need a linked account and permission to create issues. Viewing reports needs viewing permission. Manage issue status and conversations in Seerr.

docs.title: Issue Types
docs.text:
Choose Video, Audio, Subtitles, or Other in Issue Type.

How it works

Specials (season zero) and other item types are excluded. The item needs TMDB identification, which can come from the parent series or fallback lookup; submission also needs a Seerr media record (mediaInfo.id). Ordinary users need CREATE_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES; reads need VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES. Linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators bypass those local permission checks.

Missing linkage can fail submission while the button remains visible. If Seerr is inactive at initialization, the reporter is not added; if availability fails later, an eligible identified item can show a disabled reporting button. Missing identification can also make reporting unavailable.

Existing-report and indicator fetches each inspect at most 50 global issue entries, filtered locally by title, so older matching reports can be absent. The modal has no resolve, reopen, delete, or comment-posting controls.

docs.title: Requests Page
docs.text: The shared Requests page combines Seerr requests and optional issues with *arr downloads/history. This page is the guide to its Seerr parts; see *arr features for download progress, search, import outcomes, and history.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Enable the shared page to browse requests in Jellyfin.

How to use:

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Pages → Requests Page.
  2. Turn on Enable Requests Page.
  3. Press Save Settings.
Setting Default What it does Enable Requests Page Off Enables the shared page. Show Seerr Issues Section Off Adds issue browsing for authorized users when Seerr is enabled.

These are admin settings under Pages, not Seerr. See Requests Page Management for navigation choices, manual Custom Tabs HTML, and download/history visibility settings.

Connection requirements

Seerr requests need enabled/configured Seerr and linked accounts. Only the download sections need *arr configuration.

Details

Native Home tabs and built-in navigation need no companion plugin. Plugin Pages 3.0 or newer applies integration on save. Older versions need a restart after first enabling it; failed live registration also needs a restart.

docs.title: Polling Settings
docs.text:
Auto-refresh keeps the page updated while you browse.

How to use: Enable auto-refresh and choose its interval below.

Admin settings under Pages → Requests Page:

Setting Default What it does Enable Auto-Refresh On Refreshes requests and the enabled downloads/issues/history sections. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 Interval when enabled; input range 30–300 seconds. How it works

Polling stops when you leave the standalone page or switch away from its native Home or Custom Tabs tab. With Plugin Pages, it can continue after navigation until you reload or close the browser page. Hidden browser tabs are skipped. An issue-read HTTP 403 suppresses repeated issue polling while the permission-denied state persists. Updates refresh sections in place; cached upstream state can still be stale.

docs.title: Access Requests Page
docs.text:
Open the page to check your requests.

How to use: Open Requests in the configured navigation or Requests Home tab.

Details

The built-in URL is /web/index.html#/downloads; preserve your actual web/base path. Navigation placement depends on the selected integration, layout, and viewport. See page navigation.

docs.title: Request browsing and management
docs.text:
Browse your requests by status. If you have management permission, you can also approve or decline pending requests.

How to use:

  1. Choose All, Pending Approval, Processing, Coming Soon, or Available.
  2. Use the pagination arrows to browse more cards.
  3. Follow a card's link to Seerr or an available Jellyfin item.
  4. If authorized, press Approve or Decline on a pending request.

How it works

Page size adjusts to the viewport and fits whole card rows. There is no Declined filter tab; declined cards can appear in All. The Downloads search control does not search requests or issues.

Linked ordinary users see their own requests. Linked Jellyfin administrators and Seerr accounts with ADMIN, REQUEST_VIEW, or MANAGE_REQUESTS can see all requests. Request cards show requester information and status. Authorized Jellyfin/Seerr administrators and MANAGE_REQUESTS users can press Approve or Decline on pending requests. Controls follow the raw pending request status even if some media is already available.

Coming Soon uses future movie release or TV air dates and displays countdowns. Processing excludes Coming Soon and orphaned requests; the client additionally excludes Partially Available entries. Processing/Coming Soon read at most 500 upstream requests before local pagination.

Orphaned means an eligible approved/processing request is older than ten minutes from creation and every relevant configured, enabled *arr instance successfully reports no matching title. Missing instances or failed checks do not establish orphaning. Orphaned cards remain in All and are excluded from Processing/Coming Soon.

If your account has no visible requests, the section shows No requests found. Download progress, completion/import status, and paginated history use the same page. Their separate visibility/privacy controls are in Requests settings; see *arr features for their behavior.

docs.title: Issues on the Requests page
docs.text:
Browse Seerr issues in Jellyfin when your account has viewing permission. Your parental policy also filters the results.

How to use:

  1. Choose Open or Resolved and use pagination to browse.
  2. Press an issue's eye button to open the report modal.
  3. Click its card to open the Jellyfin item when a library ID exists.

Admin setting under Pages → Requests Page:

Setting Default What it does Show Seerr Issues Section Off Adds the section when the page and Seerr are enabled. Details

Ordinary linked users need VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES; linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators bypass the local viewing check. Users without viewing permission cannot load issue data; the section shows Could not load issues, with a No permission to view issues toast for an HTTP 403 response. The modal lets you read existing reports/comments or submit another report when authorized. Manage issue status and conversations in Seerr.

docs.title: Watchlist Sync
docs.text:
JE adds items between your Seerr and Jellyfin watchlists. You can sync in either direction; removing an item from one watchlist does not remove it from the other.

How to use:

  1. Enable the desired direction under Seerr → Watchlist and save.
  2. Adjust or run its task under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks.
  3. To add requested media when library items arrive or change, also restart Jellyfin or run Jellyfin Enhanced Startup once after enabling it.

Admin settings (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Add requested media to Watchlist Off Watches movie/series library additions and updates and adds matching requested titles for their requesters, including requests made outside JE. Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin Off Enables the incoming scheduled task. Sync Jellyfin Watchlist → Seerr Off Enables the outgoing scheduled task. Prevent re-adding removed items On Remembers processed incoming items so manual Jellyfin watchlist removal persists during future sync/monitoring. Memory retention (days): 365 Retains processed-item memory; input range 1–3650, used when prevention is enabled. How it works

Jellyfin watchlisting sets the user's Likes value, displayed as a watchlist by the KefinTweaks plugin.

docs.title: Seerr → Jellyfin
docs.text:
Bring Seerr watchlist entries into Jellyfin once they match items in the Jellyfin library.

How to use: Enable Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin. Sync Watchlist from Seerr to Jellyfin runs daily at 03:00 by default.

Requests are included only when Add requested media to Watchlist is also on. The event monitor is separate from this scheduled sync.

How it works

Incoming sync tries configured URLs until a user-list fetch succeeds, reads one upstream watchlist page per user, and examines up to 500 requests. The event monitor uses the first configured URL and examines up to 1000 requests. Both exclude blocked users and do not check watched status before setting Likes.

docs.title: Jellyfin → Seerr
docs.text:
Bring Jellyfin movie and series watchlist entries into Seerr.

How to use: Enable Sync Jellyfin Watchlist → Seerr. Sync Watchlist from Jellyfin to Seerr runs daily at 03:30 by default.

How it works

It uses the first configured URL, linked accounts, and TMDB-identified movie/series watchlist items. It skips entries already on Seerr's watchlist and excludes blocked users. Removals are not mirrored.

docs.title: Retention and access limits
docs.text:
Re-addition prevention remembers processed items for a limited time.

How to use: Choose Memory retention (days): above to control how long JE remembers them.

Details

Processed-item memory is stored in processed-watchlist-items.json using processing timestamps, not removal dates. Incoming sync cleans expired entries when prevention is enabled. After expiry, a still-eligible item can be added again; watched items are not exempt from incoming addition. Scheduled library matching is not scoped to the user's library access, so review this automation separately from protected UI parental filtering.

docs.title: Icon States
docs.text:
The Seerr search icon shows whether your connection and account link are working. An active icon does not itself grant request permission.

How to use: Check the icon and its tooltip against the states below.

Icon State Meaning Active Connected and linked. Tooltip: Seerr is active followed by Double-click to show only Seerr results, or Double-click to show all results in Seerr-only mode. Unlinked Hue-shifted icon; tooltip User not found on Seerr. Check import/linkage and Blocked Users. Inactive Grayscale icon; tooltip Seerr is not connected. Check integration and server connectivity.

docs.title: Connection Issues
docs.text:
Check the connection when the Seerr icon is inactive or links fail to open.

How to use:

  1. Verify Enable Seerr integration, URLs, and API key. Press Test in connection setup.
  2. If API calls work but external Seerr links fail, configure URL Mappings. Use an internal URL for API calls and a public mapping for browser links.
  3. For User not found on Seerr, check Seerr's Jellyfin connection, the stored Jellyfin user ID, and JE's Blocked Users selection. Use user import and Permission Audit.
How it works

Use the Jellyfin server/container's network context: a loopback address refers to that environment, not your browser's device. A public URL that requires an interactive proxy login may return HTML instead of API JSON.

Logs distinguish non-JSON, authentication, and Cloudflare failures and can include status, Content-Type, and cf-ray diagnostics. Container host names such as host.docker.internal/host.containers.internal can use allowed host mappings; literal link-local/metadata destinations remain blocked by the URL guard.

Identical usernames do not establish linkage. An upstream outage can also prevent user resolution.

docs.title: Search Not Working
docs.text:
Check search settings and filters when results are missing or slow.

How to use:

  1. Check the icon's active tooltip, Show Seerr Results in Search, and the current query.
  2. Remove a trailing year filter to compare results.
  3. For slow results, check server-to-Seerr connectivity, upstream response time, and server logs/browser console.
Details

Library exclusion, Hidden Content, blocklisting, and parental policies can reduce the row. A loading/retry/continuation control can indicate filtered or failed pages, rather than an empty upstream catalog. Search waits for initial data. See Seamless Scrolling and Debug and caching.

docs.title: Request Issues
docs.text:
Check account access and Seerr setup when a request fails or its status looks stale.

How to use:

  1. Check the linked account's media/quality-specific permissions, quota, Seerr Sonarr/Radarr configuration, and current request status.
  2. Fill required advanced choices and any TVDB match.
  3. For stale status, refresh the relevant page or dialog and inspect Seerr's queue.
  4. To help Seerr discover newly added library media, use Recently Added Sync to Seerr.
Details

Permission Audit checks selected permission gaps, but does not validate quotas or every request-specific permission.

Saving JE configuration clears Seerr server caches; other browser caches can persist. Triggering the recently-added scan does not finish a download/import or guarantee an immediate update.

docs.title: TMDB API Issues
docs.text:
Ordinary Seerr search uses Seerr's TMDB access. Automatic movie requests, studio-produced series, and provider displays also need JE's shared TMDB API Key.

How to use: Test the key beside its input, then check server connectivity and logs. See installation troubleshooting for network and proxy problems.

docs.title: URL Mappings
docs.text:
Map the Jellyfin server address used by your client to a browser-accessible Seerr address. These mappings affect displayed links; proxy calls continue to use Seerr URL(s) (One per line).

How to use:

  1. Open Seerr → Seerr Connection Setup → Advanced URL Mappings.
  2. Enter one jellyfin_url|seerr_url pair per line.
  3. Press Validate Mappings, then save.

Admin setting:

Setting Default What it does Seerr URL Mappings Empty Selects a browser-facing Seerr URL from the client server address. Details 
https://jellyfin.example.com|https://seerr.example.com
http://192.168.1.10:8096|http://192.168.1.10:5055
https://example.com/jellyfin|https://example.com/seerr

Matching uses ApiClient.serverAddress() or the browser origin, ignores case and trailing slashes, requires equality rather than a prefix, and takes the first matching line. Without a match, external links use the first configured Seerr URL, which may differ from the URL that successfully answered a proxy request. See connection settings.

docs.title: Auto-Request Settings
docs.text:
Server automations can request the next season or collection movie based on playback events. They use the playback user's linked Seerr account and Seerr's request authorization, without injected web controls.

How to use:

  1. Enable the desired feature under Seerr → Automatic Requests.
  2. Save, then restart Jellyfin or run Jellyfin Enhanced Startup once to start monitoring playback.

Review automation access

These are server-wide settings without personal opt-out switches. Automatic movie/season requests bypass JE's parental-request checks and do not check the Blocked Users list. Review the accounts and permissions used for these automations separately.

Details

Automatic movie/season services send requests directly to Seerr and bypass the controller's parental-request gate and import-blocklist lookup.

Requested-media watchlist monitoring also initializes at startup when enabled, but does exclude blocked users.

docs.title: Auto Season Request:
docs.text:
Request the next numeric season as you approach the end of the current one.

How to use: Enable the automation and choose the remaining-episode threshold below. In a ten-episode season with threshold 2, episode 8 meets the threshold.

Admin settings (full reference):

Setting Default What it does Enable Automatic Advance Season Requests Off Enables playback-triggered next-season checks. Require All Prior Episodes Watched Off Requires earlier locally present episodes in the current season to be watched/marked watched; current and later episodes need not be watched. Episodes Remaining Threshold 2 Maximum remaining episodes for the trigger; input range 1–20. How it works

Remaining episodes are the upstream season total minus the current episode number, clamped to zero.

Start detection requires playback at most two minutes in and below 5%; stop detection requires completion or at least 90%. The series needs a TMDB ID; counts are read through Seerr without a separate TMDB key. The next season must contain episodes and must not already be available/requested. Recent season requests are deduplicated across users for about an hour.

docs.title: Auto Movie Request:
docs.text:
Request the next collection movie when you play a movie from that collection.

How to use: Enable the automation, choose either or both playback triggers, and select a quality profile mode below.

Admin trigger settings (complete trigger and destination reference):

Setting Default What it does Enable Auto Movie Requests Off Enables playback-triggered collection checks. Requires a TMDB ID, collection membership, JE's TMDB key, and linked user access. When movie starts Off Checks at most five minutes in and below 5% playback. After X minutes watched On Checks when playback position reaches the threshold. Seeking or resuming can satisfy it. Minutes Watched Threshold: 20 Position threshold in minutes; input range 1–180. Only request if released On A valid future release date prevents submission; missing/unparseable dates do not. Quality Profile Mode: Default Uses Seerr defaults, copies the first existing request with Original, or sends configured choices with Custom. How it works

JE considers the entry immediately after the watched movie in Seerr's returned collection parts. It does not locally sort that array or search farther ahead if that next entry is already available/pending/processing or skipped by release checking.

User/movie checks are throttled to about once per hour. Original copies Seerr request settings rather than the watched file's quality. Unusable original settings and an empty Custom configuration fall back to Default. The default Use default instead of 4K fallback behavior also falls back when original settings were 4K.

docs.title: Seerr Settings
docs.text:
Configure the connection, user access, requests, discovery, and server automations here. For the workflows, see Seerr features; for account and permission checks, see Permission Audit.

All settings here are admin (server) settings unless marked as per-user.

Seerr controls account access

Permissions and quotas belong to the linked Seerr account. Enabling a JE feature does not grant those permissions.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Connect Seerr to search and request media from Jellyfin. Follow the setup steps below.

Before you start

You need a reachable Seerr instance, its API key, and Seerr accounts linked to your Jellyfin users. API calls need an address reachable from the Jellyfin server; browser-facing Seerr links need an address your users can reach.

How it works

JE sends API calls through the Jellyfin server, keeping the Seerr API key out of the browser and avoiding browser CORS requirements.

docs.title: Step 1: Enable Jellyfin Sign-In in Seerr
docs.text:
Let Jellyfin users sign in to Seerr.

How to use:

  1. In Seerr's Settings → Users, enable Enable Jellyfin Sign-In and save.
  2. Configure Seerr's Jellyfin connection before importing users.

This upstream example includes a legacy Jellyseerr annotation. Allowing new users to sign in there is separate from JE's automatic import.

Details

The upstream interface can differ between Seerr versions.

docs.title: Step 2: Import Jellyfin Users
docs.text:
Import the Jellyfin accounts you want to use with Seerr.

How to use:

  1. In Seerr's Users page, use Import Jellyfin Users.
  2. Select the accounts and press Import.

You can instead use JE's automatic or manual import.

Imported accounts still need the appropriate Seerr permissions.

This is an import selection dialog. Sample usernames do not establish whether an account has request access.

How it works

JE links accounts by the normalized Jellyfin user ID stored in Seerr's jellyfinUserId. Matching usernames alone does not link accounts.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Plugin
docs.text:
Enter your connection details in JE to enable Seerr features.

How to use:

  1. Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Seerr.
  2. Under Seerr Connection Setup, turn on Enable Seerr integration.
  3. Enter Seerr URL(s) (One per line) and Seerr API Key. The configuration help points to Seerr's Settings → General Settings → API Key for the key.
  4. Press Test beside the Seerr key.
  5. Leave Show Seerr Results in Search enabled if you want search integration. Add a TMDB API Key for the features that need it.
  6. Press Save Settings, then verify user access with Permission Audit.

Setting Default What it does Enable Seerr integration Off Enables Seerr features independently of the search-results switch. Seerr URL(s) (One per line) Empty Connection addresses for calls from the Jellyfin server. Seerr API Key Empty Authenticates server calls to Seerr. TMDB API Key Empty Shared with Elsewhere; enables the additional TMDB features listed below. Seerr URL Mappings Empty Under Advanced URL Mappings. Maps the Jellyfin address used by a client to a browser-facing Seerr address; see URL Mappings.

Testing and connection addresses

Test uses the entered values, including unsaved changes. It does not verify each user's linkage or permissions. Use an address reachable from the Jellyfin server or container. Multiple addresses should reach the same Seerr installation.

How it works

If a public proxy requires an interactive login, use an internal service address for API calls and a public address in the mappings.

Saved URL lines must parse as HTTP or HTTPS addresses; invalid lines are dropped. Proxy calls try configured addresses until one succeeds; some background tasks use only the first address.

The shared TMDB API Key is required for automatic movie requests, studio-produced TV discovery, and streaming-provider displays. It also provides fallback collection metadata. Ordinary Seerr search does not require a separate TMDB key.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure User Import (Optional)
docs.text:
Let JE create missing Seerr accounts automatically, or import users when you choose.

How to use:

  1. Open Seerr → Users.
  2. For automatic import, enable Auto import Jellyfin users to Seerr and save.
  3. For an immediate import, press Import Users Now. This saves the current configuration and imports unblocked users.
  4. Read the imported/total counts and any returned errors. Reaching Seerr does not mean every account was imported.

Setting Default What it does Auto import Jellyfin users to Seerr Off Imports missing accounts as needed and on a schedule. Already imported users are skipped. Blocked Users None Excludes selected Jellyfin accounts from JE's Seerr user lookup and import, and from watchlist monitoring/sync.

Import requirements and access

Import Users Now is an administrator action. It works with automatic import off, but the saved integration must be enabled and saved URLs/key must be nonempty. Importing an account does not grant all request permissions. Blocked Users is not a universal gate on direct server automations; see automation limits.

The Import Jellyfin Users to Seerr scheduled task runs every six hours by default when automatic import is enabled. Change its trigger under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks.

Details

Just-in-time import can run during user resolution for search and other proxy operations.

The manual import endpoint, POST /JellyfinEnhanced/jellyseerr/import-users, rejects non-admins. Disabled integration returns HTTP 400 with Jellyseerr integration is not enabled; missing credentials return HTTP 400 with Jellyseerr URL or API key not configured. Imports normally have a 30-second throttle (HTTP 429: Import was run recently. Please wait before retrying.). If no users were imported and errors were returned, JE resets the throttle so you can fix the problem and retry.

For conflicting-email errors, inspect Seerr for an old or duplicate account before changing anything. Verify the account's stored Jellyfin user ID, then run Permission Audit.

docs.title: Search and collection results
docs.text:
Add requestable titles and collections to Jellyfin search.

How to use: Open Seerr → Search & Requests and choose the options below. See Search Integration and collection requests.

Setting Default What it does Show Seerr Results in Search On Adds Seerr results to Jellyfin search when integration and user access are working. Exclude search items already in library Off Hides library matches from search, including partially owned series and lower-quality movie copies. Show Collections in Seerr Results On Derives collection cards from matching movies. Depends on Show Seerr Results in Search.

Search exclusions

Excluding library matches can hide opportunities to request missing seasons or 4K copies. Use a series' Request More action or Seerr directly if search exclusion hides something you want to request.

Details

The search exclusion is independent of Exclude items already in library, which controls discovery and recommendation cards.

docs.title: Enable 4K Requests
docs.text:
Show 4K movie request actions.

How to use: Open Seerr → Search & Requests and turn on Enable 4K Requests.

Setting Default What it does Enable 4K Requests Off Exposes 4K movie request actions; Seerr still validates the request.

4K movie requirements

Seerr needs a configured 4K Radarr destination and suitable permissions for 4K movie requests.

docs.title: Enable 4K TV Requests
docs.text:
Show 4K season requests alongside normal-quality requests.

How to use: Open Seerr → Search & Requests and turn on Enable 4K TV Requests. See 4K TV Requesting.

Setting Default What it does Enable 4K TV Requests Off Exposes Request in 4K, opening the season dialog in 4K mode. Normal and 4K availability are tracked separately.

4K series requirements

Seerr needs a configured 4K Sonarr destination and suitable 4K series permissions.

docs.title: Show Advanced Request Options
docs.text:
Let authorized users choose Destination Server, Quality Profile, and Root Folder in request dialogs. Quota information shows their remaining request allowance.

For movies, choose Request in 4K before opening the dialog; its title remains Request Movie, and matching 4K destination defaults are selected when supplied.

How to use: Open Seerr → Search & Requests and choose the options below. See advanced request options and request quotas.

Setting Default What it does Show advanced request options Off Shows destination choices to authorized linked users. Show request quota info On Shows finite Seerr quota usage, its rolling window, and estimated next-slot availability when supplied. Enables detailed quota-error handling. Details

Linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators and users with REQUEST_ADVANCED or MANAGE_REQUESTS can use advanced options. Unauthorized fields are hidden and stripped if submitted.

Unlimited quotas show no chip. One or two remaining slots show a warning; exhausted quotas show a restricted state. A recognized quota-exceeded HTTP 403 opens Request limit reached with retry guidance and advice to contact an admin. Turning quota information off uses simpler error handling; it does not remove the Seerr quota.

docs.title: More Info and detail links
docs.text:
Choose how result posters and Seerr detail links open.

How to use: Open Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras and choose the options below. See More Info and Item Details.

Setting Default What it does Open results in "More Info" modal On Opens non-library result details in JE's modal instead of following an external Seerr link. Also controls the Seerr detail-page link. Link available items' posters straight to Jellyfin Off Makes available posters open their Jellyfin item directly. Available title links already lead to Jellyfin. Show Seerr link on item detail pages On Adds a Seerr link to the External Links row for TMDB-identified movies/series, independently of *arr links. Show as text instead of icon Off Uses a text Seerr detail link. Depends on Show Seerr link on item detail pages. Details

Collection cards and membership badges use the collection request dialog. More Info's refresh button updates status and seasons manually; it does not continuously poll.

docs.title: Show 'Report Issue' Button
docs.text:
Let users report media problems from Jellyfin detail pages.

How to use: Open Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras and enable the report button. See Issue Reporting for item eligibility, permissions, and the report form.

Setting Default What it does Show "Report Issue" button on items Off Adds reporting to eligible movie, series, season, and episode details. Show open issue indicator Off Colors the report icon orange and shows the open-issue count, visually capped at 9+. Depends on the report-button switch.

Issue permissions

Reporting needs a linked account and creation permission. Viewing existing reports and the count needs viewing permission. Manage issue status and conversations in Seerr.

Details

Both the modal and indicator fetch at most 50 global issue entries and filter them by title, so older matching reports can be absent. The modal shows existing reports/comments and submits new reports.

docs.title: Streaming providers
docs.text:
Show subscription-provider icons on Seerr posters.

How to use: Open Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras and turn on Show Streaming Providers on Posters.

Setting Default What it does Show Streaming Providers on Posters Off Adds up to four subscription-provider icons from the admin's default Elsewhere region to Seerr posters.

Requires TMDB

Configure TMDB API Key to show streaming providers.

How it works

Poster icons use the server region (US by default), the server's provider selection (empty by default, meaning all), and provider exclusions (empty by default). Configure these under Elsewhere & Reviews Settings.

More Info's Streaming section is independent of this switch. With TMDB configured, it uses your per-user Elsewhere region, then the server region, then US. If that region is absent from supplied data, it tries US and then the first supplied region. It shows up to six unique subscription providers.

docs.title: Item Pages Discovery
docs.text:
Add related titles and follow-up season requests to item detail pages.

How to use: Open Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras → Item Pages Discovery and choose the options below. See Item Details.

Setting Default What it does Show similar items On Adds a Similar row to eligible movie/series details. Show recommended items On Adds a separate Recommended row. Show "Request More" button on Series On Adds Request More beside seasons when additional regular seasons with episodes are requestable. Exclude items already in library On Filters shared discovery/recommendation cards; separate from search exclusion. Exclude blocklisted items Off Filters Seerr blocklisted media from those cards. Declined requests are a different state.

Requirements

Similar and recommended rows require a TMDB ID and working Seerr user access.

Details

Each row has up to 20 items before filtering, without unlimited paging.

docs.title: More discovery
docs.text:
Find titles beyond your library from genre, studio, tag, person, and collection pages.

How to use: Open Seerr → Discovery & UI Extras → "More" Discovery and enable the types you want. See Discovery Pages for routes and matching requirements.

Setting Default What it does Show "More from Network" On Adds network/production-company discovery to Jellyfin studio pages. Studio-produced TV needs the separate TMDB key. Show "More Genre" On Adds genre discovery to Jellyfin genre pages. Show "More Tag" On Adds discovery using a TMDB keyword matched from the Jellyfin tag. Show "More from Actor" On Adds filmography discovery to person pages using a TMDB ID or name search. Show missing collection movies On Shows missing movies with request buttons on BoxSet pages that have a TMDB collection ID.

docs.title: Add Requested Media to Watchlist
docs.text:
Add requested titles to the requester's Jellyfin watchlist as they reach the library, or sync watchlist entries between Seerr and Jellyfin.

How to use:

  1. Open Seerr → Watchlist and enable the options you want.
  2. Save your settings.
  3. After enabling requested-media monitoring, restart Jellyfin or run Jellyfin Enhanced Startup once to start watching for library additions and updates.

See Watchlist Sync for schedules, limits, and additive behavior.

Setting Default What it does Add requested media to Watchlist Off Adds requested movies/series to the requester's Jellyfin watchlist when library additions or updates match them, including requests made outside JE. Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin Off Enables incoming scheduled watchlist sync. That task also includes requests when the requested-media switch is on. Sync Jellyfin Watchlist → Seerr Off Enables outgoing scheduled watchlist sync for linked accounts and TMDB-identified movies/series. Prevent re-adding removed items On Remembers processed items so removing one from Jellyfin's watchlist does not cause it to be added again during incoming sync/monitoring. Memory retention (days): 365 Keeps processed-item memory for this many days; input range 1–3650. Applies when re-addition prevention is on. Details

The KefinTweaks plugin provides the Jellyfin watchlist interface. Sync switches are checked when their scheduled tasks run. Neither direction mirrors deletions.

docs.title: Sync Seerr Watchlist to Jellyfin
docs.text:
Bring Seerr watchlist entries into Jellyfin with a scheduled task. It runs daily at 03:00 by default.

How to use: Enable Sync Seerr Watchlist → Jellyfin, then adjust or run Sync Watchlist from Seerr to Jellyfin under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks. See Watchlist Sync.

docs.title: Sync Jellyfin Watchlist to Seerr
docs.text:
Bring Jellyfin watchlist entries into Seerr with a scheduled task. It runs daily at 03:30 by default.

How to use: Enable Sync Jellyfin Watchlist → Seerr, then adjust or run Sync Watchlist from Jellyfin to Seerr under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks.

docs.title: Only Allow Requesting One Season at a Time
docs.text:
• Removes Select All from the season modal and lets users tick only one season per request
  • Applies everywhere the season modal opens (search, more info, item details)
  • Needs Partial requests enabled in Seerr; otherwise Seerr requires all seasons and this setting has no effect

docs.title: Auto Import Jellyfin Users to Seerr
docs.text:
Let JE create missing Seerr accounts for Jellyfin users.

How to use: Follow Configure User Import for the controls and manual action. Use Permission Audit after linking accounts or changing their permissions.

docs.title: Automatic requests
docs.text:
Request the next season or collection movie based on playback. These server automations can also react to native-client playback events.

How to use:

  1. Enable Seerr and the relevant automation below.
  2. Save, then restart Jellyfin or run Jellyfin Enhanced Startup once.

See Auto-Request Settings for triggers and policy limits.

docs.title: Auto Season Requests
docs.text:
Request the next numeric season near the end of the current one.

How to use: Open Seerr → Automatic Requests → Auto Season Requests. Enable the feature and choose the threshold below.

Setting Default What it does Enable Automatic Advance Season Requests Off Requests the next numeric season using the playback user's linked Seerr account when the threshold is met. Require All Prior Episodes Watched Off Requires earlier episodes present in the current Jellyfin season to be watched or marked watched. Does not require the current or later episodes to be watched. Episodes Remaining Threshold 2 Triggers when upstream season episode count minus current episode number is at most this value; input range 1–20.

Season request requirements

You need a series TMDB ID and usable Seerr request access. Episode counts come through Seerr; a separate TMDB key is not required.

docs.title: Auto Movie Requests
docs.text:
Request the next collection movie based on playback.

How to use: Open Seerr → Automatic Requests → Auto Movie Requests. Enable the feature, choose playback triggers, and select a quality profile mode.

Setting Default What it does Enable Auto Movie Requests Off Considers the immediately following movie in Seerr's returned collection entries. When movie starts Off Checks near the start of playback. After X minutes watched On Checks after playback reaches the position threshold. Seeking or resuming can meet it. Minutes Watched Threshold: 20 Playback-position threshold in minutes; input range 1–180. Only request if released On Skips a movie with a valid future release date. Missing/unparseable dates do not block a request. Quality Profile Mode: Default Default lets Seerr choose. Original copies settings from the watched movie's first Seerr request. Custom sends the configured selections below. Use default instead of 4K fallback On In Original, falls back to Seerr defaults when the copied request was 4K. Turn off to preserve those 4K settings. Radarr Server: Unset Destination used only in Custom. Quality Profile: Unset Profile used only in Custom. Root Folder: Empty Folder used only in Custom.

Movie request requirements

You need TMDB API Key, a TMDB-identified movie in a collection, and a linked account with usable request permissions.

How it works

Original uses Seerr request records, not the watched file's measured quality. It falls back to Default without usable original settings. Custom also falls back if no custom value is set. The service does not sort collection entries locally or search farther ahead when the next entry is already available/requested or is skipped by release checking.

Start-only stores OnStart; both trigger choices store Both. The default trigger mode is OnMinutesWatched.

The unset starting values are -1 for Radarr Server: and 0 for Quality Profile:.

docs.title: Recently Added Sync to Seerr
docs.text:
Help Seerr discover availability after Jellyfin library additions by triggering its recently-added scan.

How to use: Open Seerr → Recently Added Sync to Seerr, enable the automatic scan, and save. For an administrator test, press Trigger scan now.

Setting Default What it does Trigger Seerr recently-added scan when new Jellyfin items are added Off Triggers a scan after movie, series, season, and episode additions. Debounce (seconds): 60 Wait after the last addition; input range 5–3600 seconds.

Scan limits

A scan does not complete downloading/importing or guarantee an immediate status update.

How it works

New additions reset a timer. After the final event, JE waits for Debounce (seconds):, then dispatches the automatic scan to every configured Seerr URL.

Trigger scan now uses the entered URLs/key, including unsaved values, and stops at the first successful URL. It is an administrator action, not a saved setting.

After startup initialization, changing the automatic scan switch requires no restart because its listener is always registered.

docs.title: Requests Page Management
docs.text: The shared Requests page brings Seerr requests and optional issues together with *arr downloads/history. Download connection and visibility details also appear in *arr settings.

docs.title: Enable Requests Page
docs.text:
Choose how users open Requests in Jellyfin.

How to use:

  1. Open Pages → Requests Page and turn on Enable Requests Page.
  2. Choose a navigation option below, or leave the navigation modes off for built-in navigation.
  3. Save your settings.
Setting Default What it does Enable Requests Page Off Enables the shared page. Seerr requests require enabled/configured Seerr and linked viewers; download sections need configured *arr services. Add Requests as a native Home tab Off Adds a native Home tab without a companion plugin. Recommended by the UI for Jellyfin 12's experimental layout. Use Plugin Pages for Requests Off Uses the Plugin Pages plugin integration. Use Custom Tabs for Requests Off Embeds Requests with the Custom Tabs plugin. Cannot be combined with the native Home tab. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off When the page and Custom Tabs mode are enabled, creates the matching entry on save. Turning Custom Tabs mode off removes the managed entry; turning it on recreates it.

For routes, layout limits, Plugin Pages restart rules, and Custom Tabs setup, see JE Pages & Tabs.

docs.title: Show Downloads Section
docs.text:
Show active downloads and recent import history alongside requests.

How to use: Open Pages → Requests Page and choose the download visibility options below.

Setting Default What it does Show Downloads in Requests Page On Displays active *arr downloads. Also required to show the history section. Filter Downloads by User Requests On Limits queue/history for non-admins to content they requested through Seerr. Without usable Seerr linkage or matching requests, their results can be empty. Show Download History Section On Adds paginated recent import history. Restrict Download History to Admins Off Restricts history to Jellyfin administrators, enforced by the server.

Download visibility

Administrators bypass download-user filtering. Turning it off exposes other users' queue/history entries to authenticated viewers, subject to the separate admin-only history setting.

Request visibility has its own Seerr permission rules. For progress, import outcomes, history bounds, and download search, see *arr features.

docs.title: Show Seerr Issues Section
docs.text:
Let authorized users browse Seerr issues on Requests.

How to use: Open Pages → Requests Page and turn on Show Seerr Issues Section.

Setting Default What it does Show Seerr Issues Section Off Adds Issues with Open/Resolved filters and pagination when Seerr is enabled. Details

Linked ordinary users need VIEW_ISSUES or MANAGE_ISSUES to load issue data; linked Jellyfin/Seerr administrators bypass that local check. Issues returned by Seerr are subject to parental filtering. See Issues on the Requests page.
