docs.title: Auto-Refresh Settings
docs.text:
Refresh Requests automatically while users browse.

How to use: Open Pages → Requests Page and choose whether and how often to refresh.

Setting Default What it does Enable Auto-Refresh On Refreshes the page's requests, enabled downloads, issues, and history. Poll Interval (seconds) 30 Refresh interval when enabled; input range 30–300 seconds. How it works

Polling stops when you leave the standalone page or switch away from its native Home or Custom Tabs tab. With Plugin Pages, it can continue after navigation until you reload or close the browser page. Hidden browser tabs are skipped. An issue-read HTTP 403 suppresses repeated issue polling while that permission-denied state persists. The visible manual refresh/search controls belong to Downloads; request and issue lists use filters and pagination. Caching can still affect freshness.

docs.title: Seerr Recommendations Page
docs.text:
Give users a dedicated page for discovering movies and series.

How to use:

  1. Open Pages → Seerr Recommendations Page.
  2. Enable the page and choose a navigation option below.
  3. Save your settings.

See Recommendations browsing for using the page.

Setting Default What it does Enable Recommendations Page Off Enables Seerr Recommendations. Add Recommendations as a native Home tab Off Adds a native Home tab without a companion plugin. Use Plugin Pages Off Uses Plugin Pages for Recommendations. Use Custom Tabs Off Embeds Recommendations with Custom Tabs; incompatible with its native Home tab. Add the Custom Tabs entry for me Off Creates the matching Custom Tabs entry on save when the page and Custom Tabs mode are enabled; disabling/re-enabling that mode removes/recreates the managed entry.

Connection requirements

The page needs enabled/configured Seerr and a linked viewer.

For routes, layout limits, Plugin Pages restart rules, and Custom Tabs setup, see JE Pages & Tabs.

Details

Discovery exclusions apply to shared cards. Studio-produced series require the separate TMDB key; studio and network logos are bundled and need no key.

docs.title: Debug and caching
docs.text:
Use these controls to investigate stale status or permissions.

How to use: Open Seerr → Debug and adjust the cache settings below. Reload other clients as needed.

Setting Default What it does Disable server-side response cache Off Fetches Seerr responses and account lookups without using the server cache. Response Cache TTL (min) 10 Minutes to keep cached Seerr responses, such as search and discovery. User ID Cache TTL (min) 30 Minutes to keep Jellyfin-to-Seerr account lookup results. How it works

Both TTL inputs have a minimum of 1 minute and no HTML maximum. Disabling the cache increases upstream calls; it does not clear every browser cache.

Saving JE configuration clears its Seerr server caches. Permission Audit bypasses user lookup caching independently. A refresh control does not guarantee every cached layer has been cleared.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard
docs.text: Spoiler Guard helps you avoid accidental spoilers while browsing shows and movies. You choose which series, movies, or movie collections to protect. Your admin chooses how their images and metadata are shown.

docs.title: Turning Spoiler Guard on
docs.text:
Protect the titles you want to browse without spoilers. Your choices apply to your account.

Admin requirement

Your admin must turn on Enable Spoiler Guard to make protection and the JE controls available.

docs.title: Per series (TV shows)
docs.text:
Protect a series to cover its unwatched episodes and eligible later seasons.

How to use:

  1. Open the series detail page in the JE web interface.
  2. Click the dotted blur icon in the action row, normally just before the three-dot menu. The icon changes and a toast confirms the change. Its tooltip and accessibility label become Spoiler Guard: On.
  3. Click again to turn direct protection off.
With Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) enabled, the toggle reloads the page before you browse protected episodes. Setting Default What it does Enable Spoiler Guard (admin) Off Makes protection and the JE controls available. Spoiler Guard: Off / Spoiler Guard: On (per title, per user) Off; automatic modes can enable it Toggles your direct series, movie, or collection entry. These labels appear in the detail button's tooltip and accessibility label. How it works

The entry is stored on the server for your account. Other clients can use it when they fetch fresh metadata and supported image responses; see Multi-client support.

docs.title: Per movie
docs.text:
Protect a movie to hide applicable metadata while it is unplayed. The movie title stays visible.

How to use: Open the movie detail page and click the same dotted blur icon.

The poster stays visible with Keep movie posters visible enabled, while quality and rating overlays follow their separate policies.

Your admin can turn off Keep movie posters visible to protect movie posters and thumbnails too. Hiding descriptions also removes external links and trailers from eligible protected items.

Image exceptions

Movie Primary/poster and Thumb images remain visible by default. Turning off Keep movie posters visible applies image replacement to them. Chapter thumbnails, screenshots, and optionally backdrops follow their own protection rules.

docs.title: Per collection
docs.text:
Protect a collection to cover its linked movies according to each movie's played state. The collection's own name, art, and description stay visible.

How to use: Open the movie collection's detail page and click the dotted blur icon.

With Keep movie posters visible off and Blur images selected, unplayed member posters blur while the played movie stays clear.

The off-state collection button alone does not establish whether a member has direct protection.

A movie can have more than one source of protection

Turning a movie's direct entry off does not override collection protection. Turning a collection off preserves direct movie entries and protection from other collections.

How it works

Collection protection uses membership rather than copying entries into your movie list. A movie is protected if you enabled it directly or it belongs to any guarded collection. Its tooltip can show Spoiler Guard: Off while inherited protection remains.

Membership changes can take up to the 30-second scope-cache window to appear.

docs.title: Pre-arming (for titles not yet in your library)
docs.text:
You can register protection before a title arrives, even if another user requested it.

How to use:

  1. Open a movie or TV title's More Info modal in the Seerr integration.
  2. Click Enable Spoiler Guard. The button changes to Spoiler Guard (pending). The toast says Spoiler Guard will engage when this title arrives in your library.
  3. To remove pending or matching direct protection, reopen the modal and click the enabled button again. The usual disable confirmation applies.

Requirements

Turn on Enable Spoiler Guard in the admin Display tab under Spoiler Guard. You also need a working Seerr connection, access to the modal, and a title with a positive TMDB ID.

These are admin Seerr settings:

Setting Default What it does Enable Seerr integration Off Enables the integration. Seerr URL(s) (One per line) Empty Supplies your Seerr instance URLs. Seerr API Key Empty Authenticates the connection. Show Seerr Results in Search On Makes Seerr results available through search. Open results in "More Info" modal On Opens eligible non-library results in the modal.

Manual pre-arming works independently of automatic enablement and its type/library scope.

Seerr setup details

In the admin Seerr tab, configure the connection under Seerr Connection Setup, search results under Search & Requests, and Open results in "More Info" modal under Discovery & UI Extras. See Seerr settings.

Setting Internal property Enable Seerr integration JellyseerrEnabled Seerr URL(s) (One per line) JellyseerrUrls Seerr API Key JellyseerrApiKey Show Seerr Results in Search JellyseerrShowSearchResults Open results in "More Info" modal JellyseerrUseMoreInfoModal How pending protection works

When a matching Series or Movie is added or updated, its metadata must contain the same TMDB ID and the item must be accessible to you. Promotion is scheduled after a two-second settling delay. Protection becomes active after the state write succeeds.

If an accessible match already exists, clicking the button can create a real entry immediately. The modal still labels it Spoiler Guard (pending).

Pending entries survive restarts. Startup reloads their keys for later library events; it does not sweep every existing library match.

Each account has a fixed limit of 500 normal pending entries. At the limit, new inserts fail with HTTP 429. Existing entries can still be updated, removed, or promoted. You can also manage them through the authenticated endpoints.

If the update fails

A failed modal update shows Couldn't update Spoiler Guard for this title. See console. Reload and check the state before relying on protection.

docs.title: What Spoiler Guard protects
docs.text:
Spoiler Guard hides images and information that could reveal what happens next. The table below applies to eligible items when your admin has enabled the relevant policy and you have not opted out.

How to use: Protect a title, then use the metadata settings to choose which fields to hide.

With Blur images selected, unplayed episodes lose their original artwork and protected metadata. Played episodes keep theirs.

Surface Treatment Episode images Unplayed episodes use parent artwork or blur. Played episodes keep their images. Season images Season 0 (specials) and Season 1 stay visible. Later seasons use replacement until any episode in that season is played. Movie images Unplayed, guarded movies follow image policy. Posters and thumbnails stay visible by default. Descriptions Nonempty descriptions become your configured placeholder, initially Spoiler Guard activated. Series descriptions have a separate control. Episode and season titles Numbered protected episodes become Season X, Episode Y; eligible numbered seasons become Season N. Story tags and JE overlays Story tags, genre, language, and quality overlays follow Hide tags. Score overlays follow Hide ratings. Chapters Protected names become Chapter N, keeping timestamps. Thumbnail images have separate rules. Trickplay previews Protected preview sheets use image replacement while Hide trickplay seek previews is on. Saved progress can reveal whole sheets. You can opt out with Seek previews. Taglines, ratings, air date Removes taglines, community/critic scores, and premiere dates. Cast Hides guest stars or the entire cast, depending on your settings. Search hints Protected episode hints use generic titles or the placeholder. JE Reviews panel Hides reviews on guarded series, their season/episode pages, and directly guarded movies. Item eligibility and extra metadata

Advanced mode can reveal the next episode's Primary/Thumb image. Those image types are also exempt by default for movies. Missing numbering can prevent episode or season title replacement.

Hide tags empties story tags and controls JE genre, language, and stream-derived quality overlays. Hide ratings separately controls community/critic score overlays.

Guest stars only (recommended) removes entries marked as guest stars. Entire cast (regulars + guest stars) removes every People entry, including crew.

Search hints can also have matched-term echoes cleared. Advanced reveals do not relax this path.

Played state does not exempt reviews. Collection-only movie scope does not suppress the JE Reviews panel.

Metadata scope varies by item type:

Item Metadata eligibility Guarded series Applicable fields are protected without a played-state exemption. Series title and images remain visible. Season 0 or 1 Season metadata passes through; unplayed episodes within it remain independently eligible. Later season Applicable fields are protected until any episode in that season is played. Unplayed episode Protected when its parent series is guarded. Played episodes are exempt from normal item stripping. Unplayed movie Protected by a direct entry or guarded collection membership. Movie title remains visible. Extra carrying a guarded SeriesId Can receive applicable stripping without an extra-specific played exemption. Collection Its own metadata passes through; the toggle covers member movies.

Hide episode descriptions also controls eligible movie, later-season, and extra descriptions. Title or description protection can additionally clear paths, links, stream/attachment text, surviving character roles, and chapter image-path metadata. These effects can persist even when you opt out of cast or chapter-name hiding; see Auxiliary metadata.

docs.title: Saved progress: chapters and trickplay
docs.text:
Saved progress can reveal movie chapters and preview sheets you have already reached. Spoiler Guard uses Jellyfin's saved position, so hovering or seeking does not reveal more.

How to use: Resume from your saved playback position. Episode chapters stay protected until the episode is played, subject to your separate chapter-name preference.

The trickplay rules below apply while your admin's Hide trickplay seek previews is on and you have not unchecked Seek previews. Otherwise seek previews are shown in full.

How saved-progress boundaries work

The saved position is Jellyfin's PlaybackPositionTicks.

For movies, chapter names and thumbnails are revealed only when their start is strictly before saved progress. A chapter starting exactly at the resume point remains protected. Chapter image responses use a private 30-second cache window.

For both movies and episodes, a trickplay sheet is revealed only when its calculated exclusive end is at or before saved progress. A sheet crossing the resume point stays protected. Padding in the final sheet can keep it protected until the item is played.

Missing trickplay metadata or lookup failures retain protection. Advanced next-episode image reveals do not reveal chapter images or trickplay.

docs.title: Image replacement mode
docs.text:
Protected images can use parent artwork or blur, depending on your admin's choice.

How to use: As an admin, select Image replacement mode and Blur intensity. The complete image settings table lists defaults and exceptions.

Stock cardsBlur images

Show stock cards (hide images entirely, default) replaces eligible episode images with the series backdrop, season images with the series poster, and collection-only movie images with collection art.

Blur images blurs the original image. Higher Blur intensity values produce stronger blur, but recognizable silhouettes or colors can remain.

How it works

Eligible protected images on supported responses are replaced on the server before delivery. Blur images uses Gaussian blur.

In stock-card mode, missing parent artwork or a direct movie entry falls back to blur. A direct movie entry uses this fallback even when a guarded collection also covers the movie. Recognized processing failures use dark fallback images.

Unsupported response shapes, unresolved identity, and configured exemptions can still return originals.

docs.title: After toggling — what happens on your screen
docs.text:
Toggling protection on a detail page refreshes matching item images. Descriptions, titles, and ratings already on the page normally update when you next navigate.

How to use: Navigate or reload to see updated text. Your admin can enable Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) to reload the page automatically.

With Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) off, images update after the toggle; descriptions and titles update after navigation. How it works

A detail-page toggle refreshes matching Jellyfin item-image URLs in image sources, source sets, and inline backgrounds. It also invalidates JE tag data and can remove an existing Reviews panel. It does not refresh every image or trickplay URL.

Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) schedules a reload after 600 ms. Fetching and showing the updated content take further time.

Seerr-modal toggles and personal preference saves do not invoke this detail-page refresh/reload path. Navigate or reload to see their effects on existing content.

docs.title: When you mark an episode watched
docs.text:
Played episodes regain their images in the injected JE web interface. Marking them unplayed makes them eligible for protection again.

How to use: Mark the episode played or unplayed. Images update automatically; navigate or reload to update titles, descriptions, and ratings already on the page. Other clients need fresh metadata and image requests to show the change.

Images change after each played-state update; reloading reveals or protects the episode title and description. How it works

Successful supported mark-played or mark-unplayed requests schedule an image refresh after about 200 ms. Fetching and showing the updated content add time.

The hook recognizes POST/DELETE requests to /Users/<id>/PlayedItems/<id> and /UserPlayedItems/<id>. It skips the refresh if loaded Spoiler Guard state is empty and always uses an image refresh, even with strict refresh enabled.

docs.title: Auto-enable options (optional, admin-controlled)
docs.text:
Automatic modes can add protection for you when you start a show, request a title, or add titles to the library.

How to use: As an admin, turn on Enable Spoiler Guard, choose the automatic modes you want, and save.

Setting Default What it does Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on first play of a new show Off Adds a series when you start S1E1 and currently have no played episode in that series. Never protects movies. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request Off Records protection after qualifying successful requests through JE's Seerr proxy. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard when new titles are added to the library Off Queues new shows and movies for per-user protection. Scope and existing titles

The TV shows and Movies scope applies to automatic modes, although first play only supports shows. Library scope applies to first play, library add, and apply-existing; it does not restrict Seerr pending intent or its promotion. Automatic writes can fail, so check refreshed state when needed. An already-loaded web session may need reload to see additions.

For library additions, batch processing starts about ten seconds after the first addition.

Rescans do not arm existing titles. An admin can use Apply to existing titles now… or Spoiler Guard: apply to existing titles under scheduled tasks. See automatic settings and existing-title protection for eligibility, saved scope, skips, preview, and cancellation.

docs.title: Disable-confirm dialog
docs.text:
Turning protection off normally asks you to confirm, helping you avoid an accidental reveal. The dialog is titled Disable Spoiler Guard? and says:

Original images and episode details will be visible again straight away.

How to use:

  1. Turn protection off and confirm the dialog.
  2. To snooze future prompts, check Don't ask again for 15 minutes before confirming.
  3. For a permanent preference, enable Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off in your personal settings.
Confirmation and refresh details

Matching images refresh after a detail-toggle confirmation. Text already on the page updates on navigation unless Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) is enabled. Collection inheritance can still protect a movie after its direct entry is removed.

The 15-minute snooze expires and applies to your account in that browser. It is stored separately for each user in browser local storage. If the Jellyfin dialog is unavailable, a native confirmation appears without the snooze checkbox.

docs.title: Per-user overrides
docs.text:
You can reveal selected information for your account without changing anyone else's protection.

How to use:

  1. Open Enhanced Panel from the sidebar, or Jellyfin Enhanced from the user menu.
  2. Select Spoiler Guard.
  3. Under Show me this even with Spoiler Guard on, uncheck a category to reveal that information. Checked boxes inherit admin protection. Rows appear only for categories the admin enabled.

The per-user settings table covers every category and its default. Changes save immediately; navigate or reload to update existing page content.

Override limits

Metadata opt-outs do not directly turn off image replacement. Images retain their admin policy, played/progress rules, and exemptions. Seek previews is the exception: unchecking it shows trickplay thumbnails while you seek through protected unwatched items.

Advanced per-category reveals works in the other direction: unchecking it restores uniform metadata protection and disables the next-episode image exception for your account.

docs.title: Advanced per-category reveals (optional, admin-controlled)
docs.text:
Your admin can reveal selected information for your next unwatched episode and the rest of its season. With advanced mode enabled and otherwise default settings, only the next episode's real title is revealed.

How to use: Ask your admin to enable advanced mode and choose what to reveal in the advanced settings table. To opt out, uncheck Advanced per-category reveals in your own settings.

How the next episode is selected

The boundary is the first unplayed, nonvirtual episode ordered by season number, episode number, then sort name, excluding Season 0. An in-progress episode remains eligible while unplayed. This can differ from Jellyfin's rewatch-aware Next Up selection.

Only the boundary item ID receives next-episode reveals. Alternate versions sharing its numbering receive the current-season category. Other seasons and specials retain the normal enabled protections.

A missing boundary, missing episode number, nonpositive/missing season number, or resolver failure gives no category reveal.

Advanced mode can relax titles, descriptions, and ratings in supported episode metadata. Unchecking Next episode: keep image hidden can also reveal the next episode's Primary/Thumb image. Search hints and card score overlays retain their separate, stricter policies. Chapter/trickplay protection still follows its own rules.

Watched-data events normally evict the boundary cache immediately. Library changes can wait for its five-minute lifetime.

docs.title: Multi-client support
docs.text:
Native apps and external players can benefit from server protection when they use supported Jellyfin APIs with a resolvable user identity. JE's buttons and other web controls require the injected web interface.

How to use: Fetch fresh item metadata and images in your client after changing protection.

Supported responses and client limits

The server filters supported image and item-metadata responses. It covers common item lists/details, episode and season lists, Next Up, upcoming/resume/latest items, search hints, suggestions/similar items, playlists, movie recommendations, image information, playback information, item images, and trickplay images on recognized routes and response shapes.

JE's toggle buttons, preferences, confirmation, automatic page-image refresh, and Reviews-panel suppression require the injected web interface. That interface suppresses its Reviews panel according to your preferences. Other clients using JE's Reviews API need their own suppression behavior: the API does not filter reviews according to the viewer's Spoiler Guard state.

Spoiler Guard does not rewrite metadata embedded in media files or information obtained outside supported APIs. Raw-path consumers can be affected by metadata stripping. Client caching and unsupported responses can change what you see. This page does not establish a versioned test matrix for individual apps.

docs.title: What's not protected (by design)
docs.text:
Series titles/images, collection metadata/art, and Season 0/1 season metadata/art remain available for navigation. Movie titles and, by default, posters stay visible. Unplayed episodes inside Season 0/1 remain eligible for protection.

Other visible information

Ordinary item responses retain episode numbering, runtime, production year, counts, genres, and official age ratings. JE overlays can hide genres separately and retain the series age classification. Logo and Banner image types are outside image replacement. A missing season or episode number can leave an ordinary episode title unchanged; search hints have separate fallback logic, and description hiding can replace their names even with title replacement off.

docs.title: Per-user isolation
docs.text:
Your stored lists and preferences belong to your account. Spoiler Guard changes what you see; it is not an access-control boundary against someone deliberately seeking original content.

How to use: Fetch fresh authenticated metadata after changing protection. Native clients need fresh metadata to receive changed image tags; another browser's loaded JE state stays cached until reload or user switch.

How the server identifies your account

When Enable Spoiler Guard is on, recognized authenticated-user metadata responses receive per-user image identity markers. Clients that echo those image tags let the server select your policy without relying on your IP address. Userless API-key responses do not automatically receive a user marker.

Requests resolve identity in this order:

  1. Authenticated user.
  2. Image marker.
  3. Single-user-server shortcut.
  4. Session-validated browser cookie.
  5. Session users matching the request IP.

No candidates means no per-user protection. Ambiguous metadata identity passes through. For ambiguous images, the filter chooses the first candidate whose scope covers the item, then applies that user's played/progress state and exemptions. A Seek previews opt-out applies only when every candidate whose scope covers the item made it. Ambiguity does not guarantee replacement. Identity markers select presentation policy and are not credentials.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If protection does not look right, start with the checks that match what you see.

docs.title: The toggle is missing
docs.text:
1. Have your admin enable Enable Spoiler Guard under Display → Spoiler Guard.
  2. Open a series, movie, or collection detail page in the injected JE web interface.
  3. Confirm that Spoiler Guard state loaded successfully. Store problems can affect the controls.

docs.title: Images or text still look unchanged
docs.text:
1. Reload item metadata and check the dotted icon's tooltip. Text already on the page normally waits for navigation after a detail toggle.
  2. Check played-state exemptions, Keep movie posters visible, artwork policy, seek-preview settings, advanced reveals, and collection inheritance.
  3. If old images remain in a native client, use its image-cache clearing function. In a browser, try a reload or Ctrl+F5 for a stale cache.
Native client refreshes

Restart behavior depends on the client. Later state changes still require fresh metadata and changed image tags.

docs.title: Protection looks wrong behind a proxy or shared IP
docs.text:
1. Fetch fresh authenticated metadata and check that the client uses the returned image tags.
  2. Clear stale client image caches if necessary.
  3. Check your Jellyfin reverse-proxy/networking configuration.
Why old image URLs can cause problems

Old URLs without markers use fallback identity resolution. This can mix plausible users on a shared IP or resolve none.

docs.title: Preferences cannot be saved, or reviews disappear broadly
docs.text:
Check server logs and recorded health events. Repair or reconfigure the store if needed, then reload the web session.

What happens when state loading fails

A failed initial state load disables personal preference controls to avoid overwriting unknown state. Reviews can be suppressed broadly on eligible page types when state loading fails.

docs.title: Spoiler Guard Settings
docs.text:
Open Dashboard → Plugins → Jellyfin Enhanced → Display → Spoiler Guard to set server-wide policy. Users can relax individual metadata policies and seek previews in Per-user overrides. See Spoiler Guard features for title toggles, supported clients, collection inheritance, and browsing examples.

A title must be protected

Protection needs a user's direct series/movie entry or applicable collection membership. The relevant item eligibility rules also apply.

docs.title: Master switch
docs.text:
Turn on Spoiler Guard to let users protect individual titles. You can also add protection through automatic modes.

How to use: Enable Enable Spoiler Guard, then save the configuration.

Setting Default What it does Enable Spoiler Guard Off Enables server protection and JE's Spoiler Guard interface. Stored lists remain when it is off, but do not activate protection. How it works

The master gates the other controls. Cast scope depends on cast hiding; advanced category controls depend on advanced mode.

Metadata controls are under Hide metadata on unwatched episodes, although several also affect series, movies, seasons, and extras.

Setting Internal property Enable Spoiler Guard SpoilerBlurEnabled

docs.title: Image replacement mode
docs.text:
Choose whether protected images use parent artwork or blur. This lets you keep browsing without seeing the original scene.

How to use:

  1. Set Image replacement mode and adjust Blur intensity.
  2. Choose the artwork, movie-poster, and seek-preview options below, then save.
  3. Fetch fresh item metadata in your clients after changing policy.

Setting Default What it does Image replacement mode Show stock cards (hide images entirely, default) Uses parent artwork, or Blur images to blur the original. Missing parent art falls back to blur. Blur intensity 40 Blur strength; UI range 5–100. Higher values give stronger blur, but do not guarantee that all content becomes unrecognizable. Also controls stock-card fallback blur. Also hide the wide backdrop / fanart Off Protects wide backdrops and fanart on eligible items. Keep movie posters visible On Keeps guarded movie posters and thumbnails visible in either replacement mode. Hide trickplay seek previews On Protects the scrubbing previews of protected unwatched episodes and movies. Sheets ending before saved progress still reveal; users can opt out.

With Keep movie posters visible off, Also hide the wide backdrop / fanart on, and Blur images selected, both the protected movie's poster and backdrop blur. Its logo remains visible.

How it works

Image replacement mode uses SpoilerBlurMode="hide" for Show stock cards (hide images entirely, default), or "blur" for Blur images. Blur uses a Gaussian transformation on the server.

Setting Internal property Blur intensity SpoilerBlurIntensity Also hide the wide backdrop / fanart SpoilerBlurArtwork Keep movie posters visible SpoilerKeepMoviePosters Hide trickplay seek previews SpoilerBlurTrickplay

docs.title: Show stock cards
docs.text:
Stock cards replace eligible images with parent artwork. You can still recognize the show or collection without seeing the protected image.

How to use: Select Show stock cards (hide images entirely, default) in Image replacement mode and save.

Eligible item Parent artwork Episode Series Backdrop Season Series Primary/poster Movie protected only through a collection Guarded collection Primary/poster Directly protected movie, or item without suitable parent artwork Blurred original Fallbacks and exceptions

A movie with a direct entry uses fallback blur even if it also inherits collection protection. Movie Primary/Thumb replacement only takes effect with Keep movie posters visible off.

Recognized image-processing failures use dark stock/fallback images. Unsupported result shapes, unresolved identity, missing scope, or configured exemptions can still return original content. Stock-card fallback blur can retain silhouettes and colors.

docs.title: Blur images
docs.text:
Blur hides detail but leaves some color and shape information visible. Increase Blur intensity for stronger blur.

How to use: Select Blur images in Image replacement mode, adjust Blur intensity, and save.

docs.title: Image eligibility and exceptions
docs.text:
Protection focuses on unwatched content. Series, collection, and early-season artwork stays visible to help you navigate.

Which images stay protected

Primary, Thumb, Screenshot, and Chapter images are covered. Supported trickplay images are covered while Hide trickplay seek previews is on and the user has not unchecked Seek previews. Backdrop/Art are optional; Logo/Banner remain outside replacement.

When seek previews are not protected, previews of protected items are served unchanged with no-store caching, so turning protection back on takes effect at the next fetch. Previews of unprotected items are unaffected.

Series and collection images pass through. Season 0/1 images pass through; later-season images are protected until any episode in that season is played. Played movies and episodes are exempt. Unplayed episodes inside Season 0/1 remain eligible.

Keep movie posters visible leaves movie chapter thumbnails and screenshots eligible, as well as Backdrop/Art when enabled. Movie chapters starting strictly before saved playback progress are revealed; those starting at or after it remain protected. Episodes retain chapter-image protection until played. Whole trickplay sheets can be revealed for either item type when their calculated exclusive end is at or before saved progress. See saved-progress rules.

Advanced mode can exempt the next episode's Primary/Thumb image. Metadata opt-outs do not directly disable image replacement; opting out of advanced mode does disable that exception.

docs.title: Auto-enable options
docs.text:
Automatic modes add titles to users' protection lists, reducing the need to toggle each title yourself. All three default to Off.

How to use:

  1. Enable the modes you want.
  2. Set the content-type/library scope below, then save.

Master switch required

All automatic modes need Enable Spoiler Guard. Users can still remove direct entries afterward. An already-loaded JE web session may need a reload to show automatic additions.

Setting Default What it does Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on first play of a new show Off Protects the session user's series on qualifying S1E1 playback. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request Off Records pending protection after qualifying successful requests through JE. Auto-enable Spoiler Guard when new titles are added to the library Off Queues newly created shows and movies for bulk per-user additions. Internal setting names Setting Internal property Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on first play of a new show SpoilerAutoEnableOnFirstPlay Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request SpoilerAutoEnableOnSeerrRequest Auto-enable Spoiler Guard when new titles are added to the library SpoilerAutoEnableOnLibraryAdd

docs.title: Auto-enable on first play of a new show
docs.text:
This protects a new show when you start S1E1 and currently have no played episode in that series. Later episodes and movies never trigger it, regardless of Movies scope.

How to use: Enable Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on first play of a new show, save, then start qualifying S1E1 playback.

First-play eligibility

This checks current played flags, not immutable lifetime viewing history. Clearing every played flag can make later S1E1 playback qualify again. A resume point alone does not disqualify S1E1. Type and library scope apply.

docs.title: Auto-enable on Seerr request
docs.text:
This records pending protection after qualifying successful requests through JE. Manual pre-arming is also available independently; see pending protection.

How to use: Enable Auto-enable Spoiler Guard on Seerr request, save, then request a title through JE.

Check protection after requesting

Automatic protection is best-effort. A successful Seerr request can remain unprotected if the background hook fails. Refresh state to check it.

Request eligibility and failures

The hook covers qualifying 2xx results from JE's Seerr request proxy. Requests submitted directly in Seerr, HTTP 409 conflicts, and other failures do not trigger it. Type scope applies; library scope does not restrict pending intent or its later promotion.

Cap, storage, or hook failures do not turn the successful request into a failure.

docs.title: Auto-enable when new titles are added to the library
docs.text:
This adds newly created shows and movies to users' protection lists. New items are queued from any library source.

How to use: Enable Auto-enable Spoiler Guard when new titles are added to the library, choose and save scope, then add new titles.

Protection can take time

Protection becomes active after each user's changes are written successfully. It is not guaranteed while the batch is waiting or processing.

Batch timing and eligibility

Batch processing starts about ten seconds after the first addition and writes each user's changes together.

  • Only newly created titles count. Existing-title rescans and metadata refreshes do not re-arm a title a user removed. Adding a new library can arm its newly created titles. Use apply-existing for older items.
  • The batch rechecks the saved type/library scope. Turning off the master or this mode before processing drops the queued batch.
  • Users with library permissions are included, even disabled accounts. Parental-rating and tag restrictions are not applied by this bulk check. Users created after an addition do not receive its entries retroactively.
  • Played titles are not skipped. Their stored entries can become active if the titles are later marked unplayed. Existing direct entries are preserved. There is no per-user switch to opt out of this automatic mode.

docs.title: Auto-enable scope (content type and libraries)
docs.text:
Scope lets you choose which content automatic modes protect. The same saved scope also applies when you protect existing titles.

How to use: Under Auto-enable applies to, choose types and libraries, then save. Leave every library unchecked to cover all.

Setting Default What it does TV shows On Allows series in automatic modes and apply-existing. Movies On Allows movies in Seerr-request/library-add modes and apply-existing. First play still only handles shows. Libraries — leave every library unticked to cover all of them. Doesn't apply to Seerr requests (the title isn't in a library yet). All; none checked Restricts first play, library add, and apply-existing. Does not restrict Seerr pending intent/promotion. Library picker and internal values

The picker includes TV, movie, and mixed libraries, with their actual names and type suffixes. Deleted selections are flagged and dropped on save. Until then, an allowlist containing only deleted valid IDs can match nothing. If the picker cannot load, saving preserves the previous selection.

Setting Internal property TV shows SpoilerAutoEnableSeries Movies SpoilerAutoEnableMovies Libraries — leave every library unticked to cover all of them. Doesn't apply to Seerr requests (the title isn't in a library yet). SpoilerAutoEnableLibraryIds; defaults to an empty string; selected IDs are stored comma-separated.

docs.title: Guarding titles already in the library
docs.text:
Use Apply to existing titles now… for a one-time pass over existing shows and movies. It works independently of ongoing library-add auto-enable.

How to use:

  1. Enable the master, then choose and save scope. Unsaved configuration blocks the preview.
  2. Optionally check Also skip titles a user has already started watching.
  3. Click Apply to existing titles now… and inspect the preview counts. A preview with no eligible additions shows Nothing to apply.
  4. Confirm the run. You can follow progress or cancel it from the dashboard.
Setting Default What it does Also skip titles a user has already started watching Off Per-run option, not a saved plugin setting. Skips resumable movies and series with any played or resumable episode. Apply to existing titles now… Manual action Previews the saved scope, then starts the scheduled task after confirmation.

Cancellation keeps completed changes

Cancellation keeps completed writes. If tracking is lost, check task status and logs before rerunning.

Eligibility and scheduled-task behavior

Both this action and Dashboard → scheduled tasks → Spoiler Guard: apply to existing titles use these rules:

  • Scope and users: Saved content-type/library scope; users with library permissions, including disabled accounts. The bulk check does not apply parental-rating or tag restrictions.
  • Already guarded: Direct Series/Movie entries are skipped. A movie protected only through collection membership can gain a direct entry.
  • Fully watched: Played movies are skipped. Series are skipped only when they have at least one on-disk episode and all on-disk episodes, including specials, are played. A series with no episodes is not considered fully watched.
  • Partially watched: Included by default. The optional skip-started check uses Jellyfin's IsResumable state, plus played episodes for series. Its query parameter defaults to skipStarted=false.
  • Execution: Preview writes nothing; the actual run recomputes conditions, so counts can change. One actual run proceeds at a time. Each user's additions are written together. Per-user failures are reported; successful writes remain.
  • Progress: The task reports progress and can be cancelled from the dashboard.

The scheduled task has no default triggers. A normal dashboard run includes started titles. Running again can re-arm titles users removed since the earlier pass, unless watched/started skip rules exclude them. There is no removal history. Rescans never do this.

docs.title: Strict refresh mode
docs.text:
A detail-page toggle normally refreshes matching item images while text waits for navigation. Turn on strict refresh to reload descriptions, titles, and ratings too, with a brief page flash.

How to use: Enable Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) and save.

Setting Default What it does Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) Off Adds a full reload to the normal detail-toggle image refresh. How it works

The full reload is scheduled after 600 ms. Image refresh covers matching item-image URLs in sources, source sets, and inline backgrounds, not every image or trickplay URL.

Supported watched-state changes always use an image refresh after about 200 ms, without a full reload. Seerr-modal toggles and personal preference saves do not use the detail-toggle refresh path. See refresh behavior.

Setting Internal property Strict refresh mode (full page reload after toggle) SpoilerBlurStrictRefresh

docs.title: Hide metadata on unwatched episodes
docs.text:
Choose which information to hide while you browse protected titles. These admin policies also apply to eligible movies, series, seasons, and extras; see the item-scope matrix.

How to use: Open Hide metadata on unwatched episodes, choose fields to protect, and save.

Setting Default What it does Hide TV show descriptions On (effective default) Independently hides guarded TV show descriptions. Hide episode descriptions On Replaces nonempty descriptions on eligible episodes, movies, later seasons, and extras. Placeholder text Spoiler Guard activated Replacement for a protected nonempty description. Hide tags On Removes story tags and JE genre, language, and quality overlays on eligible content. Score overlays use the separate ratings policy. Hide chapter names (keep timestamps) On Uses Chapter N for protected chapter names; keeps timestamps. Image-byte protection is independent. Hide taglines On Removes eligible taglines. Hide ratings On Clears community and critic scores and suppresses their JE card overlays. Hide air date On Clears eligible premiere dates. Replace episode titles On Uses Season X, Episode Y for numbered protected episodes, and Season N for eligible numbered seasons. Hide cast on unwatched episodes On Filters eligible cast lists, including applicable non-episode items. Cast hiding scope Guest stars only (recommended) Removes only guest-star entries. Entire cast (regulars + guest stars) removes every person entry, including crew. Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series On Suppresses JE's web Reviews panel on guarded series and child pages, and directly guarded movies. Internal setting names Setting Internal property Hide episode descriptions SpoilerStripOverview Placeholder text SpoilerOverviewPlaceholder Hide tags SpoilerStripTags Hide chapter names (keep timestamps) SpoilerStripChapters Hide taglines SpoilerStripTaglines Hide ratings SpoilerStripRatings Hide air date SpoilerStripPremiereDate Replace episode titles SpoilerReplaceTitle Hide cast on unwatched episodes SpoilerStripCast Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series SpoilerStripReviews Hide TV show descriptions SpoilerStripSeriesOverview; raw default null, inheriting SpoilerStripOverview until explicitly saved. Cast hiding scope SpoilerStripCastMode="GuestStars" removes GuestStar entries; "All" removes every People entry, including crew.

docs.title: Descriptions and placeholder text
docs.text:
Protected nonempty descriptions use your placeholder text. Empty descriptions stay empty.

How to use: Set Placeholder text and save. Save a separate Hide TV show descriptions choice if you want it to differ from episode-description hiding.

Placeholder cleanup and older settings

The nullable series-description property preserves older episode-description choices on upgrade. Its fresh effective default is On because episode-description hiding defaults On. Saving an independent choice separates the policies.

Before serving the placeholder, the server takes the raw text's first 200 characters, removes HTML tags, then removes angle brackets, quotation marks, apostrophes, backticks, and ampersands. Empty or whitespace-only sanitized text falls back to Spoiler Guard activated. Items with an empty original Overview do not gain an invented description.

docs.title: Chapter names and thumbnails
docs.text:
Chapter names and thumbnail images have separate protection rules. You can keep chapter names visible without revealing protected images.

How to use: Turn off Hide chapter names (keep timestamps) to retain names, then save.

Chapter and preview limits

Turning off chapter-name hiding does not reveal protected chapter images. Effective title or description protection can also clear chapter image-path metadata.

Movie chapters starting strictly before saved progress are revealed; the chapter exactly at the resume point stays protected. Episodes use played/unplayed chapter protection. Trickplay follows Hide trickplay seek previews and whole-sheet progress rules rather than the chapter-name switch.

docs.title: Titles, ratings, and cast
docs.text:
You can replace episode titles, hide scores, and remove guest stars or the whole cast. These choices reduce spoilers in names and cast lists while you browse.

How to use: Choose Replace episode titles, Hide ratings, and Hide cast on unwatched episodes as needed. Set Cast hiding scope, then save.

Title, score, and character-role limits

Title replacement applies to supported routes/response shapes, including common lists and detail pages. Ordinary episode rewriting requires both season and episode numbers. User overrides, advanced reveals, missing numbering, and unsupported surfaces can alter results. Search hints remain stricter: enabled description hiding can replace a hint's name even when title replacement is off.

JE community/critic score overlays are suppressed on guarded series and season cards and unwatched episode cards without falling back to the series score. Played episodes keep their scores. Category metadata reveals do not relax card score overlays. Ordinary DTO genres and official age ratings remain; JE age badges can retain series classification.

The quality overlays controlled by Hide tags are derived from stream metadata. Tagline hiding empties eligible tagline arrays.

Cast filtering does not by itself clear surviving character roles. Roles are cleared when effective title replacement or the item's applicable description hiding applies, even if cast filtering is off or personally opted out.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
Spoiler Guard can hide JE's Reviews panel on protected detail pages. This helps you avoid spoilers even after an episode or directly protected movie is played.

How to use: Enable Hide reviews on Spoiler Guard series and save. Users can opt out with Reviews in their personal settings.

Reviews must also be enabled

Reviews need Show TMDB Reviews with TMDB integration, or Enable User Written Reviews. Both default Off and live outside Spoiler Guard; see Enhanced settings.

Review scope and API limits

Review suppression runs in JE's injected web client. It covers guarded Series/Season/Episode pages, including watched episodes, and directly guarded movies, including played movies. Collection-only movie protection does not suppress the panel. A failed state load can suppress the panel broadly on eligible page types.

The Reviews API applies author visibility rules but does not suppress responses based on the viewer's Spoiler Guard state.

docs.title: Auxiliary metadata
docs.text:
Title and description protection can also remove text from links, paths, and other metadata that might contain spoilers. This can affect clients or tools that require raw paths.

Fields affected by title and description protection

Effective title replacement or applicable description hiding can clear filesystem paths, episode-title/sort fields, custom rating, remote trailers, external links, stream titles/comments, attachment filenames/comments, surviving character roles, and protected chapter image paths.

Cast and chapter-name opt-outs do not independently restore those fields. Indexed subtitle delivery URLs remain available; raw external subtitle URLs can be cleared. Movie media-source version names are retained.

docs.title: Advanced per-category reveals
docs.text:
Reveal selected information for your next unwatched episode and other unwatched episodes in its season. With advanced mode on and otherwise default settings, only the next episode's real title is revealed.

How to use:

  1. Turn on Enable advanced per-category reveals.
  2. Uncheck the fields you want revealed. Checked means “keep hidden.”
  3. Save the configuration.
Setting Default What it does Enable advanced per-category reveals Off Enables selected reveals for the next episode and its season. Next episode: keep title hidden Off Permits the next unwatched episode's real title when advanced mode is enabled. Next episode: keep description hidden On Uncheck to reveal its description. Next episode: keep ratings hidden On Uncheck to reveal its community/critic metadata scores. Next episode: keep image hidden On Uncheck to exempt its Primary/Thumb image. Does not reveal chapters or trickplay. Current season: keep titles hidden On Uncheck to reveal other unwatched episode titles in the selected next episode's season. Current season: keep descriptions hidden On Uncheck to reveal those descriptions. Current season: keep ratings hidden On Uncheck to reveal those metadata scores.

Users can uncheck Advanced per-category reveals in personal settings to restore uniform protection, including disabling the next-image exception.

How it works

These masks can only relax an enabled base policy. They do not hide fields whose admin policy or personal opt-out already permits them.

The boundary is the first unplayed, nonvirtual episode ordered by season, episode, then sort name, excluding Season 0. In-progress episodes remain eligible; the selection need not match Jellyfin's rewatch-aware Next Up. Only the selected ID gets next-episode reveals. Alternate versions sharing numbering can receive the current-season mask instead.

Classification requires a positive season number and a present episode number. Missing boundary/numbering or lookup failures give no reveal. Other seasons and specials retain normal policy. Search hints and card score overlays retain separate, stricter rules.

Watched-data events normally evict the boundary immediately. Library changes can wait for the five-minute cache lifetime.

Setting Internal property Enable advanced per-category reveals SpoilerAdvancedMode Next episode: keep title hidden SpoilerNextEpisodeStripTitle Next episode: keep description hidden SpoilerNextEpisodeStripOverview Next episode: keep ratings hidden SpoilerNextEpisodeStripRatings Next episode: keep image hidden SpoilerNextEpisodeStripImage Current season: keep titles hidden SpoilerCurrentSeasonStripTitle Current season: keep descriptions hidden SpoilerCurrentSeasonStripOverview Current season: keep ratings hidden SpoilerCurrentSeasonStripRatings

docs.title: Per-user overrides
docs.text:
You can reveal selected information for your own account while keeping the rest protected. Your choices do not change server-wide policy.

How to use:

  1. Open Enhanced Panel from the sidebar, or Jellyfin Enhanced from the user menu.
  2. Select Spoiler Guard.
  3. Under Show me this even with Spoiler Guard on, uncheck a category to relax it. Checked categories inherit admin protection.

Changes save immediately. Only admin-enabled categories appear; Advanced per-category reveals appears only when advanced mode is on. The inherited defaults below appear checked when their rows are available.

Setting Default What it does TV show descriptions Inherit Uncheck to permit guarded TV show descriptions. Episode descriptions Inherit Uncheck to permit eligible episode, movie, season, and extra descriptions. Episode titles Inherit Uncheck to disable episode/eligible season title replacement. Description-driven search fallback can still hide a hint name. Chapter names Inherit Uncheck to retain names. Images and auxiliary image-path clearing remain separate. Cast list Inherit Uncheck to stop cast-list filtering; title/description protection can still clear roles. Ratings Inherit Uncheck to permit community/critic scores and their overlays. Air date Inherit Uncheck to retain eligible premiere dates. Taglines Inherit Uncheck to retain eligible taglines. Tags Inherit Uncheck to retain story tags and overlays governed by tags policy. Reviews Inherit Uncheck to permit the JE Reviews panel when otherwise available. Seek previews Inherit Uncheck to see trickplay thumbnails while seeking through an unwatched episode or movie. Appears only while Hide trickplay seek previews is on. Advanced per-category reveals Inherit Uncheck to disable category metadata reveals and the next-episode image exception. Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off Off Check to skip confirmation permanently for this account.

Refresh existing content

Preference saves do not refresh detail-page images or trigger strict reload. Navigate or reload to update existing content.

Preference storage and limits

Users cannot enable a protection category the admin disabled. Seek previews is the only image policy with a per-user override; other image replacement follows admin policy. On a shared address where JE cannot tell which signed-in user fetched a preview, the opt-out applies only when every user whose protection covers the item unchecked Seek previews; played-state and saved-progress reveals still follow the first such user. If initial state loading fails, preference controls are disabled to avoid overwriting unknown state.

Checking a category saves null (inherit); unchecking saves false. The inherited defaults are nullable. Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off defaults to false. These preferences live in UserSpoilerBlur.Prefs within spoilerblur.json.

The dialog's Don't ask again for 15 minutes is a separate per-account, per-browser local-storage snooze. Unchecking the permanent preference restores confirmation subject to any active snooze.

Setting Internal property TV show descriptions HideSeriesDescriptions Episode descriptions HideEpisodeDescriptions Episode titles ReplaceEpisodeTitles Chapter names HideChapterNames Cast list HideCast Ratings HideRatings Air date HideAirDate Taglines HideTaglines Tags HideTags Reviews HideReviews Seek previews HideTrickplay Advanced per-category reveals UseAdvancedCategories Don't ask me to confirm when turning Spoiler Guard off SkipDisableConfirm

docs.title: Automatic per-user image identity tags
docs.text:
Image tags help the server apply your account's protection behind proxies or shared networks. No separate Spoiler Guard setting is needed.

How to use: Keep the master on and fetch fresh authenticated metadata to obtain updated tags. Your client needs to use the returned image tags.

How it works

When the master is on, recognized authenticated-user DTO responses receive per-user image-tag markers. A client echoing those tags lets the server select the user's policy. Userless API-key responses do not automatically receive a user marker.

Requests without usable identity may pass through. Ambiguous image requests apply the first scope-matching candidate's played/progress state and exemptions; a Seek previews opt-out applies only when every scope-matching candidate made it. Markers are not credentials. See per-user identity and limits.

docs.title: Health: spoiler-state corruption recovery
docs.text:
Spoiler Guard stores each account's title lists and preferences in a file. Back up the per-user configuration directory so you can restore protection if that file becomes unreadable.

How to recover:

  1. Check server logs and the authenticated health endpoint described below.
  2. Restore a known-good file or reconfigure your title list and preferences.
  3. Reload any web session whose state failed to load.

Unreadable state can stop protection

Some reads return empty defaults when state is unreadable. An empty health response does not prove every store is readable. There is no in-UI health banner.

Storage and corruption handling

User state is stored at:

<Jellyfin PluginsPath>/configurations/Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/<user-id-N>/spoilerblur.json

The user ID uses 32 hexadecimal characters without hyphens. Series, Movies, and Collections are keyed by item ID; PendingTmdb uses tv:<id> or movie:<id> keys. Entries retain IDs/names and enable/request timestamps, and Prefs holds personal choices. Fresh lists are empty.

Strict Spoiler Guard operations can quarantine an unreadable store as spoilerblur.json.corrupt-<timestamp>-<suffix> and return an error. Relevant interactive endpoints record corruption and return HTTP 503 asking you to reconfigure. A quarantine move does not immediately write a replacement defaults file. If moving fails, deletion can be attempted instead.

Image/metadata filtering and the raw inspection GET use lenient reads that can return empty defaults without quarantine or a health event. Bulk operations can log failures without recording health events.

Inspecting and acknowledging health events

Use authenticated GET /JellyfinEnhanced/spoiler-blur/health to inspect recorded events. It returns healthy and corruptionEvents, with each event's userId, userDisplay, at, and reason. Viewers see their own events; admins see all.

Health retains only the latest recorded event per user in process memory. A server restart clears it.

DELETE /JellyfinEnhanced/spoiler-blur/health/{targetUserId} acknowledges your own event, or any user's event as admin. Acknowledgment clears the event, not backups or protection state.

docs.title: Inspection and automation endpoints
docs.text:
Use authenticated endpoints to inspect or automate your protection lists and preferences. They also provide admin actions for existing titles and health events.

How to use: Choose a route from the reference below and authenticate with the appropriate user or admin account. Back up current state before replacing a whole file.

Full-state replacement

A raw spoilerblur.json POST replaces the entire document rather than merging. Omitted lists or preferences can be removed or reset. Back up the current state before using this repair or automation route.

Endpoint reference

All paths below have the prefix /JellyfinEnhanced and require authentication. Current-user actions use the token's user identity. An identityless admin credential cannot select a user through those URLs.

Raw file routes allow self/admin access. Apply-existing/health actions perform their additional admin/self checks inside the actions rather than using a named admin authorization policy.

Method and path suffix Access Purpose and explicit body limit GET /spoiler-blur/series Current user Full Series, Movies, Collections, PendingTmdb, and Prefs state. No body. GET /spoiler-blur/user-prefs Current user Reads preferences. No body. POST /spoiler-blur/user-prefs Current user Replaces the preferences object from JSON; 8,192 bytes. POST /spoiler-blur/series/{seriesId} Current user Adds a direct Series entry after type/access validation. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. DELETE /spoiler-blur/series/{seriesId} Current user Removes the direct Series entry. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. POST /spoiler-blur/movies/{movieId} Current user Adds a direct Movie entry after type/access validation. Optional JSON MovieName; 8,192 bytes. DELETE /spoiler-blur/movies/{movieId} Current user Removes the direct Movie entry. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. POST /spoiler-blur/collections/{collectionId} Current user Adds a BoxSet entry after type/access validation. Optional JSON CollectionName; 8,192 bytes. DELETE /spoiler-blur/collections/{collectionId} Current user Removes the collection entry. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. POST /spoiler-blur/pending/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Current user; master on Adds pending protection or immediately promotes an accessible match. Optional query displayName; no body parameter or action-specific body limit. DELETE /spoiler-blur/pending/{mediaType}/{tmdbId} Current user Removes pending and matching accessible direct Series/Movie state. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. GET /user-settings/{userId}/spoilerblur.json Self or Administrator role Lenient full-state inspection. No body. POST /user-settings/{userId}/spoilerblur.json Self or Administrator role Full JSON replacement; 2,097,152 bytes (2 MiB), at most 1,000 entries in each dictionary. GET /spoiler-blur/apply-existing/preview?skipStarted=false Admin; master on Saved-scope dry run. No body. POST /spoiler-blur/apply-existing?skipStarted=false Admin; master on Starts the registered scheduled task; accepted start returns 202. No body parameter or action-specific body limit. GET /spoiler-blur/apply-existing/status Admin Task state, progress, and last-run data. No body. GET /spoiler-blur/health Viewer: own; admin: all Recorded process-lifetime events. No body. DELETE /spoiler-blur/health/{targetUserId} Self or admin Acknowledges an event. No body parameter or action-specific body limit.

“No action-specific body limit” does not mean unlimited server acceptance. Supplied movie/collection display names are sanitized and capped at 200 characters. Direct-entry DELETE does not require the same item lookup as POST and can succeed with removed=false. Direct-state and preference actions work even with the master off; pending POST returns 503 when it is off, and apply-existing preview/start return 409.

Pending media types normalize to tv/movie; TMDB IDs must be positive 32-bit integers. Pending POST returns {success, promoted, jellyfinId, name}, where promoted is pending, series, or movie. New pending inserts at the normal 500-entry cap return 429 with code="pending_cap_exceeded"; existing entries can still be updated or promoted. Pending DELETE reports removed, removedFrom, and a resolved Jellyfin ID when applicable; no-op success uses removed=false, removedFrom="none".

The raw file POST's 1,000-entry-per-dictionary cap differs from normal pending insertion. Exceeding it returns 413. Corrupt existing data can return 503; temporary I/O or save failures can return 500.

docs.title: What gets logged
docs.text:
JE logs Spoiler Guard activity so you can investigate automatic protection or storage problems.

How to use: Open JellyfinEnhanced_YYYY-MM-DD.log in Jellyfin's configured log directory and look for the events below.

Log events and levels

Selected diagnostic warnings are rate-limited; ordinary informational events are not all rate-limited.

Look for first-play events (SpoilerAutoEnable), library-add batches (SpoilerAutoEnableOnLibraryAdd), apply-existing per-user/summary results (SpoilerApplyExisting), Seerr pending records and promotions (SpoilerSeerrPromoter), failed cache evictions, unexpected response shapes, and corruption/quarantine paths.

Informational events normally use INFO; corruption and unexpected-shape diagnostics use WARNING.
